Article.ArticleTitle: Low-Level Light Therapy for Dry Eye Disease in Thyroid Eye Disease: A Randomized, Double-Masked, Sham-Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Dry eye disease (DED) affects the majority of patients with thyroid eye disease (TED) and frequently persists despite maximal conservative therapy. Low-level light therapy (LLLT), or photobiomodulation, is a non-invasive treatment with anti-inflammatory and pro-reparative properties whose value in autoimmune, chronically driven ocular surface disease is unknown. In this prospective, randomized, double-masked, sham-controlled trial, eyes of patients with TED-associated DED that remained symptomatic despite intensive preservative-free lubrication, bedtime ophthalmic ointment and daily periocular hygiene were allocated 2:1 to periocular LLLT (630 nm LED mask, 15 min per session, applied over closed eyelids) or to sham treatment (identical procedure with light emission reduced to <30% of therapeutic output). Background ocular surface therapy was maintained unchanged in both arms. Assessments were performed at baseline (T0), weekly during treatment (T1-T3) and at one month (T4) and two months (T5) after the last session. The primary outcome was the Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI); secondary outcomes were non-invasive break-up time (NIBUT), fluorescein break-up time (FBUT), Schirmer I test, tear osmolarity, upper- and lower-eyelid meibography, corneal fluorescein staining and lipid-layer grade. The primary OSDI assessment was the change from baseline to T3, the end-of-treatment visit. Additional follow-up assessments were performed at T4 and T5. Forty-six eyes of 46 patients were analyzed (30 LLLT, 16 sham); baseline disease was active in 14/30 (46.7%) and 6/16 (37.5%) eyes, respectively. At T3, adjusted OSDI was lower with LLLT than with sham (between-group difference -7.49 points; 95% CI -11.66 to -3.32; p < 0.001). The difference persisted at T4 and T5 (-11.97 and -16.86 points, respectively; both Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). Tear osmolarity was lower with LLLT at T4 (-10.91 mOsm/L; 95% CI -18.96 to -2.87; p = 0.009) and T5 (-13.81 mOsm/L; 95% CI -22.55 to -5.06; p = 0.004). No multiplicity-adjusted between-group differences were demonstrated for NIBUT, FBUT, Schirmer I test or meibography. The adjusted probability of corneal staining was numerically lower with LLLT (T4: 15.7% vs. 34.7%; risk difference -19.0 percentage points; p = 0.100). In exploratory analyses, the treatment-by-visit-by-activity interaction was significant (p = 0.0159), with OSDI differences of -21.45 and -25.90 points in active disease versus -5.50 and -10.09 points in inactive disease at T4 and T5. CAS and OSDI were positively correlated at baseline (Spearman ρ = 0.547; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001) and at T5 (Spearman ρ = 0.428; Holm-adjusted p = 0.003). No treatment-related adverse events occurred. In conclusion, in TED-associated DED refractory to maximal conservative therapy, LLLT produced a significant and progressively increasing reduction in symptom burden together with an objective reduction in tear hyperosmolarity. Effects on break-up time, aqueous secretion, gland morphology, and lipid layer grade were not demonstrable within two months. The pattern and pace of response differ from those observed with the same technology after cataract surgery and are consistent with a chronic, systemically driven disease in which the ocular surface insult is continuously renewed.

Article.ArticleTitle: TNF rs1800629 Genotype and Motor Response to Intensive Rehabilitation in Parkinson's Disease: An Exploratory Study.

Abstract.AbstractText: Rehabilitation is a key component of Parkinson's disease (PD) management, although individual responses differ substantially. Genetic factors involved in neuroplasticity and inflammation may contribute to this variability. We investigated whether selected polymorphisms in inflammation- and neuroplasticity-related genes influence motor outcomes following intensive multidisciplinary rehabilitation in patients with PD. Sixty-six patients with a diagnosis of idiopathic PD were consecutively enrolled and randomly allocated to an intensive multidisciplinary rehabilitation group (EXP-Group, n = 34) or a home-based stretching control group (CTRL-Group, n = 32) for six weeks. MDS-UPDRS III score was assessed at baseline (T0) and post-treatment (T1). SNPs in the TNF, IL6, IL6R, IL1A, IL1B, IL10 and BDNF genes were genotyped. Possible associations between genotype, treatment group and MDS-UPDRS III score at T1 were analyzed using ANCOVA and linear mixed-effects models, adjusting for baseline MDS-UPDRS III score, age, sex, disease duration and levodopa equivalent daily dose (LEDD). A significant treatment group x TNF rs1800629 genotype interaction was observed (p = 0.033). Among EXP-Group patients, GG homozygotes showed lower adjusted MDS-UPDRS III scores than did the A-allele carriers (29.10 vs. 36.11; p = 0.029). Longitudinal analyses revealed a significant time × treatment group × TNF rs1800629 genotype interaction (p = 0.010), with GG homozygotes showing an approximately 10-point reduction in MDS-UPDRS III score (40.87 to 30.87; p < 0.001). These findings suggest that TNF rs1800629 contributes to variability in response to intensive multidisciplinary rehabilitation in PD.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of Nurse-Delivered Chlorhexidine Versus Saline Oral Care on Ventilator-Associated Events in Medical Intensive Care Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: To evaluate the effectiveness of nurse-delivered oral care using 0.12% chlorhexidine versus normal saline in reducing ventilator-associated events and improving clinical and oral health outcomes among adults receiving invasive mechanical ventilation in a medical intensive care unit.
Single-center, parallel-group, assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial.

Adults receiving invasive mechanical ventilation were randomly allocated to receive oral care with either 0.12% chlorhexidine or normal saline every eight hours until extubation or discharge from the ICU. The primary outcome was ventilator-associated events. Secondary outcomes included ventilator-associated pneumonia, duration of mechanical ventilation, length of stay in the intensive care unit, mortality in the intensive care unit, oral health status and intervention-related adverse events.

A total of 141 participants were randomized. No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in ventilator-associated events, ventilator-associated pneumonia, duration of mechanical ventilation, length of stay in the intensive care unit, mortality in the intensive care unit, oral health status, or intervention-related adverse events.

In this single-center superiority randomized controlled trial, nurse-delivered oral care with 0.12% chlorhexidine did not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in ventilator-associated events compared with normal saline. Given the wide confidence intervals and lower-than-expected event rates, these findings do not confirm equivalence but suggest that routine chlorhexidine may provide limited incremental benefit over standardized mechanical oral hygiene in medical intensive care unit patients.

AbstractText.Label: IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE

Abstract.AbstractText: Intensive care nurses might prioritize the consistent implementation of structured, evidence-based oral care protocols. Routine use of chlorhexidine may provide limited additional benefit over normal saline in this patient population.

This study addresses the ongoing uncertainty regarding the effectiveness of chlorhexidine for routine oral care in mechanically ventilated adults. No significant differences were observed between chlorhexidine and normal saline in ventilator-associated events, clinical outcomes, oral health outcomes, or adverse events. These findings add to the growing body of evidence suggesting that the incremental benefit of chlorhexidine beyond standardized mechanical oral care may be limited and support further adequately powered multicenter trials to define its role in different intensive care populations.
This study adhered to the Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials guideline.

ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05913856. Available at: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05913856. The trial was registered after participant recruitment had commenced because of an administrative delay. No changes were made to the study design, eligibility criteria, outcomes, or analysis plan after registration.

Article.ArticleTitle: Pre-IVF lifestyle intervention and reproductive outcomes in women with overweight or obesity undergoing IVF: a randomized clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Obesity is associated with reduced female fertility and poorer in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes. Although pre-IVF lifestyle-based weight loss is commonly recommended for women with overweight or obesity, whether specific strategies improve reproductive outcomes remains uncertain. We compared two pre-IVF lifestyle interventions with usual care in women undergoing IVF.

In this single-center, parallel-group randomized clinical trial conducted at Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University, Shenyang, China, women aged 20-38 years with a body mass index (BMI) of 24-40 kg/m² planning IVF were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to 12-hour time-restricted feeding plus moderate physical activity (TRF + PA), a calorie-restricted diet (CRD), or usual care. Recruitment took place from March 14, 2023, to August 20, 2024, and follow-up was completed on February 20, 2026. The primary outcome was cumulative live birth. Secondary outcomes included cumulative clinical pregnancy, miscarriage, obstetric complications, embryological outcomes, anthropometric changes, and metabolic measures.

A total of 273 women underwent randomization. Cumulative live birth did not differ between groups, occurring in 46.6% of women in the TRF + PA group, 43.8% in the CRD group, and 44.0% in the control group (P = 0.916). After adjustment for baseline waist circumference, neither intervention was associated with cumulative live birth compared with usual care (TRF + PA vs. control: adjusted risk ratio [aRR] 1.034; 95% CI, 0.746-1.434; P = 0.839; CRD vs. control: aRR 0.936; 95% CI, 0.676-1.295; P = 0.689). TRF + PA was associated with a greater reduction in homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) than usual care (P = 0.005). In analyses treating anthropometric change as a continuous exposure, greater reduction in body fat percentage was independently associated with a higher probability of live birth (per 1-percentage-point reduction: aRR 1.065; 95% CI, 1.021-1.111; P = 0.003). Exploratory spline analyses suggested a threshold, with higher live birth probability observed above an absolute reduction of 5.16% points in body fat percentage.

Among women with overweight or obesity undergoing IVF, pre-IVF lifestyle intervention did not improve cumulative live birth compared with usual care. However, reduction in body fat percentage was independently associated with live birth, suggesting that change in adiposity may be more relevant to reproductive outcomes than weight loss alone.

Article.ArticleTitle: Comparison of the effects of normal saline versus Plasma-Lyte® on acid-base balance during living donor kidney transplantation surgery using goal-directed fluid therapy based on pulse pressure variation- a randomised controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Normal saline (NS) is commonly used during kidney transplantation but may cause hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis when administered in large volumes. Balanced crystalloids such as Plasma-Lyte® (PL) may attenuate these effects. We compared acid-base outcomes of NS versus PL when administered using pulse pressure variation (PPV)- guided goal-directed fluid therapy during living donor kidney transplantation (LDKT).

In this prospective randomised assessor-blinded trial, adult patients undergoing LDKT were allocated to receive intraoperative NS or PL. Fluid administration was titrated according to a predefined PPV-guided algorithm. Acid-base status was assessed using the Stewart physicochemical analysis. The primary endpoint was the difference in apparent strong ion difference (SIDa). Secondary outcome measurements included haemodynamics, electrolytes, lactate, serum creatinine trends, dialysis requirement, and graft function.

A total of 111 patients were analysed (NS, n = 55, PL, n = 56). Baseline characteristics and total intraoperative fluid volumes were comparable (1796 ± 337 vs 1903 ± 434 mL; p = 0.15). Apparent strong ion difference declined over time in both groups (time effect p < 0.001), but did not differ between groups (group effect p = 0.50; interaction p = 0.37). In the baseline-adjusted analysis (ANCOVA) of the primary endpoint, the adjusted between-group difference in SIDa at the end of surgery was 0.71 mmol/L (90% CI - 0.90 to + 2.32 mmol/L) against the pre-specified equivalence margin of ± 2 mmol/L; formal equivalence was not established, although no significant difference was detected (adjusted p = 0.46). Effective strong ion difference (SID e), strong ion gap (SIG), pH, serum potassium, and lactate were similar at all measured time points (p > 0.05). Early graft dysfunction (4.1% vs 7.4%; p = 0.472) and delayed graft function (3.6% vs 0%; p = 0.150) did not differ significantly; however, the trial was not powered for these exploratory outcomes. Postoperative creatinine trajectories did not differ between groups.

During LDKT, PPV-guided goal-directed fluid therapy produced no significant between-group difference in acid-base balance or early graft outcomes with NS and PL. Formal equivalence in the primary endpoint was not established; nonetheless, at the moderate volumes delivered, the findings suggest that haemodynamic strategy may influence perioperative acid-base status more than crystalloid choice.
The study was prospectively registered in the Clinical Trials Registry of India (ctri.nic.in) Registration number: CTRI/2021/01/030227 Registered on 04/01/2021.

Article.ArticleTitle: Impact of pre-chemotherapy food intake on chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting in patients with early breast cancer: a subanalysis of the randomized SUCCESS C trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) remains a challenging side effect, significantly impacting patients' quality of life [1-3]. Knowledge of eating behaviour's influence on CINV is still limited. This study improves the understanding of CINV by investigating the impact of pre-chemotherapy food intake within the randomized Phase III SUCCESS C trial.

The SUCCESS C trial (NCT00847444), enrolled ,463 women with early-stage, HER2-negative breast cancer, receiving either three cycles of 5-fluorouracil (500 mg/m2), epirubicin (100 mg/m2), and cyclophosphamide (500 mg/m2) followed by three cycles of docetaxel (100 mg/m2) every 3 weeks (FEC), or six cycles of docetaxel (75 mg/m2) and cyclophosphamide (600 mg/m2) (TC). The present analysis included patients with completed CINV diary with hourly documentation over 5 days post-chemotherapy.

CINV diary data during chemotherapy cycles 1-3 were available for 1582 patients, of whom 814 received FEC and 768 TC. Patient characteristics between chemotherapy arms were comparable. For FEC, pre-chemotherapy eating behaviour had a significant impact on nausea-free survival (NFS) in cycle 1 (p = 0.04) and on emesis-free survival (EFS) in cycle 2 (p = 0.02). For TC, no effect on NFS, but a significant effect on EFS (p = 0.04 in cycle 1; p < 0.01 in cycle 2), was observed. Median EFS was approximately 120 h for all cycles and treatments.

This analysis demonstrates in both regimens less emesis, and for FEC less nausea, of patients with pre-chemotherapy food intake. The effect was most pronounced during the first 24 h after chemotherapy administration. Thus, eating behaviour influences CINV outcomes and warrants further evaluation.

Article.ArticleTitle: Neuronavigation-assisted versus conventional endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal surgery for pituitary adenomas: a pilot randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Evidence on the benefit of intraoperative neuronavigation in endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal (EET) pituitary surgery remains mixed. We conducted a pilot randomized controlled trial comparing navigation-assisted and conventional EET surgery for pituitary adenomas, to estimate the effect size for a definitive multicentre trial.

At Ain Shams University (April 2025-February 2026), 57 patients with pituitary adenomas were assessed for eligibility; 7 were excluded for prior Gamma Knife radiosurgery. The remaining 50 were randomized 1:1 within strata of tumor size, functional status, and surgery status, with concealed computer-generated allocation. Recruitment continued until the planned 25 patients per arm were enrolled. The primary outcome was extent of resection; secondary outcomes included operative time, blood loss, visual and hormonal outcomes, and complications.

All 50 patients (25 per arm) were analyzed by intention-to-treat. Gross total resection was numerically higher with navigation (28.0% vs. 16.0%; p = 0.496); adjusted for Knosp grade, the odds ratio was 2.66 (95% CI 0.41-17.06) versus a crude 2.04. Extent of resection was strongly associated with tumor size, functioning status, and Knosp grade; no giant adenoma achieved gross total resection. Blood loss was lower with navigation (median 250 vs. 350 mL; p = 0.016), with no difference in operative time, which included navigation setup (p = 0.788).

Neuronavigation did not significantly improve extent of resection, though resection completeness trended favorably with navigation across most subgroups. The associated blood-loss reduction remains hypothesis-generating. A definitive, adequately powered multicentre trial is warranted.

Article.ArticleTitle: AS01E-adjuvanted RSV pre-F protein vaccine in adults with lung or kidney transplant: a phase 2b randomized trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Immunocompromised adults are at increased risk of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease. This multicountry, open-label phase 2b trial (NCT05921903) evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of the AS01E-adjuvanted RSV prefusion F protein vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) over 12 months in kidney or lung transplant recipients ≥18 years, randomized 1:1 to receive one (n = 131) or two doses 30-60 days apart (n = 130). A control group of non-immunocompromised adults ≥50 years (n = 125) received a single dose. The primary outcome was the mean geometric increase in RSV-A and RSV-B neutralizing titers one month following a second adjuvanted RSVPreF3 dose relative to the first dose in transplant recipients. Secondary outcomes included assessment of the safety and immunogenicity of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in transplant recipients compared with the control group. In transplant recipients receiving two doses, neutralizing titers against RSV-A and RSV-B were numerically higher one month post-dose 2 than post-dose 1 (mean geometric increases: 1.34 [95% CI: 1.20, 1.48] for RSV-A [n = 111] and 1.26 [95% CI: 1.14, 1.40] for RSV-B [n = 111]). A single dose was immunogenic in transplant recipients, but showed slower and generally lower initial neutralizing responses than in non-immunocompromised controls, specifically in individuals receiving mycophenolate. RSVPreF3-specific CD4 + T-cell frequencies increased after vaccination versus baseline in all groups. Humoral and cell-mediated immune responses remained above baseline for 12 months post-vaccination. Both doses of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 were well tolerated and had a similar and acceptable safety profile. Overall, these results support a favorable benefit-risk profile of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in kidney and lung transplant recipients.

Article.ArticleTitle: Exploring Candidate Mechanisms of Change of EMIcompass, a Novel, Transdiagnostic Ecological Momentary Intervention for Prevention and Early Intervention in Youth: Findings From a Secondary Analysis of an Exploratory Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Ecological momentary interventions targeting transdiagnostic mechanisms are promising for prevention and early intervention, but evidence on their mechanisms of change is very limited.

To explore indirect effects of EMIcompass, a transdiagnostic, compassion-focused ecological momentary intervention, on mental health outcomes (i.e., psychological distress, clinical symptoms, quality of life) via candidate mechanisms of change (i.e., stress reactivity, emotional reactivity, threat anticipation, resilience and aberrant salience) in youth with early mental health problems.

We conducted a secondary analysis of an exploratory, assessor-blind randomized controlled trial, in which youth aged 14-25 years with early mental health problems were randomly allocated to experimental (EMIcompass + treatment as usual [TAU]) or control condition (TAU). Data was collected before randomization, at post-intervention and at four-week follow-up.

N = 92 participants were recruited, of which n = 46 were allocated to the experimental condition. No signals of indirect effects of condition on any outcome through the five mechanisms (i.e., 95% confidence intervals included zero) were found. The magnitude of association, however, indicated that the association between EMIcompass and psychological distress may be mediated via pathways through threat anticipation (β = -0.12, 95% CI = -0.30-0.03). Further, we observed associations between changes in candidate mechanisms and mental health outcomes.

Although no direct signals of mediation via candidate mechanisms were observed due to lack of power, condition-linked shifts in our candidate mechanisms were associated with mental-health outcomes. Larger mechanism-powered trials are now required to delineate causal pathways and refine scalable prevention and early intervention strategies.

Article.ArticleTitle: Chin Tuck Against Resistance Exercise With Feedback to Improve Swallowing, Eating, and Drinking in Frail Older People Admitted to Hospital With Pneumonia (CTAR-SwiFt): Randomized Controlled Feasibility Study.

Abstract.AbstractText: Community-acquired pneumonia in frail older people requiring hospital admission is considered to be commonly associated with swallowing difficulties (dysphagia). A rehabilitation program (chin tuck against resistance [CTAR]) targeting the anterior neck musculature involved in laryngeal movement can improve swallowing safety. We have developed a swallowing exercise rehabilitation intervention (CTAR-SwiFt [Chin Tuck Against Resistance Exercise With Feedback to Improve Swallowing, Eating, and Drinking in Frail Older People Admitted to Hospital With Pneumonia]) by adapting a previously established swallowing exercise. The CTAR-SwiFt intervention consists of a feedback-enabled exercise ball that can be squeezed under the chin, with real-time feedback provided via a mobile app.
This study aimed to assess the usability of the CTAR-SwiFt intervention and the feasibility of recruiting participants to take part in a larger-scale multicenter randomized controlled trial.

We recruited participants aged 75 years and older who were admitted with a diagnosis of pneumonia to the acute frailty wards at 2 participating hospitals in the United Kingdom. Patients had to be medically stable. Study participants were randomized to 1 of 3 groups: standard care (control), low intensity (once daily), or high intensity (twice daily) CTAR-SwiFt exercises. The intervention period lasted for 12 weeks; the final follow-up assessment was conducted at 24 weeks. Feasibility outcomes were assessed descriptively and included participant recruitment rate, retention, compliance with the exercise regimen, and adverse incidents. The Eating Assessment Tool-10 (EAT-10) and 4 Question Test (4QT) measures were used to screen for oropharyngeal dysphagia. Additionally, we assessed the usability and acceptability of the intervention device and performance of different clinical outcome measures (chin tuck strength, Functional Oral Intake Scale [FOIS], Quality of Life in Swallowing Disorders [SWAL-QOL] questionnaire, EuroQol 5-Dimension 3-Level [EQ-5D-3L] questionnaire, and swallow speed).

A total of 24 participants were recruited, and 21 were randomized at the rate of 0.91 recruits per month (95% CI 0.59-1.0). Of those approached, 32% (24/75) were willing to take part, and of those randomized, 52% (11/21) completed the study. The major reason for failing to complete the study was medical, with people becoming unwell or being readmitted to hospital. The outcome measures assessed suggested that there was an improvement in the EAT-10 and 4QT and a minimal impact on FOIS. Quality of life as measured by the EQ-5D-3L showed improvement with time. The low-intensity intervention demonstrated the best improvement. Participants were able to partake in the CTAR-SwiFt exercises. There was an improvement in the consistency of ball squeeze over the course of the intervention and an increase in maximum chin tuck strength by a mean of 0.8 (SD 0.9) kgf.

The literature supports the benefit of CTAR in improving swallowing in community-dwelling older adults. Our study has demonstrated that older, frail adults are able to perform CTAR and could use the ExerPhager. A future study should investigate the benefits of CTAR-SwiFt in community-dwelling older, frail adults after pneumonia.

Article.ArticleTitle: Adding Nitrate to a Sucrose Rinse Reduces Acidogenicity: An in vivo Study.

Abstract.AbstractText: Potential dental health benefits, including pH buffering, have been demonstrated for nitrate in placebo-controlled studies when consumed one or several hours before sugar intake. However, its immediate local effect when co-administered with sugar is unclear. Our aim was to test the local effect of adding nitrate to a sugar rinse on human saliva acidification.

A double-blind, crossover study was conducted with three periods. In each period, 18 adults, equally distributed between men and women (n = 9 each), aged 25.4 ± 3.8 (mean ± SD), with normal salivary flow, rinsed for 2 min using 10 mL of one of the following rinses: spinach-only (blended spinach providing 8 mm nitrate), spinach+sucrose (blended spinach providing 8 mm nitrate + 20% sucrose), or sucrose-only (20% sucrose). Unstimulated saliva was collected at baseline and every 3 min up to 24 min. pH, lactate, nitrate, and nitrite were measured using Reflectoquant®. The effect of treatment and time was assessed using a linear mixed model (α = 0.05). Nitrate reduction capacity was determined in vitro using baseline saliva.

All saliva samples demonstrated nitrate reduction activity. The lowest pH values were observed 6 min after rinsing, with all groups differing from each other: sucrose only (6.56 ± 0.38; mean ± SD), spinach+sucrose (6.83 ± 0.37), spinach only (7.15 ± 0.44, no pH drop). The pH returned to baseline values 12 min after the spinach+sucrose rinse, but not after the sucrose-only rinse at any time point. Nitrate and nitrite concentrations increased in saliva after using spinach-containing rinses, returning to their baseline levels after 6 min and 12 min. Lower lactate levels were detected after 12 min, suggesting proton consumption during nitrate metabolism in the spinach+sucrose group.
Adding a low dose of nitrate to a sucrose rinse limited sugar-induced salivary acidification in vivo, supporting the potential for topical nitrate strategies to reduce sugar acidogenicity.

OtherAbstract.AbstractText: This study explored whether mixing a small amount of nitrate from spinach with sugar (i.e., 5 mg nitrate per 2 g sucrose) could reduce the drop in pH that usually occurs in saliva after consuming sugar. When sugar is eaten, bacteria in the mouth produce acid, which can lead to tooth demineralization over time. Nitrate is a natural compound found in vegetables like spinach and can be converted by bacteria in the mouth into other substances that may help reduce saliva acidogenicity. In this study, 18 healthy adults participated in three separate test sessions. In each session, they rinsed their mouths with one of three solutions: sugar-only, spinach-only, or spinach plus sugar. Saliva samples were collected before and after each rinse (up to 24 min) to measure pH (acidity), nitrate, nitrite, and lactate levels. The results showed that rinsing with the sugar-only solution caused a drop in salivary pH. However, in the spinach plus sugar condition, the drop in pH was less severe and recovered more quickly. This suggests that nitrate may help reduce the acid effects of sugar in the mouth. Saliva from all participants was also able to convert nitrate to nitrite, which supports this effect. These findings support the idea that natural nitrate, when delivered together with sugar, could help mitigate pH drops. However, more studies are needed to test whether this approach can help prevent dental demineralization in real-life settings.

Article.ArticleTitle: [Effect of nutritional support on postoperative period in diabetic patients with protein and energy deficiency after limb amputation].

Abstract.AbstractText: To analyze efficacy and safety of postoperative nutritional support using LEOVIT PHARMA therapeutic enteral nutrition in patients with diabetes mellitus after limb amputation.

A prospective randomized study included 119 patients (80 in the study group and 39 in the control group) with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM2). All patients signed an informed consent to participate in clinical study. Inclusion criteria: patient consent to participate; age over 18 years; primary diagnosis of DM2, diabetic angiopathy, and lower-limb gangrene; surgical intervention involving amputation of thigh, lower leg or toes; mild, moderate, or severe protein-energy malnutrition; ECOG score > 2-3; PG-SGA score ≥ 9. Exclusion criteria: patient refusal to participate at any stage; allergic or adverse reactions at any stage; severe mental illness. Patients were assigned to groups using a cluster method (ratio 2:1). Regarding nutritional support regimen, patients in the study group were prescribed LEOVIT PHARMA enteral nutrition according to the manufacturer's protocol. For the first 3 days prior to surgery, patients received a restorative protein shake (one single-serving packet, 4 times daily). Postoperatively, they received a detoxifying protein shake for subsequent 6 days (4 times daily). Patients received LEOVIT PHARMA protein shake for a total of 9 days. Patients in the second group received standard enteral nutrition. Preoperative nutritional management relied primarily on standard low-calorie diet, while postoperative regimen consisted of a gentle (bland) diet.

A new oral nutritional supplement (sipping formula) facilitated reparative processes at the surgical site. Microscopic analysis of wound exudate revealed a shortened alteration phase of healing process and rapid onset of reparative phase. Specifically, regenerative-degenerative index in the study group in early postoperative period was 16.3-21.2% higher than in the control group (p<0.05). Studies noted a relatively rapid transformation of polyblasts into connective tissue cells. Sipping therapy using specialized LEOVIT PHARMA enteral formulas was associated with a 17.6% reduction in total number of complications (χ²=2.78, p=0.041).

This prospective randomized study demonstrates that LEOVIT PHARMA enteral nutrition product for patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus undergoing amputation is a highly effective and safe therapeutic component.

Article.VernacularTitle: Vliyanie nutritivnoi podderzhki na techenie posleoperatsionnogo perioda u bol'nykh sakharnym diabetom s belkovo-energeticheskoi nedostatochnost'yu posle amputatsii konechnosti.

OtherAbstract.AbstractText: Клинико-лабораторная оценка эффективности и безопасности нутритивной поддержки с применением лечебного энтерального питания ЛЕОВИТ PHARMA — Коктейля белкового восстанавливающего и Коктейля белкового детоксикационного — в послеоперационный период у больных сахарным диабетом (СД), перенесших ампутацию конечности.

В проспективное рандомизированное исследование включены 119 пациентов (80 — основная группа и 39 — контрольная группа), страдающих СД 2-го типа. Все пациенты подписали добровольное согласие на участие в клиническом исследовании. Критерии включения: согласие пациента на участие в исследовании, возраст старше 18 лет, основной диагноз — СД 2-го типа, диабетическая ангиопатия, гангрена нижней конечности, хирургическое вмешательство в объеме ампутации конечности на уровне бедра, голени, а также пальцев стопы, белково-энергетическая недостаточность легкой, средней и тяжелой степени, оценка общего состояния больного по ECOG >2—3, оценка состояния пациента по PG-SGA ≥9 баллов. Критерии исключения: отказ пациента от участия в исследовании на любом этапе, развитие аллергических и побочных реакций на любом этапе исследования, тяжелые психические заболевания. Распределение по сравниваемым группам осуществлялось кластерным методом в соотношении 2:1. В соответствии с вариантом нутритивной поддержки основной группе пациентов в качестве нутритивной поддержки было назначено специализированное энтеральное питание ЛЕОВИТ PHARMA по схеме производителя. В первые 3 сут до операции пациенты получали Коктейль белковый восстанавливающий по 1 разовой упаковке 4 раза в сутки, а после операции Коктейль белковый детоксикационный в течение последующих 6 сут 4 раза в сутки. Коктейли белковые ЛЕОВИТ PHARMA пациенты получали в течение 9 дней. Пациенты из контрольной группы принимали стандартное энтеральное питание. Питание пациентов до операции — вариант стандартной диеты с пониженной калорийностью (НКД), после операции — щадящая диета.

Применение нового сиппингового питания способствовало интенсификации репаративных процессов в зоне хирургического вмешательства. При микроскопической оценке раневого экссудата установлено сокращение альтеративной фазы процесса заживления и сравнительно быстрое появление репаративной фазы. Так, регенеративно-дегенеративный индекс у пациентов в основной группе в раннем послеоперационном периоде был выше контроля на 16,3—21,2% (p<0,05). Отмечено сравнительно быстрое преобразование полибластов в клетки соединительной ткани. Сиппинг-терапия с применением специализированных энтеральных смесей ЛЕОВИТ PHARMA сопровождалась снижением общего числа осложнений на 17,6 (χ²=2,78; p=0,041).

Проведенное проспективное рандомизированное исследование показало, что включение Коктейля белкового детоксикационного и Коктейля белкового восстанавливающего ЛЕОВИТ PHARMA в комплексную терапию пациентов с СД 2-го типа, перенесших ампутацию, является высокоэффективным и безопасным компонентом комплексной терапии.

Journal.Title: The primary care companion for CNS disorders

Article.ArticleTitle: Efficacy and Safety of Intensive Continuous Theta Burst Stimulation Over the Right Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex in Insomnia Disorder:A Randomized Sham-Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Background: Insomnia disorder affects 10%-35% of the general population and is maintained by pathological cortical hyperarousal amenable to inhibitory neuromodulation. Continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS) produces rapid inhibitory effects on cortical excitability, but its efficacy in insomnia disorder has not been evaluated in adequately powered randomized sham-controlled trials. Methods: Thirty adults (n=15 per arm) meeting Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition, criteria for insomnia disorder (Sleep Condition Indicator [SCI] score <16) were randomized to active or sham cTBS targeting the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (F4 position, 80% of the resting motor threshold). The intervention comprised 21 sessions (600 pulses/session, ∼40 seconds) over 10 days.Data were collected from October 2024 to January 2026. Outcome measures were the SCI (primary), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), Functional Outcomes of Sleep Questionnaire-10 (FOSQ-10), and World Health Organization Quality of Life-Brief (WHOQOL-BREF), assessed at baseline (day 0), posttreatment (day 10), and 2-week follow-up (day 25). The trial was conducted per Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials 2010 guidelines and analyzed using intention-to-treat mixed-effects repeated-measures analysis of variance. Results:Both groups improved significantly across all outcomes (all within-group P<.001; large effect sizes). Group×time interactions were nonsignificant for sleep-specific outcomes (PSQI: F=3.32, P=.060; SCI: F=2.14, P=.147; ISI: F=0.23, P=.720; FOSQ-10: F=0.88, P=.388). A significant and large interaction was observed for health-related quality of life (WHOQOL-BREF: F=8.92, P =.002, ηp2=0.242), favoring active cTBS. Three participants experienced transient mild headache; no serious adverse events occurred. Conclusion: Right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex-targeted cTBS over 10 days is safe and well tolerated. Active cTBS conferred a significant and clinically meaningful advantage in health-related quality of life. Larger trials with objective sleep endpoints, medication-naive populations, and extended follow-up are warranted. Article.ArticleTitle: Efficacy and safety of fexuprazan versus esomeprazole for healing of endoscopic submucosal dissection-induced artificial gastric ulcers: A multicenter, randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is a standard treatment for gastric neoplasms but creates artificial ulcers requiring potent acid suppression. Potassium-competitive acid blockers (P-CABs) provide rapid and sustained acid suppression. This study compared the efficacy and safety of fexuprazan, a novel P-CAB, with esomeprazole for the healing of artificial gastric ulcers after ESD.

This multicenter, randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial enrolled patients who underwent gastric ESD. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either fexuprazan 40 mg or esomeprazole 40 mg once daily for 8 weeks. The primary endpoint was the ulcer healing rate at 8 weeks. Secondary endpoints included the incidence of delayed bleeding and adverse events.

Of 105 randomized patients, 90 were included in the full analysis set (FAS) and 85 in the per-protocol set (PPS). At 8 weeks, the complete healing rate (scar stage) in the PPS was 92.68% (38/41) in the fexuprazan group and 95.45% (42/44) in the esomeprazole group (95% confidence interval: 80.08-98.46 vs 84.53-99.44, P = .67), with an absolute difference of -2.77 percentage points (95% confidence interval: -15.32-8.85). Results were consistent in the FAS (93.02% vs 95.74%, 95% confidence interval: 80.94-98.54 vs 85.46-99.48, P = .67), with an absolute difference of -2.72 percentage points (95% confidence interval: -14.75-8.27). At 8 weeks, no patients in either group remained in the active stage. No delayed bleeding occurred in either group. Treatment-emergent adverse events were minimal and similar between groups (2.00% vs 4.08%, P > .62), with no serious adverse events.

Fexuprazan 40 mg once daily showed no statistically significant difference from esomeprazole 40 mg for healing ESD-induced artificial gastric ulcers, with a favorable safety profile. These findings indicate that fexuprazan serves as a reasonable candidate for further investigation as a potential treatment option to proton pump inhibitors for post-ESD ulcer healing.

Article.ArticleTitle: Quantitative evaluation of muscle relaxation efficacy of moving cupping therapy for chronic low back pain by shear wave elastography: A randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Moving cupping is used to reduce pain and muscle tension in chronic low back pain (CLBP), but its effect on paraspinal muscle stiffness has not been compared with that of a sham procedure. We evaluated it using shear wave elastography (SWE).

In this single-center, sham-controlled randomized trial, 68 adults with CLBP were assigned 1:1 by computer-generated simple randomization to moving cupping or sham cupping (four sessions over 2 weeks; 18-20 kPa vs 0 kPa). The 66 participants who received the allocated intervention had a mean age of 37.8 ± 9.0 years, and 71.2% were female. Assessors and the analyst were blinded. The primary endpoint was the change in multifidus shear modulus from baseline to the end of treatment; secondary outcomes included shear modulus at 1-week follow-up, pain intensity, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), EQ-5D-5L, and Patient Global Assessment. Intention-to-treat analyses used linear mixed-effects models; a per-protocol mixed 2-way analysis of variance served as a sensitivity analysis.

A significant group × time interaction was observed for shear modulus (P < .001), as the decrease was greater with moving cupping (60.23 ± 14.83 to 10.84 ± 5.67 kPa) than with sham (57.54 ± 11.09 to 39.41 ± 9.84 kPa). At follow-up, shear modulus was 15.42 ± 7.41 vs 44.88 ± 14.22 kPa, and the change after treatment did not differ significantly between groups (P = .808). Pain also showed a significant group × time interaction (P < .001; moving cupping, 5.68 ± 1.41 to 2.44 ± 1.56; sham, 5.41 ± 1.18 to 3.41 ± 1.26), whereas ODI (P = .579) and EQ-5D-5L (P = .162) did not. No cupping-related adverse events occurred.

Two weeks of moving cupping reduced multifidus stiffness more than sham cupping, and the difference persisted 1 week after treatment. Pain decreased more with moving cupping, although the between-group difference was small, and there were no significant effects on disability or quality of life. Moving cupping may reduce paraspinal muscle stiffness but is not an established treatment for the broader symptom burden of CLBP.

Article.ArticleTitle: Comparison of inhalation anesthesia and total intravenous anesthesia in patients undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

Abstract.AbstractText: The choice of anesthetic technique may influence perioperative stability and postoperative recovery. This study compared postoperative recovery between sevoflurane inhalational anesthesia and propofol-based total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) in patients undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

In this prospective, randomized clinical trial, 81 patients were assigned to receive either sevoflurane inhalational anesthesia (Group S, n = 40) or propofol-based TIVA (Group T, n = 41). The primary outcome was postoperative recovery quality assessed using the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) questionnaire preoperatively and 24 hours after surgery. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain, rescue analgesic requirement, incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting, intraoperative remifentanil consumption, and perioperative hemodynamic variables.

No statistically significant between-group difference was detected in QoR-15 scores at 24 hours postoperatively (unadjusted mean difference [TIVA minus sevoflurane], 2.39 points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -4.83 to 9.61; P = .512). After adjustment for preoperative QoR-15 scores, the difference remained statistically nonsignificant (adjusted mean difference, 0.78 points; 95% CI, -5.91 to 7.47; P = .817). Postoperative pain scores and postoperative nausea and vomiting incidence did not differ significantly between groups. However, the proportion of patients requiring rescue analgesics at 6 hours postoperatively was lower in the TIVA group (9.8% vs 30.0%; unadjusted P = .027). Intraoperative remifentanil consumption was significantly higher in the TIVA group (P < .001). Heart rate at postanesthesia care unit arrival and mean blood pressure after intubation were lower in the TIVA group (adjusted P < .05).

No statistically significant difference in postoperative recovery quality at 24 hours was detected between propofol-based TIVA and sevoflurane anesthesia. Although rescue analgesic requirements at 6 hours were lower in the TIVA group, this secondary finding should be interpreted cautiously. The CI for the primary outcome did not exclude clinically meaningful differences; therefore, these findings do not establish equivalence between the 2 anesthetic techniques.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of slow-belt split-belt treadmill training on balance, walking speed, and activities of daily living in patients with subacute stroke: A pilot randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: This study aimed to compare the effects of 3 weeks of slow-belt split-belt treadmill training (SBT) with those of tied-belt treadmill training (both belts driven at the same speed) on balance, functional reach, walking speed, and basic activities of daily living in patients with subacute stroke, and to evaluate the feasibility and safety of the SBT protocol.

In this single-center, assessor-blinded, parallel-group pilot randomized controlled trial with 1:1 allocation conducted in the inpatient rehabilitation unit of a tertiary hospital, 30 patients with subacute hemiplegic stroke (median, 13 days after onset) were randomized; 26 participants (13 per group) completed the post-intervention assessment. Thirty 30-minute treadmill sessions (twice daily, 5 days per week, for 3 weeks) were delivered in place of the routine gait-training sessions of the standard inpatient rehabilitation program. In the SBT group, the paretic limb was positioned on the slower belt at a fixed paretic-to-nonparetic belt-speed ratio of 1:2; in the control group, both belts operated at the same speed. The primary outcome was the Berg Balance Scale (BBS) at 3 weeks, compared between groups using baseline-adjusted analysis of covariance. Secondary outcomes were the functional reach test (FRT), modified FRT, gait speed (10-m walk test), and Korean version of the modified Barthel index, with Holm adjustment for multiplicity.

Both groups improved substantially (BBS, +18.8 vs +18.0 points; both P <.001); however, the baseline-adjusted between-group difference in the BBS was not significant (1.20 points; 95% confidence interval = -5.30 to 7.71; P =.706). No secondary outcome remained significant after Holm adjustment; a nominal difference in seated FRT (adjusted difference = 9.75 cm; P =.044; Holm-adjusted P =.355) was not robust in sensitivity analyses. Session completion was 99.7%, and no device- or protocol-related adverse events occurred.

In this pilot trial of patients with subacute stroke undergoing inpatient rehabilitation, SBT was feasible and well tolerated but did not demonstrate superiority over tied-belt training for balance, walking speed, or activities of daily living. An exploratory signal in seated reach warrants confirmation in adequately powered trials.

Article.ArticleTitle: Tumor Treating Fields and Quality of Life Among Patients With Locally Advanced Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: The PANOVA-3 trial demonstrated the survival benefit and tolerability of Tumor Treating Fields (TTFields) therapy concomitant with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel, but understanding the impact of TTFields therapy on quality of life (QoL) and pain is important for clinical decision-making.
To analyze the impact of TTFields therapy concomitant with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel on QoL and pain outcomes using prospective data from PANOVA-3.

This is a prespecified secondary analysis of PANOVA-3, which was a global, open-label, multicenter, phase 3 randomized clinical trial in adult patients with previously untreated locally advanced unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma (LA-PAC). A total of 571 patients were randomized between May 1, 2018, and March 31, 2023, with follow-up completed October 31, 2024. Data analysis was performed from November 2024 to May 2025.

Patients were randomized 1:1 to receive either TTFields therapy (150 kHz) with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel or gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel alone. Nab-paclitaxel (125 mg/m2) and gemcitabine (1000 mg/m2) were administered intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of 28-day cycles. Duration of follow-up was 18 months.

QoL was measured using the European Organization for the Research and Treatment of Cancer Core Quality of Life Questionnaire and the 26-item pancreatic cancer module. End points were mean changes from baseline QoL scores, deterioration-free survival of QoL, and time to opioid use. An analysis of pain medication use was performed post hoc.

At baseline, 562 patients (median [IQR] age, 67 [31-90] years; 295 [52.5%] female), including 279 of 285 patients in the TTFields plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel arm and 283 of 286 patients in the gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel arm, completed the EORTC QLQ-C30 questionnaire. Global health status was stable during the 26-month follow-up in both study arms. Digestive symptoms, pain, and pancreatic pain were improved from 2 months after treatment initiation throughout treatment and follow-up in the TTFields plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel arm. TTFields plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel was associated with longer deterioration-free survival for global health status than gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel alone (median [IQR], 7.1 [3.5-14.8] vs 5.7 [2.3-11.5] months; hazard ratio [HR], 0.77; 95% CI, 0.61-0.97; P = .02). Longer deterioration-free survival was also observed for most items on the digestive symptoms scales (indigestion and altered bowel habit were similar between the 2 arms). Median (IQR) deterioration-free survival was significantly longer with TTFields plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel for pain (10.1 [4.0-20.9] vs 7.4 [3.5-14.5] months; HR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.54-0.89; P = .003) and pancreatic pain (14.7 [6.2-46.2] vs 10.2 [5.6-18.2] months; HR, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.52-0.90; P = .006) as was median time to opioid use in the modified intention-to-treat population (9.3 [3.9-18.6] vs 6.7 [1.1-16.3] months; HR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.55-0.93; P = .01).

This secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial found that TTFields therapy with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel improved QoL and provided clinically meaningful benefits in pain outcomes compared with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel alone. This study's results suggest that TTFields therapy with gemicitabine and nab-paclitaxel is practice-changing for patients with unresectable LA-PAC.

Article.ArticleTitle: Clinician Training, Text Messages, and Human Papillomavirus Vaccination Among Children Aged 10 to 12 Years: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination rates among adolescents remain below recommendations.
To evaluate the effectiveness of clinician communication training and parent-targeted text messages at increasing HPV vaccination among children aged 11 to 12 years.

This doubly randomized, 2-level nested clinical trial was conducted from February 2022 to September 2024 among clinicians at 30 pediatric primary care clinics in Florida, children aged 10 to 12 years who had not received any of the 3 adolescent HPV vaccines, and their parents. Interventions occurred for 1 year, and vaccine records were collected for 2 years.

Clinics were randomized 1:1:1 to 3 training groups: (1) the bundled approach, which presents the HPV vaccine in the middle of 2 other recommended vaccines; (2) the focused approach, which emphasizes cancer prevention; and (3) deferred, which offered clinicians the opportunity to participate in the focused training after the trial concluded. Clinicians in the first 2 groups completed a 1-hour communication training and a 5-minute booster session. Patients within clinics were randomized 1:1:1 to 3 text message groups, aligned with the communication strategies: (1) bundled, (2) focused, and (3) no text messages. Parents were sent text messages at the start of the study or prior to their child's 11th birthday as well as prior to appointments.

Primary outcomes were HPV vaccine initiation (receipt of first dose) and completion (receipt of second dose). Analyses accounted for clinic-level clustering. Effects were analyzed as randomized and text messages as received.

At baseline, 59 clinicians (44 [75%] female; 12 [20%] Asian, 21 [36%] Hispanic, and 21 [36%] non-Hispanic White) within 30 randomized clinics were included, with 17 randomized to the focused group, 21 to the bundled group, and 21 to the deferred group. A total of 7234 children were aged 10 (3576 [49%]), 11 (2617 [36%]), and 12 (1041 [14%]) years at study start (1673 [23%] Hispanic, 1001 [14%] non-Hispanic Black, and 1210 [17%] non-Hispanic White). A total of 28 clinics (93%), 50 clinicians (85%), and 6498 children (90%) completed the 2-year follow-up. The mean pre-post clinic-level difference for HPV vaccine initiation was 28.2 (95% CI, 25.3-31.1) percentage points and for completion was 16.1 (95% CI, 13.3-18.9) percentage points. Risk ratios for clinician training and text messaging did not differ between groups for initiation or completion. Among patients whose parents received text messages vs not, the risk ratio for initiation was 1.17 (95% CI, 1.08-1.26) and for completion was 1.29 (95% CI, 1.06-1.56).

In this study of Florida children aged 10 to 12 years, clinic-level HPV vaccination increased over time. No differences in HPV vaccination by random assignment of clinician training or text messages were detected. When received, text messages were associated with higher HPV vaccination.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of different CO₂ insufflation pressures on endotracheal cuff pressure, airway pressures, and postoperative respiratory complications during robotic radical prostatectomy: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Robot assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) requires prolonged pneumoperitoneum and steep Trendelenburg positioning, which raise airway pressures that may be transmitted to the endotracheal tube (ETT) cuff. We investigated whether the level of carbon dioxide (CO₂) insufflation pressure affects ETT cuff pressure during RARP. In this single centre, three arm, parallel group randomized controlled trial, 90 patient undergoing elective RARP were randomly assigned to an intraabdominal CO₂ insufflation pressure of 10, 12, or 15 mmHg (30 per group) under a standardized anaesthetic. Cuff pressure was measured with a manometer and readjusted to baseline at eleven perioperative time points; peak and plateau airway pressures, end-tidal CO₂, and postoperative sore throat, hoarseness, and cough (1, 24, and 72 h) were also recorded. The primary outcome was the time-averaged cuff pressure during the pneumoperitoneum and steep Trendelenburg phase. Time averaged cuff pressure did not differ among the 10, 12, and 15 mmHg groups (30.3 ± 3.7, 28.7 ± 2.2, and 29.9 ± 2.8 cmH₂O; P = 0.089; pairwise differences - 1.6 to + 1.3 cmH₂O, all 95% confidence intervals within ± 3.5 cmH₂O), nor did peak cuff pressure, airway pressures, or end-tidal CO₂ at any time point. Between consecutive measurements, cuff and peak airway pressures rose and fell together at insufflation, Trendelenburg positioning, and return to supine, but the size of a patient's airway-pressure change did not predict the cuff-pressure change. Postoperative respiratory symptoms were infrequent and similar between groups. Within all groups, cuff and airway pressures changed significantly over time. Within the 10-15 mmHg range, CO₂ insufflation pressure had no detectable dose-dependent effect on ETT cuff pressure during RARP; between-group differences larger than approximately 3.5 cmH₂O are unlikely. Cuff pressure nonetheless frequently exceeded the recommended range, supporting regular manometric monitoring during surgery.

Article.ArticleTitle: A Two-Dimensional Perspective on Quality Of Life: Changes After the Balancing Everyday Life Intervention for Mental Health Service Users and Relationships to Everyday Occupations - An RCT Study.

Abstract.AbstractText: A randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluating the Balancing Everyday Life (BEL) intervention compared with care as usual (CAU) for mental health service users found no group differences when quality of life (QoL) was treated as a single construct. However, research suggests that (QoL) consists of two dimensions: a personalized life-and-health dimension (e.g., life satisfaction, health, leisure, and work) and an environmental dimension (e.g., safety, housing, and family situation). The current study re-examined data from the BEL study to investigate whether the BEL group and the CAU differed regarding improvements on the two aforementioned QoL dimensions and explore how changes in everyday occupations were related to QoL improvements.

A total of 226 mental health service users were assigned to BEL or CAU. Data were collected at baseline, post-intervention, and six-month follow-up. QoL was measured using the Manchester Short Assessment of Quality of Life (MANSA) and analyzed as two dimensions. Everyday occupations were assessed through measures of actual participation and subjective experiences. Change scores were analyzed using t-tests and Pearson correlations.

The BEL group showed significantly greater improvement in the life-and-health dimension of QoL after the intervention, with marginal significance at follow-up. Positive perceptions of everyday occupations were moderately associated with improvements in both QoL dimensions, whereas actual activity participation showed weaker associations.

Treating QoL as a two-dimensional construct revealed intervention effects that were not detected in previous analyses. Interventions emphasizing meaningful everyday occupations may enhance QoL and recovery among mental health service users. Trial Registration The study was registered with ClinicalTrial.gov. Reg. No. NCT02619318. Retrospectively registered: 20-11-2015.

Journal.Title: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology

Article.ArticleTitle: Association of sex and age on outcomes of maintenance treatment in pati​ents with advanced esophagogastric adenocarcinoma: an exploratory analysis of the randomized AIO-YMO-0111-MATEO trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Sex and age have an impact on efficacy and toxicity of chemotherapy (ctx) in patients (pts) with esophagogastric adenocarcinoma (EGA). However, data are limited, as clinical trials frequently do not report sex-specific differences and older pts are often underrepresented.

MATEO is an international randomized trial, confirming non-inferiority of S-1 maintenance therapy compared to continued platinum-based ctx in pts with advanced EGA without disease progression after 3 months of ctx. Toxicity pattern favored S-1 monotherapy. We conducted a post hoc exploratory analysis to assess the impact of sex and age on treatment outcomes.

In the per-protocol population, 112 pts (72.7%) were male and 42 (27.3%) were female. 37.7% of pts were ≥ ​70 years. Female pts more often had distal stomach tumors (64.3%), while male pts had more esophagogastric junction tumors (76.7%). In a pooled analysis, female pts showed significantly longer progression-free survival (PFS) (median 9.9 vs. 4.3 months, HR 0.56 [95% CI 0.38-0.83], log-rank: p = 0.0033), and overall survival (OS) (median 14.4 vs. 12.2 months, HR 0.65 [95% CI 0.44-0.97], log-rank: p = 0.0348). No age-related differences in PFS and OS were observed between pts ≥ 70 years and < 70 years. In multivariate analyses, female sex, but not younger age, was associated with a trend towards improved OS. No significant sex- or age-specific differences in terms of toxicity were observed.
Primary tumor location differed by sex. A trend for superior outcome in female pts was observed, whereas age did not have a significant impact on outcome.

Journal.Title: The western journal of emergency medicine

Article.ArticleTitle: Prehospital Facial Recognition Technology: Randomized Controlled Simulation Study.

Abstract.AbstractText: The risk of medical errors increases for the approximately 689,000 unidentified, noncommunicative patients who present to emergency departments annually. The concomitant rise in hospital admissions, lengths of stay, and mortality will likely persist unless approaches to identifying noncommunicative patients are developed and adopted. Facial recognition technology could provide a solution where scanning the face reliably provides access to identification and medical history of patients who self-enroll in the application database. Our objective was to compare paramedics' ability to identify noncommunicative patients and make related clinical decisions using a cloud-based facial-recognition application vs standard practice.

We conducted a double-blind, randomized controlled study with 90 participating firefighterparamedics in a simulated patient encounter. Our primary outcome was patient identification. Secondary outcomes included identification of key medical information, appropriateness of treatment decisions, and transport to the patient's preferred hospital. We uploaded facial photographs and simulated medical profiles to a secure cloud-based app. Participants used a tablet to scan the patient's face (standardized patient or actor). Successful matches returned identifying information, medical history, emergency contacts, preferred hospital, and primary care physician contact information. The 48 experimental participants had access to this patient information, while the 42 controls did not, even if they scanned the face. Standardized patients (SP) portrayed a noncommunicative urosepsis patient. Participants reported their findings to the facilitators and evaluated the technology on a 5-point Likert scale.

We analyzed 90 study participants (48 experimental, 42 control), of whom 40/48 (83.3%) experimental group identified the SP compared with 9/42 (21.4%) control group (OR [odds ratio], 13.87; 95% CI, 5.03-38.25; P < .001). Identification of important medical information of the SP by the study participants occurred in 30/48 (62.5%) in the experimental group versus 4/42 (9.5%) in control (OR, 15.83; 95% CI, 4.84-51.76; P < .001). Correct transport decision to the preferred hospital occurred in 27/48 (56.3%) experimental participants compared with 10/42 (23.8%) controls (OR, 4.11; 95% CI, 1.65-10.23; P = .02). Overall, 80% of participants reported that the technology would benefit their day-to-day clinical work.

The use of a cloud-based facial-recognition application significantly improved firefighter-paramedics' ability to identify noncommunicative patients and access critical medical information, with an appropriate transport decision to the patient's preferred hospital.

Article.ArticleTitle: Mixed-method process evaluation of the Evidence-based Medication knowledge Brokers in Residential Aged CarE (EMBRACE) helix-counterbalanced randomised controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Effective implementation of guidelines into residential aged care facilities (RACFs) is important for high-quality care. The 12-month Evidence-based Medication knowledge Brokers in Residential Aged CarE (EMBRACE) helix-counterbalanced randomised controlled trial evaluated three strategies to implement Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Appropriate Use of Psychotropic Medications in People Living with Dementia and in Residential Aged Care: (i) passive distribution of Guideline material, (ii) pharmacist-led staff education and (iii) knowledge broker-led Guideline implementation. All three strategies reduced Guideline non-concordance over time, with no significant difference between strategies. This mixed-method process evaluation examined delivery of the implementation strategies, including contextual factors important for Guideline implementation.

Semi-structured interviews conducted with 34 health and care professionals at 12 months were thematically analysed using a deductive approach informed by the Grant framework. Descriptive statistics summarised quantitative data from a post-trial survey completed by intervention pharmacists.

Distribution of Guideline materials occurred opportunistically with RACF staff preferring summary materials (e.g. one-page factsheets). Pharmacist-led staff education was tailored to be shorter, more frequent and delivered one-on-one or in small groups. Knowledge broker pharmacists spent a median 70% of time delivering quality improvement activities including audit and feedback and integrating psychotropic best practice into RACF procedures and digital systems. Facilitators of successful Guideline implementation included early engagement with aged care leadership and knowledge broker integration into the team.

Guideline implementation efforts in RACFs may benefit from a multifaceted implementation approach involving early engagement with aged care leadership and contextualised delivery of implementation strategies according to staff preferences and needs.

Journal.Title: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

Article.ArticleTitle: Patient-Centred Communication About AI-Related Information in Perioperative Care: An Attention-Controlled Randomised Trial of Anxiety, Perceived Control and Interpretive Preparedness.

Abstract.AbstractText: Patients encountering artificial intelligence (AI) in health care may be uncertain about whether AI supports or replaces clinicians, who remains accountable and how general AI-related information applies to their own care. These are questions about how clinicians talk about AI rather than about how AI performs, and they may be particularly salient before surgery. This trial evaluated communication about AI-related information only: no AI system, clinical algorithm, device or decision-support tool was used, tested or applied to any participant's care.

The aim of this study was to evaluate whether a brief, public-informed, clinician-delivered protocol of structured AI communication improves immediate interpretive preparedness before surgery compared with time-matched attention-control supportive communication.
Single-centre, two-arm, parallel-group, attention-controlled superiority randomised trial with 1:1 allocation.

Adult patients scheduled for elective surgery at Ağrı Training and Research Hospital, Ağrı, Türkiye, were randomised 1:1 to structured AI communication (n = 60) or attention-control supportive communication (n = 60).

Structured AI communication was a 5-7-min nurse-delivered session explaining that AI may support but does not replace health professionals, that responsibility for clinical decisions remains with the care team, that AI-related information may be general or probabilistic, and that such information should be interpreted within the patient's own clinical context. Attention-control supportive communication was time-matched nurse-patient contact about routine perioperative preparation without AI-specific content.

The primary outcome was pre-surgery anxiety measured using the Amsterdam Preoperative Anxiety and Information Scale (APAIS) anxiety subscale. The key secondary outcome was perceived control. AI-related uncertainty, information clarity and trust in the clinical team were measured immediately after the session as study-specific communication-uptake indicators rather than as validated independent clinical endpoints.

All 120 randomised participants completed the pre-surgery endpoint assessment. Pre-surgery anxiety was lower after structured AI communication than after attention-control supportive communication (9.28 ± 2.55 vs. 12.48 ± 3.01; baseline-adjusted mean difference [MD], -2.56; 95% CI, -2.87 to -2.26; p < 0.001). Structured AI communication was also associated with higher perceived control (25.83 ± 4.04 vs. 22.62 ± 3.90; adjusted MD, 3.73; 95% CI, 3.34 to 4.12; p < 0.001), greater information clarity and trust, and lower AI-related uncertainty. Clinically meaningful anxiety reduction (≥ 2 APAIS points) was more frequent after structured AI communication (48/60, 80.0%) than after attention-control supportive communication (1/60, 1.7%). The unblinded design and the immediate self-reported assessment may have amplified these differences through expectancy, novelty, social desirability and measurement reactivity. The responder result should therefore be interpreted as a short-term self-reported difference rather than evidence of durable clinical benefit.

In a single centre, a brief public-informed protocol was associated with better immediate self-reported psychological and interpretive preparedness before surgery. Structured AI communication about AI-related uncertainty and human accountability is a plausible patient-centred component of technology-enabled care. These findings do not show that AI technology itself improves patient outcomes, and they do not establish durable anxiety reduction, behaviour change or clinical benefit beyond the immediate preoperative window.

Three lived-experience advisors reviewed patient-facing materials during protocol refinement. After analysis, a six-member public advisory group reviewed plain-language findings and advised on interpretation, practitioner-facing wording and calibrated trust, accountability and human oversight. Their feedback informed the Discussion and Practitioner Points.

Three lived-experience advisors with previous sur cal experience reviewed the patient-facing communication materials during protocol refinement. After analysis, a six-member public advisory group reviewed a plain-language summary of the findings and informed interpretation, practitioner-facing wording and the framing of calibrated trust, accountability and human oversight.
This randomised controlled trial was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT07393945).

Article.ArticleTitle: Pilot prospective crossover study assessing the role of bile acid malabsorption in the causation and treatment of major low anterior resection syndrome: randomized clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Major low anterior resection syndrome (LARS) affects approximately 60% of rectal cancer survivors, causing urgency and decreased bowel control, reducing quality of life. Bile acid malabsorption (BAM) is an under-recognized contributor whose prevalence and treatment efficacy remain unclear. This proof-of-concept study evaluated the effectiveness of colesevelam for treating LARS and described the prevalence of BAM.

This double-blind randomized placebo-controlled crossover trial was conducted between 2021 and 2024 in New Zealand. Adults aged 18-85 years with major LARS received colesevelam (up to 1.25 g, three times daily) or placebo for 5 weeks, separated by a 6-week washout period. A subset of patients underwent 75-selenium homocholic acid taurine (SeHCAT) testing for BAM. The outcomes of interest included changes in the LARS score, Fecal Incontinence Quality of Life Scale (FIQL), and Short-Form 12 (SF-12) questionnaire, with a composite outcome reflecting clinically important improvements.

Of 80 eligible patients, 49 were randomized. However, 36 patients completed the study after washout and were included in a per-protocol analysis (mean age 71 years; 69% male). In these 36 patients, colesevelam did not significantly improve LARS scores, but did significantly improve the SF-12 mental component summary (median +2.36; 95% confidence interval 0.00 to 10.25; P < 0.01) and FIQL depression/self-perception. Eight of 19 patients (42%) had BAM and exhibited significant improvements in SF-12 physical and mental item scores with colesevelam. Using composite criteria, colesevelam produced a 33% response rate, versus 8% for placebo, with higher rates in BAM-positive (50%) than BAM-negative (11%) patients.

BAM is a treatable contributor to LARS, present in 40% of tested patients. Although treating all LARS patients with bile acid sequestrants provides limited benefit, SeHCAT testing identifies patients likely to respond. BAM assessment would be beneficial if incorporated into LARS management.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effectiveness of a Program for Pain Intensity and Knee Osteoarthritis Reduction Among Elderly Individuals in Thailand: A Randomized Controlled Trial Study.

Abstract.AbstractText: The objective of the study was to assess the effects of the Pain Intensity and Knee Osteoarthritis Reduction (PIKOR) program on pain and severity of knee osteoarthritis (KOA) among older people in Thailand.

This randomized controlled trial, conducted in Northern Thailand, enrolled 58 older adults with KOA. Participants were randomly allocated to either an intervention group, which received the PIKOR program, or a control group receiving standard care. The intervention consisted of the PIKOR program, which combined Court-Type Traditional Thai Massage (CTTM), Hot Herbal Compress (HHC), Leg and Knee Stretching (LKS), and Herbal Knee Poultice (KPH). This integrated protocol sought to maintain therapeutic efficacy while minimizing the direct time burden on the Thai traditional physician. Treatment outcomes were evaluated using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC). Statistical significance was determined at a 95% confidence level (p < 0.05), utilizing both independent and paired t-tests for inter-group and intra-group comparisons, respectively.
Participants in the intervention group demonstrated greater reductions in mean VAS and WOMAC scores compared with those in the control group.

The PIKOR program resulted in significantly greater reductions in pain, stiffness, and functional limitations among older adults in the intervention group compared with those in the control group. It may represent a viable alternative for managing KOA, particularly by reducing the time required for consultation with a Thai traditional medicine practitioner.
Thai Clinical Trial Registry: TCTR20260415004 on April 15, 2026 (https://www.thaiclinicaltrials.org/export/pdf/TCTR20260415004).

Article.ArticleTitle: Influence of vitamin D binding protein isoforms on the total and free serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D responses to vitamin D supplementation in older adults in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.

Abstract.AbstractText: Genetic variants that determine the vitamin D binding protein isoform (GC) are consistently associated with total serum 25(OH)D concentration in cross-sectional genome-wide association studies. Previous studies suggest GC isoforms may influence the increment of total 25(OH)D in response to vitamin D supplementation. The free serum 25(OH)D concentration may better reflect vitamin D status, but whether GC isoforms modify the effect of supplementation on free 25(OH)D requires further study.
This study aimed to determine the associations between GC isoforms and the increments of total and free 25(OH)D3 in response to vitamin D3 supplementation among older adults.

Data were derived from the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis Individualized Response to Vitamin D Treatment (MESA INVITe) Study (NCT02925195). Participants (n = 666) were randomized 3:1 to 16 weeks of 2,000 IU of vitamin D3 or placebo daily. Complete data from 559 participants (414 vitamin D3; 145 placebo) were used for analysis. Total serum 25(OH)D3 concentration, GC isoforms, and serum VDBP concentration were determined by LC-MS/MS. Free serum 25(OH)D3 was measured by LC-MS/MS following sample preparation by size-exclusion separation. Additionally, an established prediction equation was used to estimate free 25(OH)D3 from common biochemical measurements. The associations of GC isoforms with baseline, endpoint, and 16-week changes in total and free 25(OH)D3 were modeled with linear regression. Models were adjusted for sex, age, season, body mass index, estimated glomerular filtration rate, and genetic ancestry.

Mean age (SD) of the participants was 72 (8) y; 53% were females, 36% White, 33% Black, 18% Hispanic/Latino, and 13% Chinese. In each treatment group at both baseline and endpoint, total 25(OH)D3 was lower among individuals carrying GC2 isoform (3 to 6 ng/mL lower per GC2 allele), whereas free 25(OH)D3, whether measured or calculated, did not vary according to GC isoform. Supplementation significantly increased total and free 25(OH)D3, but the increments of total and free 25(OH)D3 were independent of GC isoform.

At baseline and endpoint, total serum 25(OH)D3 concentration, but not free 25(OH)D3, was lower among individuals with GC2 isoform. However, neither the total nor free 25(OH)D3 response to vitamin D3 supplementation varied according to GC isoform.

Article.ArticleTitle: Bilateral cerebellar high-frequency rTMS for refractory epilepsy: a randomized, single-blind, sham-controlled study.

Abstract.AbstractText: For patients with drug-resistant epilepsy who are not suitable for surgery, transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is an important non-invasive neuromodulation therapy. The cerebellar cortex can inhibit cortical excitability via the cerebello-thalamo-cortical pathway. Here, we explore whether high-frequency (20 Hz) cerebellar repetitive TMS (rTMS) reduces seizure frequency and interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) in refractory epilepsy.

Eighty-seven patients with refractory epilepsy were included in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population (n = 87) and then randomized to active rTMS (n = 44) or sham stimulation (n = 43). One patient in treatment group had no post-baseline efficacy data; efficacy analyses were therefore performed in the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population (n = 86). The active group received two cycles of 20 Hz rTMS targeting the cerebellum. Seizure frequency and IEDs were assessed before and after treatment.

Poisson generalized linear mixed models revealed a significant group×time interaction for seizure frequency [F(2,236) = 162.65, p < 0.001]. The active group had significantly lower seizure frequencies at months 1, 2, and 3 (all p < 0.001), with the largest difference at month 2. Percentage reductions of seizure frequency in the active group were 64.6%, 73.2%, and 13.3%, respectively, compared with 3.9%, 0.6%, and -8.4% in the control group (all P < 0.001). Responder rates (≥50% reduction) in the active group were 90.7%, 95.3%, and 0% vs. 0% in controls (p < 0.001 for months 1-2). Within-group analysis showed significant IED reduction after active rTMS (p < 0.001) but no change in controls. Moreover, a significant group × baseline interaction (p < 0.001) indicated greater suppression in patients with higher baseline IEDs. Exploratory subgroup analysis further confirmed this. All adverse events were mild, with no significant difference in the incidence between the two groups.

Active cerebellar rTMS was associated with reduced seizure frequency, improved responder rates, and suppressed IEDs in refractory epilepsy with no obvious discomfort. The optimal efficacy duration was approximately 2 months, with greater IED suppression in patients with higher baseline levels.
