Article.ArticleTitle: Oral versus intravenous postoperative antibiotics after laparoscopic appendectomy following complicated appendicitis: an open-label cluster-randomized cluster-crossover multiperiod non-inferiority study.

Abstract.AbstractText: The optimal administration route and duration of postoperative antibiotics for complicated appendicitis after source control remain debated. The aim of this non-inferiority cluster-randomized trial was to compare oral versus intravenous antibiotics following laparoscopic appendectomy.

In this pragmatic, open-label, cluster-randomized, cluster-crossover, non-inferiority trial across 12 Danish hospitals, adults undergoing laparoscopic appendectomy for complicated appendicitis received either a 3-day oral or intravenous postoperative antibiotic regimen. The primary outcome was 30-day intra-abdominal abscess, analysed in both intention-to-treat and per-protocol populations using a 5% points non-inferiority margin. Secondary 30-day outcomes included length of hospital stay, readmission, and postoperative complications.

Of 5424 patients screened, 1021 with complicated appendicitis were allocated to oral (n = 567) or intravenous (n = 454) antibiotics. In the intention-to-treat analysis, intra-abdominal abscess occurred in 39 of 567 oral and 22 of 454 intravenous patients; weighted 30-day incidences were 6.8% and 4.9% (absolute risk difference, 1.9%; 90% c.i., -0.4 to 4.2), meeting non-inferiority. In the per-protocol analysis, abscess occurred in 19 of 395 and 9 of 294 patients; weighted incidences were 4.9% and 3.0% (absolute risk difference, 1.8%; 90% c.i., -0.3 to 3.9). Oral antibiotics shortened hospital stay (-41.1 h; 95% c.i., -46.7 to -35.6) but increased readmission (difference, 4.7%; 95% c.i., 0.5 to 8.9).

A 3-day oral antibiotic regimen was non-inferior to intravenous antibiotic therapy in preventing intra-abdominal abscess after laparoscopic appendectomy for complicated appendicitis. Reduced hospital stay and comparable clinical outcomes support oral antibiotics as a routine postoperative option in clinically stable patients.

Article.ArticleTitle: Fuzuloparib in combination with apatinib versus fuzuloparib alone for recurrent ovarian cancer: a randomized, open-label, phase 2 trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: A randomized, open-label, phase 2 trial assessed fuzuloparib (a PARP inhibitor) plus apatinib (a vascular endothelial growth factor receptor [VEGFR] inhibitor) versus fuzuloparib alone in patients with recurrent ovarian cancer (ROC).

Patients with ROC who had failed ≥ 2 lines of platinum-based chemotherapy were enrolled. Patients with primary platinum resistance were also eligible. Patients were randomized 1:1 to receive fuzuloparib plus apatinib or fuzuloparib. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR).

As of Jan 11, 2024, 76 eligible patients were enrolled (39 with fuzuloparib plus apatinib and 37 with fuzuloparib). The ORR was 38.5% for fuzuloparib plus apatinib and 35.1% for fuzuloparib alone, with median progression-free survival (PFS) of 7.3 months and 5.5 months, respectively. In patients with platinum resistance, the ORR was 29.6% with fuzuloparib plus apatinib compared to 20.0% with fuzuloparib alone, and the median PFS was 5.6 months versus 3.7 months (HR = 0.63; 95% CI, 0.34 to 1.15; p = 0.1306). In patients without prior VEGFR inhibitor exposure, the ORR was 50.0% with fuzuloparib plus apatinib compared to 36.7% with fuzuloparib alone, and the median PFS was 7.4 months versus 5.5 months (HR = 0.67; 95% CI, 0.38 to 1.19; p = 0.1667). Treatment-related adverse events of grade ≥ 3 occurred in 61.5% and 40.5% of patients in fuzuloparib plus apatinib and fuzuloparib groups.

In treating ROC, fuzuloparib plus apatinib didn't show a significant advantage over fuzuloparib alone. However, in patients with platinum-resistant disease or without prior VEGFR inhibitors exposure, fuzuloparib plus apatinib showed a trend towards benefit.
ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04517357 (Registration Date: August 16, 2020).

Article.ArticleTitle: In-person versus telehealth pelvic floor physiotherapy for primary vaginismus: a parallel randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Pelvic floor physiotherapy (PFPT) is a first-line effective treatment for vaginismus, but significant barriers limit access to in-person care. Remotely delivered online therapy presents a potential solution, yet robust comparative evidence on its efficacy remains scarce.

This parallel randomized controlled trial was conducted to compare the efficacy of in-person versus remotely delivered online PFPT for improving sexual function in women with primary vaginismus. Sixty-two women with primary vaginismus (Lamont grades III-IV) were randomly allocated to receive either in-person (n=31) or online (n=31) physiotherapy. Both groups completed an identical, structured 4-session protocol over two weeks, comprising psychoeducation, diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor awareness and relaxation exercises, and a progressive vaginal desensitization/dilation protocol. The primary outcome was sexual function measured by the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) at baseline and immediately post-intervention.

Both groups demonstrated significant within-group improvements in all FSFI domains post-intervention (p<0.001). In between-group comparisons, the in-person group achieved significantly greater improvement in the FSFI total score (mean change difference: 6.88; p < 0.001) and in the domains of arousal (1.14; p < 0.001), orgasm (1.29; p < 0.001), satisfaction (1.45; p < 0.001), and pain reduction (1.25; p < 0.001). No statistically significant between-group difference was found for the desire (0.83; p > 0.05) or lubrication (0.92; p > 0.05) domains.

While both in-person and online physiotherapy were effective for treating vaginismus, the in-person modality led to statistically and clinically superior gains in overall sexual function and key physiological domains. This superiority may be attributed to manual components and tactile feedback. However, the online model, which yielded significant improvements, presents a viable and accessible alternative in the face of geographical or logistical barriers. Studies with longer-term follow-up and greater statistical power are warranted.
Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT20140811018760N8 Registration date 2023531).

Article.ArticleTitle: Neuroprotection in the early window: a randomized controlled trial of butylphthalide initiation within 3 hours in acute ischemic stroke.

Abstract.AbstractText: Neuroprotective agents have shown promise in preclinical studies but failed to demonstrate efficacy in clinical trials, potentially due to delayed treatment initiation. The optimal therapeutic window for neuroprotection in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains undefined. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of DL-3-n-butylphthalide (NBP) initiated within 3 h versus 3-6 h after symptom onset in AIS patients.

This multicenter, randomized, open-label trial with blinded endpoint assessment was conducted across 19 stroke centers in China from July 29, 2024, to November 1, 2025. AIS patients presenting within 3 h of symptom onset and with an NIHSS score of 4-25 were randomized 1:1 to early NBP (< 3 h) or late NBP (3-6 h) groups. Both groups received intravenous NBP (100 mL twice daily) for 14 days. The primary efficacy outcome was the proportion of patients achieving favorable functional outcomes (90-day modified Rankin Scale [mRS] score 0-2, a standard disability scale from 0 [no symptoms] to 6 [death]) at 90 days, assessed by certified raters blinded to group allocation. The results are presented as the risk ratio (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (95% CI). P < 0.05 indicated statistical significance.

A total of 204 patients were enrolled (early group: 104; late group: 100), with a median (IQR) age of 67 (59-74) years and 68.1% male. Favorable functional outcomes were achieved in 67.3% of the early group and 58.0% of the late group (unadjusted RR, 1.16; 95% CI, 0.94-1.44; P = 0.17). Each additional hour of delay reduced the risk of a favorable outcome by 11% (RR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.81-0.98; P = 0.02). Serious adverse events occurred in 12.9% of the early group and 9.1% of the late group (hazard ratio, 1.43; 95% CI, 0.61-3.34; P = 0.41).

In patients with AIS, initiating neuroprotective treatment with NBP less than 3 h after symptom onset, compared with initiation between 3 and 6 h, did not significantly improve the proportion of patients achieving favorable functional outcome. However, a significant dose-response relationship was observed between treatment initiation time and favorable outcome. This finding warrants further verification through larger-scale clinical trials.
NCT06472921. Registered on June 19, 2024.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of thermal ablation on persistent HPV infection in Danish women ≥ 40 years of age: a quasi-randomized clinical study.

Abstract.AbstractText: Thermal ablation is a cervical heat treatment that destroys a defined area of the cervix. We evaluated whether thermal ablation facilitates HPV clearance in women with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection, using HPV status and FAM19A4/miR124-2 DNA methylation as molecular markers for treatment efficacy.

A total of 131 women aged ≥ 40 years with persistent HR-HPV infection but without histologically confirmed high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (≥ CIN2) were enrolled at three outpatient gynecological clinics. After exclusions, 39 women were allocated to the intervention arm (thermal ablation) and 34 to the no treatment only control arm. Allocation was based on date of birth (even dates: intervention; odd dates: control), using quasi-randomization. HPV genotyping and FAM19A4/miR124-2 methylation status were assessed at baseline (0 months), 3 months, and 10 months. Thermal ablation was performed using the WISAP probe at 65 °C for 2 min and at 100 °C for 40 s, administered across two sessions 2-3 days apart.

At 10 months, 64.1% of women in the intervention arm and 79.4% in the control arm remained HR-HPV positive. No significant difference in HPV positivity was observed between arms at any time point. FAM19A4/miR124-2 methylation positivity showed a transient decrease in the intervention arm (-10.2%) at 3 months but increased in both arms over 10 months to above baseline levels, with no significant treatment effect.

Thermal ablation does not facilitate HPV clearance in women with persistent HR-HPV infection without significant cervical disease. Methylation positivity increased over time in both study arms, consistent with ongoing oncogenic transformation. Women treated with thermal ablation remain HR-HPV positive and require continued surveillance, indicating no clinical benefit over observation alone.
ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07376031, registered 21 January 2026.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of high-definition transcranial direct current stimulation on muscle strength, proprioception, cutaneous sensitivity and their relationship with balance in older adults with a history of falls.

Abstract.AbstractText: This study aims to investigate the effects of High-Definition Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (HD-tDCS) on muscle strength, proprioception, cutaneous sensitivity and their relationship with static/dynamic balance in older adults with a history of falls.

In this randomized, double-blind trial, 30 older adults with a history of falls were assigned to an active (a-tDCS, n = 15) or sham (s-tDCS, n = 15) group. The 4-week intervention consisted of 12 sessions (three times weekly). The a-tDCS group received 2 mA of continuous stimulation targeting the sensorimotor cortex for 20 min per session, whereas the s-tDCS group received current only during the initial and final 30-second ramp-up/down periods. Balance, muscle strength, proprioception and cutaneous sensitivity were assessed pre- and post-intervention.

Significant interactions were identified in RMSML (p = 0.009, [Formula: see text] = 0.222), DC scores (p = 0.046, [Formula: see text] = 0.134), peak hip abduction torque (p = 0.007, [Formula: see text] = 0.231), and ankle inversion proprioception threshold (p = 0.038, [Formula: see text] = 0.144). Post-hoc analyses revealed that the a-tDCS group demonstrated a significant reduction in RMSML (p = 0.034, d = 0.577) and ankle inversion threshold (p = 0.010, d = 1.040), alongside significant increases in DC scores (p = 0.002, d = 0.863) and hip abduction torque (p = 0.008, d = 0.740) compared to baseline. No significant improvements were observed in cutaneous sensitivity (p > 0.05). Correlation analysis in the a-tDCS group revealed a significant negative correlation between the change in RMSML and the change in peak hip abduction torque (r = -0.649, p = 0.009).

A 4-week HD-tDCS intervention significantly improves static and dynamic balance, hip strength, and ankle inversion proprioceptive in older adults with a history of falls. Improved static balance is positively correlated with increased hip abduction strength.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens on the gut microbiome in a randomized phase 3 trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation can cure certain hematological disorders but has many complications. In retrospective studies, low gut microbiome diversity is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. In 2023, the Blood and Marrow Transplant Clinical Trials Network 1703 randomized phase 3 trial demonstrated the superiority of post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy) and mycophenolate mofetil to tacrolimus and methotrexate (Tac/MTX) for graft-versus-host disease prophylaxis in participants with hematological malignancies undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation. Here we report on the microbiome-focused companion study to 1703, Blood and Marrow Transplant Clinical Trials Network 1801, which coenrolled participants and shared trial registration. The primary endpoint was association between microbiome diversity at neutrophil engraftment and non-relapse mortality after 1 year; secondary endpoints included associations with other clinical outcomes and with baseline microbiome diversity. Based on 2575 longitudinally collected stool samples from 304 participants (Tac/MTX n = 147, PTCy n = 157), no association between engraftment microbiome diversity and non-relapse mortality was observed (P = 0.314), not meeting the primary endpoint. Lower baseline microbiome diversity was associated with shorter overall survival (P = 0.007). Safety data were reported in the original 1703 publication. In exploratory analyses, microbiome diversity and absolute microbial load were lower in PTCy compared to Tac/MTX on days 14-28 following HCT, independent of non-prophylaxis antibiotics exposure. Microbial domination events, when a single species exceeds 30% relative abundance, did not differ significantly between study arms and reflected both pathogen blooms and less severe disruptions of the microbial community. Clostridium scindens and secondary bile-acid metabolism pathways were less prevalent in PTCy than in Tac/MTX following HCT. In summary, we find prophylaxis regimens likely exert independent effects on both the microbiome and immune compartments and can also impact their interaction. Understanding whether and how microbiome-targeted interventions might improve transplant outcomes will therefore require careful disentangling of these effects within each specific treatment context. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03959241 .

Article.ArticleTitle: Dynamic trajectories of electrolytes and bone metabolism with tofogliflozin and glimepiride: A post-hoc analysis.

Abstract.AbstractText: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors influence electrolyte balance and bone metabolism. However, their effects in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and type 2 diabetes remain unclear.

40 participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD were randomly assigned to tofogliflozin (20 mg/day) or glimepiride (0.5-6.0 mg/day) for 48 weeks. Changes in anthropometric measures, electrolytes, and bone metabolism markers were evaluated.

Tofogliflozin significantly increased serum magnesium (2.0 ± 0.19 to 2.13 ± 0.18 mg/dL) and transiently elevated serum calcium (9.15 to a maximum of 9.60 mg/dL) and tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase 5 b (283.5 to 352.0 mU/dL). It also transiently reduced serum potassium (4.05 ± 0.31 to 3.89 ± 0.21 mEq/L) and uric acid (5.10 to a minimum of 4.55 mg/dL), accompanied by increased urinary potassium excretion and fractional uric acid excretion. Urinary magnesium and calcium excretion did not change significantly. In the tofogliflozin group, reductions in steatosis and hepatocellular ballooning scores were significantly correlated with increases in serum type I collagen cross-linked N-telopeptide.

Tofogliflozin modified electrolyte profiles and transiently influenced bone turnover markers. The observed correlations suggest a potential association between improvements in hepatic histology and changes in bone metabolism during SGLT2 inhibitor therapy.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of intensive blood pressure control on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes: prespecified analysis of secondary outcomes of BPROAD randomised controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: To evaluate the effect of intensive compared with standard treatment of systolic blood pressure (SBP) on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes.
Multicentre, open label, outcome assessor masked, randomised controlled trial.
145 clinical centres across seven geographical regions in China.

12 821 adults aged ≥50 years with type 2 diabetes, raised SBP, and increased cardiovascular risk, of whom 12 434 without probable dementia at baseline were included in this cognitive ancillary study. Further assessments were performed annually and at the end of study.
Participants were randomly assigned to receive intensive treatment targeting SBP <120 mm Hg or standard treatment targeting SBP <140 mm Hg for up to five years.

The primary cognitive outcome was a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment. Secondary cognitive outcomes included all cause dementia, mild cognitive impairment, changes in cognitive functions, and changes in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics. A subset of participants underwent brain MRI at baseline (n=862) and at the end of study (n=605) to assess changes in white matter lesion volume and total brain volume.

6219 participants were assigned to receive intensive treatment and 6215 to receive standard treatment. Baseline mean age was 63.7 years, and 5567 (44.8%) participants were women. After one year, mean SBP was 121.6 mm Hg in the intensive treatment group and 133.2 mm Hg in the standard treatment group. During a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the primary cognitive outcome of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment occurred in 747 participants (3.69 events per 100 person years) in the intensive treatment group and 783 participants (3.89 events per 100 person years) in the standard treatment group (hazard ratio 0.96, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.86 to 1.06; P=0.38). In the MRI substudy (428 intensive treatment v 434 standard treatment), the intensive treatment group had a smaller increase in white matter lesion volume compared with the standard treatment group (between group difference -0.09 inverse hyperbolic sine (asinh) transformed cm3, 95% CI -0.15 to -0.02; P=0.01).

Over a median of about four years, no statistically significant difference in incidence of a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment was observed among adults with type 2 diabetes receiving standard treatment of SBP (target <140 mm Hg) and intensive treatment (target <120 mm Hg). Intensive treatment was, however, associated with a reduction in the accrual of cerebral white matter lesion volume.
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03808311.

Article.ArticleTitle: Empirical tuberculosis treatment in infants living with HIV hospitalised with severe pneumonia in Africa (EMPIRICAL): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, 2 × 2 factorial, controlled superiority trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Mortality among infants with severe HIV-associated pneumonia remains high globally. The EMPIRICAL trial evaluated whether empirical tuberculosis treatment (eTB-T) improves survival compared with the currently recommended microbiologically and clinically guided strategy.

This multicentre, open-label, group-sequential designed, 2×2 factorial, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 19 hospitals across Côte d'Ivoire, Malawi, Mozambique, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Infants aged 28-365 days admitted with severe HIV-associated pneumonia, without a current tuberculosis diagnosis or contact, were centrally and individually randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) using a secure web-based system stratified by site and severity. A computer-generated block randomisation schedule was used, with fixed blocks of eight allocations (two allocations to each factorial treatment group) within each stratum. Participants received standard of care (SoC) comprising treatment for bacterial (WHO-recommended antibiotics) and Pneumocystis jirovecii (cotrimoxazole and steroids) pneumonia, SoC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir (16 mg/kg per 12 h), or SoC plus 6 months of tuberculosis treatment (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for 2 months, plus isoniazid and rifampicin for 4 subsequent months), or both interventions combined. Here, we report the comparison between the eTB-T (ie, SoC plus tuberculosis treatment and SoC plus oral valganciclovir plus tuberculosis treatment) and non-eTB-T (ie, SoC or SoC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir) groups. Nasopharyngeal aspirates, stools for Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra testing, and urine for tuberculosis lipoarabinomannan assay were collected at recruitment. In the non-eTB-T groups, tuberculosis treatment was initiated if microbiological results collected at recruitment yielded positive results or if, during follow-up, the treating clinician suspected tuberculosis on clinical grounds, including radiological findings, in accordance with routine clinical practice and guidelines. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality (at 15 days and 360 days). Survival was estimated using flexible parametric models with covariate-adjusted conditional estimates; missing data were imputed by chained equations. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03915366) and is now complete.

Between March 15, 2020, and Jan 31, 2024, 563 participants were enrolled; 558 were analysed after excluding five patients who did not meet eligibility criteria. 276 participants were allocated to the eTB-T groups (n=140 eTB-T and n=136 valganciclovir plus eTB-T) and 282 to the non-eTB-T groups (n=142 SoC and n=140 valganciclovir). 17 (6%) of 276 in the eTB-T groups and 20 (7%) of 282 in the non-eTB-T groups were lost to follow-up. Median age was 4·4 months (IQR 3·2-7·4) and 274 (49%) of participants were female and 284 (51%) were male. In the non-eTB-T groups, 130 (46%) of 282 participants eventually initiated tuberculosis treatment at a median of 4·0 days (IQR 3·0-15·0) after recruitment due to positive microbiological findings in 55 (20%) cases (53 confirmed by tuberculosis lipoarabinomannan assay and two by nasopharyngeal aspirates Xpert MTB/RIF) or clinical decision in 75 (27%) cases. There was no evidence of interaction between valganciclovir and eTB-T (adjusted hazard ratio 1·19, 95% CI 0·73-1·95; pheterogeneity=0·4836). At 12 months, 132 (48%) of 276 participants in eTB-T groups and 121 (43%) of 282 participants in non-eTB-T groups died. In the eTB-T groups, the adjusted hazard ratio for death was 1·12 (95% CI 0·87-1·43; p=0·3868). At 15 days, the odds ratio was 1·24 (95% CI 0·83-1·84; p=0·2950). Serious adverse events did not differ between groups (1·19, 0·82-1·73; p=0·3523). There were no treatment-related deaths. The most common adverse events were elevation of transaminases (72 [26%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 74 [26%] in the non-eTB-T group), anaemia (163 [59%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 169 [60%] in the non-eTB-T groups), and infectious disease requiring antimicrobial treatment (161 [58%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 176 [62%] in the non-eTB-T groups).

In contrast to empirical treatment with valganciclovir, there was no evidence that eTB-T was superior to a clinically and microbiologically guided strategy in reducing all-cause mortality among infants with HIV-associated pneumonia. However, the high proportion of infants who eventually initiated tuberculosis treatment during follow-up in the non-eTB-T groups might have reduced the contrast between strategies and attenuated the ability to detect differences in outcomes.

Article.ArticleTitle: Biomarker Synergy in Relapsing Multiple Sclerosis: Neurofilament Light Chain and B Cells in Relation to Disease Outcomes.

Abstract.AbstractText: Anti-CD20 B-cell-depleting therapies demonstrate robust efficacy in people with multiple sclerosis (pwMS). This study addressed the limited understanding of relationships between B-cell populations before and after treatment with ocrelizumab and outcomes in people with relapsing MS (pwRMS) or primary progressive MS (pwPPMS).

Total circulating blood B cells and B-cell subsets were examined at baseline and longitudinally in pwRMS and pwPPMS enrolled in the pivotal Phase 3 trials (OPERA I, OPERA II, and ORATORIO). Relationships to disease outcomes before and after treatment with ocrelizumab or comparators were evaluated using generalized linear models and time-to-event analyses.

Ocrelizumab rapidly depleted total B cells in pwRMS. Blood samples (n = 15,025) were assessed from 3 Phase 3 trials from 2,370 pwMS, demonstrating depletion in all B-cell subsets. Greater depletion was observed with higher ocrelizumab exposure and longer treatment duration. In limited pwMS with detectable B cells, the majority were mature-naive B cells. Findings from the double-blind treatment period considered robust were that pwRMS with detectable mature-naive, memory, or total B cells had greater risk of developing new/enlarging T2 lesions (odds ratio: 3.8-4.9; p < 0.001), while pwPPMS with higher circulating plasmablasts had greater thalamic volume loss (β: -1.4; p < 0.001). Above-median baseline memory B-cell levels identified interferon beta-1a-treated pwRMS at greater risk of disability progression (hazard ratio: 2.0; p < 0.01), with larger numbers of slowly expanding lesions (p < 0.01). When interferon beta-1a-treated pwRMS presented both high baseline B cells and high serum neurofilament light (NfL; B cells/NfL high), they showed an even higher risk of disability progression (HR: 3.10; p < 0.001). Treatment with ocrelizumab in this subgroup of pwRMS with B cells/NfL high resulted in a near 4-fold reduction in risk of disability progression (HR: 0.25, p < 0.001).

Ocrelizumab treatment depleted total B cells and all B-cell subsets in an exposure-dependent and duration-dependent manner. PwRMS with detectable on-treatment B cells had greater risk of new/enlarging T2 lesions, suggesting that sustained deep B-cell depletion may be important for preventing disability worsening. High baseline B cells when present with high NfL identified a population at increased risk of disease worsening who could benefit from ocrelizumab treatment.

Article.ArticleTitle: Web-Based Isha Kriya Meditation and Breathwork in Long COVID: Mixed Methods Randomized Controlled Pilot Study.

Abstract.AbstractText: Long COVID affects millions of adults, causing fatigue, dyspnea, cognitive symptoms, and mood disturbances. Effective treatments are limited, and many patients cannot access multidisciplinary rehabilitation because of symptom fluctuation, distance, or specialist shortages. Web-based mind-body interventions may offer accessible, scalable support alongside existing care.
We assessed the feasibility and efficacy of a 3-week web-based yogic breathing and meditation program for long COVID symptoms.

In this completed, parallel-group, 6-week waitlist-controlled, mixed methods randomized trial, adults aged 18-70 years with physician-confirmed long COVID were recruited from US clinics and self-referral and randomized 1:1 to immediate intervention or waitlist control, crossing over at week 3. The program included live webinars and video guides for daily self-practice. The primary outcome was adherence, defined as practicing at least 1 of 3 techniques on ≥4 days/week across all 3 active-intervention weeks. Secondary outcomes included perceived stressmood, quality of life, dyspnea, and somatic symptom burden, assessed at baseline, 3 weeks, and 6 weeks. Quantitative outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Semistructured interviews and focus groups underwent conventional content analysis and were integrated with quantitative findings via joint display.

Of 189 randomized participants, 1 was excluded post-randomization for a protocol deviation; 188 (96 intervention, 92 waitlist) began the study. Of these, 124 reached the active intervention period. Among 58 with complete adherence data, 55% met the adherence threshold (60% intervention, 50% waitlist). Secondary analyses included 185 participants with ≥1 assessment. No adverse events were reported. Compared with waitlist control, the intervention group showed greater reductions in total mood disturbance (MD=-10; 95% CI -19 to -1.6; P=.02), negative mood (MD=-7.5; 95% CI -15 to -0.44; P=.04), fatigue (MD=-2.9; 95% CI -4.6 to -1.2; P=.001), MDP immediate perception (MD=-5.5; 95% CI -9.4 to -1.6; P=.007), MDP sensory dimension (MD=-5.1; 95% CI -8.5 to -1.7; P=.003), and somatic symptom burden (MD=-2.0; 95% CI -3.6 to -0.38; P=.02), and greater increases in positive mood (MD=2.9; 95% CI 0.66 to 5.1; P=.01) and vigor (MD=1.7; 95% CI 0.18 to 3.2; P=.03). Stress and quality of life did not differ significantly. Qualitative findings identified medical-system struggles, digital delivery, online support, and practices' effects on resilience and identity. Integration showed convergence for dyspnea and mood, divergence for stress and quality of life, and expansion through themes of medical-system experience, identity, and social connection.

This web-based yogic breathing and meditation program appears feasible and accessible for people with long COVID. By combining 3 practices in a brief protocol and integrating quantitative and qualitative evidence, this study provides novel insight into both symptom outcomes and dimensions of recovery not captured by standardized measures. Further evaluation should assess longer-term effects and integration into scalable telehealth and virtual rehabilitation pathways.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of mandibular advancement device versus continuous positive airway pressure on cardiac remodeling in obstructive sleep apnea: a randomized CMR substudy.

Abstract.AbstractText: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with adverse cardiac remodeling, including diffuse myocardial fibrosis. Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) is the standard treatment for OSA, while mandibular advancement devices (MAD) may represent an alternative. However, their comparative effects on myocardial structure remain incompletely defined. To compare the effects of MAD and CPAP on cardiac remodeling assessed by cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in patients with OSA. This prespecified CMR substudy of the randomized CRESCENT trial included patients who agreed to participate in both baseline and 12-month CMR examinations (aged 59±8 years, 89% male, with hypertension, elevated cardiovascular risk and moderate-to-severe OSA). The mean body mass index was 28.6±4.6 kg/m2. Participants underwent contrast-enhanced CMR at baseline and after 12 months of treatment with either MAD (n = 36) or CPAP (n = 49). CMR-derived measures included left ventricular (LV) mass, cardiac volumes and function; and extracellular volume (ECV) fraction as a marker of diffuse myocardial fibrosis. At baseline, mean 24-hour systolic blood pressure was 126 ± 11mmHg, ECV fraction was 25.0 ± 2.0% and 27% of participants met CMR criteria of LV hypertrophy. After 12 months, a modest but significant reduction in ECV fraction was observed in patients treated with MAD (24.9 ± 2.3% to 24.0 ± 2.2%; P = 0.047) and CPAP (25.1 ± 1.9% to 24.4 ± 1.6%; P = 0.004). There was no significant difference in ECV fraction reduction between MAD and CPAP (P = 0.576). No significant between-group differences were observed for changes in LV mass, cardiac volumes and function. Both MAD and CPAP were associated with modest reductions in ECV fraction over 12 months, with no detectable between-group difference. No accompanying improvements in LV mass or cardiac function were observed, likely reflecting the predominantly preserved myocardial phenotype at baseline. (Cardiosleep Research Program on Obstructive Sleep Apnea, Blood Pressure Control and Maladaptive Myocardial Remodeling-Non-inferiority Trial [CRESCENT]; NCT04119999).
The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-67940-w.

Article.ArticleTitle: Training executive control and multitasking abilities in older adults: training gains and transfer effects of an online pilot randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Developing meaningful and effective cognition-oriented treatments to enhance cognition and dementia prevention is a major public health need. This online randomized controlled trial assessed the effects of a new web-based cognitive training platform, the Breakfast Game (BG), which simulates real-life executive control/multitasking demands. Participants were randomized into 1) experimental group: BG using the Emphasis Change (EmCh), a strategy to facilitate flexible attention allocation, or 2) active control group: BG without EmCh. Thirty-eight cognitively unimpaired older adults, highly educated (mean 16.4 years) and mostly White (78%), were included in the study. Participants underwent pre- and post-assessments with 12 intervention sessions, three times per week. The intent-to-treat approach and linear-mixed models were implemented, and all models controlled for baseline performance. Both groups improved the game performance over the sessions, but the EmCh presented significantly greater improvement. There were time-by-group interactions in the game metrics and near-transfer outcomes on multitasking and executive/attention control, indicating greater training gains and transfer effects in the EmCh group. There were no distant-transfer effects on self-efficacy, mood, or cognitive activities in daily life. The BG with the EmCh is a promising online intervention tool to promote cognitive health and enhance executive control / multitasking abilities in aging.
The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-56974-9.

Article.ArticleTitle: Procalcitonin- and Presepsin-Guided Antibiotics for Early-Onset Sepsis in Preterm Infants: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Early administration of antibiotics in the absence of proven sepsis, such as for treatment of early-onset sepsis (EOS), has been associated with adverse outcomes in very preterm infants. Reference values for procalcitonin (PCT) and presepsin (P-SEP) have been established in preterm infants.
To determine whether PCT- and P-SEP-guided antibiotic treatment for EOS was noninferior to universal antibiotic treatment with respect to survival without major morbidity.

This randomized multicenter noninferiority clinical trial was conducted in 17 Italian neonatal intensive care units between June 1, 2023, and January 31, 2025, among preterm infants born at 25 weeks and 0 days to 31 weeks and 6 days of gestation.

Enrolled infants were randomly allocated to receive either PCT- and P-SEP-guided antibiotic treatment, administered if PCT and P-SEP levels exceeded prespecified thresholds, or universal antibiotic treatment for EOS.

The composite primary outcome was defined as survival without late-onset sepsis (LOS), bronchopulmonary dysplasia, grade 3 or 4 intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), grade 2 or higher necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), periventricular leukomalacia (PVL), or stage 3 or higher retinopathy of prematurity (ROP). The prespecified noninferiority margin was -5 percentage points. Both a primary intention-to-treat analysis and a secondary per-protocol analysis were performed, as recommended for noninferiority trials.

The study enrolled and randomized 283 very preterm infants (mean [SD] gestational age, 30.2 [2.2] weeks; 161 girls [57%]); 143 received procalcitonin- and presepsin-guided treatment and 140 received universal antibiotic treatment. The primary outcome did not differ between the PCT- and P-SEP-guided treatment group and the universal antibiotic treatment groups (76 of 143 [53%] vs 77 of 140 [55%]; risk difference, -1.8 percentage points; 90% CI, -11.9 to 8.3 percentage points; P = .32). Noninferiority of PCT- and P-SEP-guided treatment compared with universal treatment was not demonstrated, because the lower bound of the 2-sided 90% CI crossed the prespecified noninferiority margin. The risk differences for LOS, IVH, NEC, PVL, ROP, and death were not significantly different between the groups. PCT and P-SEP values were not different between the groups. No patient developed EOS.

In this randomized clinical trial conducted among neonates born between 25 weeks and 0 days and 31 weeks and 6 days of gestation, a PCT- and P-SEP-guided strategy for the treatment of EOS did not demonstrate noninferiority to universal antibiotic treatment with respect to survival without major morbidity. Within the limits of this study, these findings do not support the routine use of a biomarker-guided approach as an alternative to universal treatment for this high-risk population.

Article.ArticleTitle: Hand-Arm Bimanual Intensive Therapy Including Lower Extremities in Preschoolers With Bilateral Cerebral Palsy: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Intensive interventions for children with cerebral palsy (CP) have traditionally focused on the upper extremities, despite frequent impairments in gross motor function and the critical period of motor development occurring before age 5 years. Hand-Arm Bimanual Intensive Therapy Including Lower Extremities (HABIT-ILE) has demonstrated efficacy in improving manual dexterity and gross motor function in school-aged children, but evidence in preschool children with bilateral CP remains limited.
To determine whether early HABIT-ILE improves gross motor function more than usual unstructured motor activities in preschool-aged children with bilateral CP.

This multicenter randomized clinical trial was conducted between December 2019 and December 2021. Recruitment was from European university hospitals, CP-specialized centers, and spontaneous applications at 4 sites: Brussels, Belgium; Brest and Angers, France; and Pisa, Italy. Children aged 12 to 59 months with spastic or dyskinetic bilateral CP who were able to follow instructions were included. Exclusion criteria were uncontrolled seizures, scheduled botulinum toxin injections or orthopedic surgery during the 6 months before or during the study period, severe visual or cognitive impairments, and contraindications to magnetic resonance imaging. Data were analyzed in May 2024.
Children were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive 2 weeks of usual motor activity, including usual rehabilitation (control group), or 2 weeks (50 hours) of HABIT-ILE (HABIT-ILE group).

The primary outcome was Gross Motor Function Measure-66 (GMFM-66; range, 0-100, with lower scores indicating lesser gross motor ability). Secondary outcomes included Both Hand Assessment (BoHA), Melbourne Assessment 2, Pediatric Evaluation of Disability Inventory-Computer Adaptive Test (PEDI-CAT), and Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (COPM). Assessments were performed at baseline (immediately before intervention) and 2 weeks and 3 months after baseline.

Among 49 preschool children with CP (mean [SD] age, 40.18 [11.53] months; 18 girls [36.7%] and 31 boys [63.3%]), Gross Motor Function Classification levels were I in 5 children, II in 14 children, III in 17 children, and IV or V in 13 children and Mini-Manual Ability Classification levels were I in 10 children, II in 27 children, III in 7 children, and IV or V in 6 children. Change in mean (SD) GMFM-66 score from baseline to 3 months was significantly greater in the HABIT-ILE group (5.01 [2.52] logits) than the control group (0.70 [1.98] logits) (adjusted mean difference [aMD] in score, 4.33 logits; 95% CI, 3.03-5.62 logits; P < .001). Likewise, mean (SD) scores favored the HABIT-ILE group vs the control group for secondary outcomes of BoHA (5.32 [4.47] vs 0.13 [5.16]; aMD, 5.15; 95% CI, 2.23-8.08; P < .001), PEDI-CAT mobility domain (1.70 [2.18] vs -0.40 [4.38]; aMD, 2.27; 95% CI, 0.20-4.33; P = .03), and COPM performance (4.22 [1.61] vs 1.14 [1.35]; aMD, 3.55; 95% CI, 2.86-4.24; P < .001) and satisfaction (4.37 [1.38] vs 1.15 [1.63]; aMD, 3.11; 95% CI, 2.25-3.97; P < .001).

In this randomized clinical trial, early HABIT-ILE significantly improved upper and lower extremities motor performance in preschool-aged children with bilateral CP at 3 months after the intervention. These findings suggest that HABIT-ILE is effective in improving gross motor function in preschool-aged children with bilateral CP.

Article.ArticleTitle: Cerebellar Intermittent Theta-burst Stimulation Reduces Dual Task Cost in Walking and Balance in Stroke Patients.

Abstract.AbstractText: The cerebellum plays a key role in integrating cognitive and motor functions. After stroke, impairments in cognitive-motor dual task (DT) performance increase fall risk and limit functional independence. We aimed to investigate whether cerebellar intermittent theta-burst stimulation (CRB-iTBS) can improve DT performance in patients with subacute ischemic stroke. In this randomized controlled trial, 26 patients with subacute ischemic stroke and lower-limb impairment were assigned to receive CRB-iTBS or sham-iTBS combined with physiotherapy. Stimulation targeted the cerebellar hemisphere contralateral to the lesion. Cognitive task, single-task (ST: standing/walking), and cognitive-motor DT task (counting backward while standing/walking) completion pre- and post-intervention were compared. The primary outcome was the dual-task cost (DTC) of sway area. Secondary outcomes included DTCs for other balance and gait outcome measures, as well as balance and gait performance, electroencephalographic measures, and functional connectivity. CRB-iTBS significantly reduced the DTC for sway area, the primary outcome. DTCs for cadence and double support time were also reduced. Improvements in standing balance and gait performance were observed across ST and DT conditions. During DT walking, CRB-iTBS was associated with increased theta, alpha, and beta power and enhanced global connectivity. Increased frontal theta power correlated with a reduced DTC for cadence. CRB-iTBS improved DT performance, particularly balance as reflected by reduced DTC for sway area, in patients with subacute stroke. Cerebellar neuromodulation may be a promising adjunctive therapy during stroke rehabilitation.

Article.ArticleTitle: A pilot study on the impact of Hydroxiram D supplementation on nutritional status and sarcopenia-related parameters.

Abstract.AbstractText: Sarcopenia is a frequent and prognostically relevant complication of chronic liver disease. The SARCIRAM pilot trial investigated the effect of Hydroxiram D, a formulation of branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB), and vitamin D, on nutritional status and sarcopenia-related parameters in patients with compensated cirrhosis due to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). In this single-center, randomized pilot study, adults with compensated MASLD-related cirrhosis (Child-Pugh A) received Hydroxiram D plus standard care or standard care alone for 6 months. The primary outcome was phase angle (PA), while secondary outcomes were appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASMM)/height², handgrip strength (HGS), and 4-meter walk test (4-mWT). Between-group comparisons used baseline-adjusted models. Post-hoc simulation analyses were used exploratorily to inform the design of future studies. Thirty-two patients were analyzed. After 6 months, the adjusted change in PA was significantly more favorable in the treated group versus controls (+ 0.36° vs. - 0.45°, p = 0.046). Between-group differences in muscle mass, HGS, and gait speed were not statistically significant, although effect estimates directionally favoured the intervention. No treatment-related adverse events were observed. Six months of Hydroxiram D was associated with a more favorable change in PA in patients with compensated MASLD-related cirrhosis, with favorable trends in muscle parameters. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant confirmation in larger, prospectively registered, double-blind trials to confirm efficacy and long-term outcomes.

Article.ArticleTitle: Subcutaneous Apomorphine for OFF-related Pain in Parkinson Disease: A Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Cross-over Pilot Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: OFF-related pain is a disabling and underrecognized nonmotor symptom of Parkinson disease. Oral dopaminergic therapy may provide inconsistent relief due to erratic gastrointestinal absorption and fluctuating levodopa levels. Subcutaneous apomorphine, a rapid-acting dopamine agonist, may represent a rational rescue strategy.

We conducted a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2-period cross-over pilot trial in Parkinson disease patients with motor fluctuations and reproducible OFF-related pain. Participants received subcutaneous apomorphine (2 mg followed by 3 mg) and placebo on separate visits 1 week apart during defined OFF states established by withholding antiparkinsonian medications overnight for at least 12 hours. The primary outcome was the change in pain severity measured by visual analogue scale (VAS) 30 minutes after the 3 mg dose (90 min from baseline). Secondary outcomes included Movement Disorder Society-Unified Parkinson Disease Rating Scale Part III (MDS-UPDRS Part III) scores, Clinical Global Impression (CGI), and adverse events.

Eleven participants were randomized; 10 completed both treatment periods. At the primary endpoint (n=7 paired), apomorphine produced greater pain reduction than placebo (Hodges-Lehmann median difference -3.85; 95% CI: -6.90 to -1.85; P=0.016; dz=1.57). Motor improvement paralleled analgesic response and correlated with pain reduction (ρ=0.68; P=0.030). Adverse events were mild and comparable between treatments.

Subcutaneous apomorphine was associated with clinically meaningful improvements in OFF-related pain and motor symptoms in this pilot cross-over trial. These findings support further evaluation of dopaminergic rescue therapy as a potential treatment strategy in larger studies.

Article.ArticleTitle: A randomized study on migration of the Spectron EF and the Charnley flanged 40 cemented femoral stems: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial using radiostereometric analysis (RSA) with 10 years' follow-up.

Abstract.AbstractText: Our primary aim was to compare the 10-year migration of the proximally roughened Spectron EF stem with the Charnley flanged 40 stems in cemented THA. Secondary aims were to assess the influence of polyethylene type on Spectron EF migration, and clinical outcomes.

In this randomized trial (NCT00698672), 150 patients (70% women; mean age 70 years) underwent cemented THA with either a Charnley stem (n = 30) or a Spectron EF stem (n = 120, 4 groups with different articulating surfaces). The articulations utilized conventional polyethylene (CPE) or highly crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE) cup liners combined with either cobalt-chromium (CoCr) or Oxinium (OxZr) femoral heads. RSA was performed postoperatively and up to 10 years. Migration was analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Clinical outcome was assessed with the Harris Hip Score (HHS).

After 10 years, 48 patients (14 Charnley, 34 Spectron EF) had evaluable RSA data. Both stems showed posterior translation, subsidence, and retroversion. Retroversion was greater for the Charnley stem than the Spectron EF stem at 3.2° (95% confidence interval [CI] 2.7-3.8) and 1.5° (CI 1.2-1.8), respectively, with a mean difference of 1.7° (CI 1.1- 2.4). The Spectron EF stem had more subsidence at 0.72 mm (CI 0.56-0.88) vs 0.32 mm (CI 0.06-0.57) for the Charnley stem, with a difference of 0.41 mm (CI 0.11-0.71). Spectron EF stems articulating with XLPE had 0.44 mm (CI 0.12-0.76) more subsidence than stems articulating with CPE. HHS improved from 41 (SD 15) to 86 (SD 19) for the Charnley stem and 45 (SD 13) to 86 (SD 15) for the Spectron EF stem with no statistically significant difference between the groups.

After 10 years, the Spectron EF stem showed less retroversion, but more subsidence than the Charnley stem, with otherwise similar migration and clinical outcomes. XLPE articulating stems had more subsidence than CPE with the Spectron EF stem.

Article.ArticleTitle: Brief Report: Prognostic Value of Kaposi Sarcoma Herpes Virus-Associated Clinical Symptom Scores in HIV-Associated Kaposi Sarcoma.

Abstract.AbstractText: Kaposi sarcoma herpes virus (KSHV)-associated inflammatory cytokine syndrome (KICS) is defined by clinical, laboratory, and radiographic findings and KSHV viremia. Whether the presenting clinical symptoms of KICS have prognostic value in patients with HIV-associated Kaposi sarcoma (HIV-KS) initiating therapy is unknown.

Two prospective clinical trials were conducted among participants with mild-to-moderate (A5264/AMC067) and advanced (A5263/AMC066) HIV-KS in low-income and middle-income countries. All participants received antiretroviral therapy, and chemotherapy was given according to the randomly assigned treatment arm.

We developed a Kaposi sarcoma clinical symptom score (KSCS score), derived from the previously described KICS definition to determine whether the score could inform prognosis. The score ranging from 0 to 3 was based on increasing severity of clinical manifestations. We evaluated the impact of baseline KSCS score on progression-free and overall survival using Cox proportional hazard regression.

Of 190 participants in A5264/AMC067 and 329 in A5263/AMC066, 150 (78.9%) and 239 (72.6%) had KSCS score ≥1 and 15 (7.9%) and 95 (28.9%) had KSCS score 3, respectively. Independent of the treatment arm, participants with KSCS score 3 had a higher risk of death (A5264/AMC067: adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) = 9.17; 95% CI: 3.60 to 23.41; A5263/AMC066: aHR = 2.99; 95% CI: 1.69 to 5.28) and shorter progression-free survival (A5264/AMC067: aHR = 2.36 95% CI: 1.26 to 4.43; A5263/AMC066: aHR = 2.31; 95% CI: 1.23 to 3.60) compared with those with KSCS score ≤2.

KSCS score symptoms are common, especially in advanced HIV-KS. KSCS score 3 is associated with higher risk of progressive KS disease or death, despite treatment with antiretrovirals and chemotherapy. This population may benefit from improved diagnostic and management options.

Article.ArticleTitle: Ropivacaine in oblique subcostal transversus abdominis plane block for laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy: a randomized, double-blind clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: To evaluate the analgesic efficacy, opioid consumption, and inflammatory response of oblique subcostal transversus abdominis plane (OSTAP) block with 0.2% ropivacaine versus control in patients undergoing laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG).

This is a prospective, randomized, double-blind, clinical trial. After standardized anesthetic induction, patients received a bilateral OSTAP block with 0.2% ropivacaine or 0.9% saline. Pain, rescue morphine, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15), enhanced recovery after bariatric surgery (ERABS) discharge criteria, and inflammatory markers were assessed.

Rest pain was similar between groups at all time points. During movement, a lower score was observed at 24 h in the ropivacaine group (RG), median 1 (0-6) versus 2 (0-6), but the difference was not statistically significant after adjustment (p = 0.024; Benjamini-Hochberg [BH] adjusted p = 0.096). Total morphine consumption was similar, 10 (2-50) versus 11 mg (1-30), p = 0.926, as were PONV, QoR-15 118 points, p = 0.717, diet resumption 98, ambulation 76, and ERABS discharge criteria. Interleukin-8 at T3 was numerically lower in the RG, 7.2 (0.6-27.1) versus 9.8 (1.3-18.6) pg/mL, without statistical significance after adjustment (p = 0.073; BH adjusted p = 0.142).
OSTAP block with 0.2% ropivacaine was not associated with consistent differences in analgesic, recovery, or inflammatory outcomes.

Article.ArticleTitle: Exercise training program in children and adolescents with asthma: a randomized clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: To evaluate, in children and adolescents with asthma, the effects of an 8-week exercise training program on exercise capacity.

Single-blind, randomized clinical trial in participants with asthma between six and 17 years old under regular treatment. The intervention group performed supervised aerobic and resistance training, and the control group performed supervised stretching in 60-minute sessions twice a week for eight weeks. They were assessed at baseline and following the intervention. The primary outcomes were (VO2peak) and distance walked on the Modified Shuttle Test (MST). Secondary outcomes included quality of life, physical activity in daily living, and serum inflammatory profile. The analyses were intention-to-treat and per protocol.

Thirty participants in the intervention group and 29 in the control group, mean age 10±3 years old, normal lung function (forced expiratory volume - FEV1/forced vital capacity - FVC: 86±8), Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) step: 2 (1-3). No significant differences between groups were observed at the end of the protocol regarding all outcomes. The VO2 peak was 40.3±12.4 mL/kg in the intervention group and 39.2±16.0 mL/kg in the control group (p=0.764). The distance walked on the MST was 852±219 m for the intervention group and 759±255 m for the control group (p=0.142).

A twice-weekly, 8-week exercise program for children and adolescents with asthma did not improve exercise capacity, quality of life, or the inflammatory profile. The optimal frequency of intervention for this population requires further investigation.

OtherAbstract.AbstractText: Avaliar, em crianças e adolescentes com asma, os efeitos de um programa de treinamento físico de oito semanas na capacidade de exercício.

Ensaio clínico randomizado, simples-cego, com participantes com asma de 6 a 17 anos de idade. O grupo de intervenção realizou treinamento aeróbico e resistido e o grupo controle realizou alongamento, em sessões de 60 minutos, duas vezes por semana, durante oito semanas. Os desfechos primários foram o consumo de oxigênio de pico (VO2pico) e a distância percorrida no Shuttle Test Modificado (STM). Desfechos secundários: qualidade de vida, atividade física na vida diária e perfil inflamatório sérico. As análises foram realizadas por intenção de tratar e per protocol.

Trinta participantes no grupo intervenção e 29 no grupo controle, média de idade de 10±3 anos, função pulmonar normal (volume expiratório forçado — VEF1/capacidade vital forçada — CVF: 86±8), etapa da Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA): 2 (1–3). Não foram observadas diferenças significativas entre os grupos ao final do protocolo com relação a todos os desfechos. O VO2 pico foi de 40,3±12,4 mL/kg no grupo intervenção e de 39,2±16,0 mL/kg no grupo controle (p=0,764). A distância percorrida no STM foi de 852±219 m para o grupo intervenção e de 759±255 m para o grupo controle (p=0,142).

Um programa de exercícios realizado duas vezes por semana, durante oito semanas, não melhorou a capacidade de exercício de crianças e adolescentes asmáticos, nem a qualidade de vida ou o perfil inflamatório.

Article.ArticleTitle: [Clinical observation of Sanju Lihe decoction combined with low-intensity pulsed ultrasound in the treatment of type ⅢA prostatitis with qi stagnation and blood stasis].

Abstract.AbstractText: Objective To observe the clinical efficacy and safety of Sanju Lihe decoction combined with low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) in the treatment of type ⅢA prostatitis of qi stagnation and blood stasis pattern. Methods From September 2024 to December 2025, a total of 204 patients with type ⅢA prostatitis of qi stagnation and blood stasis pattern treated at the First Hospital of Hunan University of Chinese Medicine were enrolled and randomly divided equally into a control group and a treatment group. The control group received tamsulosin hydrochloride sustained-release capsules, moxifloxacin hydrochloride tablets, Sanju Lihe decoction, and health education. The treatment group was additionally treated with LIPUS on the basis of the control regimen. The treatment course lasted 4 weeks. During the treatment period, the dropped and excluded cases were recorded. Eventually, 195 cases were completed in the study, including 98 cases in the control group and 97 cases in the treatment group. The National Institutes of Health Chronic Prostatitis Symptom Index (NIH-CPSI), 5-item International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-5), Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS), traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) syndrome scores, uroflowmetry parameters (Qmax, Qave), grading of leukocytes and lecithin bodies in expressed prostatic secretions, clinical efficacy, and follow-up outcomes were compared between the two groups before and after treatment. Results After treatment, NIH-CPSI scores, TCM syndrome scores, and SAS/SDS scores were improved in both groups compared with baseline (P<0.05). The improvements in NIH-CPSI, IIEF-5, SAS, Qmax, Qave, and leukocyte grading in prostatic secretions were significantly better in the treatment group than those in the control group (P<0.05). No significant differences were observed between the two groups in SDS scores, TCM syndrome scores, or lecithin body grading in prostatic secretions after treatment (P>0.05). The total effective rate was 77.55% in the control group and 92.78% in the treatment group, with a significantly higher rate in the treatment group (P<0.05). At the 4-week follow-up after treatment, NIH-CPSI scores remained lower in the treatment group than in the control group (P<0.05). No serious adverse events occurred in either group during treatment. Conclusion On the basis of conventional medication and health education, Sanju Lihe decoction combined with LIPUS further relieves pain and voiding symptoms, improves sexual function, anxiety status, and uroflowmetry, and alleviates local prostatic inflammation in patients with type ⅢA prostatitis of qi stagnation and blood stasis pattern. The regimen is safe and worthy of clinical application.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of Two Desflurane Concentration-Based Anesthetic Strategies on Flash Visual Evoked Potential Monitoring During Spine Surgery: A Randomized Superiority Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Intraoperative flash visual-evoked potential (FVEP) monitoring is valuable for assessing visual function. However, it can be influenced by inhaled anesthetics. This trial aimed to compare two desflurane concentration-based anesthetic strategies for FVEP monitoring.

Seventy patients undergoing elective spinal surgery were enrolled in this prospective, randomized controlled, superiority trial and randomized 1:1 to either the desflurane-based balanced anesthesia group (BA group), receiving 0.5 MAC desflurane with propofol and remifentanil, or the desflurane-dominant inhalational anesthesia group (IA group), receiving 0.7-1.0 MAC desflurane with remifentanil. Baseline measurement in both groups was obtained 30 min after induction (T1) under total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA). The primary outcome was N75-P100 amplitude measured 60 min after induction (T2). Secondary outcomes included decline rates of N75-P100 and P100-N145 amplitudes from T1 to T2.

Among 69 analyzed patients (35 in the BA group and 34 in the IA group), the N75-P100 amplitude of BA group was significantly superior (10.1 [5.2] µV vs 6.3 [2.7] µV; δ = 0.47 µV; mean difference = 3.81 µV, 95% CI: 1.81 to 5.80 (µV); P for superiority < 0.001). The median [IQR] decline rates of the N75-P100 amplitude (0.16 [-0.04 to 0.25] vs 0.49 [0.40 to 0.57], P < 0.001) and the P100-N145 amplitude (0.08 [-0.11 to 0.20] vs 0.44 [0.36 to 0.56], P < 0.001) from T1 to T2 were significantly higher in the IA group than in the BA group.

Desflurane-based balanced anesthesia is superior to desflurane-dominant inhalational anesthesia for preserving FVEP waveforms. When volatile anesthesia is required, the 0.5 MAC desflurane-based balanced regimen may serve as a viable alternative option for intraoperative FVEP monitoring.

OtherAbstract.AbstractText: Flash visual evoked potential (FVEP) monitoring during spine surgery to help preserve patients’ visual function. Total intravenous anesthesia is widely considered the best anesthesia choice for this monitoring. However, it remains unclear how different concentrations of inhaled anesthetic gas affect FVEP signals. We aimed to find out whether higher or lower levels of desflurane change these FVEP waveforms during spine surgery.

We found 0.5MAC desflurane worked better for preserving FVEP signals than 0.7-1.0 MAC desflurane.Meaning: These findings suggest that 0.5 MAC desflurane combined with a propofol-remifentanil regimen is a feasible anesthetic protocol for intraoperative FVEP monitoring when volatile anesthesia is required.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of collective volleyball cooperative tactical training on social anxiety and peer interaction ability in school-aged children: a controlled intervention study.

Abstract.AbstractText: School-aged children that experience social anxiety and have difficulty with interactions among peers can create significant challenges to their development in terms of both psychology and behavior. A team sport such as volleyball provides a common setting that naturally includes all aspects of social interaction (communication, cooperation, role coordination, etc.) and shared goals which is essential to improve the child's confidence in interacting socially and abilities to interact socially with peers.
This research is an examination of the effect that a 12-week collective volleyball cooperative tactical training program will have on social anxiety and peer interaction in children (8-12).

A sample of 80 healthy school-age children was obtained via two methods of campus based, voluntary and/or open recruitment. These children were then randomly assigned to either an experimental intervention group (n = 40) or an active control group receiving standard physical education (n = 40). For 12 consecutive weeks, participants in the experimental group engaged in a type of volleyball cooperative tactical team training that occurred on 3 days each week at 1 h per day. During this time the participants in the control group engaged in standard physical education classes of matched frequency and duration. Social anxiety was measured by use of the Social Anxiety Scale for Children (SASC); SASC measures include total social anxiety, fear of negative evaluation and social avoidance/distress. Participant peer interaction was evaluated using a study-specific 25-item peer-interaction questionnaire covering interaction initiative, peer acceptance, interaction coordination, interaction openness, and conflict resolution ability. Data collection occurred prior to, as well as subsequent to, the intervention. Statistical analyses were conducted utilizing SPSS version 26.0 software. A 2 × 2 mixed-design ANOVA was conducted to examine Group × Time interaction effects, with group (intervention vs. control) as the between-subjects factor and time (pre-intervention vs. post-intervention) as the within-subject factor. Effect sizes were reported using partial eta squared (η 2 p), and post hoc comparisons were performed when significant interactions were identified.

Group × Time Interaction Effects from a mixed-design ANOVA were found to be statistically significant for both of the outcomes (social anxiety and peer interaction) of this study. Children participating in an intervention that included an instructional program using the Collective Volleyball Cooperative Tactical Training Model showed significantly greater improvement than did those in the Control Condition in reducing their level of social anxiety as well as improving their peer interaction abilities over the course of the 12-weeks. Although we found a statistically-significant improvement in both children's social anxiety, and their peer interaction skills through a 12-week program, there is no data available for us to understand if those positive results will continue into the future because we did not assess children at later points in time. Thus, future researchers are encouraged to consider extended assessment periods as part of their study designs to determine how long such interventions have an impact. Secondly, as a feasibility study in a controlled environment showed promise for implementation of cooperative tactical volleyball programs, there may be barriers to successful implementation in regular school settings such as lack of facilities, class size and teacher workload. Future research is needed to examine how cooperative tactical volleyball programs can be adapted to encompass large groups of students and incorporated into routine physical education curriculum. Furthermore, although the intervention showed feasibility under controlled conditions, implementation in regular school settings may face practical challenges, including limited facilities, larger class sizes, and teacher workload. Future studies should examine how cooperative volleyball tactical training can be adapted for broader school-based implementation.

Collective Volleyball Cooperative Tactical Training is an effective method for reducing social anxiety and improving the ability of school aged children to interact with peers. The program offers a viable, school-based model for integrating sport skills acquisition (training) and psychosocial growth through physical activity.

Article.ArticleTitle: Bladder instillation cocktail for preventing catheter-related bladder discomfort after gynecologic surgery: A randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: ObjectiveTo investigate the effectiveness of intravesical instillation of a drug cocktail in preventing postoperative catheter-related bladder discomfort.MethodsIn total, 112 patients were randomized into the "cocktail" or control group. Twenty minutes before the end of the surgery, the "cocktail" group received intravesical instillation of the "cocktail," which contained 1 ug/kg of dexmedetomidine, 5 g of magnesium sulfate, and 10 mg of dexamethasone, totaling 30 mL, while the control group was infused with 30 ml of normal saline. The catheter-related bladder discomfort and visual analog scale of the patients were recorded at 0, 1, 2, and 6 h postoperatively. The 15-item Quality of Recovery scale was used 24 h after surgery to assess the patient's postoperative recovery status.ResultsThe "cocktail" group exhibited significantly decreased catheter-related bladder discomfort severity at 0, 1, 2, and 6 h postoperatively (p = 0.002, p < 0.001, p < 0.001, and p < 0.001, respectively). For the primary outcome (any catheter-related bladder discomfort at 1 h), the risk ratio was 0.52 (95% confidence interval 0.37 to 0.72). Specifically, compared with the control group, the "cocktail" group exhibited a significant decrease in moderate-to-severe catheter-related bladder discomfort at 0, 1, and 2 h postoperatively (5 (8.9%) vs. 13 (23.2%), p = 0.040; 6 (10.7%) vs. 14 (25.0%), p = 0.048; 4 (7.1%) vs. 12 (21.4%), p = 0.031) with rate ratio 0.33-0.43 (95% confidence interval 0.11 to 0.99). Rescue tramadol dose was significantly lower in the cocktail group (35 ± 8 vs 50 ± 12 mg, p = 0.002; median difference = -15.0 mg, 95% confidence interval -19.2 to -10.8).Moreover, patients in the "cocktail" group exhibited significantly higher postoperative recovery scale scores than those in the control group (median difference = 9.0, 95% confidence interval: 7.0-11.0, p < 0.001).ConclusionBladder instillation of the "cocktail" significantly reduces the severity and incidence of moderate-to-severe catheter-related bladder discomfort and improves postoperative recovery in gynecologic patients.

Article.ArticleTitle: Invasive versus conservative strategy for older patients with myocardial infarction based on cognitive function: the SENIOR-RITA cognition analysis.

Abstract.AbstractText: Older adults with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) and cognitive impairment experience higher cardiovascular risk than patients with normal cognition. It remains unclear how cognition should influence whether older adults receive an invasive or conservative treatment strategy.
To compare an invasive and conservative treatment strategy among older adults with NSTEMI and cognitive impairment.

This study is a pre-specified analysis of the SENIOR-RITA randomised controlled trial. Cognition was measured at randomisation using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). Patients were followed up for a median of 4.1 years postrandomisation. The primary outcome was a composite of time to cardiovascular death or nonfatal myocardial infarction (MI).

MoCA was available for 1455 patients (95.8%) who underwent randomisation. Within the cognitively impaired group (909 patients), the primary outcome occurred in 116 patients (26.8%) in the invasive group and in 141 patients (29.6%) in the conservative group (hazard ratio [HR], 0.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 1.10; P = 0.20). Nonfatal MI occurred in 48 patients (11.1%) in the invasive group and in 75 patients (15.8%) in the conservative group (HR 0.64; 95% CI, 0.44 to 0.92). However, there was no interaction between treatment strategy and cognition.

Among those with evidence of cognitive impairment at randomisation, an invasive treatment strategy did not reduce the primary composite outcome of cardiovascular death or nonfatal MI, and there was no evidence of treatment effect heterogeneity based on cognition. The reduction in nonfatal MI events among those with cognitive impairment should be interpreted as an exploratory finding.

Journal.Title: The Journal of international medical research

Article.ArticleTitle: Effectiveness of neck stabilization exercises versus neck and scapular exercises on fear-avoidance beliefs in people with non-specific neck pain.

Abstract.AbstractText: ObjectiveWe aimed to investigate the effect of 8 weeks of neck and scapular stabilization exercises plus conventional physiotherapy on fear-avoidance beliefs and compare this effect with that of neck stabilization exercises plus conventional physiotherapy in individuals with non-specific neck pain.MethodsThis single-blind randomized controlled trial involved 68 participants with non-specific neck pain from three hospitals. They were divided into a control group, which received only conventional physiotherapy (n = 22); a second group that performed neck stabilization exercises and received conventional physiotherapy (n = 23); and a third group that performed neck and scapular stabilization exercises and received conventional physiotherapy (n = 23). The fear-avoidance beliefs questionnaire-physical activities and work subscales-was used to assess fear-avoidance beliefs. Treatment was administered three times weekly for 8 weeks, with fear-avoidance beliefs measured at baseline, week 4, and week 8.ResultsThe median participant age was 54 years; baseline variables of the groups were comparable. Within-group comparisons of the neck and scapular stabilization exercise and neck stabilization exercise groups at baseline, week 4, and week 8 demonstrated a significant reduction in the fear-avoidance beliefs-physical activity score (z = -3.930, p < 0.001, (effect size) r = 0.579) and fear-avoidance beliefs-work score (z = -3.727, p < 0.001; r = 0.559). Between-group comparisons at 8 weeks showed reductions in fear-avoidance beliefs between the neck and scapular stabilization exercise and neck stabilization exercise groups compared with the conventional physiotherapy group, as evidenced by reduced fear-avoidance beliefs-physical activity score (F(2, 65) =, p < 0.001, (effect size) ηp2 = 0.579) and fear-avoidance beliefs-work score (F(2, 65) = 66.88, p < .001, ηp2 = 0.673). At week 8, reductions in the fear-avoidance beliefs-physical activity score between the neck and scapular stabilization exercise and neck stabilization exercise groups did not differ significantly (mean difference = 6.50, SE = 3.47, p = 0.197, 95% confidence interval: -4.08 to 17.07); however, the reduction in fear-avoidance beliefs-work scores between the groups differed significantly (mean difference = 8.06, SE = 3.10, p = 0.035, 95% confidence interval: 0.44-15.68).ConclusionNeck and scapular stabilization exercises and neck stabilization exercises combined with conventional physiotherapy effectively reduced fear-avoidance beliefs in individuals with non-specific neck pain. Neck and scapular stabilization exercise with conventional physiotherapy was more effective at reducing work-related fear-avoidance beliefs than neck stabilization exercise with conventional physiotherapy. Both combinations outperformed conventional physiotherapy alone.

Article.ArticleTitle: Computerised cognitive training combined with nutritional counseling in mild cognitive impairment - results of a 2 × 2 factorial randomized controlled trial (BrainFit-nutrition study).

Abstract.AbstractText: Computerized cognitive training (CCT) and nutritional interventions may improve cognitive functioning in individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI). This study investigated whether a combination of CCT and online nutritional counseling can improve global cognition in individuals with MCI. We also evaluated differences between MCI-specified and active control versions of the interventions.

In this 2 × 2 factorial randomized controlled trial (BrainFit-Nutrition study), conducted fully remotely, participants in Germany with a psychometric diagnosis of MCI (age 60+) were randomized into four groups (Intention to treat, n = 270). For each intervention, one MCI specified and one active control version were developed (cognition: individualized CCT (iCCT) vs. basic CCT (bCCT); nutrition: whole-food plant-based nutrition (WFPB) vs. German Nutrition Society (DGE)). At baseline and after six months, cognitive functioning was assessed with the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA; primary outcome: change after six months). A mixed-model ANCOVA (t0-t6, complete case strategy (CC), n = 228) was applied for the main analysis.

All four groups achieved a significant improvement of approximately 2 points on the MoCA after six months. Estimated marginal means varied from M = 2.44 (iCCTxDGE) to M = 1.77 (iCCTxWFPB), notably without significant group differences. The 2 × 2 mixed ANCOVA revealed a significant main effect of time (F = 3.96, p = 0.048, partial η2 = 0.018). The specific content of the respective modalities being compared (iCCT vs. bCCT; WFPB vs. DGE-oriented counseling) did not appear to make a relevant group difference with regard to the primary outcome. After 6 months, 55% of all participants reached non-MCI values on the MoCA.

The results of this study suggest, that in people with MCI, notable improvement in global cognition can be achieved in a six-months intervention period. When CCT is combined with digital nutritional counseling, the form of intervention - whether elaborate or basic - apparently did not modify the outcome; rather, this data set suggests that it is worthwhile to proactively undertake something in both domains. Future clinical studies in mixed-methods-designs, including usual-care comparators, basic science study modules, qualitative aspects and health economic variables are warranted to gain a better understanding of mechanisms, sustainability of effects, clinical relevance, and cost-effectiveness.

Permission to use the MoCA was obtained. AI-assisted writing (nutritional parts): Artificial intelligence (AI) tools (Claude Code) were used in the preparation of the nutritional parts of this manuscript in a limited and supervised capacity. Specifically, AI-assisted summarization was employed to support the synthesis of relevant literature. Also, text optimization of few selected passages was AI-supported to a very limited extend. All AI-generated or AI-assisted content was critically reviewed, edited, and approved by the authors. The authors take full responsibility for the accuracy, integrity, and intellectual content of the final manuscript. AI tools were not used for data analysis, conceptualization, program development, interpretation of results, or scientific decision-making. This applies only to the sections on nutritional aspects, but not to the rest of the manuscript.
