Article.ArticleTitle: Sigh ventilation versus conventional protective ventilation in cardiac surgery: a proof-of-concept randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Lung protective ventilation is crucial for preventing ventilator-induced lung injury in cardiac surgery. The protective role of a low tidal volume (VT) has been established, whereas the added protection afforded by lung recruitment remains uncertain. We investigated whether sigh breaths could provide additional lung protection, when added to protective ventilation with low VT.

This randomized, assessor-blinded, phase 2 proof-of-concept trial enrolled 192 patients undergoing elective on-pump cardiac surgery from February to August 2024. Patients were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to receive sigh ventilation (sigh breaths plus protective ventilation with low VT; 96 patients) or conventional ventilation (protective ventilation with low VT; 96 patients). Sigh breaths targeting a plateau pressure of 35 cmH2O (or 40 cmH2O for BMI >35 kg/m2) were delivered once every 6 min. Perioperative respiratory mechanics and gas exchange were monitored. The primary outcome was postoperative oxygenation, a marker of lung injury, as measured by the time-weighted average SpO2/FiO2 ratio during the first postextubation hour. There were 9 predefined secondary outcomes, including the severity of respiratory failure within postextubation day 7.

All 192 patients completed the trial (53% male; median age, 64 [55-72] years). Perioperatively, sigh ventilation produced sustained improvements in oxygenation and respiratory system compliance, together with reductions in driving pressure and mechanical power (All P interaction<0.001). After extubation, the mean time-weighted SpO2/FiO2 ratio was higher in the sigh ventilation group (380 ± 86 vs 338 ± 93; mean difference 42.1, 95% CI [16.7 to 67.5]; P=0.001). The severity and occurrence of respiratory failure was reduced in the sigh ventilation group compared with conventional ventilation group (common odds ratio for lower severity 2.2; 95% CI [1.2 to 3.8]; P=0.007). There was no difference in adverse events of interest between groups.

In patients undergoing on-pump cardiac surgery, adding sigh breaths was safe and resulted in a statistically significant improvement in postoperative oxygenation. Nevertheless, the clinical importance of this finding is uncertain because oxygenation was adequately maintained in both groups. Reduction in driving pressure and mechanical power, together with findings in secondary outcomes, suggest additional lung protection and justify future trials.

Article.ArticleTitle: The effect of reduced carbohydrate diet on cardiometabolic risk factors and gut microbiota in children and adolescents with obesity: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: To compare the effects of a reduced-carbohydrate diet (RCD) with a standard diet (STD) on cardiometabolic risk factors and gut microbiota composition in children and adolescents with obesity.

In this randomized controlled trial, 84 children and adolescents with obesity, aged 7-16 years, were randomly assigned to either a RCD (30-40% of total energy from carbohydrates, emphasizing high‑fiber sources) or a STD for 12 weeks. A calorie deficit was applied in both groups. Dietary assessments, anthropometric measurements, body composition analysis, biochemical measurements, and gut microbiota composition were evaluated at baseline and at the end of follow-up. Change in body mass index at 12 weeks was considered the primary outcome.

Sixty-one participants (72.6%) completed the intervention. Both the reduced-carbohydrate diet (RCD) and standard diet (STD) groups showed significant reductions in BMI, BMI z-score, waist circumference, and percent body fat over the 12-week intervention, with no significant differences between groups (p > 0.05).Triglyceride levels and the triglyceride-to-HDL cholesterol ratio decreased significantly in the RCD group compared with the STD group (between-group mean difference - 40.31 mg/dL, 95% CI - 73.79 to - 6.82, p = 0.019 for TG; - 1.03, 95% CI - 1.85 to - 0.20, p = 0.016 for TG/HDL-C). The relative abundance of Verrucomicrobia increased in the RCD group, whereas it decreased in the STD group.

The reduced carbohydrate diet did not show superiority to standard diet in reducing anthropometric indices. However, reduced carbohydrate diet showed beneficial effects on Triglyceride levels and Triglycerides to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio. Further investigation of gut microbiota composition is needed.

Article.ArticleTitle: Efficacy and safety of urokinase intravenous thrombolysis in minor stroke according to large vessel occlusion status: a subgroup analysis of the TRUST trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: The risk-benefit profile of thrombolytic therapy in minor stroke patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO) remains uncertain. This post hoc analysis of the TRUST trial (ThRombolysis with Urokinase for minor Stroke Trial) sought to comparatively assess whether the presence of large vessel occlusion (LVO) modifies the efficacy and safety of urokinase intravenous thrombolysis, compared with best medical treatment(BMT), in patients with minor stroke.

This post-hoc exploratory analysis included patients from the TRUST trial with available vascular imaging data, categorized in the LVO and the non-LVO group. Each group was further divided into the UK thrombolysis group and the BMT group. Primary efficacy outcome was the proportion of patients achieving a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-1 at 90 days. Safety outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) within 36 h and all-cause mortality within 90 days.

Of the 999 patients enrolled in the TRUST trial, 605 were included in the current study. UK thrombolysis was not associated with a 90-day excellent functional outcome in minor stroke patients, either in LVO patients (adjusted risk ratio [RR] 1.90, 95% CI 0.63-2.26) or in non-LVO patients (adjusted RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.84-1.23) compared with the BMT group (p for interaction = 0.41). In the LVO group, UK thrombolysis showed a non-significant trend toward reduced mortality (adjusted RR 0.04, 95% CI 0.01-1.65), whereas no such effect was observed in non-LVO patients (adjusted RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.11-2.52). No significant interaction was found between groups (p for interaction = 0.25). In addition, there were no patients who experienced sICH in subgroup analysis.

This subgroup analysis found no improvement in 90-day functional outcomes with UK thrombolysis in minor stroke patients, irrespective of LVO presence, while maintaining a comparable safety profile with regard to mortality and sICH.
The TRUST trial was registered with ClinicalTrials. gov (NCT04420351). Registration Date: June 04, 2020.

Article.ArticleTitle: Process evaluation of a complex intervention to improve the oral health of nursing home residents (MundZaRR): a multimethod study.

Abstract.AbstractText: The oral health of nursing home residents is often poor. In the cluster-randomised controlled MundZaRR trial, a complex intervention to improve oral health was investigated across 18 nursing homes (n = 271 participants). A comprehensive process evaluation aimed to explore the experiences of various target groups and gain insights into the implementation of the intervention.

The process evaluation followed international guidelines. The study was conducted in Germany and the data collection took place between July 2022 and October 2023 and comprised 23 individual, semi-structured interviews and three focus groups with dentists, dental assistants, nursing home managers and staff, and members of the resident council, 20 participatory observations, written surveys, structured protocols and document analysis. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively; qualitative data were analysed using content analysis.

Three educational training courses over approximately nine hours for dentists and dental assistants were performed largely as planned and evaluated positively. The intervention could not be implemented in one out of nine nursing homes due to staff and time shortages, and the remaining intervention clusters showed considerable variations in implementation fidelity and cooperation between dental assistants and nursing home staff. Participatory observations revealed that individual oral care recommendations were only completely implemented in around half of the observed participants and that more specific oral care measures (e.g., interdental cleaning) were only rarely performed. The main barriers to the intervention's implementation were staff and time shortages, lack of interest or engagement of nursing staff, and individual resident barriers (e.g., poor health condition, uncooperative behaviour). The COVID-19 pandemic posed a major challenge during the recruitment phase, but predominantly did not affect the further course of the study, according to the participating target groups.

Despite the overall positive perception of the intervention concept by the target groups, we found several inconsistencies in the implementation across the nursing homes of the intervention group. The barriers identified can provide indications for the future development and implementation of comparable oral health interventions in the nursing home setting.
ClinicalTrials.gov (Trial registration number NCT04140929). Registered on 24 October 2019, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04140929 .

Article.ArticleTitle: Continuous ultrasound-guided rhomboid intercostal-subserratus plane block versus thoracic paravertebral block for analgesia and respiratory recovery in patients with multiple rib fractures: a single-center randomized trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Effective analgesia is essential in multiple rib fractures to preserve respiratory function. Thoracic paravertebral block (TPVB) is effective but may be limited by technical difficulty and complications. Rhomboid intercostal-subserratus (RISS) plane block is a newer ultrasound-guided alternative.
To compare the analgesic efficacy and pulmonary function recovery associated with ultrasound-guided RISS block and TPVB in patients with traumatic multiple rib fractures.

In this prospective, randomized, blinded trial conducted in an emergency ICU, 50 adults aged 18-60 years with unilateral traumatic fractures of three or more ribs were randomized 1:1 to receive continuous ultrasound-guided TPVB or RISS block with catheter infusion in addition to standardized systemic analgesia. The primary endpoint was pulmonary function at 24 h, assessed using forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1). Secondary outcomes included pain scores at rest and during coughing, pulmonary function, diaphragmatic excursion, rescue opioid consumption, adverse events, and ICU and post-ICU ward stay.

Fifty patients were randomized, with 25 patients in each group. At 24 h, FEV1 increased from 56.2 ± 3.2% to 72.8 ± 5.4% in the TPVB group and from 57.7 ± 3.0% to 73.8 ± 5.6% in the RISS group. The baseline-adjusted between-group difference was not statistically significant (adjusted RS-TP difference, 0.47 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.63 to 3.57; p = 0.768). At 24 h, median VAS pain scores at rest were 1 (0-2) and 0 (0-2), while scores during coughing were 3 (2-4) and 2 (2-4), in the TPVB and RISS groups, respectively. Total rescue morphine consumption over 72 h was comparable between groups (13.3 ± 3.2 mg vs 11.7 ± 4.6 mg; p = 0.205). Needle visibility was significantly better with RISS. Vascular puncture and block-related pneumothorax each occurred in two TPVB patients and no RISS patients, although the between-group differences were not statistically significant.

Continuous ultrasound-guided RISS block provided analgesia and 24 h pulmonary-function recovery similar to TPVB in stable, spontaneously breathing patients with unilateral multiple rib fractures. RISS also provided better needle visibility. Although procedure-related complications were observed only in the TPVB group, this trial was not powered to establish comparative safety.
ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05898958. Registered on June 12, 2023. Retrospectively registered.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of time-restricted eating and supervised exercise on intrahepatic fat and cardiometabolic health in adults with obesity: the TEMPUS randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Lifestyle interventions targeting intrahepatic fat remain limited. We investigated whether 8-hour time-restricted eating (TRE), supervised exercise, or their combination reduced intrahepatic fat fraction (IHFF) more than usual care (UC; Mediterranean diet and physical activity education) and each other. This investigator-initiated, parallel-group randomized controlled trial was conducted in Granada, Spain. Participants were recruited from May 2023 to April 2024, and the trial was completed on 5 September 2025. Primary outcome assessors and statisticians were blinded to group allocation, whereas intervention personnel were not. All 187 randomized adults with obesity (50% women) were included in the primary intention-to-treat analysis: UC (n = 48), TRE (n = 46), Exercise (n = 47), and TRE+Exercise (n = 46). The primary outcome was change in IHFF measured by magnetic resonance imaging after 12 weeks. IHFF change did not differ with TRE (-0.4%; 95% CI, -2.0 to 1.2; P = 0.93), Exercise (-0.8%; -2.4 to 0.8; P = 0.54), or TRE+Exercise (-1.1%; -2.7 to 0.5; P = 0.28) compared with UC, nor among intervention groups. These findings do not support greater short-term IHFF reductions with TRE, exercise, or their combination than with UC or between intervention groups. Trial registration: NCT05897073.

Article.ArticleTitle: Rapid Renin Angiotensin Aldosterone System inhibitor optimisation in patients with chronic kidney disease and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction using potassium binder: a randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone inhibitors (RAASi) improve outcomes in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), but their use is often limited by hyperkalaemia in chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients. This double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial evaluated whether sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) enables RAASi up-titration in HFrEF patients with CKD stages 3-5 and serum potassium of 5.0-5.5 mmol/L over 14 weeks. The primary binary outcome was defined as achieving the target dose of RAAS inhibition therapy without reaching hyperkalaemia (serum potassium ≥5.6 mmol/L) over 14 weeks or otherwise. Participants (n = 112) were randomised 1:1 to receive sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) or placebo. The per-protocol (PP) analyses included 43 out of 53 (81%) in the SZC arm and 53 out of 59 participants (90%) in the placebo arm; the intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses included all 112. At the end of the trial, 24 of 43 participants (56%) in the SZC group achieved the target RAASi dose without developing hyperkalaemia compared with 15 of 53 patients (28%) in the placebo group (PP analysis, p = 0.006, ITT analysis, p = 0.007,). Participants in the SZC group were 3 times more likely to reach the target dose without reaching potassium 5.6 mmol/L (OR = 3.16; 95% CI 1.35-7.39; p = 0.008) than in the placebo group (ITT analysis). No significant differences in adverse events between the two groups were observed. SZC appears to safely support rapid RAASi optimisation in HFrEF patients with CKD. This trial was funded by AstraZeneca via Externally Sponsored Scientific Research grant ESR-19-20174. Trial Registration: Clinicaltrials.gov NCT05004363 and EudraCT number 2020-002946-18.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of a lacto-vegetarian diet combined with 14-hour time-restricted eating on metabolic outcomes in women with Type 2 diabetes: a 24-week randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Women with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) often require interventions that are culturally acceptable, practical, sustainable, and can be easily fit into their daily routine to manage their blood sugar levels. Although plant-based dietary patterns and time-restricted fasting have demonstrated metabolic benefits, limited evidence exists on their combined effects in Indian women with T2DM.
This trial evaluated whether a lactovegetarian diet combined with 14-hour time-restricted eating improves glycemic and cardiometabolic outcomes compared with usual diabetes care.

96 women (25-60 years) with T2DM were enrolled in a 24-week, multicenter, randomized, open-label parallel-arm trial; 90 completed the study. The participants were divided into two groups: an intervention group following a structured lacto-vegetarian diet combined with 14-hour fasting, and control group receiving usual diabetes care. The diet contained 15-20% protein, 20-25% fat, and improved carbohydrate quality (50-55% from whole grains/high-fiber foods). Biochemical estimations and anthropometric measurements were taken at baseline and 24 weeks. The study employed an intention-to-treat analysis protocol, and the perceived benefits and safety of the intervention were reported.

At 24 weeks, baseline-adjusted between-group comparisons showed significantly greater improvements in the intervention group compared with usual diabetes care. The intervention group had lower adjusted values for body weight, BMI, glycemic, and lipid profiles. The adjusted mean HbA1c was 6.53% in the intervention group compared with 7.65% in the control group, with an adjusted mean difference of -1.12% (95% CI: -1.35 to -0.89; p < 0.001). HOMA-IR was also significantly lower in the intervention group, with an adjusted mean difference of -1.84 (95% CI: -2.27 to -1.41; p < 0.001). Adverse events were mild and transient, while most participants reported improved energy, mood, weight loss, and overall health.

A culturally adaptable lacto-vegetarian diet combined with a 14-hour time-restricted fasting regimen safely improves metabolic control and insulin sensitivity in women with Type 2 Diabetes, offering a practical, women-centric strategy that may be implementable within structured clinical nutrition services, although its staffing requirements, cost, and scalability require further evaluation.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of discontinuing antihypertensives on perioperative hypotension in older patients before non-cardiac surgery: multicentre, randomised, double blind, controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: To determine whether discontinuing versus continuing angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) on the morning of surgery reduces perioperative hypotension in older patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery.
Multicentre, randomised, double blind, placebo controlled trial.
Five tertiary teaching hospitals in China, November 2020 to December 2023.
2036 older patients (60-80 years) using ACE inhibitors or ARBs for at least two weeks and scheduled for non-cardiac surgery under general anaesthesia.
Patients were randomised to receive their usual ACE inhibitor or ARB or a placebo in identical capsules on the morning of surgery.

The primary outcome was the incidence of perioperative hypotension (mean blood pressure <65 mm Hg or a ≥30% decrease from baseline requiring treatment). Secondary outcomes included duration of hypotension, requirement for a vasopressor, intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, and 30 day complications (neurocognitive disorders, major cardiocerebral events) or mortality.

2012 patients (mean age 68.8 years; 54.4% male) completed the study: 1004 were included in the antihypertensive group and 1008 in the no antihypertensive group. The incidence of perioperative hypotension was lower in the no antihypertensive group (314/1008, 31.2%) versus antihypertensive group (457/1004, 45.5%): adjusted odds ratio 0.52 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.43 to 0.63); absolute risk difference -14.4% (95% CI -18.5% to -10.1%); P<0.001. The duration of hypotension and requirement for a vasopressor were both reduced in the no antihypertensive group: adjusted mean difference -1.3 minutes (95% CI -1.8 to -0.8 minutes) and 28.5% v 41.1%; adjusted odds ratio 0.54 (95% CI 0.44 to 0.66). Intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, 30 day complications, and mortality did not differ significantly between groups.

Discontinuing ACE inhibitors or ARBs on the morning of surgery in older patients with hypertension statistically significantly reduced perioperative hypotension and the requirement for vasopressors without increasing 30 day complications or mortality. This simple strategy provides high certainty evidence for preoperative drug management in this patient population.
Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2000039376.

Article.ArticleTitle: Development and Initial Clinical Evaluation of a Stress-Induced Computerized Bowel Sound Analysis System for Irritable Bowel Syndrome.

Abstract.AbstractText: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is diagnosed using symptom-based criteria because no established physiological test objectively supports the diagnosis. We developed and evaluated a computerized bowel sound analysis system incorporating a dichotic listening task as a psychological stress challenge in three phases. In Phase 1, a short-time energy (STE)-based bowel sound extraction algorithm showed high sensitivity and specificity in technical evaluation. In Phase 2, six individuals with IBS and 10 healthy controls underwent two dichotic listening conditions in a randomized crossover study. Bowel sounds and heart-rate variability were recorded during consecutive 10-min resting, stress-loading, and recovery periods. Despite no significant between-condition differences, the condition showing numerical LF and HF increases during stress loading in participants with IBS was selected exploratorily. Using this condition, Phase 3 evaluated 15 individuals with IBS and 38 healthy controls. The percentage change in STE from rest to stress loading (rest-to-stress ΔSTE) showed an AUC of 0.79 (95% confidence interval, 0.66-0.91), with 0.80 sensitivity and 0.68 specificity at an exploratory cutoff of 20.1%. Computerized bowel sound analysis during psychological stress showed preliminary potential as a non-invasive physiological adjunct for distinguishing IBS from healthy controls. Validation in larger independent cohorts is required. J. Med. Invest. 73 : 503-518, August, 2026.

Article.ArticleTitle: Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement.

Abstract.AbstractText: Studies comparing aspirin with anticoagulants for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty have had conflicting results.

In a comparative-effectiveness noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned patients undergoing elective hip or knee arthroplasty to receive aspirin (81 mg twice daily), warfarin (to a target international normalized ratio of 2.0), or rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) for 30 days. The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion. The noninferiority margin for the risk difference was 0.69 percentage points.

Among 18,883 participants who had undergone randomization, 15,317 (7214 with hip arthroplasty and 8103 with knee arthroplasty) were included in the primary per-protocol analysis. A primary effectiveness outcome event occurred in 77 of 6090 participants (1.26%) in the aspirin group, in 52 of 4231 (1.23%) in the warfarin group, and in 47 of 4996 (0.94%) in the rivaroxaban group; a primary safety outcome event occurred in 177 (2.91%), 142 (3.36%), and 174 (3.48%), respectively. In pairwise comparisons, 6-month risks of a primary effectiveness outcome event were 1.24% and 0.94% for aspirin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.30 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.20 to 0.81); 1.24% and 1.01% for aspirin versus warfarin (difference, 0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.34 to 0.81); and 1.13% and 1.10% for warfarin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.57 to 0.63). Risks of a primary safety outcome event were 3.70% and 3.02% for rivaroxaban versus aspirin (difference, 0.68 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.41); 3.65% and 2.88% for warfarin versus aspirin (difference, 0.77 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.58); and 3.59% and 3.61% for rivaroxaban versus warfarin (difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.89 to 0.85). Intention-to-treat analyses yielded similar results.

Aspirin prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty was not noninferior to rivaroxaban or warfarin with respect to death or symptomatic VTE. Warfarin and rivaroxaban were not noninferior to aspirin for safety. (Funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute; PEPPER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02810704.).

Article.ArticleTitle: Home-Based, Digitally Assisted Dyadic Tai Chi Intervention for Patients With Chronic Heart Failure and Their Caregivers: Development of an Intervention and Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Chronic heart failure (CHF) imposes a dual and dynamically interrelated burden on patients and family caregivers, whose health and illness management behaviors are interdependent. Exercise interventions that actively engage the patient-caregiver dyad as the unit of rehabilitation in the home setting remain underdeveloped.

This study aimed to develop a home-based, digitally assisted, dyadic tai chi (HDTC) intervention and evaluate its feasibility, acceptability, safety, and preliminary effects among dyads of patients with CHF and their caregivers.

This sequential, multiphase study comprised intervention development followed by a single-center, assessor-blinded, parallel-group pilot randomized controlled trial. Phase 1 integrated literature review, theoretical frameworks, and stakeholder focus group interviews to develop and refine the HDTC intervention. In phase 2, eligible adults with CHF (aged 18-75 years; New York Heart Association class I-III) and their primary caregivers were recruited from a tertiary medical center in Qingdao, China, from October 14 to November 12, 2024, and followed for 12 weeks. Forty dyads were allocated 1:1 to the 12-week HDTC intervention plus usual care or usual care alone (n=20 per group). Outcome assessors and the data analyst were blinded to group allocation. Feasibility, acceptability, and safety were the primary focus of the pilot trial. Patient, caregiver, and dyadic health outcomes were preliminarily explored at baseline and 4 and 12 weeks. All 40 randomized dyads were included in the intention-to-treat analyses.

The HDTC intervention comprised an online educational seminar, nurse-led dyadic coaching, preliminary face-to-face tai chi training, and supervised HDTC practice. The recruitment rate was 83.3% (40/48), mean session attendance was 73.7% (SD 8.6%), and 70% (14/20) of participants achieved high adherence rate (≥75% attendance). All intervention dyads rated the intervention as acceptable. No intervention-related adverse events were identified. Exploratory generalized estimating equation analyses suggested greater improvements from baseline to 12 weeks in the intervention group than in the control group in functional capacity (β=38.858; P=.001), together with greater reductions in Minnesota Living With Heart Failure Questionnaire scores (β=-1.850; P=.002), sedentary time (β=-1.025; P=.01), and fear of activity (β=-6.550; P=.01). Caregiver burden also decreased (β=-4.350; P<.001), while mutuality improved more for both patients (β=10.508; P<.001) and caregivers (β=6.450; P<.001).

The HDTC intervention was feasible and acceptable, with preliminary improvements across patient, caregiver, and dyadic outcomes. By integrating shared patient-caregiver participation with digitally supported home-based tai chi, the HDTC intervention extends patient-centered rehabilitation toward a dyad-oriented model. If confirmed in a fully powered trial, this approach may offer a practical strategy for expanding home-based cardiac rehabilitation.

Article.ArticleTitle: Civil Society Organization-Led Home Visit Intervention to Reduce Unintentional Child Injury in Rural China: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Unintentional injuries are a leading cause of childhood death and disability, but evidence on scalable home visit interventions in rural settings is limited.
To evaluate whether a civil society organization-led home visit intervention can reduce unintentional injuries among children and improve caregiver and household safety.

This outcome assessor-blinded cluster randomized clinical trial was conducted in 24 rural communities in Guizhou and Shaanxi, China, from May 6 to October 1, 2025. After baseline assessment, communities were randomized as clusters in a 1:1 ratio. Participants were households with children aged 3 to 12 years.

Control communities received routine social worker home visits; intervention communities received routine services plus 3 monthly structured visits with home safety and first aid tool kits and a follow-up visit at month 4.

The primary outcome was caregiver-reported cumulative child unintentional injury incidence during 4 months, a subjective outcome with caregivers unblinded to group allocation. Secondary outcomes were caregiver knowledge, safety attitudes, and supervisory behaviors, with scores ranging from 0 to 40, 0 to 8, and 0 to 80, respectively, with higher scores indicating better knowledge, more positive safety attitudes, and more appropriate supervisory behaviors, respectively, and household environmental hazards, with scores ranging from 0 to 230 and higher scores indicating more household environmental hazards and a less safe home environment. Generalized estimating equations accounted for clustering.

Among 24 randomized clusters, caregivers (mean [SD] age, 45.4 [13.0] years; 271 [75.3%] female) and children (mean [SD] age, 8.6 [2.3] years, 198 [55.0%] female) from 360 households were enrolled, with 180 each randomized to intervention and control groups. After baseline, 9 households withdrew with missing outcome data; all 360 households were included in the intention-to-treat analyses with multiple imputation. Injury occurred in 21 of 178 households (11.8%) with observed outcomes in the intervention group and 33 of 173 (19.1%) in the control group. The intervention was associated with lower injury odds (adjusted odds ratio, 0.36 [95% CI, 0.18-0.73]; P = .005). At month 4, adjusted mean differences favored the intervention for supervisory behaviors (17.08 [95% CI, 14.71-19.46] points) and household environmental hazards (-36.66 [95% CI, -42.87 to -30.46] points).

In this cluster randomized clinical trial of households with children aged 3 to 12 years, a civil society organization-led home visit intervention reduced caregiver-reported unintentional injuries and improved caregiver supervisory behaviors and household safety during the 4-month intervention period. Longer follow-up is needed to assess durability of the response.

Journal.Title: Plant foods for human nutrition (Dordrecht, Netherlands)

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects on Sleep Quality and Bioelectrical Parameters of Cellular Health After Administration of a Plant Protein Supplement Combined with Ashwagandha and Rhodiola: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Sleep disturbances affect a significant portion of the global population, impacting health and quality of life. While plant-based proteins and adaptogens such as ashwagandha and rhodiola have shown individual benefits, their combined effects remain poorly understood. This study evaluated whether a nutritional intervention combining plant protein with ashwagandha-rhodiola could improve sleep quality in middle-aged adults. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial was conducted with 100 participants aged 35-70 years, assigned to VERUM (n=50) or PLACEBO (n=50) groups. The VERUM group received plant protein (27 g/day: pea, rice, hemp isolate) plus adaptogen tablets (Rhodiola rosea 300 mg + Withania somnifera KSM-66® 500 mg) for 30 days. Sleep quality was assessed using the validated Sleep Quality Questionnaire (SQQ) completed daily. Phase angle was measured by bioimpedance (BIA-TELELAB) pre- and post-intervention. Data were analyzed using longitudinal mixed models and non-parametric tests. Seventy-seven participants completed bioimpedance analysis (VERUM group; n= 38, PLACEBO group n=39; mean age 47.8±8.2 years), and sixty-one completed sleep assessments (VERUM group n=32; PLACEBO group n=29). The VERUM group showed highly significant improvements: sleep difficulty reduced by 56% (p<0.001, d=0.91), daytime sleepiness decreased by 60% (p<0.001, d=0.85), and total sleep score improved by 58% (p<0.001, d=0.96), representing a 3.7-fold greater improvement than placebo. Phase angle changes were minimal in both groups. No adverse events were reported. The combination of plant protein with ashwagandha-rhodiola for 30 days produces substantial, clinically relevant improvements in sleep quality with an excellent safety profile, with statistically greater improvements compared to placebo.

Article.ArticleTitle: Differential effects of pea protein isolate, pea protein concentrate, and whey protein isolate supplementation on gut microbiota and metabolic markers in healthy adults: a 3-arm parallel randomised intervention.

Abstract.AbstractText: As origin and quality of dietary protein are key modulators of gut microbiota and host metabolism, characterising health effects of different proteins is increasingly important given the need to shift towards more plant-based protein sources for environmental sustainability. Yet, direct comparisons across protein sources and food matrices in humans remain limited. This randomised, double-blind, 3-arm parallel, dietary intervention study examined the effects of four-week pea protein concentrate (PPC), pea protein isolate (PPI) or whey protein isolate (WPI) supplementation (0.5 g/kg body mass/day) on gut microbiota composition in healthy adults as the main outcome.

Faecal samples and lifestyle questionnaires were collected weekly, with fasting blood and 24-h urine samples obtained at baseline, mid- and post-intervention. Proteins were compared using two contrasts - PPC vs. PPI and PPI vs. WPI - investigating differences between plant and animal-based proteins as well as between plant-based proteins with different matrixes.

Supplementation of PPC and PPI significantly reduced α-diversity and increased β-diversity, partly modulated by BMI. At species level, relative abundances of Anaerobutyricum hallii and Bifidobacterium longum increased significantly in subjects consuming PPC. A similar result was observed for Lactobacillus crispatus and Limosilactobacillus frumenti in subjects consuming PPI.

Our findings demonstrate that different dietary proteins selectively modulate beneficial gut microbial species, highlighting the importance of investigating individual responses to dietary interventions. Further studies are needed to verify how compositional changes translate into changes in microbial functionality.

Article.ArticleTitle: Ventilation distribution assessed by electrical impedance tomography during robot-assisted laparoscopic prostatectomy: A randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: During robot-assisted laparoscopic prostatectomy (RALP), the combination of intra-abdominal pressure and a steep Trendelenburg position increases the risk of alveolar collapse and shifts the center of ventilation toward the abdomen, leading to intraoperative and postoperative hypoxia. This study evaluated whether fixed positive end-expiratory pressure(PEEP) 10 cmH2O, compared with zero PEEP (ZEEP), maintained a more central ventilation distribution during RALP as assessed by electrical impedance tomography (EIT).

Sixty-five adult patients undergoing RALP were randomly assigned to either a PEEP 0 cmH2O group or a PEEP 10 cmH2O group. The primary endpoint was the mean center of ventilation (COV), as assessed using EIT. Secondary endpoints included other EIT parameters: the region of interest, global inhomogeneity index, and regional ventilation delay, as well as the P/F ratio, pulmonary compliance, peak airway pressure, and driving pressure (ΔP). Hemodynamic effects, lung injury biomarkers, and inflammatory cytokines were also evaluated. EIT and ventilator parameters were recorded at 6 time points: pre-intubation, post-intubation, during the Trendelenburg position, during pneumoperitoneum, pre-extubation, and post-extubation. Arterial blood gas and hemodynamic data were collected at the same points, plus 4 hours after ICU admission and again at ICU discharge. Lung injury biomarkers and inflammatory cytokines were measured pre- and postoperatively.

The group-by-time interaction for COV was not statistically significant (P = .057). In exploratory Tukey-adjusted comparisons, COV was closer to 50% in the PEEP 10 group after intubation (PEEP 0 vs PEEP 10: 58.2% vs 53.4%; P = .038) and before extubation (58.6% vs 53.1%; P = .007). ΔP was lower, and lung compliance was higher, in the PEEP 10 group during the Trendelenburg position and pneumoperitoneum. No improvement in the P/F ratio or consistent between-group differences in major hemodynamic variables, KL-6, or IL-6 were observed.

During RALP, with a fixed PEEP of 10 cmH2O, there was no group-by-time interaction effect observed for COV. However, in exploratory time-point comparisons, it was associated with a tendency for ventilation to be more centrically shifted after intubation and before extubation, and was also associated with an attenuated increase in ΔP and an attenuated decrease in lung compliance during the Trendelenburg position and pneumoperitoneum.

Article.ArticleTitle: Risk-tailored antiemetic prophylaxis with NEPA in Chinese cancer patients receiving moderately emetogenic chemotherapy: MyRisk study subgroup analysis.

Abstract.AbstractText: Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) remains a key challenge for patients receiving moderately emetogenic chemotherapy (MEC), especially those at high risk. This study is the first to apply a validated risk algorithm to guide antiemetic prophylaxis in Chinese MEC patients.

MyRisk was a phase IV, randomized, open-label, multinational trial (NCT04817189) enrolling adult patients with a high-risk CINV score (≥13), scheduled for 3 cycles of MEC. Patients were randomized to oral netupitant-palonosetron (NEPA capsule) + dexamethasone or standard of care (SoC), including a 5-hydroxytryptamine-3 receptor antagonist + dexamethasone. The primary endpoint was model-estimated complete response (no emesis/no rescue medication) during the overall phase (0-120 hours) across 3 consecutive cycles. This report describes a prespecified analysis of the Chinese subgroup in the MyRisk study.

Of 53 enrolled Chinese patients, 50 were included (NEPA: n = 24; SoC: n = 26). NEPA showed a numerically higher overall complete response rate than SoC (89.1% vs 77.3%; odds ratio = 2.39, 95% confidence interval = 0.57-9.98) as well as higher rates of no emesis (92.2% vs 80.0%) and no significant nausea (80.6% vs 70.7%) across delayed and overall phases across all cycles. However, these differences were not statistically significant. NEPA was well tolerated across all 3 cycles, with no serious adverse events.

In this Chinese subgroup analysis, risk-tailored prophylaxis with NEPA provided effective and safe control of delayed and overall CINV. Although statistically insignificant, consistent numerical benefits support consideration of neurokinin-1 receptor antagonist-based strategies for high-risk MEC patients. Future studies with larger sample sizes in the Chinese population are warranted to permit statistical evaluation.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of cervical stability exercises using proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation on physical function and activity in patients with neck pain and forward head posture: A randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: We investigated the effects of proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation cervical stability exercises (PNFCSEs) on pain intensity, craniocervical flexor endurance (CCFE), forward head posture (FHP), and neck disability in patients with neck pain and FHP.

Patients were randomly allocated to 3 groups using a randomized controlled trial. The PNFCSE (n = 23), CSEs (n = 23), and traditional physical therapy (TPT; n = 21) groups received TPT, which included a hot pack, interferential current therapy, and ultrasound. In addition, the PNFCSE group received CSE using PNF, while the CSE group received CSE using a pressure biofeedback unit. Interventions were conducted thrice weekly for 6 weeks. Pain intensity and CCFE were measured before and after the intervention. FHP and neck disability level were also measured before and after the intervention. A total of 67 participants (35 women, 32 men; mean age 45.7-47.4 years across groups) completed the study.

A 3 × 2 (group × time) mixed analysis of variance showed significant group × time interactions for pain intensity, craniovertebral angle (CVA), CCFE, and neck disability level (all P < .001). All 4 outcomes changed significantly over time within each group (all P < .001, except TPT-group CVA, P = .003): pain intensity and disability level were reduced, and CVA and CCFE were increased. Post hoc comparisons of the pre-to-post change scores showed significantly greater improvements in the PNFCSE and CSE groups than in the TPT group for all 4 outcomes (all P < .05), and a significantly greater increase in CCFE in the PNFCSE group than in the CSE group (P = .022); no other differences were found between the PNFCSE and CSE groups.

In patients with neck pain and FHP, PNFCSEs significantly reduced pain intensity and neck disability and improved CCFE and FHP, with greater improvements than TPT alone and a greater gain in CCFE than CSE using pressure biofeedback. CSEs based on the PNF concept may be an effective intervention to reduce pain and neck disability in patients with neck pain and FHP.

Article.ArticleTitle: [Effect of zinc selenium L-carnitine compound nutrient combined with tamoxifen citrate on routine semen parameters and sperm DNA fragmentation index in male infertility patients].

Abstract.AbstractText: Objective To explore the effect of zinc selenium L-carnitine compound nutrient combined with tamoxifen citrate on routine semen parameters and sperm DNA fragmentation index of male infertility patients with abnormal sperm DNA fragmentation index. Methods A total of 903 male infertile patients with sperm DFI (>15%) were selected and randomly divided into control group (453 cases) and combination group (450 cases). The control group was treated with vitamin E soft capsule, and the combination group was treated with zinc selenium L-carnitine compound nutrient combined with tamoxifen citrate. The percentages of normal morphology sperm, sperm volume, sperm concentration, percentage of forward moving sperm（PR）, percentage of non-forward moving sperm（NP）, and DFI of patients in the two groups were collected before treatment and 1, 2 and 3 months after treatment. The effective rates of combined medication treatment for patients with abnormal DFI in different age groups were compared. Results After 1 month of treatment in the combination group, PR increased significantly and DFI decreased significantly (P<0.01). After 2 months of treatment, compared with before treatment, PR (P<0.01) and NP increased (P<0.05), DFI decreased (P<0.01). After 3 months of treatment, the semen volume increased compared with before treatment (P<0.05), and DFI decreased continuously (P<0.01). However, there was no significant difference in the percentage of normal morphological sperm and sperm concentration compared with before treatment (P>0.05). In the control group, PR increased significantly after 1 and 2 months of treatment compared with before treatment (P<0.01, P<0.05), and DFI decreased significantly (P<0.001, P<0.01). However, there was no statistically significant difference in the percentage of normal morphological sperm, semen volume, sperm concentration, and NP compared with before treatment. There was no significant difference in any parameters after 3 months of treatment compared with before treatment (P>0.05). Before treatment, the differences in various parameters between the two groups were not significant (P>0.05). After 1 and 2 months of treatment, compared with the control group, the DFI of the combination group showed a significant decrease (P<0.01, P<0.05), and the differences in other parameters were not significant (P>0.05). After 3 months of treatment, the differences in various parameters between the two groups were not significant (P>0.05). Among the patients in the combination group with DFI>25%, the treatment effectiveness rate of patients aged ≥35 years was higher than that of those aged <35 years old (P<0.01); while among the patients in the combination group with 15%<DFI≤25%, the difference in the treatment effectiveness rate between those aged ≥35 years and those aged <35 years was not statistically significant (P>0.05). Conclusion The zinc selenium L-carnitine compound nutrient combined with tamoxifen citrate can improve PR and sperm DNA integrity of male infertility patients. Meanwhile, patients with higher baseline DFI values combined with older age have better therapeutic effects.

Article.ArticleTitle: [Effects of biofeedback electrical stimulation integrated with Chinese medicine emotional care on alleviating symptoms in the patients with chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome].

Abstract.AbstractText: Objective To evaluate the efficacy of biofeedback electrical stimulation combined with Chinese medicine emotional nursing in improving symptoms among patients with chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CP/CPPS). Methods Seventy patients who met the inclusion criteria of CP/CPPS were randomly divided into the conventional group and the combined intervention group, with 35 cases in each group. The control group received oral tamsulosin sustained-release capsules along with routine care. In addition to the conventional treatment, the patients in combined intervention group received biofeedback electrical stimulation combined with Chinese Medicine emotional nursing. Biofeedback electrical stimulation was administered three times per week for a total of 8 weeks. The National Institutes of Health Chronic Prostatitis Symptom Index (NIH-CPSI), International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA), and Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD) were used to assess patients at baseline, 4 weeks, and 8 weeks of intervention. Results No significant differences in baseline data were observed between the two groups before the intervention (P>0.05). After 4 and 8 weeks of intervention, both groups showed significant improvements in NIH-CPSI, IPSS, HAMA and HAMD scores compared to baseline (P<0.05). Compared to the control group, the combined intervention group demonstrated significantly greater reductions in the total NIH-CPSI score, its pain subscore, IPSS score, and HAMA score at both 4 and 8 weeks (P<0.05). By the 8th week, the combined intervention group also showed a significantly greater reduction in the NIH-CPSI urination subscore and HAMD score (P<0.05). However, no statistically significant intergroup difference was found in the NIH-CPSI quality of life subscore (P>0.05). Furthermore, the combined intervention group achieved significantly higher rates of nursing satisfaction (97.05%) and overall efficacy (91.18%) compared to the control group (P<0.05). Conclusion The combined intervention of biofeedback electrical stimulation and Chinese Medicine emotional nursing can significantly alleviate urinary symptoms, pelvic pain, and anxiety-depression moods in patients with CP/CPPS. Although there was no statistically significant difference in the quality of life scores between the two groups, the combined intervention may provide potential benefits for the long-term improvement of patients' quality of life in terms of the improvement of core clinical symptoms and emotional states.

Article.ArticleTitle: [Comparative study on urinary incontinence control between "push stripping" and "pry stripping" techniques in patients with transurethral thulium laser enucleation of the prostate].

Abstract.AbstractText: Objective To explore the value of "pushing stripping" transurethral thulium laser enucleation of the prostate in preventing postoperative urinary incontinence. Methods A total of 155 benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) patients admitted to 924 Hospital, Joint Logistic Support Force from April 2022 to October 2024 were randomly divided into 2 groups according to the random number table. Seventy-seven patients were included in Group A who underwent ThuLEP using the "pry stripping" technique. While 78 BPH patients were included in Group B treated with modified ThuLEP procedure using the "push stripping" technique. Perioperative parameters and the incidence of urinary incontinence after 1, 3 and 6 months of operation were analyzed to assess the efficacy and safety of the "push stripping" technique. Results There was no significant difference in prostate volume (［105.0±42.3］ mL vs ［109.0±51.2］mL), operation time(［45.3±21.2］ min vs ［48.6±25.5］ min) and postoperative urinary catheter indwelling time (［3.0±2.5］ d vs ［3.3±2.8］ d)between the two groups of patients (P>0.05). The incidences of urinary incontinence in group A and group B were 19.5% (15 cases) and 7.7% (6 cases) 24 hours after extubation, respectively. The incidences of urinary incontinence in group A and group B were 13.0% (10 cases) and 3.8% (3 cases) 1 month after surgery, respectively. There were significant differences in the incidences of urinary incontinence between the two groups 24 hours after surgery and 1 month after surgery (P<0.05). There was no significant difference in the incidences of urinary incontinence between the two groups three months after operation (P>0.05). No urinary incontinence occurred in both groups 6 months after surgery, and no permanent incontinence occurred. Conclusion With good safety and effectiveness, the "push stripping" technique for transurethral thulium laser enucleation of the prostate reduces the incidence of early postoperative urinary incontinence and improves the quality of life during the recovery period, making it worthy of clinical promotion.

Article.ArticleTitle: [Application of Fuyang moxibustion based on the Zhou Tian theory in patients with erectile dysfunction of kidney-yang deficiency type].

Abstract.AbstractText: Objective To investigate the clinical efficacy of Zhou Tian Fuyang moxibustion in patients with erectile dysfunction of the kidney-yang deficiency pattern. Methods A total of 76 patients of the kidney-yang deficiency pattern who met the inclusion and exclusion criteria were selected and randomly divided into a control group and a Zhou Tian Fuyang moxibustion group, with 38 cases in each group. The control group received conventional care combined with oral administration of low-dose tadalafil (5 mg per time, once daily). Zhou Tian Fuyang moxibustion group received Zhou Tian Fuyang moxibustion therapy once weekly in addition to the treatment given to the control group. The treatment courses for both groups were 4 weeks. Outcome measures including clinical efficacy, International Index of Erectile Function-5 (IIEF-5) score, Erectile Dysfunction Inventory of Treatment Satisfaction score, Traditional Chinese Medicine syndrome score, and hemodynamic parameters of the penile cavernous body were recorded. Results The total clinical effective rate in the Zhou Tian Fuyang moxibustion group was 89.20%, which was significantly higher than that (66.67%) in the control group. After treatment, the IIEF-5 score and Erectile Dysfunction Inventory of Treatment Satisfaction scores increased, and the Traditional Chinese Medicine syndrome scores decreased in both of two groups (all P<0.05). The improvements in all scores were greater in the Zhou Tian Fuyang moxibustion group compared to the control group (P < 0.05). Regarding hemodynamics, the patients receiving the treatment of Zhou Tian Fuyang moxibustion showed better improvement compared to the patients in control group in terms of the peak systolic velocity, resistance index of the penile cavernosal artery and decreasing the end-diastolic velocity (all P < 0.05). Conclusion Zhou Tian Fuyang moxibustion can effectively improve penile vascular function in patients with erectile dysfunction of the kidney-yang deficiency pattern, thereby effectively enhancing erectile function and treatment satisfaction, alleviating Traditional Chinese Medicine clinical symptoms, and demonstrating significant overall therapeutic efficacy.

Article.ArticleTitle: Dirozalkib versus Crizotinib in Advanced Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase Inhibitor-Naïve ALK-Positive Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer: A Multicenter, Randomized Phase III Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Background: Dirozalkib is a highly selective anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) inhibitor with intracranial antitumor activity against crizotinib-resistant mutations. This phase III trial evaluated dirozalkib versus crizotinib in patients with ALK inhibitor-naïve, ALK-positive, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Methods: In this multicenter, randomized, open-label DIAMOND-2 trial, adult patients with ALK inhibitor-naïve, ALK-positive, advanced NSCLC who either had received no prior systemic therapy or had experienced disease progression or intolerance after one prior chemotherapy regimen were randomly assigned 1:1 to dirozalkib (500 mg once daily) or crizotinib (250 mg twice daily). The primary end point was investigator-assessed progression-free survival (PFS). Results: Between 2022 January 24 and 2023 April 30, 275 patients were randomly assigned to receive dirozalkib (n = 137) or crizotinib (n = 138). As of 2025 May 31, the median follow-up durations were 32.8 and 31.6 months, respectively. Median investigator-assessed PFS was 29.5 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 20.3 to not reached) months with dirozalkib versus 12.9 (95% CI = 11.1 to 17.6) months with crizotinib (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.47, 95% CI = 0.34 to 0.66; P < 0.001). Blinded-independent-central-review-assessed PFS was also significantly prolonged with dirozalkib (median PFS, 27.5 versus 12.9 months; HR = 0.54, 95% CI = 0.39 to 0.74; P < 0.001). Grade ≥3 treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were less frequent with dirozalkib than with crizotinib (60.6% versus 72.5%), and TEAEs led to treatment discontinuation in 2.2% and 7.2% of patients, respectively. Conclusions: Dirozalkib significantly improved PFS versus crizotinib, with a manageable safety profile, supporting its use as a first-line therapy for ALK-positive advanced NSCLC. Trial registration: This trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov on 2022 January 24 (NCT05204628).

Article.ArticleTitle: Adjunctive Multisensory Passive Immersive Virtual Reality With Synchronized Plantar Tactile Stimulation for Gait and Balance Disorders in Parkinson's Disease: An Exploratory Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Postural-locomotor disorders, particularly freezing of gait and postural instability, are among the most disabling symptoms of advanced Parkinson's disease (PD) and respond only partially to dopaminergic therapy. Evidence for virtual reality (VR) approaches in moderate to severe PD remains limited. This prospective randomized controlled open-label exploratory trial evaluated the addition of multisensory passive immersive VR with synchronized plantar tactile stimulation to conventional rehabilitation for gait, balance, and freezing disorders in moderate-to-severe PD (Hoehn and Yahr Stages 2-4). In the study, 80 PD patients were randomized into an experimental group (EXP, n = 40) receiving standard pharmacotherapy and conventional rehabilitation plus 10 sessions of passive immersive VR with synchronized plantar tactile stimulation and a comparison group (COM, n = 40) receiving standard pharmacotherapy and conventional rehabilitation only. Because the VR sessions were added to an otherwise identical program, the trial evaluates the effect of adding this intervention rather than a VR- or tactile-specific effect. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and after 10 days using the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS), Berg Balance Scale (BBS), and Freezing of Gait Questionnaire (FoG-Q). The EXP group showed significant improvements in the UPDRS "Gait" cluster (an eight-item composite of UPDRS items 2.11, 2.12, 2.13, 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13, range 0-32; median from 12.5 to 8.0 points, p < 0.001), BBS (from 38.0 to 43.5 points, p < 0.001), and FoG-Q (from 9.0 to 6.5 points, p < 0.001). A formal group × time analysis confirmed a differential treatment effect for every outcome. For the main outcome, the UPDRS "Gait" cluster, the baseline-adjusted between-group difference was -2.48 points (95% CI -3.37 to -1.59; p < 0.001; Hedges' g = 1.16). Large effects also favored the EXP group for the FoG-Q (-2.14 points, 95% CI -2.62 to -1.66; g = 1.65), the BBS (+2.20 points, 95% CI 1.31 to 3.10; g = 1.06), the UPDRS freezing subscore (items 2.13 + 3.11; -0.89 points, 95% CI -1.13 to -0.66; g = 1.32), and the UPDRS postural subscore (items 3.12 + 3.13; -0.74 points, 95% CI -1.08 to -0.41; g = 0.93). Secondary outcome p-values were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Holm and Benjamini-Hochberg procedures. By contrast, in the COM group, no significant change was observed for freezing of gait (p = 0.083), and improvements in other outcomes were smaller than in the EXP group. No serious adverse events were recorded. The trial was exploratory, so the effect estimates require confirmation rather than supporting robustness in themselves. Overall, multisensory passive immersive VR with synchronized plantar tactile stimulation was well tolerated and shows preliminary promise as an adjunct to conventional rehabilitation for gait and balance disorders in moderate-to-severe PD. Wider clinical implementation requires long-term multicenter studies with standardized assessment criteria and analysis of long-term sustainability. These findings support integrating passive VR technologies into personalized neurorehabilitation programs.

Journal.Title: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research

Article.ArticleTitle: Impact of early versus delayed mobilization after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair in small and medium-sized tears: a prospective randomized study.

Abstract.AbstractText: To compare early versus delayed mobilization following arthroscopic single-row knotless rotator cuff repair for small and medium-sized tears, performed in the beach-chair position without the use of an abduction sling.

A prospective randomized study was conducted on 70 patients aged 20-70 years with small and medium-sized full-thickness supraspinatus tears repaired using single-row knotless suture anchors (one or two depending on tear size). Patients were assigned to early mobilization (EPM, n = 35) or delayed mobilization (DPM, n = 35). Outcomes were assessed using range of motion (ROM), pain (VAS), Constant-Murley and UCLA scores, and MRI tendon integrity at 12 months.

EPM patients showed faster ROM recovery at 3 months (mean 130° vs. 115°; p = 0.02), but one re-tear (2.8%) occurred in this group compared to DPM, where no re-tears occurred. At 12 months, both groups achieved comparable functional and pain outcomes.

Early mobilization accelerates short-term ROM recovery, whereas both early and delayed protocols result in comparable functional and pain outcomes by 12 months. Given the limited number of retear events and the absence of a prespecified tear size subgroup analysis, no definitive recommendation can be made regarding a differential mobilization strategy according to tear size.

Article.ArticleTitle: Comparison of salivary fluoride levels following the application of rice-based and commercial fluoride gels: a randomized crossover trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Salivary fluoride concentration is commonly used as an indicator of short-term fluoride exposure and clearance following topical fluoride application. Rice-based fluoride gels, formulated as rice-starch-HEC hybrid gels, may serve as alternative delivery systems; however, data regarding their salivary fluoride retention compared with standard commercial formulations remain limited. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the salivary fluoride retention of two novel fluoride rice-based gels in comparison with a commercial acidulated phosphate fluoride (APF) gel following professional application using a tray delivery method.

A randomized, single-blind (participants), three-period crossover clinical trial was conducted in 32 healthy participants aged 18-30 years. Each participant received three different fluoride gel applications in a randomized sequence: a commercial APF gel (control), a fluoride non-glutinous rice-based gel, and a fluoride glutinous rice-based gel, with a 7-day washout period between treatments. Unstimulated saliva samples were collected at baseline and at 0, 5, 10, 20, 30, 45, and 60 min post-application. Fluoride concentration was measured using an ion-selective electrode. The area under the curve (AUC) and fluoride half-life (t½) were calculated to assess fluoride bioavailability and clearance rates.

All three fluoride gel formulations produced an immediate increase in salivary fluoride concentration, with mean concentrations at 0 min ranging from 345.99 to 404.53 ppm, followed by a rapid decline over time. Salivary fluoride concentrations changed significantly over time (p < 0.001), whereas no significant overall effect of gel formulation, gel-by-time interaction, sequence effect, or period effect was observed. AUC values did not differ significantly among the three formulations. At 60 min, mean salivary fluoride concentrations ranged from 4.94 to 5.62 ppm. The k and t½ also showed no statistically significant differences among formulations.

The two rice-based APF gels showed short-term salivary fluoride concentration-time profiles, AUC values, and fluoride clearance parameters (k and t½) that did not differ significantly from those of the commercial fluoride gel. Salivary fluoride concentrations remained above the reference threshold for at least 60 min. However, further studies are needed to evaluate enamel fluoride uptake, CaF₂-like reservoir formation, acid resistance, and clinical anticaries efficacy.

This study was registered in the Thai Clinical Trials Registry (TCTR; registration number TCTR20240707002) on 7 July 2024. The full registration details are available at: https://www.thaiclinicaltrials.org/show/TCTR20240707002 .

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of sodium hypochlorite concentrations and irrigant activation on postoperative pain after single-visit root canal treatment in asymptomatic molars with chronic apical periodontitis: a randomized clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: This randomized, single-blind clinical trial evaluated whether sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) concentration and irrigant activation influence postoperative pain after single-visit root canal treatment in molars with chronic apical periodontitis.

One hundred twenty asymptomatic patients were randomly allocated to six groups (n = 20) in a 2 × 3 factorial design (NaOCl concentration: 2.5% vs. 5.25% and nonactivation [NA], EDDY [VDW; Munich, Germany], or passive ultrasonic irrigation [PUI]). Postoperative pain was recorded using a 10-cm visual analog scale (VAS) at 6, 12, 24, 48, and 72 h. Repeated VAS measurements were analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model with an autoregressive AR (1) covariance structure, including fixed effects for concentration, activation, time, prespecified interactions, and age as covariates; prespecified simple effects at 6 h were examined with Bonferroni adjustment.

VAS scores decreased significantly over the course of postoperative assessments in all groups (time effect, P < .001). In the overall model, the activation technique had a significant effect on postoperative pain (P = .011), whereas the NaOCl concentration did not (P = .529). Significant concentration × activation (P = .037) and activation × time (P < .001) interactions were also observed. At 6 h, the only pairwise difference that remained significant after Bonferroni adjustment was between NA and PUI (mean difference 1.546; P < .001), whereas the comparisons between NA and EDDY and between EDDY and PUI were not statistically significant. Analgesic intake (18.3%) was analyzed as a secondary outcome using patient-level logistic regression. The NaOCl concentration was not associated with analgesic intake (P = .972). In contrast, compared with those in the PUI group, participants in the EDDY group had significantly greater odds of analgesic intake than those in the PUI group (OR = 4.022; P = .036).

Overall, under this clinical protocol, the activation modality appeared to have a greater influence on early postoperative pain than the NaOCl concentration alone did. However, postoperative pain scores remained generally low across all groups, suggesting that the clinical significance of these differences should be interpreted with caution.
Current controlled trials NCT07033247 registered on 13 June 2025. Retrospectively registered.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of gluma® on the oral health-related quality of life in patients with dentine hypersensitivity: a triple-blind, randomized, controlled clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of Gluma® treatment on the oral health-related quality of life of patients with dentine hypersensitivity (DH).

Adult participants with DH in more than one tooth were included. They were randomized into two groups: Gluma® or control (saline solution). Block randomization was performed by computer and remained electronically hidden until the time of treatment. Gluma® was applied to the dried and clean cervical area of the tooth with DH and maintained for 3 min; afterward, the material was removed. The control followed the same application protocol. To assess oral health-related quality of life, all participants completed the DHEQ-15 questionnaire at baseline and 30 days post-treatment. DH was assessed using tactile and air-jet tests at baseline and 30 days post-treatment, using a numerical pain scale. Data were subjected to the Wilcoxon, Mann-Whitney, and X2 tests and Spearman's correlation. The significance level was set at p < 0.05.

The sample consisted of 147 (77.8%) women and 42 (22.2%) men, with a mean age of 31 years. There was a significant reduction in pain level (p < 0.001) and in DHEQ-15 scores (p < 0.001) after treatment with Gluma®. In the placebo group, there was no significant difference in pain level (p > 0.05) or in the DHEQ-15 score (p > 0.05). There was a moderate positive correlation between the DHEQ-15 domains and the level of pain measured by tactile stimulation and air-jet in both groups.
The desensitizing agent Gluma® can improve oral health-related quality of life.

This study was prospectively registered on the Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (ReBEC) platform, under the identifier RBR-9fmjf77 ( https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-9fmjf77 ), prior to participant recruitment. Date of registration: March 31, 2024.

Article.ArticleTitle: Assessing the psychometric properties of the Symptom Checklist Five-Items (SCL-5) instrument in a clinical setting for treating intimate partner violence.

Abstract.AbstractText: Research suggests that the Symptom Checklist Five Items (SCL-5) instrument is a reliable and valid scale for assessing mental health in a range of populations. Yet, to date, the SCL-5 has not been validated in a population of perpetrators of intimate partner violence (IPV) and their partners. Hence, the current study aimed to examine the psychometric properties of the SCL-5 within a clinical IPV context characterized by elevated mental health symptoms.

This validation study is part of a randomised controlled trial evaluating a group intervention for men voluntarily seeking treatment for IPV in Norway. The study was conducted in accordance with the guidelines Consensus-based standards for the selection of health measurement instruments (COSMIN). We evaluated floor and ceiling effects, internal consistency and estimated the area under the curve to determine optimal diagnostic sensitivity and specificity. Additionally, we explored scale responsiveness using data from a subsample of participants.

The highest percentage of respondents with the lowest possible score (value 1) across the 5 items was 8.7%, indicating no floor effect assuming the 15% criterion. The highest percentage with the highest possible score (value 4) across the 5 items was 1.9%, indicating no ceiling effect either. Cronbach's alpha was 0.86 for the total sample (N = 161), 0.83 for perpetrators only (n = 118) and 0.89 for partners only (n = 44). The area under the curve was 94.6% (95% CI 0.913-0.978) for the total sample, 93.5% (95% CI 0.893-0.977) for the perpetrators and 96.9% (95% CI 0.922-1.017) for the victims. Regarding responsiveness, we set a criterion of a statistically significant reduction in mean scores over time as a test of the adequate responsiveness of the SCL-5 from the baseline to the one-year follow-up point. As predicted, it fell from 1.98 to 1.74 and the mean change was significant (t -4.021, CI -0.360 to -0.121; p < 0.001). The mean total SCL-5 score decreased in 54% of cases (n = 43).
The results provide evidence that the SCL-5 has adequate psychometric properties in a Norwegian sample of perpetrators and victims of IPV.
Not applicable.

Article.ArticleTitle: Early clinical outcomes and learning curve study of robot-assisted precision osteotomy in total knee arthroplasty in the context of enhanced recovery after surgery.

Abstract.AbstractText: To compare the early clinical outcomes of robot-assisted total knee arthroplasty (RA-TKA) with those of conventional manual total knee arthroplasty (CM-TKA) and analyse their learning curves.

Patients who underwent initial unilateral total knee arthroplasty for osteoarthritis of the knee at Panzhihua Central Hospital between June and November 2023 were included in the study. A total of 130 patients were randomly divided into two groups: RA-TKA group underwent total knee arthroplasty with the HURWA Orthopaedic System (65 patients), and CM-TKA group patients underwent surgery with conventional tools (65 patients). Basic data, surgical information, imaging data and postoperative functional data were compared between the two groups. Surgical time was analysed via the cumulative sum analysis method (CUSUM), and the goodness of fit was assessed via R².

The baseline data were consistent between the two groups; moreover, the FFC of the patients in RA-TKA group was closer to 90° than that in CM-TKA group (89.1 ± 1.0° vs. 87.6 ± 1.9°, respectively; P < 0.001), the LTC was concentrated at 87° (86.8 ± 0.9° vs. 85.9 ± 2.3°, respectively; P = 0.006), and the HKA was concentrated at 180° (179.1 ± 1.0 vs. 176.7 ± 1.7, P < 0.001). There was no significant difference observed in inflammatory indicators or perioperative blood loss. Overall, 7.80% (RA-TKA group) and 9.52% (CM-TKA group) of the patients developed lower extremity intermuscular venous thrombosis, but there was no difference in knee function, pain or satisfaction. The operation time of RA-TKA group was approximately 11.3 min longer than that of CM-TKA group. The learning curve was best fitted as a cubic curve, and the fitted curve reached its apex when the number of surgical cases increased to 22. During the entire learning curve, no surgical termination or accidental injury caused by the failure of the robotic system occurred, and none of the patients suffered from serious complications such as infections, periprosthetic fracture, or cardiac and cerebral vascular accidents.

HURWA robot-assisted TKA with learning curve fixation in approximately 22 patients achieved good lower limb force line reconstruction and precise implantation of the prosthesis, which is a safe and effective surgical procedure for treating osteoarthritis of the knee.
The study was retrospectively registered on China Clinical Trials Registry (identifcation number: ChiCTR2400086729) on 07/09/2024. https://www.chictr.org.cn/bin/project/edit?pid=201488 .

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of a wearable-assisted walking program on longitudinal trajectories of cognitive function and loneliness in older adults: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Cognitive decline and loneliness are important challenges in later life. Although walking-based interventions may support cognitive and psychosocial health, less is known about how these outcomes change over time or whether baseline physical capacity explains individual differences in their trajectories. This study examined the parallel growth trajectories of cognitive function and loneliness during a 12-week wearable-assisted walking intervention and evaluated whether baseline muscle health and functional mobility were associated with these changes.

A 12-week, two-arm randomized controlled trial was conducted with 120 community-dwelling older adults. Participants were randomly assigned to a wearable-assisted walking group (n = 60) or a control group without structured walking intervention (n = 60). Cognitive function, assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment, and loneliness, assessed using the 8-item UCLA Loneliness Scale, were measured at baseline, week 4, week 8, and week 12. Baseline appendicular skeletal muscle mass index and timed up-and-go performance were selected a priori as physical predictors. Data were analyzed using conditional parallel-process latent growth curve modeling adjusted for age and education.

Compared with the control group, the wearable-assisted walking intervention was associated with a significantly steeper increase in cognitive function (slope estimate = 0.39, p < .001) and a significantly steeper decrease in loneliness (slope estimate = - 1.28, p < .001). The covariance between cognitive and loneliness slopes was not statistically significant, suggesting partially distinct longitudinal trajectories. Poorer baseline functional mobility was associated with higher initial loneliness (intercept estimate = 0.55, p = .001). Lower baseline appendicular skeletal muscle mass index was associated with a greater reduction in loneliness over time (slope estimate = 0.52, p = .010).

A 12-week wearable-assisted walking intervention was associated with more favorable longitudinal trajectories of cognitive function and loneliness than the control condition among community-dwelling older adults. Baseline functional mobility was associated with initial loneliness, whereas lower appendicular muscle mass was associated with greater psychosocial improvement. Wearable-assisted walking may represent an accessible strategy for promoting cognitive and psychological well-being in older adults.

Article.ArticleTitle: Comparison of modified thoracoabdominal nerve block via perichondrial approach with serratus intercostal plane block and rectus sheath block combination in laparoscopic cholecystectomy: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Patients undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) may experience severe postoperative pain. Peripheral nerve blocks, as a component of multimodal analgesia, are now widely employed in postoperative pain management. This study investigated the effects of modified thoracoabdominal nerve block (M-TAPA) compared with the combination of rectus sheath block (RSB) and serratus intercostal plane block (SIPB) on postoperative NRS scores, tramadol consumption, and dermatomal spread.

This randomized, assessor-blinded trial enrolled 72 patients scheduled for LC. One group received bilateral M-TAPA (Group 1, n = 35), while the other received a combination of bilateral RSB and right-sided SIPB (Group 2, n = 37). All peripheral nerve blocks were performed following surgery and prior to emergence from general anesthesia, using 0.25% bupivacaine; RSB was administered as 10 mL per side, M-TAPA as 20 mL per side, and SIPB as 20 mL on the right side. The primary outcome was postoperative tramadol consumption within the first 24 h; NRS scores, rescue analgesia requirement, and dermatomal spread were secondary outcomes.

Static NRS (Numeric Rating Scale) scores measured at 0, 1, and 6 h differed significantly between groups (mean difference [Group 2 - Group 1] 1.27 [95% CI 0.54-2.00], 0.69 [0.14-1.24], and 0.56 [0.12-1.00], respectively). Dynamic NRS scores assessed at 0, 12, and 18 h were also found to be statistically significant between groups (mean difference 1.06 [95% CI 0.25-1.87], 0.45 [0.05-0.85], and 0.52 [0.05-0.99], respectively). Total tramadol consumption over the first 24 h, the primary outcome, did not differ significantly between groups (92.6 ± 26.3 mg vs. 103.9 ± 39.3 mg; mean difference 11.3 mg, 95% CI - 4.4 to 26.9; p = 0.108); however, tramadol consumption between 12 and 24 h was significantly higher in Group 2 compared to Group 1 (24.0 ± 11.7 mg vs. 31.7 ± 17.3 mg; mean difference 7.6 mg, 95% CI 0.7 to 14.6; p = 0.030). The number of patients requiring rescue analgesia was also significantly greater in Group 2 than in Group 1 (absolute risk reduction 24.4%, 95% CI 2.5% to 46.3%; p = 0.034).

Both M-TAPA and the combination of RSB with SIPB provided effective postoperative analgesia following LC. Under the conditions of this trial, M-TAPA was associated with lower NRS scores and lower opioid requirements than the combination of bilateral RSB and unilateral SIPB.
The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06241794, registered on January 28, 2024.
