Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of orofacial myofunctional therapy with auto-monitoring on the apnea-hypopnea index in patients with mild-to-moderate obstructive sleep apnea: a multicenter randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Orofacial myofunctional therapy (OMT) is a promising treatment for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but protocols vary and outcomes are inconsistent. The primary aim was to evaluate the effect of a standardized OMT protocol on changes in apnea-hypopnea index (AHI). Secondary aims were to analyze associations between OMT adherence and change in objective and self-reported outcomes.

Treatment-naive adults with mild-to-moderate OSA were randomized in a multicenter trial to 12 weeks of OMT or a waitlist control group. Three nights of polysomnography were completed before and after the intervention. Adherence was registered electronically. The primary outcome was change in AHI. Pre-defined secondary outcomes were changes in desaturation measures and in the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) score. Intention-to-treat analyses were performed using linear mixed-effects models, whereas per-protocol analyses were based on analysis of covariance.

A total of 104 participants (mean age 47.1 ± 12.2 years) were included. Intention-to-treat analysis included 104 participants (52 treatment, 52 waitlist) and showed no significant effect of OMT on AHI. Difference in AHI change between groups was 0.6 (95% CI -3.3 to 4.5; P = .774). Overall mean adherence across all days and participants was 64.6% (95% CI 61.0 to 76.8). Higher adherence was not associated with significantly greater reduction in AHI (β = -0.1, 95% CI -0.2 to 0.1; P = .353). No change was detected in pre-defined secondary outcomes.
Twelve weeks of standardized OMT had no significant effect on AHI, desaturation measures or ESS score in treatment-naive patients newly diagnosed with OSA.

Orofacial myofunctional therapy (OMT) is increasingly considered a non-invasive treatment for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but existing evidence is heterogeneous and often limited by methodological shortcomings. We therefore conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effects of a standardized OMT protocol in adults newly diagnosed with mild-to-moderate OSA.

The intervention did not improve pre-defined OSA outcomes, highlighting the importance of rigorous trials even when results are negative. These findings help refine the evidence base for OMT in adults with OSA while supporting continued investigation of alternative protocols and populations stratified by endo- or phenotyping.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effectiveness of bitter almond (Amygdalus communis L. var. Amara) gum as a prebiotic on glycemic indices, oxidative stress, and antioxidant biomarkers in women with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a randomized, placebo-controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is marked by hyperglycemia, oxidative stress, and systemic inflammation. Prebiotics, such as bitter almond gum (Amygdalus communis L. var. amara), have the potential to influence gut microbiota and metabolic parameters, suggesting their role as dietary interventions for enhancing glycemic control in the management of T2DM. This study evaluated the effects of bitter almond gum on glycemic indices, oxidative stress, and oxidant biomarkers in individuals with T2DM.

This randomized, triple-blinded, placebo-controlled, clinical trial included 44 women with T2DM. They were assigned to either the intervention (n = 22) or control (n = 22) groups receiving 5 g per day of bitter almond gum or maltodextrin, respectively, for a duration of 8 weeks. Various outcomes, including glycemic indices, lipopolysaccharide (LPS) levels, oxidative stress markers, and antioxidant biomarkers, were measured at baseline and again after 8 weeks.

Bitter almond gum supplementation significantly reduced insulin levels (-1.23 mg/dL; 95% CI, [-2.40, -0.03]), LPS ( - 6.32 mg/dL; 95% CI, [-9.51, -3.09]), pentosidine (-38.02 mg/dL; 95% CI, [-55.18, -20.71]), and oxidative stress index (OSI) (-5.59 mg/dL; 95% CI, [-10.81, -0.30]), and increased McAuley_index (0.20 mg/dL; 95% CI, [0.14, 0.32]), total antioxidant capacity (TAC) (0.18 mg/dL; 95% CI, [0.07, 0.26]), superoxide dismutase (SOD) (180.20 mg/dL; 95% CI, [65.27, 295.14]), and glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px) (2.21 mg/dL; 95% CI, [0.78, 3.62]) compared with the placebo group (P < 0.05, ANCOVA adjusted for baseline and confounding factors).

Bitter almond gum supplementation for 8 weeks led to improvements in glycemic control, a reduction in oxidative stress, and an enhancement of antioxidant defenses in women with T2DM. These findings indicate its potential as a complementary functional food for managing diabetes.

Article.ArticleTitle: Cost-effectiveness of a digital parenting intervention for reducing violence and related health burden among adolescents in Tanzania.

Abstract.AbstractText: Violence against children is a major global public health concern associated with substantial physical and mental health burden across the life course. Parenting interventions are effective in preventing violence against children, yet evidence on their cost-effectiveness, particularly for digitally delivered programmes in low-resource settings, remains limited. We evaluated the cost-effectiveness of a blended-digital parenting intervention in Tanzania.

We conducted cost-effectiveness and cost-benefit analyses alongside a cluster-randomised controlled trial of ParentApp for Teens delivered to caregivers and adolescents aged 10-17 years. Trial outcomes were combined with programme cost data to estimate delivery costs at scale. Cost-effectiveness ratios (CERs) were calculated as cost per incident averted using incidence risk ratios from 14-month follow-up data. A discounted CER approach proportionally allocated intervention costs across multiple outcomes. Cost-benefit analysis compared prevention costs with immediate public-sector labour costs associated with formal case response.

The intervention achieved significant reductions in multiple violence outcomes, including adolescent sexual violence victimisation, child maltreatment, and caregiver intimate partner violence-forms of violence associated with substantial health consequences. Using observed RCT implementation expenditure of US$69.02 per enrolled dyad, estimated costs per incident averted were US$30.83 for adolescent sexual violence, US$5.43 for child maltreatment and US$12.03 for caregiver IPV. Under a prospective routine-delivery scenario of just under US$6 per dyad at n = 10,000, corresponding CERs were US$2.67, US$0.47 and US$1.04, respectively. At scale, routine delivery was estimated at approximately US$6 per caregiver-adolescent dyad, compared with an estimated US$121.10 in immediate labour costs for a reported case entering formal response.

ParentApp is a cost-effective preventive intervention with potential to reduce violence-related health burden at scale. Blended-digital parenting programmes can reduce violence against children at low cost and may generate short-term public-sector savings where prevented cases would otherwise require formal response.

Article.ArticleTitle: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy to Optimize Post-Operative Fracture Recovery (COPE): a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Persistent pain after extremity fracture requiring surgical repair is common and associated with long-term morbidity. We sought to determine whether app-based cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) reduces persistent postsurgical pain after fracture repair.

We performed a randomized controlled trial of adults from 11 American and Canadian hospitals with an extremity fracture treated with internal fixation. We allocated participants 1:1 to an app-based CBT program or usual care, and followed them at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months post-fracture. Our primary outcome was moderate-to-severe persistent post-surgical pain. We constructed a mixed-effects log-binomial model to explore the effect of CBT versus usual care on moderate-to-severe persistent post-surgical pain over 12 months postfracture.

We randomized 1009 participants to app-based CBT (n = 506) or usual care (n = 503). The mean age of participants was 44.5 years, and 129 (12.8%) presented with an open fracture. Adherence to CBT was modest, with 237/506 patients (46.8%) completing all 7 modules. App-based CBT, compared with usual care, did not reduce the risk of persistent postsurgical pain over 12 months postfracture (30.8% v. 30.3%, adjusted relative risk 1.02, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.89 to 1.16). The 365-day probability of returning to leisure activities without restrictions was 29.0% in the intervention group and 22.4% in the control group (hazard ratio 1.33, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.77). The other secondary outcomes showed no significant differences between treatments.

Among adults with an operatively managed extremity fracture, app-based CBT did not reduce the risk of persistent postsurgical pain over 12 months. Future research is warranted to develop more effective CBT approaches for adults with extremity fractures and to evaluate alternative supportive interventions that may be more acceptable to patients with fracture.

Article.ArticleTitle: Comparison of physiological responses and experiences between sitting semi-recumbent in bed and sitting in a chair - A randomised, crossover clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: ObjectiveEarly mobilisation of patients in intensive care is considered feasible and beneficial. However, the safety and effects of different mobilisation interventions require further research. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate and compare patient experiences and physiological responses between sitting semi-recumbent in bed and sitting in a chair.MethodsA pragmatic, randomised, clinical crossover trial was conducted as a single-day intervention. Forty-seven consecutively included patients (men/women: 34/13; mean age (SD): 70.4 (12.5)) in intensive care were randomised to begin the intervention either sitting semi-recumbent in bed or in a chair. Each treatment period lasted 40 minutes, with a minimum washout period of two hours between sessions. The haemodynamic and respiratory variables used to assess mobilisation readiness or suspension, were collected, as well as self-rated variables of pain, exertion and satisfaction.ResultsPhysiological responses to sitting were comparable between the two positions. Estimated treatment effects were small for both primary outcomes (mean arterial pressure: 0.7 mmHg, 95% CI -5.5 to 6.9, p = 0.822; PaO2/FiO2: -3.3, 95% CI -51.2 to 44.6, p = 0.890), with the confidence intervals suggesting no clinically meaningful differences between the interventions. Oxygen saturation tended to be lower in the semi-recumbent position. The self-rated variables indicated that pain increased (p=0.028) and satisfaction decreased (p=0.044) in the semi-recumbent position, while exertion was non-significant in both positions (bed: p=0.169; chair: p=0.913). No adverse events were noted.ConclusionSitting in a chair was safe and exerted similar physiological demands on the patient as the semi-recumbent position in bed. However, in the semi-recumbent position, pain increased over time, satisfaction decreased, and a trend toward decreased saturation was also observed. The findings support considering mobilisation to a chair when clinically appropriate, while taking precautions to avoid falls and other adverse events.

Article.ArticleTitle: Radiographic evaluation of the impact of hyaluronic acid and bone graft on peri-implant tissue: A randomized clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Aim: The objective of this randomized clinical trial was to enhance the effect of HY alone or in combination with a bone graft in changing peri-implant tissue dimensions radiographically.

Materials and Methods: Thirty-six patients who required posterior dental implants were randomly assigned to three groups (n=12 each): a control group (CONT) with conventional implant placement was performed, one group treated with HA (HY), and another test group treated with HA and bone graft together (HYB). The same surgical procedure was performed for all implants in the posterior regions of jawbones. Measurements were taken before surgery, after surgery, and at eight and sixteen weeks after surgery.

Results: Hybrid group (HYB) had a significantly greater increase radiographic soft tissue thickness at all-time points (P < 0.001). The HYB group had higher radiographic bone height at week 16 and stability of bone width (P = 0.088) than the other groups (P < 0.001).
Conclusion: The combined application of a bone graft and hyaluronic acid (HYB) significantly improves the radiographic soft tissue thickness and bone height.

Journal.Title: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of Remote Ischemic Conditioning on Cerebral Blood Flow Regulation in Atherosclerosis: A Randomized Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Impaired dynamic cerebral autoregulation (dCA) contributes to cerebral perfusion instability in patients with cerebrovascular atherosclerosis. Remote ischemic conditioning (RIC) has shown neuroprotective potential; however, its acute effects on dCA in this population remain unclear. In this randomized, sham-controlled trial, patients with intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ICAS) and/or extracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ECAS) received a single session of RIC or sham-RIC. dCA was assessed at baseline and at 0-1, 6-9, and 24 h using transfer function analysis. The prespecified primary endpoint was the affected-side phase difference (PD) at 6-9 h. Of the 140 randomized participants, 132 with valid primary endpoint data were included in the primary analysis. For the primary outcome, the affected-side PD at 6-9 h was significantly greater in the RIC group than in the sham-RIC group (adjusted β = 12.166, 95% CI: 6.787-17.545; p < 0.001). Secondary analyses at other time points and of the unaffected side supported an acute physiological effect of RIC on dCA. These findings suggest that a single RIC session may rapidly improve impaired dCA in patients with ICAS and/or ECAS. Larger studies are needed to determine whether this response varies across clinical presentations and vascular territories.

Article.ArticleTitle: Changes in self-related cognitive processes and depressive symptom severity following a single, moderate dose of psilocybin in depressed patients.

Abstract.AbstractText: Psychedelic-assisted therapy, particularly with psilocybin, is increasingly proposed as a treatment for major depressive disorder, yet the neural and psychological mechanisms underlying its effects remain under investigation. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial, individuals diagnosed with major depressive disorder received a single, moderate dose of psilocybin (0.215 mg kg-1) or placebo, with the same psychological support. We analysed N = 37 individuals with major depressive disorder undergoing assessments of depressive symptoms (Beck's depression inventory and Montgomery-Åsberg depression rating scale), self-concept (Frankfurt self-concept scale) and neural markers of self-referential processing using an fMRI-based task. Compared with placebo, the psilocybin group exhibited significant reductions in depressive symptoms and a significant increase in positive self-concept two weeks after substance administration. Changes in self-concept were significantly correlated with decreased depressive scores. Neuroimaging revealed psilocybin-associated modulation of caudate activation during externally oriented attention after two weeks, contrasting with placebo-induced caudate changes during self-referential processing. These findings extend prior evidence linking psychedelics to changes in self-referential processing and self-concept and demonstrate that such changes occur concurrently with reductions in depressive symptoms. Future research should aim to replicate and extend these results and refine therapy protocols targeting self-processing and self-concept in psychedelic-assisted therapy in major depressive disorder. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue 'From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self'.

Article.ArticleTitle: Inhaled Corticosteroids and Sickle Cell Disease Severity in Adults Without Asthma: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: People living with sickle cell disease (SCD) who have episodic cough and wheeze (ECW) without a diagnosis of asthma have high rates of pain episodes and acute chest syndrome. A previous trial, in which patients with SCD and ECW without asthma received 15 weeks of inhaled mometasone or placebo, showed that inhaled mometasone improved daily pain and reduced soluble vascular cell adhesion molecule 1 (VCAM-1), a marker of disease severity in SCD.
To examine the biologic effects and safety of long-term daily inhaled mometasone in patients without asthma but with SCD and ECW.

This placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial recruited patients with SCD from December 2018 to May 2022. Participants were randomly assigned to receive either inhaled mometasone or placebo for 48 weeks. Data analyses followed the modified intention-to-treat principle and were performed between July and November 2023.
The inhaled mometasone group received 220 μg of inhaled mometasone furoate dry powder once daily. The placebo group received a matching placebo inhaler.

The primary outcome was percentage change in soluble VCAM-1 levels from baseline to end of study. Secondary outcomes included laboratory results, functional outcomes, patient-reported outcomes, and health care utilization.

Of the 77 patients who received the intervention and were included in the analysis, 40 were assigned to inhaled mometasone (mean [SD] age, 36.0 [11.6] years; 26 females [65%]) and 37 were assigned to placebo (mean [SD] age, 31.5 [8.6] years; 19 males [51%]). Compared with the placebo group, the inhaled mometasone group increased their soluble VCAM-1 levels by 42% (95% CI, -11% to 96%; P = .02). Point estimates for clinical outcomes favored the placebo group, although the findings were not statistically significant.

In this trial of adults with SCD and ECW, extended courses of inhaled mometasone were associated with worsened markers of disease severity. Inhaled mometasone should not be used long-term in patients with SCD and ECW without a definitive diagnosis of asthma.

Article.ArticleTitle: The effect of listening to Qur'an on quality of life and sleep quality in breast cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: To investigate the effect of listening to Qur'an on quality of life and sleep quality in women undergoing chemotherapy for breast cancer. This randomized controlled trial used an open-label design at the participant level, with blinded statistical analysis. Participants were assigned using block randomization to either a Qur'an listening group (QLG) or a control group (CG). During each chemotherapy session, the QLG listened through headphones to a standardized recording of Surah Yasin played on a music player and repeated until the chemotherapy session was completed. The intervention was administered once every 21 days for a total of four sessions, while the CG received standard care only. Data were collected at four time points (T1-T4) using a Breast Cancer Patient Information Form, the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Core 30 (EORTC QLQ-C30), Version 3.0, and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Analyses were performed using SPSS 26. Significant Group × Time interactions were observed for several EORTC QLQ-C30 functional and symptom domains after adjustment for multiple comparisons. Global quality of life also showed a significant Group × Time interaction (p = 0.008), indicating different patterns of change between the QLG and CG across the four measurement points. Between-group differences in global quality of life were significant at T2 and T3. For sleep quality, the Group × Time interaction for PSQI total scores was significant after Holm correction (p < 0.001), and PSQI scores were significantly lower in the QLG than in the CG at T4 (p < 0.001). Qur'an listening during chemotherapy was associated with changes in patient-reported quality of life and sleep quality among women with breast cancer. Given the study limitations, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and require confirmation in larger randomized controlled trials.Trial registrationNCT06893770.

Article.ArticleTitle: Low-Dose CT Lung-RADS 2022 for the Management of Screening- and Non-Screening-detected Lung Cancer Associated with Cystic Airspaces.

Abstract.AbstractText: Background Lung cancer associated with cystic airspaces (CA) can be misinterpreted as a benign lesion, leading to missed or delayed diagnosis; however, the effect of the Lung Imaging Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) 2022 criteria remains unverified. Purpose To retrospectively determine the frequency and outcomes of lung cancer associated with CA during screening and explore the potential effect of Lung-RADS 2022 on earlier diagnosis. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis included participants with lung cancers from three trials: the National Lung Screening Trial (2002-2007); Italian Lung Cancer Screening Trial, or ITALUNG (2004-2010); and German Lung Cancer Screening Intervention trial, or LUSI (2007-2016). Two radiologists jointly reviewed low-dose CT images to identify and morphologically characterize lung cancer associated with CA. Associations with histologic features, stage, and other variables were assessed. Lung cancer-specific survival was analyzed using Fine-Gray regression accounting for the competing risk of non-lung cancer death. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, stage, detection status, and trial. Lung-RADS 2022 criteria for atypical pulmonary cysts were applied. Results Seventy-three cancers associated with CA were identified in 1258 participants (median age, 64 years [IQR, 61-69 years]; 43 male), including 44 of 716 (6.1%) screening-detected and 29 of 542 (5.4%) non-screening-detected cancers. Multilocular morphologic type was associated with a more advanced stage than unilocular morphologic type (12 of 24 vs 15 of 49; P = .02). The 5-year lung cancer-specific survival was 51.4% (95% CI: 39.3, 62.3) for cancers associated with CA and 53.2% (95% CI: 50.1, 56.2) for 1054 participants with noncystic non-small cell lung cancer. No evidence of a difference in survival was observed (subdistribution hazard ratio, 1.15 [95% CI: 0.81, 1.63]; P = .44), and results remained consistent in multivariable models. Lung-RADS 2022 might have enabled earlier diagnosis in 55 of 73 cancers associated with CA (75%). Conclusion Lung cancer associated with CA accounted for 6.1% of screening-detected and 5.4% of non-screening-detected lung cancers. Outcomes were similar to those of noncystic non-small cell lung cancer, and Lung-RADS 2022 may facilitate earlier diagnosis. Clinical trial registration nos. Article.ArticleTitle: Patient Engagement in a Virtual Cardiac Rehabilitation Platform: Secondary Analysis of the ERA-Nudge Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Mobile health interventions have the potential to motivate healthy behaviors. Optimal strategies for engaging patients in cardiac rehabilitation (CR) through mobile health interventions remain unclear.
This study aimed to examine patient engagement in a mobile app platform for CR across patient characteristics and by the method of delivery of nudge messages over the 12 weeks of CR.

The authors analyzed data from the ERA-Nudge (Enhancing Rehabilitation Adherence Through Optimized Nudge) study, a pragmatic randomized trial conducted at an urban safety-net hospital testing nudges (short messages designed using behavioral economics to elicit behavior change) to enhance CR adherence and log healthy activity. Trial patients were given access to a smartphone-based app. Nudges were initially sent as app notifications. Later in the study, patients received nudges as text messages. We assessed patient characteristics associated with app engagement, and we compared time spent in the CR app among patients receiving nudges as app notifications vs text messages. The trial enrolled patients who could engage with messages in either English or Spanish at an urban safety-net hospital with a qualifying CR diagnosis and a smartphone from May 2019 to May 2023. We describe minutes spent in the app across patient characteristics and by type of nudge delivery, and we compare the 2 approaches using unadjusted and multivariate negative binomial regression over the 12 weeks of CR.

In total, 223 patients received nudges: 74 via app notification and 149 via text message. Overall, patients spent an average of 219 (SD 328) minutes in the app, and 3 (1.3%) patients used the app for zero minutes. Patients receiving only app nudges spent a mean of 167 (SD 365) minutes in the app, and patients receiving text messages and app nudges spent 245 (SD 306) minutes in the app (unadjusted ratio 1.5, 95% CI 1.1-2.0; P=.02). After adjusting for age category, sex, primary language, CR location (hospital vs home), and highest education achieved, Spanish-preferring patients, patients with some college education, and patients receiving text messages spent more time in the app. Patients receiving nudges as text messages and app notifications spent an adjusted ratio of 1.8 (95% CI 1.2-2.5; P=.002) times as many minutes in the app compared to those getting nudges as app notifications.

Among an urban safety-net population, text message nudges were associated with greater time in the app compared to nudges delivered as app notifications. These findings suggest that text messages may result in greater patient engagement for mobile health interventions.

Article.ArticleTitle: The Effect of Shoulder Support on Shoulder Subluxation in Stroke Survivors Based on Ultrasonography Findings: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: This study evaluated the effectiveness of a standardized shoulder support in reducing shoulder subluxation, alleviating pain, and improving upper limb motor function and functional independence in stroke survivors using ultrasonography as the primary outcome measure for subluxation.

In this single-blind randomized controlled trial, 40 stroke survivors with clinically confirmed shoulder subluxation were randomly allocated to either an intervention group (n = 20) or a control group (n = 20). Both groups received conventional rehabilitation consisting of 45-min sessions, 5 days per week, over a seven-week period. Participants in the intervention group additionally wore a standardized shoulder support during waking hours. Outcome evaluations were performed at baseline (before the intervention), week 3 (mid-intervention), and week 7 (end of the intervention) by independent assessors (physicians and rehabilitation therapists) who were blinded to group allocation. The primary and secondary endpoints included ultrasonographic measurement of the Acromion-Greater Tuberosity (AGT) distance, pain intensity assessed by the visual analog scale (VAS), upper extremity motor performance measured with the Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA), and functional independence evaluated using the Functional Independence Measure (FIM).

Within-group analyses revealed statistically significant changes in shoulder subluxation (p = 0.02), pain reduction (p < 0.001), upper limb function (p < 0.05), and functional independence (p = 0.001) in both groups over time. However, between-group comparisons showed no significant differences in any of the outcome measures (p > 0.05).

Adding a standardized shoulder support to conventional rehabilitation did not produce a statistically significant additional benefit over 7 weeks in reducing shoulder subluxation, pain, or improving upper-limb motor function and functional independence. The observed changes over time should be interpreted in the context of rehabilitation received by both groups, spontaneous recovery, and other time-related factors cannot be distinguished.

Article.ArticleTitle: The clinical efficacy of a tailored exercise program on cardiopulmonary function and fatigue in patients with HER2-positive breast cancer undergoing trastuzumab treatment: a post-hoc analysis of the CARDAPAC study.

Abstract.AbstractText: Physical exercise is increasingly recognized as an effective non-pharmacological intervention to mitigate treatment-related adverse effects in cancer patients. However, evidence remains limited regarding the benefits of structured exercise programs in HER2-positive breast cancer patients treated exclusively with trastuzumab.
To investigate the impact of a 3-month supervised, tailored exercise program on fatigue and cardiorespiratory fitness in this population.
Phase II, randomized, prospective, multicenter trial.
Outpatient oncology centers.
Eighty-nine women with HER2-positive breast cancer receiving adjuvant trastuzumab.

Participants were randomly assigned to a training group (TG) undergoing 36 supervised intermittent aerobic exercise sessions (55 minutes/session, 3 days/week, combining moderate and high intensities) or to a control group (CG) receiving usual care. Cardiopulmonary exercise testing and fatigue assessments (MFI-20) were conducted at baseline (T0), 3 months (T3), and 6 months (T6) post-intervention.

At T3, TG showed clinically meaningful improvements in peak oxygen uptake (+2.6 mL/min/kg; 95% CI: 1.8-3.4), oxygen pulse (+0.7 mL/beat), and maximal power output (+21.3 W). Ventilatory thresholds (VT) occurred at higher workloads with reduced heart rate and respiratory rate at submaximal intensities, indicating improved aerobic efficiency. Scores for general fatigue, physical fatigue, and reduced activity significantly decreased, although these changes did not reach the minimal clinically important difference. Moderate negative correlations were observed between fatigue scores and V̇O<inf>2</inf> at VT<inf>1</inf> and V̇O<inf>2</inf> peak, suggesting that improved fitness may alleviate fatigue.

A tailored, supervised exercise program significantly enhances cardiorespiratory fitness and reduces fatigue symptoms in HER2-positive breast cancer patients treated with trastuzumab. Specifically, a clinically meaningful increase in peak V̇O<inf>2</inf>, maximal power output, and oxygen pulse was observed, along with significant reductions in general fatigue, physical fatigue, and reduced activity scores.

Incorporating supervised, individualized exercise into standard oncology care improves functional capacity and fatigue management, supporting its integration into rehabilitation programs for this population.

Article.ArticleTitle: Short-term safety and local tolerability of repeated exposure to aerosolized hypochlorous acid dry fog in healthy adults: a randomized controlled pilot study.

Abstract.AbstractText: Hypochlorous acid (HOCI) is an oxidizing chlorine-based compound with broad antimicrobial activity and potential application as a dry-fog disinfectant in healthcare environments. However, human safety data for repeated exposure to aerosolized HOCI remain limited. This study evaluated the short-term safety and local tolerability of aerosolized HOCI dry fog under controlled conditions.

This prospective, randomized, open-label pilot study included healthy adult volunteers aged 18-65 years. Participants were enrolled into two independent exposure cohorts and randomized 1:1 to aerosolized HOCI or aerosolized 0.9% sodium chloride. The investigational product was a 300-ppm HOCI solution dispersed as dry fog at 20 mL/m3. In the short repeated exposure cohort, participants underwent three 3-min exposures per day for 3 consecutive days. In the prolonged repeated exposure cohort, participants underwent one 60-min exposure per day for 9 consecutive days. Safety assessments included adverse events, vital signs, hematology, routine biochemistry, serum cytokines, laryngological examination with rhinoscopy, nasal cytology, and conjunctival assessment.

Eighty participants were randomized, 40 in each exposure cohort. No serious adverse events occurred, and no participant discontinued the study because of an adverse event. In the short repeated exposure cohort, adverse events were reported in 9/20 participants receiving HOCI and 3/20 receiving sodium chloride (45% vs. 15%; p = 0.082). In the prolonged repeated exposure cohort, adverse events were reported in 13/20 participants receiving HOCI and 0/20 receiving sodium chloride (65% vs. 0%; p < 0.001). All adverse events in the prolonged exposure cohort were mild; two were classified as definitely related to HOCI exposure. No persistent laryngological or conjunctival abnormalities were observed. Cytokine concentrations showed no consistent exposure-related pattern or sustained systemic inflammatory activation. Vital signs and routine laboratory parameters showed no clinically relevant systemic toxicity signal.

Under the controlled exposure conditions tested, aerosolized HOCI dry fog was generally well tolerated in healthy adults. Prolonged repeated exposure was associated with more frequent non-serious, mild adverse events, but without serious adverse events, persistent local irritation, systemic inflammatory activation, or clinically meaningful laboratory toxicity.

Article.ArticleTitle: Targeting the Gut-Brain Axis in Functional Dyspepsia: Buspirone and Mirtazapine Improve Anxiety and PAGI-SYM Scores.

Abstract.AbstractText: Functional dyspepsia is a chronic gastrointestinal disorder with uncertain causes, often linked to anxiety and depression, which can worsen symptoms and hinder treatment success. Although psychological therapies and antidepressants have shown some benefit, the role of anti-anxiety medications remains unclear. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of buspirone and mirtazapine in reducing symptoms and improving the quality of life for patients with functional dyspepsia.

In a semi experimental study, 71 patients with functional dyspepsia were randomized to receive either buspirone 15 mg, mirtazapine 7.5 mg, or pantoprazole 40 mg once daily for 12 weeks. Outcomes-anxiety severity, dyspepsia symptom score, quality of life, and adverse events-were assessed at baseline and monthly. Efficacy was analyzed by repeated-measures ANOVA and adverse event rates by chi-square tests.

Both buspirone and mirtazapine significantly outperformed pantoprazole alone in reducing anxiety (buspirone vs. control at 3 months, p = 0.01; both active treatments vs. control, p < 0.05) and in alleviating functional dyspepsia symptoms by Week 12 (both vs. control, p < 0.05), with no difference between the two active drugs.

This study suggests that buspirone and mirtazapine are effective in reducing anxiety and improving symptoms in patients with functional dyspepsia. These findings highlight the potential role of anti-anxiety medications in managing both the psychological and gastrointestinal aspects of this disorder.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of Cold Atmospheric Plasma on Wound Healing in a Standardized Wound Model-A Prospective, Monocentric, Self-Controlled Clinical Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) has demonstrated antimicrobial and tissue-stimulatory effects and represents a promising supportive treatment modality in wound care. However, clinical evidence remains limited, particularly regarding acute and aseptic wounds and the quantification of wound-healing acceleration. In this randomized intraindividual split-wound study, patients (n = 33) with split-thickness skin graft (STSG) donor site wounds received postoperative CAP treatment on one wound half, while the other half served as control. CAP was applied according to a standardized treatment protocol for 2 min each on postoperative days 3, 5 and 7. Re-epithelialization was quantified longitudinally by image analysis. The primary endpoint was wound-healing rate from postoperative day 3 to day 14, assessed using a linear mixed-effects model. An accelerated wound healing following CAP (p = 0.017) could be shown. Furthermore, treated wound halves exhibited significantly smaller residual wound areas at postoperative days 14, 21 and 28. No significant differences were observed in microbiological outcomes, clinical wound healing score, signs of infection or scar quality. The treatment was well tolerated, and no severe adverse events were reported. CAP therapy accelerated re-epithelialization in STSG donor site wounds and may represent a promising adjunctive treatment option. Further studies are warranted to define optimal treatment protocols and clinical indications for its effective and rational use.

Article.ArticleTitle: Oliceridine vs Sufentanil Combined With Ondansetron for Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting and QTc Interval in Hysteroscopic Surgery: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Study.

Abstract.AbstractText: BACKGROUND Postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) is common after hysteroscopic surgery, and opioid use can raise concerns regarding cardiac safety. This prospective study aimed to compare the effects of oliceridine plus ondansetron versus sufentanil plus ondansetron on 24-hour PONV incidence and perioperative changes in the corrected QT interval (QTc) in patients undergoing non-intubated hysteroscopy under general anesthesia. MATERIAL AND METHODS In this randomized, double-blind, controlled study, 62 patients undergoing hysteroscopic surgery under general anesthesia were analyzed. Patients received propofol 2 mg/kg with either oliceridine 0.039 mg/kg plus ondansetron 4 mg (O group) or sufentanil 0.1 μg/kg plus ondansetron 4 mg (S group). The primary endpoint was 24-hour PONV. Secondary endpoints included emergence time, post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) pain scores, and change in QTc from baseline (ΔQTc) measured by 5-lead electrocardiography at predefined time points. RESULTS PONV incidence within 24 h did not differ significantly between groups (0% vs 3.2%, P>0.05). Time to anesthesia emergence was comparable between groups (P=0.960). Numerical rating scale scores at PACU discharge were also comparable (P=0.186). Repeated-measures ANOVA showed a significant time effect for ΔQTc (P=0.001), but no significant group effect (P=0.076) or group×time interaction (P=0.171). CONCLUSIONS Oliceridine plus ondansetron did not significantly reduce 24-hour PONV compared with sufentanil plus ondansetron, and this finding should be interpreted cautiously because of limited statistical power. Perioperative ΔQTc changes were minimal and similar between groups, with no clinically significant QTc prolongation.

Article.ArticleTitle: The Safety, Pharmacokinetics, and Antiviral Activity of ABI-4334, A Novel Next-Generation Hepatitis B Capsid Assembly Modulator.

Abstract.AbstractText: Novel, well-tolerated, short-term therapeutics for chronic hepatitis B virus infection (cHBV) are needed. ABI-4334 is a next-generation capsid assembly modulator that targets the HBV core protein. The safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of ABI-4334 in healthy volunteers and participants with cHBV and antiviral effects in participants with cHBV were examined in two Phase 1 studies. Study 101 was a placebo-controlled study of healthy volunteers that included four single-ascending dose cohorts and two once-daily multiple-ascending dose cohorts randomized 6:2 (ABI-4334:placebo), and one crossover food-effect cohort randomized 3:3 (fed:fasted). Study 102 was a randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled study where participants with cHBV were randomized 8:2 (ABI-4334 [2 dose cohorts]:placebo). Overall, 54 healthy volunteers and 20 participants with cHBV were included in Studies 101 and 102, respectively. Most participants (75%) in Study 102 were hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) negative and generally had lower baseline HBV DNA and pregenomic RNA (pgRNA) levels. ABI-4334 was well tolerated, with no treatment-emergent serious adverse events (AEs) or treatment-emergent AEs leading to study discontinuation. The mean ABI-4334 plasma half-life ranges were comparable across doses in both studies. Following multiple-dose administration in participants with cHBV, the steady-state mean plasma half-life ranged from 17.5 to 27.5 h. HBV DNA declines were observed in both HBeAg-positive (n = 3) and -negative (n = 13) participants across doses. Reductions in pgRNA were observed in participants with detectable pgRNA at baseline. ABI-4334 was well tolerated, with pharmacokinetics and antiviral results supporting the continued development of ABI-4334 as a monotherapy or component of novel combination regimens for cHBV. Trial Registration: Study 101 (NCT05569941). Study 102 (NCT06384131).

Article.ArticleTitle: The effect of a therapeutic quality-of-life-based program on happiness in older women with breast cancer.

Abstract.AbstractText: Breast cancer is one of the most prevalent malignancies among older women and can adversely affect their psychological well-being, happiness, and overall quality of life. Happiness plays an important role as a key indicator of psychological well-being in patients' adaptation to illness and health outcomes. Given the importance of supportive interventions for this population, the present study aimed to investigate the effect of a therapeutic quality-of-life-based program on happiness among older women with breast cancer.

This quasi-experimental pretest-posttest study with a control group was conducted in 2025 among 50 older women with breast cancer attending the chemotherapy unit of Peymanieh Educational Hospital in Jahrom, Iran. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling and were then randomly allocated to either the intervention group or the control group (n = 25 per group). Data were collected using a questionnaire on demographic characteristics and the Oxford Happiness Questionnaire. The intervention group participated in an 8-week therapeutic quality-of-life-based educational program consisting of eight weekly 60-minute sessions, whereas the control group received routine care. Data were analyzed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences version 22. Descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-test, paired-samples t-test, chi-square test, and analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) were applied. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

No statistically significant difference was observed in the mean happiness scores at baseline between the two groups (p > 0.05). The mean happiness score in the intervention group significantly increased from 34.72 ± 9.20 to 44.84 ± 5.74 (p < 0.001), whereas no significant change was observed in the control group (p = 0.92). Furthermore, ANCOVA, which controlled for baseline happiness scores, confirmed a significantly higher post-intervention happiness score in the intervention group than in the control group (p < 0.001).

The therapeutic quality-of-life-based program appears to be an effective, low-cost, and feasible supportive intervention for enhancing happiness and promoting psychological adjustment among older women with breast cancer. Integrating such structured interventions into supportive care and educational services may improve psychosocial outcomes in this population. To evaluate the sustainability of the intervention effects, further studies with larger sample sizes and longer follow-up periods are recommended.

Article.ArticleTitle: Baduanjin improves motor function and cortical activation in children with developmental coordination disorder: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Children with developmental coordination disorder (DCD) exhibit significant deficits in both gross and fine motor functions. Baduanjin, a traditional Chinese mind-body exercise, has demonstrated potential in improving motor functions, including balance and neuromuscular coordination, in various rehabilitation settings. This study aims to investigate the effects of Baduanjin intervention on motor function in children with DCD, and further explore whether its potential benefits are mediated through improved cortical activation in motor-related brain regions, as reflected by cerebral hemodynamic responses.

This single-blind randomized controlled trial enrolled 40 children aged 5-10 years who met the DSM-5 diagnostic criteria for DCD and had an MABC-2 standard score of ≤ 7. Participants were randomly assigned, using a SAS 9.4-generated randomization sequence with sealed opaque envelopes for allocation concealment, to either an experimental group receiving Baduanjin training plus health education or a control group receiving health education alone. The intervention lasted 8 weeks, with five sessions per week, including two instructor-led hospital sessions and three parent-supervised home sessions. After the intervention, motor coordination and balance were assessed using the Movement Assessment Battery for Children-2 (MABC-2) and the ProKin 254 balance test system, respectively. In addition, functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) was used to measure hemodynamic responses in motor-related cortical regions during functional tasks, to evaluate cortical activation and examine its associations with changes in motor function.

The per-protocol (PP) dataset included 36 participants, whereas the intention-to-treat (ITT) dataset included all 40 randomized children. Both PP and ITT analyses showed that the experimental group had significantly higher total MABC-2 scores than the control group (PP: P = 0.002; ITT: P = 0.001). Subscale analyses demonstrated significant improvements in aiming and catching (PP: P = 0.019; ITT: P = 0.005) and balance (PP: P = 0.008; ITT: P = 0.004). In addition, the experimental group showed significant improvements in key static balance parameters, including reduced sway area (PP and ITT: P < 0.001) and shorter sway path length (PP and ITT: P < 0.001). Dynamic postural stability also improved significantly (PP and ITT: P = 0.004). However, no statistically significant between-group differences were observed in manual dexterity (PP and ITT: P > 0.05). fNIRS results revealed that during the aiming and catching task, the experimental group exhibited significantly greater activation in the left premotor cortex and supplementary motor area (PMC + SMA) compared to the control group (CH31: FDR-adjusted P = 0.015; CH32: FDR-adjusted P = 0.041). In the one-leg balance task, the experimental group showed significantly enhanced activation in the left hemispheric regions, including the frontopolar area (FPA), dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), inferior frontal gyrus (IFG), primary motor cortex (M1), as well as the PMC + SMA (FDR-adjusted P = 0.018). No significant between-group differences in brain activation were observed during the manual dexterity task (FDR-adjusted P ≥ 0.05). Furthermore, correlation analysis indicated a significant positive association between improvements in motor performance and activation of motor-related brain regions in the experimental group.

Baduanjin training improved motor coordination and balance in children with DCD. The observed changes in activation within motor-related cortical regions provide preliminary support for a possible neurophysiological basis of these functional improvements, although the underlying mechanisms require further investigation.

Article.ArticleTitle: A randomized controlled trial investigating the effect of thermal steam spray on nasal condition, neurological function, and sleep quality in young adults with nasal congestion and irregular sleep patterns.

Abstract.AbstractText: Intranasal thermal steam spray (ITSS) has been suggested to relieve nasal stuffiness and improve sleep-related symptoms. However, its mechanistic effects on respiratory capacity, neurological functions, including autonomic nervous system (ANS) and brain activities, remain underexplored. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the effects of an ITSS intervention on nasal condition, respiratory and neurological functions, and sleep quality in young adults with nasal congestion and irregular sleep patterns.

Sixty university students (aged 20-26 years) with an average duration of nasal congestion and sleep irregularity of over three years participated. Two dormitories were randomly assigned to either a control group (CON; n = 30) or an intervention group (ITSS; n = 30). The ITSS device, delivering 43 °C thermal wet steam using jet stream (80 mm H₂O) technology, was administered for 15 min, 3 times per week, 30 min before bedtime for 8 weeks.

After the intervention, subjective nasal congestion and sleep conditions deteriorated in the CON but improved in the ITSS (p < 0.001). Pulmonary outcomes, including reduced respiratory rate (p < 0.001) and increased FEV₁ (p < 0.001) and PEF (p < 0.001), improved only in the ITSS. Heart rate variability and blood pressure indices also showed favourable changes. Electroencephalographic analysis revealed increased wide band, alpha, and gamma powers in the ITSS, contrasting with declines in the CON (p < 0.05). In the ITSS group, PSQI-K components improved, with daytime dysfunction reduced by 32.78 ± 41.40% (p < 0.001). Total PSQI-K scores rose in the CON group (+ 14.64 ± 22.44%) but declined in the ITSS group (- 38.90 ± 21.99%), showing a significant difference (p < 0.001).

These findings suggest that ITSS enhances airflow by humidifying the nasal environment, thereby facilitating respiratory function and stabilizing ANS activity and brain function. This process ultimately contributes to improved overall sleep quality in young adults experiencing nasal congestion and irregular sleep patterns.
The study was retrospectively registered on April 3, 2025, in the Clinical Research Information Service ( https://cris.nih.go.kr/cris/search/listDetail.do/ ) under registration number KCT0010381.

Article.ArticleTitle: Influence of diabetes mellitus on dapagliflozin response after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR): insights from the DAPA-TAVI trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: The DAPA-TAVI trial demonstrated that dapagliflozin reduced the composite of all-cause mortality or worsening heart failure (HF) at 1 year in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with prior HF. Whether the magnitude of this benefit differs according to diabetes mellitus (DM) status remains uncertain.

This pre-specified subgroup analysis of the multicenter randomized DAPA-TAVI trial conducted at 39 centers in Spain, which enrolled 1222 patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVR with prior HF and at least one high-risk condition. Patients were stratified by the presence or absence of DM. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality or worsening HF at 12 months. Secondary endpoints included the individual components of the primary endpoint, cardiovascular death, and safety outcomes. Cox proportional-hazards models adjusted for age, sex, coronary artery disease, baseline ejection fraction and baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate were used to estimate treatment effects.

Among 1222 patients, 537 (43.9%) had DM. In patients with DM, dapagliflozin significantly reduced the primary endpoint compared with standard care (15.2% vs. 22.7%; HR 0.580; 95% CI 0.389-0.866; p = 0.008; number needed to treat [NNT] = 11), driven primarily by fewer worsening HF events. In patients without DM, the reduction was numerically lower and non-significant (15.0% vs. 18.0%; HR 0.814; 95% CI 0.560-1.183; p = 0.280; NNT = 32). Genital infections were more frequent with dapagliflozin in patients with DM, whereas symptomatic hypotension was more common in those without DM. No significant differences in serious adverse events were observed in either subgroup. No statistically significant interactions between DM status and treatment effect were observed for the primary or secondary endpoints.

In this pre-specified subanalysis of the DAPA-TAVI trial, dapagliflozin significantly reduced the risk of death or worsening HF in patients with DM undergoing TAVR, with a favorable benefit-risk profile, whereas a more modest and non-significant effect was observed in non-DM patients. Although no statistically significant interaction according to diabetes status was observed, the apparently greater benefit among patients with DM warrants further investigation.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of opioid-free intraoperative anesthesia versus opioid-based anesthesia on postoperative immune function in elderly patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty: a single-center, prospective, randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) in elderly patients may involve postoperative immune suppression. This study compares intraoperative opioid-free anesthesia (OFA) and opioid-based anesthesia (OBA) effects on postoperative proportion of immune cells. The core pharmacological difference between groups lies in the intraoperative anesthetic regimen: the OBA group received sufentanil for induction and continuous remifentanil infusion for maintenance, while the OFA group replaced all intraoperative opioids with esketamine. Both groups received opioid-containing patient-controlled intravenous analgesia and rescue analgesia after surgery, and the opioid-free anesthesia protocol was only applied during the intraoperative phase.

A single-center, prospective, randomized controlled trial of 60 patients (60-80 years) undergoing unilateral TKA. The opioid-free strategy was exclusively implemented during the intraoperative period, and both groups received identical opioid-inclusive postoperative analgesia. Patients were randomized into OFA (n = 30) and OBA (n = 30) groups.
change in natural killer (NK) cell proportion.

T-cell subsets (CD3⁺, CD4⁺, CD8⁺), B cells, dynamic/static visual analogue scale (VAS) scores, patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) demands, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), hemodynamics, and adverse events.

We conducted an intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis in 60 patients (30 in each group). Baseline demographics and preoperative immune indices showed no significant differences between the groups. Compared with the levels one day before the operation, the postoperative reduction in NK cell proportion was significantly smaller in the OFA group than in the OBA group (Δ = -5.51% ± 4.89% vs. Δ = -10.12% ± 5.39%; P < 0.001). The OFA group demonstrated superior early postoperative analgesia, with lower dynamic and static VAS scores at 4-48 h (P < 0.05), reduced PCIA demands at 24 h (5.8 ± 0.9 vs. 7.2 ± 1.1) and 48 h (6.1 ± 1.0 vs. 8.5 ± 1.3; P < 0.05), and better PSQI (7.50 ± 3.34 vs. 10.86 ± 4.01; P < 0.001). The OFA group had significantly lower intraoperative vasoactive agent consumption (atropine, norepinephrine, ephedrine) and 72-hour postoperative opioid consumption (all P < 0.05), and exhibited superior postoperative functional exercise capacity (active knee flexion angle and maximum walking distance) at 48 and 72 h postoperatively (all P < 0.05). No significant differences were observed between the groups in CD8⁺ T cell, B cell proportions, extubation time, length of hospital stay, rescue analgesia rate or postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) incidence (all P > 0.05).

In elderly patients undergoing unilateral total knee arthroplasty, intraoperative esketamine-based opioid-free anesthesia was associated with a smaller decline in NK-cell proportion, superior early analgesia, and improved short-term sleep quality compared with opioid-based anesthesia. These findings are limited to the comparison of intraoperative strategies and cannot be extrapolated to full perioperative opioid-free management.

Article.ArticleTitle: Comparison of QLB block and TAP block in morbid obese patients: a randomized controlled study.

Abstract.AbstractText: Quadratus lumborum block (QLB) and Transverses abdominis plane block (TAP) are a fascial plane block. The study aimed to compare the efficacy of the TAP block and QLB-2 in terms of postoperative pain assessed by the VAS and morphine consumption following laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy.

This study was conducted as a randomized controlled trial involving patients who underwent laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy in the operating room. Patients were randomly assigned to one of three groups: groups 1 (TAP block), 2 (QLB-2 block), and 3 (control). Analgesic consumption was assessed by evaluating morphine use at the postoperative 1st, 6th, 12th, and 24th hours, as well as the total morphine consumption and VAS scores. Quality of life was preoperatively evaluated, at 48 h, and 1 week using the WHOQOL-BREF scale.

One hundred twenty-six patients (female:103 and male:23) were included in the final analysis (44, 42, and 40) in the control, TAP and QLB-2 block groups, respectively. The block duration in the QLB-2 group was significantly longer than that in the TAP block group (p = 0.001). Total morphine consumption differed between the groups (p = 0.001). Morphine consumption in the TAP block group was lower than that in the control (p = 0.001) and QLB-2 (p = 0.001) groups. The total morphine consumption in the QLB-2 group was also significantly lower than that in the control group (p = 0.035) - 0.001) and QLB-2 (p = 0.019) groups. WHOQOL scores (48 h and 1 week postoperatively) were no statistical differences in any subgroup or timeline (p > 0.05). There was a statistically significant difference in postoperative VAS scores (1st, 6th, 12th and 24th hours) among the study groups (p < 0.001).

TAP and QLB-2 blocks were associated with reduced postoperative pain scores and opioid requirements in morbidly obese patients undergoing laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy compared to no regional block. TAP block consumed less morphine overall, had a shorter block performance time, and mobilized earlier than QLB-2 block. There were no changes in quality of life outcomes and it was no statistically significant difference in the preoperative VAS scores between the study groups.

Article.ArticleTitle: The efficacy of suprascapular nerve radiofrequency and intra-articular steroıd injectıon in frozen shoulder treatment: randomızed controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: This study aims to address the impacts of intra-articular steroid injection (IASI) alone versus the combination of suprascapular nerve (SSN) pulsed radiofrequency (PRF) and IASI on pain relief and improvement in shoulder range of motion (ROM) in patients with adhesive capsulitis (AC) (frozen shoulder).

This study included 80 patients with AC. Participants were randomly assigned to two groups. A combination of suprascapular nerve pulsed radiofrequency and IASI were administered to the first group and IASI to the second. Both groups underwent a standardized physical therapy program for three weeks following the intervention. Outcome measures included active and passive ROM (AROM and PROM), Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for pain, and the Shoulder Pain and Disability Index (SPADI), assessed at baseline and 4th week, and 12th week post-treatment.

80 patients (40 patients in each group) completed this study. Both interventions were found to be effective in both groups (p < 0.05). However, intergroup comparisons revealed that patients in the SNNR group experienced significantly better improvements in pain levels (as measured by VAS and SPADI scores) and ROM (p < 0.05). No post-procedural complications were observed in either group.

This study revealed that the administration of PRF lesioning of the SSN utilizing a UG method combined with intra-articular steroid injection yielded better and faster pain relief, reduced disability, and better AROM and PROM in comparison to intra-articular injection alone in AC patients.
This study was retrospective registered with the U.S. Clinical Trial Registry (U.S. Clinical Trial Registry No NCT06778577, date 20241125).

Article.ArticleTitle: Dose-dense neoadjuvant bi-weekly nab-paclitaxel followed by epirubicin-cyclophosphamide versus bi-weekly docetaxel followed by epirubicin-cyclophosphamide in patients with HR+/HER2- early breast cancer: a multicentre, randomised, phase III trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Dose-dense adjuvant chemotherapy prolongs survival in breast cancer and has been translated into neoadjuvant settings. Although weekly nanoparticle albumin-bound (nab)-paclitaxel yields superior pathological complete response (pCR) rates relative to solvent-based paclitaxel, data supporting its incorporation into a dose-dense neoadjuvant regimen-particularly for hormone receptor positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 negative (HR+/HER2-) tumours-remain limited. This trial therefore evaluated whether a bi-weekly dose-dense nab-paclitaxel schedule improves the proportion of residual cancer burden (RCB) 0/Ⅰ compared with a comparable dose-dense docetaxel regimen, each followed by dose-dense epirubicin plus cyclophosphamide.

This was a multicentre, randomised, phase III trial done at three hospitals in China. HR⁺/HER2⁻ patients (cT1-3/N0-1/M0) were randomised 1:1 using dynamic allocation with Pocock minimisation on Ki-67 and TNM stage. The experimental arm received nab-paclitaxel 260 mg/m² intravenously on day 1 every two weeks for four cycles; the control arm received docetaxel 100 mg/m² on the identical schedule. Both cohorts subsequently received epirubicin 90 mg/m² plus cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² intravenously on day 1 every two weeks for four cycles. Primary endpoints were RCB 0/Ⅰ rate; secondary endpoints encompassed disease free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and safety.

Between December 2019 and December 2020, 388 patients (194 per arm) were enrolled. The nab-paclitaxel arm attained an RCB 0/Ⅰ rate of 20.1% (95% CI 14.41-26.72), significantly exceeding the docetaxel arm's 11.34% (95% CI 6.92-15.81; χ²=5.62, P = 0.018). pCR was achieved in 15.98% (95% CI 10.81-21.16) of the nab-paclitaxel group versus 10.31% (95% CI 6.01-14.60) of the docetaxel group (χ²=2.73, P = 0.098). Multivariate analysis confirmed a statistically significant favourable impact of nab-paclitaxel on RCB 0/Ⅰ. Five-year DFS was comparable (90.21% vs. 87.11%; HR: 1.14, 95% CI 0.64-2.05; P = 0.656), as was five-year OS (96.34% vs. 95.31%; HR: 0.64, 95% CI 0.29-1.42; P = 0.274), indicating no significant survival disparity. Grade 3/4 adverse event incidence was similar (30% vs. 38%). The most frequent all-grade toxicities (neutropenia, nausea, myalgia) occurred at comparable rates; however, grade 3/4 peripheral sensory neuropathy was observed exclusively in the nab-paclitaxel cohort. No treatment-related mortality was reported.

A bi-weekly dose-dense nab-paclitaxel regimen followed by dose-dense epirubicin-cyclophosphamide constitutes a feasible and efficacious neoadjuvant strategy for early stage HR+/HER2- breast cancer, delivering a higher RCB 0/Ⅰ rate without compromising overall safety. The increased incidence of high-grade peripheral neuropathy mandates vigilant monitoring, yet the regimen represents a valuable addition to contemporary neoadjuvant options.

Article.ArticleTitle: Safety and immunogenicity of a BPL-inactivated, whole-virus, universal influenza vaccine: a randomized, double-blinded, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, phase 1 clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Influenza inflicts substantial burden of disease, but current vaccines have limited breadth of protection against strains and subtypes not in the vaccine. BPL-1357, a whole-virus, inactivated vaccine containing four wild-type, low-pathogenicity avian influenza viruses has demonstrated remarkable protection in animal models against a wide range of influenza viruses. In this phase I trial, forty-five healthy participants were randomized to receive BPL-1357 intramuscularly (IM), intranasally (IN), or placebo, in a prime and boost strategy, 28-days apart. The primary endpoints consisted of adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) from enrollment through 28 days after the boost. The secondary endpoints were AEs and SAEs through 182 days after the boost and measurement of serum IgG and nasal IgA titers against hemagglutinin and neuraminidase vaccine antigens. Adverse effects were mostly mild and, other than mild injection-site pain more frequently observed in the IM group, occurred in a minority of patients. IM BPL-1357 induced higher serum IgG titers against H3, H5, and H7 relative to placebo, with 71.4%, 71.4%, and 85.7% of participants demonstrating a response. IM BPL-1357 vaccinated participants also experienced serum neutralizing and NA-specific responses, but no mucosal IgA responses against HA or NA. Subtle mucosal and serum responses were observed after IN vaccination, similar to preclinical experiments. These results suggest that BPL-1357 is well tolerated and immunogenic, particularly when given IM, but more work is needed to assess other dose levels, further characterize induced immunity, and evaluate efficacy against influenza infection and disease (NCT05027932).

Article.ArticleTitle: Clinical performance of i-gel and classic laryngeal mask airway in different head positions in patients aged ≥75 years: A prospective randomized study.

Abstract.AbstractText: ObjectiveSupraglottic airway devices are alternatives to endotracheal intubation under general anesthesia. However, their performance in older patients remains understudied, particularly in different head positions.MethodsThis prospective randomized controlled study included 120 patients aged ≥75 years undergoing elective urologic surgery. Patients were randomly allocated into four groups based on the device type and head position during insertion: (a) i-gel with neutral head position; (b) i-gel with right head rotation; (c) classic laryngeal mask airway with neutral head position; and (d) classic laryngeal mask airway with right head rotation. The primary outcome was the insertion time. Secondary outcomes included insertion attempts, oropharyngeal leak pressure, and perioperative variables, which were assessed in patients with successful device placement.ResultsThe overall insertion success rate was 94.2% (113/120). The i-gel was associated with a significantly shorter insertion time and higher oropharyngeal leak pressure than the classic laryngeal mask airway (both p = 0.001). Two-way factorial analysis revealed that device type significantly influenced insertion time and oropharyngeal leak pressure, whereas head position and device-by-head position interaction exerted no significant effects. No significant differences were observed in the number of insertion attempts, fiberoptic view scores, peak airway pressure, recovery times, hemodynamic variables, or perioperative and postoperative complications.ConclusionsIn patients aged ≥75 years undergoing elective surgery, the i-gel was associated with a shorter insertion time and higher oropharyngeal leak pressure than the classic laryngeal mask airway. Head position did not significantly influence insertion time, oropharyngeal leak pressure, or peak airway pressure. These findings suggest that airway device selection exerts a greater impact on supraglottic airway performance than head position, whereas the i-gel may offer practical advantages in selected clinical settings.Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov (https://clinicaltrials.gov), Identifier: NCT07027293, registered on 27 May 2025.

Article.ArticleTitle: Prevalence and Consequences of Guideline-Directed Indications for Aortic Valve Replacement in the EARLY TAVR Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: The current American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association valvular heart disease guidelines were published before several recent trials that provide greater support for early intervention in patients with asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS).
This study sought to investigate the prevalence and clinical impact of American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Class II recommendations for AVR in the EARLY TAVR trial.

The EARLY TAVR trial randomized patients with asymptomatic severe AS to transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance (CS) with conversion to TAVR based on development of ACC/AHA Class I indications. Patients in the intention-to-treat cohort were stratified by presence of a Class II indication for AVR at randomization. The primary endpoint of the present analysis was the composite of all-cause death, stroke, or heart failure hospitalization. Interaction tests were performed to assess whether the treatment effect differed by level of guideline recommendation. Timing of conversion to AVR in the CS group according to the presence/absence of Class II indications was also assessed.

Of the 901 patients randomized to TAVR (N = 445) and CS (N = 446), 636 (70.6%) patients had no guideline recommendation, and 265 (29.4%) had at least1 1 Class II recommendation for AVR at the time of randomization. At a median follow-up of 3.8 years, patients with a Class II indication for AVR experienced higher rates of the primary endpoint (Class II: 24.5% vs no recommendation: 14.5%; HR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.30-2.44; P < 0.001) and were more likely to have acute valve syndrome at the time of conversion. Compared with CS, the relative benefit of early TAVR on the primary endpoint was similar regardless of the presence or absence of a Class II guideline recommendation (HR = 0.62; 95% CI: 0.37-1.02 vs 0.61; 95% CI: 0.40-0.92; Pinteraction = 0.96).

Among patients in the EARLY TAVR trial, Class II indications for AVR were present in almost one-third of patients at baseline. The benefit of early TAVR was consistent regardless of the presence or absence of Class II indications. These findings support the strategy of early TAVR over CS in asymptomatic patients with severe AS, independent of guideline indications.

Article.ArticleTitle: Prosthesis-Patient Mismatch and Patient-Centered Outcomes After TAVR.

Abstract.AbstractText: Prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement has been widely studied for its association with clinical outcomes, but its effect on patient-reported health status remains less defined.
This study sought to evaluate the association between PPM severity and health status through 3-year follow-up after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.

This post hoc analysis of the SCOPE I (Safety and Efficacy of the ACURATE Neo/TF Compared to the SAPIEN 3 Bioprosthesis) randomized trial categorized patients according to PPM severity using Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 criteria. Endpoints included survival and patient-reported health status, with an integrated outcome defined as being alive with good health status (Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score ≥75 without a decline of >10 points from baseline).

Among 662 patients, moderate and severe PPM occurred in 184 (27.8%) and 69 (10.4%), respectively. All-cause mortality at 1 and 3 years was 7.0% and 20.5%, with no differences across PPM categories. Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score was similar through 1 year but lower at 3 years in patients with severe vs no PPM (median 71.1 vs 83.9; P = 0.027). Fewer patients with severe PPM were alive with good health status at 3 years (30.6% vs 49.4%; P = 0.021). In multivariable analysis, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of the integrated outcome (OR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.27-0.96; P = 0.036), but this association was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for 30-day mitral regurgitation (OR: 0.59; 95% CI: 0.30-1.15; P = 0.121).

Among survivors, severe PPM was associated with a lower likelihood of good health status at 3 years. This association was attenuated after accounting for 30-day residual mitral regurgitation, suggesting a possible contributory role. Given the post hoc design, the findings are hypothesis-generating.

Article.ArticleTitle: Cardiac Damage and Clinical Outcomes in Symptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.

Abstract.AbstractText: The extent of cardiac damage in patients with aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with worse clinical outcomes.
This study sought to investigate the clinical impact of cardiac damage using the updated criteria incorporating the echocardiographic probability of pulmonary hypertension.

This post hoc subanalysis of LANDMARK trial, which randomized 768 patients with severe AS to the Myval transcatheter heart valve (THV) series or to contemporary THVs (Sapien and Evolut series), used updated cardiac damage classification: stage 0, no cardiac damage; stage 1, left ventricular damage; stage 2, left atrial or mitral valve damage; stage 3, pulmonary artery or tricuspid valve damage; and stage 4, right ventricular damage. The impact of cumulative cardiac damage, defined as meeting all criteria for stages 1 to 4, was also assessed. The primary endpoint was 1-year all-cause mortality.

Cardiac damage stages were assessed in 596 patients (stage 0, n = 36; stage 1, n = 88; stage 2, n = 284; stage 3, n = 84; stage 4, n = 104), with a mean age of 80.2 (5.7) years and a mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons score of 3.3% (2.4%). One-year mortality was 0%, 1.1%, 4.7%, 7.2%, and 20.4% in stages 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively (log-rank P < 0.001). The area under the curve for predicting 1-year mortality was 0.739. Patients with cumulative cardiac damage had the highest mortality (23.6%). In the multivariable analysis, stage 4 was independently associated with higher 1-year mortality.

The updated cardiac damage staging stratified 1-year mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement, highlighting the importance of comprehensive echocardiographic assessment in severe AS. (LANDMARK Trial: a Randomised Controlled Trial of Myval THV [LANDMARK]; NCT04275726).

Article.ArticleTitle: Inforatio Technique and Foot Ulcer Closure Among Patients With Diabetes: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are common complications of diabetes, a disease increasing in prevalence worldwide. Novel adjunctive treatments that are affordable and feasible to implement in both high- and low-income settings are urgently needed.
To assess whether the inforatio technique promotes healing of DFUs compared with standard of care (SOC).

This multicenter, evaluator-blinded randomized clinical trial was conducted at 4 outpatient clinics specializing in wound care in Denmark from February 15, 2022, to December 18, 2024. One-year medical record follow-up was completed August 14, 2025. Participants included patients with noninfected Wagner grade 1 DFUs.

Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive the inforatio technique every third week for 12 weeks with SOC or SOC only. The inforatio technique involved making incisions on wound beds with 2-mm biopsy punch tools.

The primary outcome was the proportion of ulcers achieving closure within 20 weeks. Secondary outcomes were health-related and disease-specific quality of life. Safety outcomes included serious and target ulcer-related adverse events.

A total of 101 patients were randomized, of whom 100 had DFUs and were included in the primary analysis (49 in the inforatio group and 51 in the SOC only group; 85 men; mean [SD] age, 64.4 [11.4] years; median ulcer size, 0.76 [range, 0.09-23.23] cm2). Twenty-four patients in the inforatio group (49.0%) vs 14 in the SOC-only group (27.5%) achieved ulcer closure within 20 weeks (adjusted odds ratio, 3.01 [95% CI, 1.20-7.58]; P = .02). No between-group difference was found in quality of life change from baseline to 20 weeks. Within 20 weeks, 7 patients in the inforatio group vs 13 in the SOC-only group experienced the serious adverse events, including death, amputation, or target ulcer-related hospitalization (relative risk, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.24-1.29]; P = .25), and 16 patients in the inforatio group vs 30 in the SOC-only group experienced target ulcer-related adverse events (relative risk, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.35-0.88]; P = .02).

In this randomized clinical trial, the inforatio technique improved DFU healing compared with SOC alone. Fewer ulcer-related adverse events were also observed with the inforatio technique, although this exploratory finding should be interpreted cautiously.
ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05189470.

Article.ArticleTitle: Association of HTR3A and COMT polymorphisms with electroacupuncture response for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting in breast cancer: a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Preliminary findings indicate that electroacupuncture (EA) reduces chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV), yet individual responses vary. This study aimed to explore associations between selected single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and complete protection (CP) against CINV and to conduct an exploratory evaluation of their predictive value.

This exploratory analysis was based on a randomized controlled trial (RCT) of EA (NCT05275569). Three candidate SNPs in HTR3A and COMT were genotyped by Sanger sequencing. The primary outcome measure was CP against CINV, defined according to the endpoint of the prospective study. Firth logistic regression was applied to evaluate associations between clinical or genetic variables and CP under additive, dominant and recessive models.

A total of 189 patients with breast cancer (BC) were enrolled, with 96 allocated to true EA group and 93 to sham EA group. The two groups were comparable in clinical variables and genotype distribution, and all three SNPs conformed to Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (HWE). In the true EA group, CP achievement rates varied by rs909411 genotype: 42.9% (AA), 32.1% (AG), and 62.3% (GG) (P = 0.027). Univariable Firth logistic regression indicated that rs909411 was associated with a higher likelihood of achieving CP under both additive (OR = 2.088, 95% CI: 1.089-4.249, P = 0.026) and recessive models (OR = 3.080, 95% CI: 1.327-7.429, P = 0.009). After Multivariable adjustment, rs909411 remained statistically significant (additive: OR = 2.138, P = 0.027; recessive: OR = 3.241, P = 0.011). rs4633 was associated with a lower likelihood of achieving CP under the recessive model (univariable OR = 0.089, P = 0.035; Multivariable OR = 0.059, P = 0.016). No consistent association was observed for rs4680, and no significant SNP-by-treatment interactions were detected.
Exploratory treatment-stratified analyses identified associations of rs909411 and rs4633 with CP within the true EA group.
