Article.ArticleTitle: A change in STRIDE: site-reported adaptations of an evidence-based inpatient mobility program.

Abstract.AbstractText: Hospital-based inactivity among older adults leads to functional decline. Mobility programs like STRIDE (assiSTed eaRly mobIlity for hospitalizeD older vEterans) are effective. Implementation in clinical settings and whether site-initiated adaptations are possible remain understudied.
To report adaptations to STRIDE across Veterans Affairs Medical Centers during implementation, using the Framework for Reporting Adaptations and Modifications-Enhanced (FRAME).
Site-level contacts completed forms at pre-implementation, six months, and ten months, documenting adaptations. Adaptations were analyzed using collaborative coding to determine fidelity.

The adaptations were classified per FRAME criteria including timing, planning status, decision makers, modification type, delivery level, and fidelity consistency. All sites reported at least one adaptation. The largest number of adaptations per site was seven. This study demonstrates that hospitals can adapt an evidence-based program and maintain fidelity.

We found in a large, nationwide implementation trial, site-initiated adaptations are possible. Promoting adaptability among implementing teams and designing interventions for adaptability is feasible.

Article.ArticleTitle: The pen-and-paper tube figures mental rotation task for patients with trauma-related disorders: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Introduction: Most patients with trauma-related disorders have intrusive memories (IMs) of trauma. Recently a new type of digital treatment (imagery-competing task intervention; ICTI) has been shown to reduce the rate of IMs and other symptoms. Here we examine a novel pen-and-paper ICTI called 'Tube figures' suitable for settings without digital resources.Methods and analysis: Forty patients with trauma-related disorders participated in a mono-centre, single-blind randomized controlled trial with two parallel arms (Intervention: Tube figures ICTI vs. Control: Wikipedia). Participants selected one IM to monitor daily for four weeks. After two weeks, a single intervention or control session was administered for the monitored IM. Primary outcome was the frequency of the IM monitored per week for the two weeks following the intervention. A mixed Poisson regression was fitted with intervention and study phase (baseline/pre- and post-intervention) as fixed effects and a random effect for patient. Severity of symptoms at study start and two weeks after randomization was assessed with the PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5).Results: The frequency of the monitored IM per week reduced significantly more after the intervention versus control (22% versus 2% reduction in the two weeks post-intervention compared to two weeks pre-intervention, respectively). PCL-5 score reduced significantly more after intervention (53-38) than control (55-47).Discussion: This single-session pen-and-paper Tube figures ICTI reduced IM frequency and trauma-related symptoms, consistent with digital ICTI studies. Limitations include the reliance on self-report measures and only having data for the two weeks after intervention. Future studies should explore the different components of the intervention and test practical aspects that could promote its use in low-resource settings.

OtherAbstract.AbstractText: Breaking the cycle of intrusive memories: Many people struggling with the aftermath of trauma experience distressing, involuntary ‘mental images’ of the event. This study provides first evidence that a simple visuospatial task can significantly reduce the frequency of these painful memories.Science for a low-tech solution: While previous treatments required computers or smartphones, this research successfully adapted the method into a ‘pen-and-paper’ format using pictures of 3D figures. This makes the treatment accessible to anyone, anywhere – even in areas without electricity or internet.Single session intervention: In a controlled clinical trial, patients with trauma-related disorders using this ‘mental rotation’ task saw a 22% drop in weekly intrusive memories after just one session. The intervention is easy to use and offers a promising new tool for global mental health.

Introducción: La mayoría de los pacientes con trastorno relacionados con trauma tienen recuerdos intrusivos (RIs) del trauma. Recientemente, se ha demostrado que un nuevo tipo de tratamiento digital (intervención basada en tareas de competencia de imágenes; ICTI), reduce la tasa de RIs y otros síntomas. En este trabajo se examinó una novedosa ICTI en papel y lápiz llamada “Figuras tubulares” adecuada para entornos que no disponen de recursos digitales. Métodos y análisis: Cuarenta pacientes con trastornos relacionados con trauma participaron en un ensayo controlado aleatorizado uni-centro y de simple ciego con dos brazos paralelos (Intervención: figuras tubulares ICTI vs. Control: Wikipedia). Los participantes seleccionaron un RI para monitorearla diariamente por cuatro semanas. Después de dos Semanas, se realizó una única intervención o sesión de control para el RI monitoreado. El resultado primario fue la frecuencia del RI monitoreado semanalmente durante las dos semanas que siguieron a la intervención. Se ajustó un modelo de regresión de Poisson de efectos mixtos con la intervención y la fase de estudio (nivel basal/pre y post intervención) como efectos fijos, y un efecto aleatorio para paciente. Se evaluó la gravedad de los síntomas al inicio del estudio y a las dos semanas después de la aleatorización con la Lista de Chequeo para TEPT para el DSM-5 (PCL-5). Resultados: La frecuencia del RI monitoreado semanalmente disminuyó significativamente más después de la intervención versus el control (22% versus 2% de disminución en las dos semanas posteriores a la intervención comparada a las dos semanas previas, respectivamente). La puntuación de la PCL-5 disminuyó significativamente más después de la intervención (53 a 38) que en grupo de control (55 a 47). Discusión: Esta intervención de una sola sesión de Figuras tubulares ICTI en papel y lápiz disminuyó la frecuencia del RI y síntomas relacionados con el trauma, en consonancia con los estudios ICTI digitales. Las limitaciones incluyen la dependencia de medidas de autorreporte y solo tener datos para las dos semanas posteriores a la intervención. Los estudios futuros deberían explorar los distintos componentes de la intervención y probar aspectos prácticos que pudieran promover su uso en entornos de bajos recursos.

Article.ArticleTitle: BAK-preserved hyaluronate and corneal nerves.

Abstract.AbstractText: Benzalkonium chloride (BAK) is the most commonly used preservative in multidose ophthalmic solutions, and experimental studies indicate that it damages corneal nerves in a concentration- and duration-dependent manner. No randomized trial has examined whether BAK-preserved artificial tears alter the corneal subbasal nerve plexus in dry eye disease. This analysis asks whether six months of exposure to BAK at the concentration used in artificial tears is associated with detectable alterations in corneal innervation.

In this substudy of a six-month, randomized, single-masked trial, imaging was a protocol-defined secondary objective. We compared 0.15% sodium hyaluronate preserved with 0.005% BAK (BAK HA) with the preservative-free formulation of the same product (PF HA), both instilled pro re nata. Thirty-two of the 43 trial completers underwent in vivo confocal microscopy of the central cornea at baseline and at six months, with 19 receiving PF HA and 13 receiving BAK HA. We analyzed seven corneal nerve parameters using mixed-effects models that accounted for both eyes.

Baseline characteristics and all baseline nerve parameters were comparable. Over six months, no parameter showed a statistically significant between-group difference in change. For corneal nerve fiber density, the change in the BAK HA group exceeded that in the PF HA group by 3.52 fibers/mm² (95% confidence interval, -2.32 to 9.37; P = 0.238).
Our design removes the active drug that confounds the glaucoma literature, but the estimates are imprecise, and the design cannot establish equivalence.
This substudy detected no between-group difference in corneal subbasal nerve parameters.

Article.ArticleTitle: Liposomal Bupivacaine versus Ropivacaine for Rhomboid Intercostal and Subserratus Plane Blocks in Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery: A Randomised Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: The rhomboid intercostal and subserratus (RISS) plane block provides effective early analgesia for video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS), but its duration is limited by conventional local anaesthetics. To compare the analgesic efficacy of liposomal bupivacaine (LB) versus ropivacaine (RP) in RISS blocks for patients undergoing VATS.

In this single-center randomized trial, 93 of the 96 enrolled VATS patients were analyzed (LB, 47; RP, 46). Patients received an ultrasound-guided RISS block with 266 mg LB or 100 mg RP. The primary endpoint was the area under the curve (AUC) of resting Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) pain scores over the first 48 postoperative hours. Secondary endpoints included rescue analgesia rate, and Quality of Recovery-40 (QoR-40) scores.

The resting NRS-AUC over 48 hours was lower in the LB group than in the RP group (66.5 [55.0 to 84.8] vs 112.0 [104.0 to 123.4]; P < 0.001). Similarly, the dynamic NRS-AUC over 48 hours was significantly lower in the LB group (137.0 [116.2 to 149.0] vs 191.0 [183.1 to 208.5]; P < 0.001). The 12-hour resting NRS-AUC was higher postoperatively in the LB group (22.0 [19.0 to 26.2] vs 16.5 [14.0 to 22.0]; P < 0.001), while the dynamic NRS-AUC was comparable between the groups (P = 0.846). The LB regimen also reduced the rescue analgesia rate (23.40% vs 54.35%; P = 0.004) and improved QoR-40 scores 48 hours (172.00 [169.50 to 175.00] vs 162.50 [159.25 to 164.75]; P < 0.001) postoperatively. Both groups experienced similar perioperative complications.

Compared with RP, LB for the RISS block prolonged postoperative analgesia after VATS surgery, and facilitated postoperative recovery, although its initial analgesic effect was less potent. Larger multicenter trials are needed due to the small sample size and the 72-hour follow-up period.
Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500107186).

Article.ArticleTitle: Adjunctive Treatment with Subconjunctival and Topical Bevacizumab to Prevent Recurrence after Excision of Primary Pterygium: A Multi-centric Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Pterygium is a common ocular condition, and excision with conjunctival autografting is the standard treatment. Recurrence after surgery is a known complication, and various adjunctive modalities are used along with excision to reduce recurrence. The use of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) inhibitors, such as bevacizumab (Avastin), has been shown to reduce recurrence in several studies. This study was conducted to evaluate the efficacy of subconjunctival and topical Bevacizumab (BVZ) in preventing recurrence after pterygium surgery.

This was a multi-center randomized controlled trial in which 1,800 patients were recruited and divided into three groups. In Group C, standard treatment of pterygium excision and conjunctival autografting was performed. Additionally, in Group A, subconjunctival BVZ was administered post-operatively and again 1 week after surgery, whereas in Group B, topical BVZ was administered for 4 weeks post-operatively. Recurrence was assessed at six and twelve months, along with visual acuity and complication rates.

Out of 1,800 patients recruited, 332 patients (18.44%) were lost to follow-up. Visual acuity in all three groups showed significant improvement at six and twelve months. The recurrence rate in Groups A and B was significantly lower than in Group C at both the six- and twelve-month follow-ups. The complication rates among the three groups were comparable.

The findings demonstrate that both subconjunctival and topical bevacizumab significantly reduce pterygium recurrence when used as adjuncts to conjunctival autografting, without increasing complications. These results support the role of VEGF inhibition in limiting postoperative fibrovascular proliferation and are consistent with previous studies. Although follow-up losses occurred, the large multicenter design strengthens the reliability and clinical applicability of the findings.
When used as an adjunct, both subconjunctival and topical bevacizumab reduce the recurrence rate following primary pterygium excision with conjunctival autografting.

Article.ArticleTitle: The Effect of Counseling Based on Watson's Human Caring Theory (HCT) on Reproductive Concerns in Women Diagnosed With Cancer: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Despite advances in cancer treatments, fertility loss remains a significant psychological burden, and counseling is often inadequate. This study aimed to examine the effect of counseling based on Watson's Human Caring Theory (HCT) on reproductive concerns and patient satisfaction in women diagnosed with cancer.

This outcome assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial was conducted between October 2023 and September 2024 with 50 women aged 18-45 years diagnosed with cancer, who were randomly allocated to the intervention group (n = 25) or the control group (n = 25). A pre-test, mid-test, and post-test design was applied to the intervention group, while a pre-test and post-test design was applied to the control group. The intervention group received three sessions of counseling based on Watson's Human Caring Theory, whereas the control group received routine care, consisting of a single session of fertility counseling provided at the study center. Data were collected using a descriptive information form, the Reproductive Concerns After Cancer (RCAC) Scale, and the Patient Satisfaction Evaluation Form Based on Watson's Processes of Healing.

At post-test, the intervention group had significantly lower scores than the control group on the total RCAC score (Cohen's d = 0.74) and on the Child Health and Future Concerns and Acceptance Concerns subscales, whereas no significant between group differences were observed for the Fertility and Partner Relationship Concerns and Pregnancy Concern subscales. Participants in the intervention group reported uniformly high patient satisfaction scores; however, interpretation of this outcome is limited by ceiling effects and the restricted discriminative capacity of the measure. These findings were further contextualized through a descriptive summary of participants' open-ended feedback, which highlighted recurring topics of emotional relief, informed decision-making, and practical coping.

In this single-centre trial, counseling based on Watson's Human Caring Theory was associated with lower reproductive concerns in women diagnosed with cancer. Although satisfaction scores in the intervention group were uniformly high, this outcome should be interpreted with caution given the ceiling effect and the limited discriminative capacity of the measure. These preliminary findings require confirmation in larger, multicentre trials with longer follow-up.

Article.ArticleTitle: Acute effects of arabica and chicory coffee on exercise performance and post-exercise biomarkers in young male adults: A controlled crossover study.

Abstract.AbstractText: To compare the acute effects of a single serving of Arabica and chicory coffee with a no-coffee reference condition on exercise performance, cardiometabolic responses, and post-exercise biomarkers in healthy young male adults. Twenty-two moderately active young male adults aged 18-25 years completed a single-blind controlled crossover study. The no-coffee reference session was completed first; the Arabica and chicory coffee order was randomized with a 3-day washout. Beverages (180 mL) were consumed 45 min before a 20-m shuttle-run test. Performance, cardiometabolic variables, and post-exercise LPL, TNF-α, adiponectin, and IL-6 were assessed. Shuttle-run performance, perceived exertion, and estimated VO2max did not differ among conditions (all p > 0.05). No significant condition × time interactions were observed for cardiometabolic variables. Post-exercise LPL protein concentrations differed significantly among conditions (p = 0.038) and were numerically highest after chicory coffee (27.72 ng/mL). IL-6 showed a non-significant trend toward lower concentrations after chicory coffee (38.03 pg/mL; p = 0.094); TNF-α and adiponectin did not differ significantly. Neither beverage improved acute exercise performance. Arabica and chicory coffee nevertheless showed different post-exercise biomarker patterns that warrant confirmation in larger crossover studies.

Article.ArticleTitle: Modelling indirect protection from typhoid conjugate vaccines in the TyVAC-Bangladesh trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: In the TyVAC-Bangladesh cluster-randomized trial, a dose of typhoid conjugate vaccine (TCV) in children aged 9 months to <16 years conferred strong protection against typhoid fever. However, indirect protection among unvaccinated residents was modest and not statistically significanct, raising questions about TCV's effectiveness against Salmonella Typhi transmission and ability to induce herd effects in endemic settings. We hypothesize that this low observed indirect protection could be explained by some combination of transmission across cluster boundaries, limited vaccine protection against infection, and insufficient vaccine coverage. To evaluate these hypotheses, we simulated the trial using a primary transmission dynamic model calibrated against clinical surveillance data, and an alternative model incorporating serological data. Vaccinating 64% of eligible children (the observed trial coverage) induced up to 67% and 54% indirect protection in the primary and alternative models, respectively, depending on the transmissibility of chronic carriers and TCV efficacy against S. Typhi infection. The trial results were consistent with 15% to 85% TCV efficacy against infection in the primary model, and 60% to 90% protection in the alternative model. If adults were vaccinated at the same coverage level as children, we estimate that indirect protection would have increased from 19% to 40%-57%. These findings suggest that TCV confers protection against transmission from acute S. Typhi infections, and that the low indirect protection observed in the TyVAC-Bangladesh trial can be explained by transmission from unvaccinated adults.

Article.ArticleTitle: Testing the Impact of the #Chatsafe Intervention on Young People's Ability to Communicate Safely About Suicide on Social Media: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Suicide-related content online may contribute to social transmission of suicide-related behaviors and interventions designed to improve communication safety may reduce risk and increase help-seeking in young people.

We conducted a randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluating the #chatsafe intervention among young people aged 16-25 years. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to the #chatsafe intervention or the PROSPEct sexual health intervention (control), each comprising 24 pieces of social media content delivered over 8 weeks. Outcomes were measured at three timepoints and the primary outcome was change in safety when communicating online about suicide.

Nine hundred and six participants were included (453 per arm). Post-intervention, mean safety scores changed by 0.04 in the #chatsafe arm and -0.23 in the control arm. The primary analysis showed a non-significant mean difference of 0.27 (95% CI 0.00-0.54, p = 0.051). No significant between-arm difference was observed at 4 weeks post-intervention. Significant improvements were evident in secondary outcomes for confidence in safe online communication and willingness to intervene in the #chatsafe arm.

This first RCT of #chatsafe demonstrates that social media can be used safely and acceptably to improve young people's confidence and willingness to intervene against suicide online, pointing to a potential scalable, under-utilized lever in suicide prevention.

Article.ArticleTitle: Prolonged exposure, eye movement desensitization and reprocessing therapy, and cognitive restructuring versus waiting-list for individuals with PTSD and psychosis (RE.PROCESS): A multicenter, four-arm, assessor-masked, superiority randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Evidence indicates the potential efficacy of trauma-focused therapies for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in psychosis. This is the first randomized controlled trial to evaluate the superiority of Prolonged Exposure (PE), Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing therapy (EMDR), and Cognitive Restructuring (CR) plus treatment as usual, compared to a waiting-list (WL) plus treatment as usual control group.

We conducted a multicenter, assessor-masked, randomized controlled trial in patients with a lifetime schizophrenia spectrum psychotic disorder and PTSD. Participants (N = 162) were randomized (1:1:1:1) to PE, EMDR, CR, or WL and followed up until 6 months post-randomization. Therapy conditions had a maximum of 16 twice-weekly sessions. Primary outcome was researcher-rated PTSD symptom severity (Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5; CAPS-5).

PE, EMDR, and CR significantly reduced PTSD severity compared to WL over time from baseline to 6-month follow-up. At 6-months, adjusted differences and between-group effect sizes on the CAPS-5 were -9.76 (95% CI -16.13,-3.38; p= 0.0029) with d= -0.90 (95% CI -1.36,-0.44) for PE, -11.74 (95% CI -18.04,-5.44; p= 0.0003) with d= -1.04 (95% CI -1.50,-0.58) for EMDR, and -12.72 (95% CI -18.89,-6.55; p= 0.0001) with d= -1.00 (95% CI -1.46,-0.54) for CR. Significant therapy effects were also found for secondary PTSD (-related) outcomes, but not for psychosis.

In comparison to WL, PE, EMDR, and CR were effective in reducing PTSD symptoms in individuals with PTSD and psychosis, with large effects. Replication in larger samples is needed, although these results support expanding access to trauma therapies in this underserved population.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of Group-Based CBT/ERP and ACT on Emotion Dysregulation, Sleep, Anxiety Sensitivity and Psychological Flexibility in Adults With OCD.

Abstract.AbstractText: Cognitive behavioural therapy with exposure and response prevention (CBT/ERP) is the recommended first-line psychological treatment for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). Acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) has emerged as a promising alternative, yet treatment comparisons have primarily focused on symptom severity and even less is known about their effects on other domains.
We examined the effect of group-based ACT and CBT/ERP on emotion regulation, anxiety sensitivity, insomnia and psychological flexibility in adults with OCD.

176 adults with OCD were randomized to CBT/ERP or ACT and assessed with the Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale (DERS), Sleep Condition Indicator (SCI), Anxiety Sensitivity Index-Revised (ASI-R) and Acceptance and Action Questionnaire for Obsessions and Compulsions (AAQ-OC) at baseline, post-treatment, 6-month and 12-month follow-up and analysed with Mixed-Model Repeated Measures (MMRM).
Both treatments showed similar improvements in the four domains across timepoints.

In line with our hypotheses, our results indicated that ACT may be non-inferior to CBT/ERP for all secondary outcomes. However, as the trial was powered for the primary outcome (symptom severity) rather than for these secondary measures, our findings should be interpreted as suggestive. Nonetheless, these findings add to the growing evidence that ACT may be considered a viable treatment for OCD.

Article.ArticleTitle: A randomized, placebo-controlled, double blind Phase 1 trial of the Aβ vaccine, AV-1959R, in non-cognitively impaired participants: prelude for secondary preventive therapy in preclinical AD.

Abstract.AbstractText: Active immunotherapy targeting amyloid-β (Aβ) represents a promising strategy for preventing Alzheimer's disease (AD) in cognitively normal individuals at risk, referred to as the preclinical AD population. However, all Aβ vaccines tested so far in people with disease have faced significant challenges, primarily due to inadequate immunogenicity and insufficient antibody titers required to clear, reduce, or slow amyloid pathology. AV-1959R is a new generation MultiTEP-based Aβ vaccine specifically designed to overcome self-tolerance, provide broad T helper cell support, avoid the activation of Aβ-specific T cells, and elicit high levels of antibodies that selectively target pathological Aβ species in 100% of vaccinated individuals.

We conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1 trial in 16 healthy adults aged 40-60 years. Participants received three intramuscular immunizations of AV-1959R (100-300 µg) or placebo formulated with Advax-CpG55.2 adjuvant (Day 1, Week 4, Week 14). Primary endpoints were safety and tolerability; secondary endpoints included humoral immunogenicity, antibody specificity, and isotype profiling. Antibody responses were assessed using validated ELISA and conformational Aβ microarray assays, and antibody kinetics were modeled to estimate durability.

AV-1959R was safe and well-tolerated, with no serious adverse events or ARIA observed. Adverse events were predominantly mild, transient injection-site reactions typical of adjuvanted vaccines. After receiving only two immunizations (priming), all vaccinated participants (12/12) developed antibody titers exceeding those reported for other Aβ vaccines in clinical trials. Induced antibodies selectively targeted pathological Aβ42 protofibrils and fibrils, with weaker binding to oligomers and minimal reactivity to monomers. Modeling based on priming and a single booster immunization predicts that antibody titers will remain 5 times above the baseline for approximately 1 year after priming, supporting an annual booster strategy. Vaccine-induced antibodies were of the IgG isotype and bound to amyloid plaques in human AD brain tissue.

AV-1959R combines a favorable safety profile with potent, selective, and durable anti-Aβ immunity. Its 100% responder rate, induction of high antibody titers, selective targeting of pathogenic Aβ species, and dosing regimen distinguish AV-1959R from all previously discontinued Aβ vaccines and several AD vaccines tested in Phase 1/2 trial with Alzheimer's and/or Down Syndrome individuals. These features classified AV-1959R as the top-tier, scalable immunogenic Aβ vaccine that can be safely used in the preclinical AD population with the evidence of amyloid pathology, with or without tau pathology, aiming to clear, reduce, prevent, or at least slow Aβ accumulation and the onset of Alzheimer's. The protocol for a planned Phase 2 preventive trial of AV-1959R under IND 30925-0004, has received IRB approval. Once initiated, the study will evaluate the vaccine's biological efficacy using established AD brain and blood biomarkers.

Article.ArticleTitle: Acceptability of at-home urine self-testing for bladder health problems: a qualitative study.

Abstract.AbstractText: Haematuria can be a sign of bladder cancer. The YORKSURe feasibility study assessed at-home haematuria dipstick self-testing to inform future effectiveness trials of screening for bladder cancer. Potential participants were mailed self-testing kits and asked to undertake 2-6 dipstick tests. Participants reported results using an app to send the image to the trial team or by phone (matching their test strip colour to a chart and entering the corresponding number). The dipstick tested five parameters and participants were randomised to reveal different panel outcomes. Those with predefined abnormal results were offered further investigation in community clinics. We qualitatively explored the acceptability of urine self-testing, self-reporting results, follow-up tests and the trial design (including revealing/concealing results) in addition to participants' experience receiving the results and barriers and facilitators to the test.

We carried out semi-structured interviews, informed by the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability. We purposively sampled responders and non-responders by participation, test result and socioeconomic deprivation. We analysed verbatim transcripts thematically using the Framework method.

We interviewed 29 people: 21 responders, 6 non-responders, and 2 people who attended an early detection clinic following abnormal dipstick findings. The idea of urine self-testing was acceptable. Many people felt capable of collecting and testing their urine and reporting the results. For others, the stipulations required to collect the urine increased the perceived complexity and the need to self-report the results made the test feel burdensome. Results were understood though some people expected more than one result. Follow-up tests for abnormal results were expected. The most common barrier to testing was timing of the invitation. The most common facilitators were interest in health and past health experiences. There were mixed views on the acceptability of concealing results and concerns around concealing abnormal results.
On balance, most people found the kit and self-reporting acceptable. Simplifying instructions could improve acceptability. Concealment could be further explained in any future trial.
YORKSURe was registered with the ISRCTN on 09 June 2022 under Registration Number 34273159.

Article.ArticleTitle: Impact of rapid pathogen detection in ICU patients with suspected pneumonia on antimicrobial therapy: randomized, controlled open-label feasibility trial (IRISPAT-1).

Abstract.AbstractText: Evidence that multiplex polymerase chain reaction (mPCR) improves antimicrobial therapy and clinical outcomes in the critical care setting is limited. We assessed the impact of rapid mPCR on antibiotic therapy in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients with suspected pneumonia.

IRISPAT-1 was a single center, randomized, controlled open-label trial designed to determine the feasibility, safety, and potential impact of rapid respiratory pathogen detection on antibiotic therapy in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients with suspected pneumonia. Mechanically ventilated adults with suspected pneumonia and treated with new antibiotics within 24 h were randomized to standard care or mPCR using BioFire® FilmArray® Pneumonia Panel in addition to standard care (FA Pneumonia Panel group). Primary outcome was time interval (hours) to appropriate antimicrobial therapy.

Forty mechanically ventilated patients with suspected pneumonia were randomized (20 = standard care, 20 = FA Pneumonia Panel) between July 7, 2024 and October 4, 2025. Median (IQR) time to appropriate antibiotic therapy was shorter in the FA Pneumonia Panel group compared to the standard care group (7 [5-16] vs. 72 [41-140] hours, HR 3.3; 95%CI [1.6, 6.6], p = 0.001). Adherence to treatment algorithm was observed in 90% (18/20) of patients in the FA Pneumonia Panel group. There were no differences in use of broad-spectrum antibiotics, duration of antibiotics, ventilator free days or vasopressor free days and 28-day mortality between treatment groups.
Rapid mPCR with high adherence to antibiotic algorithms shortened time to appropriate antibiotics compared to standard care in mechanically ventilated patients with suspected pneumonia.
Registered at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT06478953) on June 23, 2024.

Article.ArticleTitle: Impact of rhomboid intercostal plane block on chronic pain incidence and acute pain scores after oncologic breast surgery: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Persistent chronic pain after oncologic breast surgery remains a major clinical problem, affecting approximately 25-60% of patients and significantly impairing quality of life. Although the rhomboid intercostal plane block (RIB) has been shown to reduce acute postoperative pain, its role in preventing chronic postoperative pain remains inadequately investigated.

This prospective, single-center, randomized, double-blind, controlled trial included 254 adult women undergoing oncologic breast surgery with or without lymph node dissection. Patients were randomized to receive either a pre-operative ultrasound-guided single-shot RIB using 30 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine or no regional block (control group). All patients received standardized multimodal systemic analgesia. The primary outcome was the incidence of chronic pain at 3 months postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included chronic pain at 6 months, Brief Pain Inventory-Short Form scores at 3 and 6 months, neuropathic pain assessed using the Douleur Neuropathique 4 questionnaire, acute postoperative pain scores, and 24-h postoperative opioid consumption.

Of the 254 randomized patients, 247 completed the study. Chronic pain incidence was significantly lower in the RIB group at 3 months (17% vs 31%; p = 0.009) and 6 months (13% vs 30%; p < 0.001), with reduced neuropathic pain at 6 months. The RIB group had lower 24-h opioid consumption than controls (p = 0.01).

Pre-operative single-shot RIB significantly reduced chronic postoperative pain and opioid consumption following oncologic breast surgery, and may be considered as part of multimodal analgesia to decrease chronic pain incidence, neuropathic pain and improve acute postoperative pain control.
Clinicaltrials.gov (NCT06019325 registered August 17, 2023).

Article.ArticleTitle: Cardioprotective Effects of Low-Dose Bisoprolol Against Anthracycline-Induced Subclinical Cardiotoxicity in Breast Cancer: A Triple-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial Using Advanced Echocardiographic Parameters.

Abstract.AbstractText: Anthracyclines are cornerstone agents in breast cancer chemotherapy. However, they can cause dose-dependent cardiotoxicity, potentially impairing long-term cardiac function. Beta-blockers have demonstrated cardioprotective effects. However, evidence regarding bisoprolol, particularly using comprehensive echocardiographic evaluations, remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the cardioprotective effects of low-dose bisoprolol against anthracycline-induced subclinical cardiac dysfunction in patients with breast cancer.

This triple-blind, randomized controlled trial was conducted in Isfahan, Iran, between January and December 2023. Eligible women with locally advanced breast cancer receiving anthracycline-based chemotherapy were randomized to bisoprolol (2.5 mg/day) or a placebo. Cardiac function was assessed at baseline, mid-treatment, and the end of treatment during a 6-month follow-up period. The evaluated echocardiographic parameters included left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), left ventricular end-diastolic and end-systolic dimensions (LVEDD, LVESD), left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV), global longitudinal strain (GLS), and tricuspid annular systolic excursion (TAPSE). Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS software (version 25.0). Continuous variables were analyzed using paired or independent-samples t tests, and categorical variables were analyzed using the Chi square test. Statistical significance was defined as P<0.05.

A total of 50 patients completed the trial (25 in the bisoprolol group and 25 in the placebo group). LVEF remained stable in both groups. Compared with the placebo group, bisoprolol demonstrated significantly more favorable structural and functional changes, including a reduction in LVEDD (mean change=-0.172 cm; 95% CI=-0.343 to -0.001; P=0.049), LVESD (mean change=-0.156 cm; 95% CI=-0.295 to -0.172; P=0.029), and LVEDV (mean change=-7.920 mL; 95% CI=-15.174 to -0.666; P=0.033); improved GLS (mean change=0.974; 95% CI=0.083 to 1.865; P=0.033); and better preserved TAPSE (mean change=0.168 cm; 95% CI=0.101 to 0.234; P<0.001).

Prophylactic bisoprolol might attenuate early subclinical cardiotoxicity in patients with breast cancer receiving anthracyclines, primarily through the stabilization of LVEDV and a more favorable GLS trajectory.Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials: IRCT20130701013828N8.

Article.ArticleTitle: A Pilot Clinical and Experimental Study of Type I Collagen Matrix Implantation Versus Microfracture for Knee Cartilage Defects.

Abstract.AbstractText: BACKGROUND Microfracture is used to treat cartilage defects but may compromise subchondral bone integrity. Type I collagen matrix implantation has emerged as a potential alternative for advanced (Outerbridge III-IV) lesions, although supporting evidence remains limited. This study combined clinical evaluation with an animal model to validate treatment outcomes. The aim was to compare short-term clinical efficacy and cartilage repair quality of Type I collagen matrix implantation versus microfracture and to validate clinical findings in an animal model. MATERIAL AND METHODS This prospective, randomized, exploratory pilot translational study included both animal and clinical experiments. Full-thickness cartilage defects were created in 18 rats and treated with a blank control, microfracture, or Type I collagen implantation. After 12 weeks, gross and histological evaluations (Safranin O/Fast Green staining) were performed. Concurrently, 36 patients with knee cartilage defects were enrolled in a randomized, single-blind trial (collagen group, n=20; microfracture group, n=16) and followed for 12 months. Lysholm, International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC), and Magnetic Resonance Observation of Cartilage Repair Tissue (MOCART) scores were recorded preoperatively (Lysholm and IKDC only) and at 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively. RESULTS In the animal model, Type I collagen implantation produced superior cartilage and subchondral bone repair compared with the control and microfracture groups. Clinically, both groups showed significant improvement; the collagen group consistently achieved higher functional and MOCART scores (P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS Type I collagen matrix implantation was associated with more favorable cartilage regeneration and better short-term clinical outcomes than microfracture, representing an effective biomaterial-assisted treatment strategy for knee cartilage defects.

Article.ArticleTitle: Home Blood Pressure-Guided Lifestyle Intervention for Elevated Blood Pressure Detected at Workplace Health Checkups: A Randomized Pilot Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Workplace health checkups may identify elevated blood pressure (BP), but a single measurement may not reflect usual BP. We evaluated home BP-guided lifestyle management after elevated BP was detected at a workplace health checkup.

Fifty-eight municipal employees were randomized to home BP monitoring plus physician-led lifestyle counseling (n = 31) or the same counseling without home BP feedback (n = 27). Both groups received two scheduled counseling sessions. The primary outcome was change in systolic BP at the subsequent annual health checkup.

Compared with the control group, the intervention group had greater reductions in systolic BP (between-group difference, -9.9 mmHg; 95% CI, -17.0 to -2.8; p = 0.007). After excluding three participants who initiated antihypertensive medication, the systolic BP difference remained significant (-7.7 mmHg; 95% CI, -14.6 to -0.8; p = 0.029).
Home BP-guided lifestyle counseling may improve management of elevated BP detected at workplace health checkups.

Article.ArticleTitle: Eight-week omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid supplementation alters but does not attenuate exercise-induced muscle damage in older adults: a randomised controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) serves as a model to study muscle plasticity and recovery. Exercise recovery declines with age, and while omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFA) exhibit inconsistent effects in younger adults, the effect in older adults is unknown.

In a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial, 43 healthy, older women and men (65-85 years) ingested 5 mL of n-3 PUFA algae oil (2 g PUFA) or placebo for eight weeks. After eight weeks participants performed a bout of 10 × 10 eccentric-emphasised leg extensions. Outcome measures included quadriceps maximal voluntary contraction (MVC), muscle soreness, creatine kinase (CK) and inflammation (Interleukin-6, high-sensitive C-reactive protein; CRP) assessed at baseline and post-exercise.

EIMD symptoms such as muscle soreness and function were modest and consistent with previous reports in older adults. Overall, n-3 PUFA supplementation did not improve functional recovery. However, a borderline greater MVC loss was observed in the n-3 PUFA group (time × group: P = .064), which resulted from significantly lower MVC in the n-3 PUFA group at 24 h (difference: -10.9%, 95%CI: -21.4;-0.40%, P = .042) and at 72 h (difference: -9.80, 95%CI: -18.3;-1.27, P = .025) post-exercise compared to the placebo. No significant overall group differences were observed for CK, interleukin-6, CRP, but CK concentrations significantly increased from baseline at 24 h post-exercise in the placebo group (change: +81.1%, 95%CI:10.5;152%, P = .014). Habitual physical activity and sex emerged as significant moderators of molecular recovery in an exploratory analysis.

n-3 PUFA supplementation did not improve functional recovery, but different molecular response patterns were observed. Habitual physical activity and sex may be determinants of post-exercise response; this exploratory finding warrants confirmation in larger studies.

Article.ArticleTitle: Prophylactic dexamethasone for prevention of opioid-induced nausea and vomiting in cancer patients: a randomised controlled trial (DEX-OINV Trial).

Abstract.AbstractText: Opioid-induced nausea and vomiting (OINV) is a common, distressing complication when starting opioids in cancer patients, yet evidence for prophylaxis is limited, and no randomised trial has evaluated dexamethasone in this setting. We assessed whether prophylactic dexamethasone reduces nausea and vomiting following initiation of oral morphine in opioid-naïve cancer patients.

In this open-label, randomised controlled trial at a tertiary cancer centre, opioid-naïve adults initiating oral morphine were randomised 1:1 to prophylactic oral dexamethasone or no prophylaxis. Rescue antiemetics were given in both arms. The primary outcome was nausea severity on an 11-point numerical rating scale (NRS) at Days 1, 3 and 5. Secondary outcomes were vomiting episodes and rescue antiemetic use. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle, with multivariable logistic regression adjusting for clinical covariates.

Of 180 patients screened, 150 were randomised (dexamethasone n = 74; control n = 76). Mean nausea severity was lower with dexamethasone at all timepoints (Day 1: 1.36 vs 2.93; Day 5: 0.74 vs 1.53; both p ≤ 0.01), with a number needed to treat of 5 on Day 1 to prevent one episode of clinically meaningful nausea (NRS ≥ 4). The benefit persisted after adjustment (Day 1 aOR 0.38, 95% CI 0.19-0.75). Vomiting episodes were significantly reduced on Day 1. No serious adverse events occurred, and no patient discontinued treatment because of an adverse event.

Prophylactic dexamethasone was associated with lower nausea severity during the critical early period of oral morphine initiation and was well tolerated. Dexamethasone is a widely available and inexpensive agent that warrants confirmation in larger multicentre trials.

Article.ArticleTitle: Clinical efficacy of warm acupuncture on wind-cold-dampness rheumatoid arthritis.

Abstract.AbstractText: The current study aimed to explore the clinical efficacy of warm acupuncture in the management of wind-cold-dampness rheumatoid arthritis (RA).

Eighty patients diagnosed with wind-cold-dampness RA and admitted to our hospital between January 2024 and December 2024 enrolled in this study. Patients were randomly allocated into two groups: a control group (methotrexate tablets) and a study group (warm acupuncture + methotrexate tablets). Comparative analyses were conducted between the two groups regarding the primary outcomes (clinical symptoms, levels of inflammatory factors, serum RF and ESR levels, and degree of pain) and secondary outcomes (TCM syndrome score, total incidence of adverse reactions and quality of life).

Two months post-treatment, the study group demonstrated significant improvements relative to the control group, including a shorter duration of morning stiffness (P<0.01), a reduced number of painful and swollen joints (P<0.01), lower levels of TNF-α, IL-6 and CRP (P<0.01), lower serum RF and ESR levels (P<0.01), lower VAS scores (P<0.01), lower TCM syndrome scores of joint deformity, joint functional impairment, pain and fear of cold (P<0.01), lower total incidence rate of adverse reactions (P<0.05) and higher WHOQOL-BREF scores of physiology, psychology, society and environment (P<0.01).

Warm acupuncture, when used as an adjunct therapy, effectively ameliorates symptoms, alleviates pain, mitigates inflammatory responses, enhances quality of life, and exhibits a high safety profile in the treatment of RA.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of external diaphragm pacing combined with breathing training on pulmonary function of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease patients.

Abstract.AbstractText: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a progressive respiratory disorder with high global prevalence, yet current therapeutic strategies often fail to fully restore lung function or improve quality of life.
This study aimed to explore the effects of external diaphragm pacing (EDP) combined with breathing training in improving pulmonary function and quality of life for COPD patients.

From January 2021 to January 2023, a total of 97 COPD patients admitted to our hospital were selected and randomly divided into the control group (n=48) and the observation group (n=49). The control group received breathing training. The observation group received EDP after 30 minutes of breathing training. The clinical efficacy, lung function, arterial blood gas, oxidative stress, adverse effects that occurred during the treatment process and quality of life between the two both were compared.

Compared with the control group, the observation group had higher total effective rate, higher forced expiratory volume in the first second (FEV1), higher forced vital capacity (FVC), higher FEV1/FVC ratio, lower partial pressure of carbon dioxide in artery (PaCO2), higher partial pressure of oxygen (PaO2), lower malonaldehyde (MDA), higher superoxide dismutase (SOD), higher glutathione (GSH) and higher chronic obstructive pulmonary disease assessment test (CAT) scores.
The combination of EPD and breathing training has a better effect on improving lung function and quality of life in patients with COPD, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic strategy for COPD.

Article.ArticleTitle: Fluid-intolerance signals as bedside safety limits during early septic shock resuscitation: a multicenter randomized trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Fluid resuscitation in early septic shock has a narrow therapeutic index. Signals of fluid intolerance are frequently present during early resuscitation, yet current resuscitation strategies do not incorporate them to guide when to limit fluid administration. We evaluated whether integrating fluid-intolerance signals as safety limits could reduce fluid-induced harm without compromising hypoperfusion resolution.

In this multicenter, open-label randomized trial in three Chilean ICUs, mechanically ventilated adults with septic shock, persistent hypoperfusion, fluid responsiveness, and at least one high-risk criterion for fluid-induced harm were randomized 1:1 to a fluid-intolerance-limited resuscitation strategy or standard care during a 6-hour protocol window. In the intervention arm, before each bolus, fluid-intolerance signals (lung ultrasound score, VExUS, E/lateral e', and central venous pressure) were graded as traffic-light: green received a 500-mL bolus, yellow 250 mL, and red no further fluid. Standard care delivered 500-mL boluses while hypoperfusion and fluid responsiveness persisted. The primary outcome was the change in PaO2:FiO2 from baseline to 6 h (ΔPaO2:FiO2).

Recruitment was discontinued before the planned sample size was reached because continued enrollment was no longer feasible. Among 113 screened patients, 36 of a planned 62 were randomized, and 35 were analyzed (18 standard care, 17 intervention). The intervention group received a lower protocol bolus volume during the 6-hour intervention window than the standard-care group (250 [125-500] vs. 650 [500-1500] mL; between-group difference, - 500 mL [95% CI, - 750 to - 250]). Cumulative fluid exposure from pre-randomization through the end of the protocol window was similar between groups (3375 [2375-3875] vs. 3750 [1875-4851] mL; between-group difference, - 150 mL [95% CI, - 1470 to 1250]). The primary outcome favored the intervention: median ΔPaO2:FiO2 was 40.5 [24.0-58.5] versus - 37.9 [-69.2 to -12.5]; p < 0.001 (between-group median difference + 78.3 points; 95% CI 50.5 to 110.0), and 0-6-hour changes in lactate and capillary refill time did not differ.

Because the trial was stopped early, the effect of a fluid-intolerance-limited resuscitation strategy on oxygenation remains uncertain. A larger trial would be needed to determine whether this strategy improves oxygenation. Such a trial appears feasible.
ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier NCT06568744, registered August 21, 2024.

Article.ArticleTitle: Stakeholders' experiences of the implementation of a multifactorial intervention for safe patient handling and movement: a qualitative explorative and descriptive study.

Abstract.AbstractText: Despite growing evidence for the effectiveness of safe patient handling and movement (PHM) interventions, there is limited insight into implementation and sustainment in routine healthcare. By focusing on stakeholders directly involved in implementation following a cluster randomised controlled trial (RCT), this study provides insight into the mechanisms through which a safe PHM intervention is enacted in practice and how the implementation processes contribute to implementation.

To explore stakeholders' experiences of implementing a multifactorial intervention for safe PHM, and to examine the determinants and perceived outcomes influencing its integration and sustained use in clinical practice.

A qualitative explorative design was employed, using individual interviews with 25 implementation stakeholders (leaders, external facilitators, and implementation team members). The stakeholders were recruited from a cluster RCT evaluating the effectiveness and implementation of a multifactorial safe PHM intervention in Swedish regional and municipal healthcare units. Data were analysed with qualitative deductive-inductive content analysis using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) as a theoretical framework.

The analysis resulted in five deductive categories corresponding to CFIR constructs (innovation, inner setting, individuals, implementation process, and actual implementation outcomes) and 13 inductively developed categories. Determinants influencing the implementation of a safe PHM practice were described. The implementation outcomes reflected implementation, enactment of the intervention in practice, and conditions for sustained use, manifested through perceived changes in safety culture, work routines, and use of patient handling equipment.

This study identified key determinants and perceived outcomes influencing the implementation of safe PHM practices. The interdependence between leadership, facilitation, and participants' active engagement with knowledge shaped the implementation process, enabling translation into practice. Outcomes were reflected in the perceived integration of practices into clinical routines and changes in safety culture, indicating implementation. These findings highlight the importance of organisational and social processes in supporting the sustained use of new practices.
This study is part of a cluster randomised controlled trial, registered at ClinicalTrials.gov on 2 November 2022 (ref NCT05276180).

Article.ArticleTitle: Intra-arterial tenecteplase for acute basilar artery occlusion with sufficient recanalization after thrombectomy: the INSIST-IT randomized clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: The clinical effect of adjunctive intra-arterial tenecteplase after successful recanalization in acute basilar artery occlusion (BAO) remains uncertain. In this prospective, randomized, adaptive-enrichment, open label, blinded-end point, multi-center trial, patients with BAO within 24 h of estimated symptom onset who achieved successful reperfusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) were randomized (1:1) to intra-arterial tenecteplase (n = 75) or control (only received standard medical therapy, n = 69). The primary efficacy outcome was independent ambulation (modified Rankin Scale 0-3) at 90 days; the primary safety outcome was symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH). The trial was stopped early due to safety concerns and lack of efficacy per Data Safety and Monitoring Committee recommendation. Among 144 randomized patients, 143 (99.3%) completed follow-up. At 90 days, independent ambulation was achieved in 40.0% of the tenecteplase group versus 50.0% in the control group (OR 0.67; 95% CI 0.34-1.29; P = 0.23). sICH occurred in 6.2% versus 4.8% (OR 1.31; 95% CI 0.28-6.89; P = 0.73). All-cause mortality at 90 days was 41.3% versus 26.5% (OR 1.96; 95% CI 0.97-4.03; P = 0.063). In this prematurely terminated trial, adjunctive intra-arterial tenecteplase did not improve functional outcomes in patients with BAO.

Article.ArticleTitle: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke: the BRETIS-TNK2 trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during endovascular treatment (EVT) may increase first-pass recanalization and dissolve microcirculatory thrombi, but its efficacy and safety are uncertain. We hypothesised that this strategy would improve functional outcomes versus EVT alone. This phase 3, randomised, adaptive-enrichment, open-label, blinded-endpoint multicentre study aims to evaluate whether intra‑arterial tenecteplase improves clinical outcomes for patients with acute ischemic stroke. Patients with large‑vessel occlusion eligible for EVT within 24 hours of symptom onset were randomly assigned (1:1) to the tenecteplase group receiving intra‑arterial tenecteplase during EVT or the control group receiving EVT alone. The primary endpoint was favorable functional outcome. Of 380 randomised patients (192 in the tenecteplase group and 188 in the control group), primary outcome data were available for 190 and 186 patients, respectively. Favorable 90-day functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) occurred in 40.0% of the tenecteplase group versus 46.8% of the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 0.76, [95% CI 0.50-1.14], P = 0.19). This work suggests intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy did not improve 90-day functional outcomes in this population. (Funded by National Science and Technology Major Project and hospital-initiated grants; ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05657444).

Article.ArticleTitle: Rescue treatment for medium vessel occlusion by intra-arterial tenecteplase: the RESCUE-TNK randomized clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: In patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by medium vessel occlusion (MeVO), intra-arterial tenecteplase may offer a targeted strategy to improve recanalization; we hypothesized that intra-arterial tenecteplase would increase successful reperfusion compared with standard care with a comparable safety profile. This phase 2, prospective, randomised, open-label, blinded-endpoint, multicentre study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of intra-arterial tenecteplase for patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by MeVO. Patients with MeVO were randomly (1:1) assigned to receive intra-arterial tenecteplase or standard care. The primary outcome was successful reperfusion of medium vessel occlusion. A total of 80 patients were randomized to either the tenecteplase group (n = 41) or control group (n = 39). Successful reperfusion reached 61.0% (25/41) in the tenecteplase group versus 28.2% (11/39) in the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 3.98, 95% CI 1.56-10.16; P = 0.004). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 24 h was similar between the tenecteplase and control groups. This work suggests that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increased the probability of successful reperfusion compared with standard care, with a comparable safety profile in this stroke population. (Funded by Shenyang Science Tech Project and hospital-initiated grants; ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05657470).

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects and safety of Korean red ginseng on the clinical course of uterine leiomyoma: A double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Korean red ginseng (KRG) is widely used as a dietary supplement, but its effects on uterine leiomyoma growth and reproductive hormones are unclear. We evaluated whether KRG affects leiomyoma growth, routine laboratory indices, or endocrine profiles in premenopausal women with uterine leiomyoma managed expectantly.

In this single-center, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial, premenopausal women aged 20 to 45 years with a uterine leiomyoma of 1 to 8 cm suitable for expectant management were allocated 1:1 to KRG 3 g/d or matching placebo for 6 months. Participants, investigators, ultrasonography examiners, and analysts were blinded. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in the 6-month change in maximal diameter of the index leiomyoma on ultrasonography, analyzed by analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline diameter. Secondary outcomes were complete blood count, ferritin, liver enzymes, and reproductive hormones.

Between December 2015 and September 2019, 69 participants were randomized (placebo 34, KRG 35) and 61 completed the 6-month assessment (placebo 30, KRG 31); all 8 noncompletions were losses to follow-up. Maximal diameter increased modestly in both groups, with no significant between-group difference in change (mean difference -0.11 cm; 95% confidence interval: -0.33 to 0.12; P = .34); the upper confidence limit lay below the prespecified target difference of 0.33 cm. There were no significant between-group differences in laboratory changes or in baseline-, age-, and body mass index-adjusted log scale hormone ratios, and the multivariate hormone profile did not differ between groups (Pillai's trace = 0.056; P = .68). In exploratory post hoc analyses, the internal correlation structure among hormone changes was similar in both arms. No treatment-related serious adverse event and no discontinuation for intolerance was documented, although adverse events were ascertained passively.

In premenopausal women with uterine leiomyoma managed expectantly, 6 months of KRG supplementation did not meaningfully alter leiomyoma growth, routine laboratory indices, or reproductive hormone homeostasis compared with placebo. Within the constraints of a modest sample size, incomplete characterization of the study product, and passive adverse-event ascertainment, these findings do not establish the safety of KRG, and they support no conclusion regarding nonserious adverse effects.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effectiveness of a Multicomponent Digital Therapeutic Program on Inhaled Medication Adherence in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Poor medication adherence is a critical impediment to effective chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) management and remains challenging to track in routine care. Digital therapeutic interventions may improve chronic disease management through remote monitoring and patient education. However, most existing digital interventions focus on individual components of disease management, and evidence from longer-term pragmatic randomized controlled trials evaluating integrated digital therapeutics in routine clinical practice remains limited.

This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a multicomponent digital therapeutic program combining electronic inhaler monitoring (EIM) with behavioral support in improving medication adherence and symptom-related outcomes among patients with COPD prescribed pressurized metered-dose inhalers, and to assess patient engagement and implementation in routine clinical practice.

In this prospective, open-label, unblinded, randomized controlled trial, patients with COPD prescribed pressurized metered-dose inhalers were enrolled and randomized in a 2:1 ratio to either the intervention group or the control group. All participants received an EIM device to objectively record inhaler use throughout the 24-week study period. Patients in the intervention group also received personalized medication reminders from the EIM, adherence feedback, educational content, and clinician-supported follow-up through an integrated digital management platform based on EIM-derived data, whereas the control group received usual care. The primary outcome was medication adherence over 24 weeks. Secondary outcomes included exacerbations, COPD symptoms, quality of life, and lung function.

A total of 158 participants were randomized, including 106 in the intervention group and 52 in the control group. The median monitoring coverage was 161.5 (IQR 86.3-168.0) days during the follow-up period. The self-reported adherence measured using the Test of Adherence to Inhalers showed no significant between-group differences at any follow-up time point. However, the electronically monitored adherence was significantly higher in the intervention group than in the control group (59.5% vs 33.1%, P=.009). Adherence declined over time in both groups, decreasing from 85.3% during weeks 0 to 4 to 43.0% during weeks 12 to 24 in the intervention group and from 76.8% to 11.9% in the control group over the same intervals, resulting in a progressively larger between-group difference over follow-up. No significant differences were observed in exacerbations, health-related quality of life, symptom burden, lung function, or mental health outcomes. In an exploratory analysis, a significantly greater proportion of participants in the intervention group achieved the minimal clinically important difference in the COPD Assessment Test score than in the control group (odds ratio 2.21, 95% CI 1.11-4.41; P=.02).

The multicomponent digital therapeutic program significantly improved objective medication adherence in patients with COPD over 24 weeks. While most clinical outcomes did not differ significantly between groups, the higher proportion of participants achieving a clinically meaningful improvement in the COPD Assessment Test score warrants further investigation.

Article.ArticleTitle: Efficacy of diadynamic currents versus transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation for transcutaneous tibial nerve stimulation in subjects with overactive bladder syndrome: A double-blind randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: In the traditional treatment of overactive bladder (OAB) with transcutaneous posterior tibial nerve stimulation (TTNS), physical therapists currently use only transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS). However, the literature has commonly replaced TENS with diadynamic currents for various musculoskeletal pain syndromes. Moreover, no literature describes the use of diadynamic currents in the TTNS procedure. Therefore, our study aimed to determine the efficacy of diadynamic currents (DDC) versus TENS for TTNS in OAB Treatment.

A randomized controlled trial was conducted among female patients with OAB aged 18-80 years. Subjects were randomly allocated to control and experimental groups. Participants in the control group received TTNS with TENS, and those in the experimental group underwent TTNS using DDC. Both groups received 8 TTNS sessions, two per week for 4 weeks. We measured pre- and post-intervention improvements using the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire (ICIQ) for OAB and the ICIQ OAB Quality of Life (QOL). The study is registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India under registration number CTRI/2025/12/099269.

The mean age of the included sample was 59.75 years. Pre- and post-intervention ICIQ-OAB and ICIQ-OAB QOL scores showed significant improvements in disease symptoms and quality of life among patients with OAB in both the control and experimental groups. Comparison of improvements between the two groups on the ICIQ questionnaires showed no significant difference (p-values of 0.87 and 0.95). Correlations between patient-related characteristics and improvements in outcome measures were also not significant.

Eight sessions of TENS and DDC, combined with conventional physical therapy, including Kegel and breathing exercises, can reduce OAB symptoms and improve QOL in subjects with OAB syndrome. Diadynamic current can be used as an adjunct to conventional TENS in TTNS for treating OAB syndrome.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effectiveness of dose-matched immersive virtual reality-stationary cycling combined with neurological physiotherapy versus neurological physiotherapy alone in individuals with chronic stroke (CIVIS): A single-blind, randomized crossover trial protocol.

Abstract.AbstractText: Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability worldwide and frequently results in persistent motor and functional impairments, particularly affecting gait and balance. Given the high prevalence and impact of these limitations on independence and quality of life, innovative rehabilitation strategies are needed. Immersive virtual reality combined with stationary cycling (IVR-SC) has emerged as an innovative rehabilitation approach with the potential to improve mobility and functional outcomes after stroke.

To analyze the comparative effectiveness of two dose-matched programs, one combining IVR-SC plus neurological physiotherapy (NP), versus the other consisting of NP alone, in individuals with chronic stroke.

A randomized, single-blind, crossover clinical trial will be conducted. After calculating the sample size, a minimum of 8 participants with chronic stroke (≥6 months), hemiparesis, and gait and balance impairments will be randomly assigned to one of two sequences of intervention. Each participant will receive both neurological physiotherapy and IVR-SC across two 4-week intervention periods separated by a washout period (4 weeks). Each intervention period consists of 8 sessions delivered over a 4-week period, with each session lasting 60 minutes. The primary outcome will be gait quality, assessed using Wisconsin Gait Scale (WGS), while secondary outcomes will include walking endurance, balance, motor function, and muscle tone. Clinical outcomes will be assessed at baseline and after each intervention period. Satisfaction with using the IVR-SC intervention will also be evaluated. Statistical analyses will follow an intention-to-treat approach using a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) with treatment, period, sequence, baseline, and center as fixed effects, and participant as a random effect. Statistical significance will be set at p < 0.05. An individual responder analysis will be performed to determine if participants exceeded the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) of 2.25 points on the WGS.

This study will contribute to understanding the potential comparative effects of IVR-SC in stroke rehabilitation. Given the heterogeneity of individuals with stroke, which may limit the conclusiveness of findings in parallel-group studies, the crossover design allows each participant to serve as their own control, reducing inter-individual variability and strengthening the interpretation of the results. If effective, IVR-SC could represent a feasible and scalable option for partially replacing NP within standard neurorehabilitation, with potential for implementation in both clinical and home-based settings.

ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT07529665. Article.ArticleTitle: Efficacy of tranexamic acid in reducing perioperative blood loss and transfusion requirements following limb-salvage surgery for bone tumors: A randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: BackgroundLimb salvage surgery with endoprosthetic reconstruction for malignant bone tumors is frequently associated with substantial perioperative blood loss and high transfusion requirements. Although tranexamic acid (TXA) has demonstrated efficacy in reducing blood loss in total joint arthroplasty, high-level evidence supporting its use in orthopaedic oncology remains limited.MethodsWe conducted a prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial between April 2023 and September 2025. Thirty-six patients undergoing tumor resection and endoprosthetic reconstruction of the femur(Proximal/distal/total), proximal tibia, or proximal humerus were randomized to receive either intravenous TXA (15 mg/kg at induction; n = 18) or placebo (n = 18). The primary outcome was calculated total blood loss at 72 hours using the hemoglobin balance method. Secondary outcomes included transfusion requirements, postoperative hemoglobin concentration, drain output, hospital stay, wound complications, and thromboembolic events. All patients completed a minimum follow-up of six weeks.ResultsMean calculated blood loss at 72 hours was lower in the TXA group than in the control group (995 ± 324 mL versus 1708 ± 508 mL; mean difference 713 mL; p < 0.001). Patients receiving TXA required fewer packed red blood cell transfusions (1.1 ± 0.7 versus 1.7 ± 0.7 units; mean difference 0.6 units; p = 0.01). Postoperative hemoglobin concentration was higher in the TXA group (9.3 ± 1.1 versus 8.7 ± 0.9 g/dL), although this difference was not significant (p = 0.073). No differences were observed in drain output, wound complications, or hospital stay. No symptomatic deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism occurred in either group.ConclusionIn this single-center randomized controlled trial, tranexamic acid was associated with reduced calculated total blood loss at 72 hours. However, the relatively small sample size limits conclusions regarding uncommon adverse events. Larger multicenter randomized controlled trials are warranted to confirm these findings and further evaluate safety across diverse orthopaedic oncology settings.

Article.ArticleTitle: Testing the EQ-HWB-9 with seven-day versus today recall periods in dementia: variability and recall adherence under health fluctuations.

Abstract.AbstractText: To compare a "7-DAY" and "TODAY" recall period of the EQ-HWB-9 in people living with dementia (PlwD) with regard to day-to-day health changes (health fluctuations) and recall period adherence.

In this mixed-methods study, PlwD-caregiver dyads from German primary care were randomized to complete the EQ-HWB-9 (self- and proxy-proxy report) using either a "7-day" or "today" recall period over a two-week time period on day 1, day seven and day 14. In addition, caregivers recorded daily health fluctuations over 14 days via a diary. Health fluctuations were examined in relation to EQ-HWB-9 score variability and recall adherence, which was assessed via semi-structured caregiver interviews. Quantitative analyses included recall group comparisons, effect sizes, and variance analyses.

Seventy-four dyads were included (PlwD mean age 77 years; 41.9% female; caregiver mean age 71 years; 71.6% female). Proxy EQ-HWB-9 scores were higher (worse health) than self-reports and higher with the "7-day" versus "today" recall. Caregivers reported at least one health fluctuation in 92% of PlwD; fluctuations occurred in 41% of daily assessments. Greater diary-documented fluctuation was associated with higher EQ-HWB-9 score variability. Recall adherence differed by health fluctuation status: caregivers of PlwD with no to low health fluctuations favored TODAY, whereas those of PlwD with high health fluctuations favored the 7-DAY recall time frame.
No single recall period appears optimal for all PlwD. Recall period selection should consider individual health fluctuation patterns to improve the performance of HRQoL assessments in dementia.

OtherAbstract.AbstractText: People living with dementia (PlwD) often experience recurrent, often unpredictable, day-to-day changes in their health, with some days better (e.g. better memory), others worse (e.g. aggressive behaviour), so-called health fluctuations. Measuring the quality of life in PlwD has become an essential goal in the treatment and research of dementia. Nevertheless, it is unknown how quality-of-life questionnaires can capture these day-to-day changes in PlwD across different recall periods. In our study, we compared a "7-day" recall period with a “today” recall period using the EQ-HWB-9 questionnaire, an instrument of health and well-being. PlwD and their caregivers completed the questionnaire over 2 weeks, on days 1, 7, and 14. At the same time, caregivers kept a daily diary documenting whether the PlwD’s health had improved, worsened, or stayed the same compared to the previous day. We found that health fluctuations were very common: caregivers reported to perceive at least one change in most of PlwD, which are often related to exhaustion, depression and cognitive changes. We also found that caregivers who document no to low health fluctuations are more likely to use the today recall period than those who report greater day-to-day changes in PlwD. These caregivers often adhere to the 7-day recall time frame. We conclude that the choice of recall periods matters. In conditions like dementia, where health can change frequently, selecting an appropriate recall period is essential for accurately capturing quality of life.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of CT-guided Radiofrequency Versus Microwave Ablation on Pulmonary Function in Individuals with Pulmonary Tumors: A Prospective Multicenter Randomized Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Purpose To compare short-term changes in pulmonary function after radiofrequency ablation (RFA) versus microwave ablation (MWA) in participants being treated for pulmonary tumors. Materials and Methods This prospective, multicenter, randomized trial (Chinese Clinical Trial Registry no. ChiCTR2400079813) included participants who underwent CT-guided RFA or MWA between November 2023 and July 2024 at six institutions. Pulmonary function tests, including vital capacity, forced vital capacity, forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1), percentage of predicted FEV1, maximum midexpiratory flow, and single-breath diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide, were performed at baseline and 1 month after ablation. Secondary outcomes included procedure time, complications, and ablation completion rate. Intergroup comparisons and intragroup changes were analyzed. Results Overall, 138 participants with pulmonary tumors (mean age ± SD, 61.9 years ± 9.4; 72 female) were randomly assigned to undergo CT-guided RFA (n = 46) or MWA (n = 92). There was no evidence of a difference between the RFA and MWA groups for any pulmonary function parameter at baseline and at 1 month after ablation (eg, mean FEV1 for RFA vs MWA, 2.27 L ± 0.70 vs 2.26 L ± 0.64 at baseline [P = .92]; 2.24 L ± 0.60 vs 2.20 L ± 0.60 at 1 month [P = .77]), nor was there evidence of a difference in pulmonary function parameters within each group (eg, mean FEV1 with RFA, P = .32; mean FEV1 with MWA, P = .10). The mean procedure time was significantly shorter for MWA than for RFA (48.1 vs 61.4 minutes, respectively; P = .004). The rates of major complications were similar between the two groups (eg, pneumothorax requiring chest tube drainage [20% for MWA vs 26% for RFA; P = .38]). Complete ablation rates were high for both techniques (98% [90 of 92] for MWA vs 93% [43 of 46] for RFA; P = .33). Conclusion RFA and MWA demonstrated similar short-term influences on pulmonary function in participants with pulmonary tumors; however, MWA was associated with a shorter procedure time, with outcomes similar to those seen with RFA. Keywords: Interventional-Oncology, Pulmonary Tumor, Radiofrequency Ablation, Microwave Ablation, Pulmonary Function Supplemental material is available for this article. Article.ArticleTitle: In-the-Bag Stability of a New Hydrophilic Acrylic Toric Intraocular Lens.

Abstract.AbstractText: To assess tilt, decentration, and axial stability of the RayOne EMV toric intraocular lens (TIOL) (Rayner Intraocular Lenses Ltd) over a 6-month follow-up period.

This was a single-center, prospective, interventional clinical trial at the Department of Ophthalmology and Optometry, Medical University of Vienna, Vienna, Austria. A total of 119 eyes from 79 patients with age-related cataract were implanted with a RayOne EMV TIOL. Tilt, decentration, and aqueous depth (AQD) were measured using anterior segment optical coherence tomography (Casia 2; Tomey Corporation) preoperatively, at 1 hour, 1 week, and 6 months postoperatively. Individual changes in tilt and decentration were evaluated using vector analysis.

Mean absolute tilt and decentration values were 5.30 ± 1.38° and 0.14 ± 0.10 mm for the crystalline lens, 5.28 ± 1.27° and 0.21 ± 0.11 mm for the TIOL at 1 hour, 5.22 ± 1.25° and 0.20 ± 0.10 mm at 1 week, 5.33° ± 1.81° (range: 0.90 to 11.10°) and 0.22 ± 0.11 mm (range: 0.04 to 0.57 mm) at 6 months. Mean changes in tilt and decentration from preoperatively to 6 months were 1.59 ± 1.66° (range: 0.09 to 8.43°) and 0.17 ± 0.09 mm (range: 0.02 to 0.47 mm). Seven TIOLs showed a tilt change over 5° within 6 months. A posterior axial shift of 0.13 ± 0.14 mm (range: -0.06 to 0.69 mm) was observed between 1 week and 6 months and correlated with anterior fibrosis severity (P < .001).

Although mean absolute tilt and decentration values were low, in some cases, a pronounced tilt and posterior axial hyperopic shift occurred. Excessive anterior fibrosis development was responsible for these changes.
