Article.ArticleTitle: Therapeutic plasma exchange improves survival in alcohol-related acute-on-chronic liver failure: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) is associated with high short-term mortality and limited therapeutic options. Therapeutic plasma exchange (PLEX) may improve outcomes by removing inflammatory mediators, but randomized evidence in ACLF is limited. This study evaluated the efficacy of PLEX in alcohol-related ACLF (A-ACLF).

In this randomized controlled trial, 100 patients with A-ACLF were randomized (1 : 1) to PLEX plus standard medical therapy (SMT) or SMT alone. PLEX was performed for up to three sessions. Coprimary outcomes were in-hospital mortality and 30-day survival. Secondary outcomes included hospital stay, ventilator requirement, and longitudinal changes in disease severity scores and laboratory parameters.

All 100 patients (PLEX n = 50; SMT n = 50) completed follow-up. In-hospital mortality was lower with PLEX [24 vs. 52%; P = 0.007], with an absolute risk reduction of 28% (number needed to treat: 3.6). Thirty-day survival was higher with PLEX (72 vs. 36%; P < 0.001), with an adjusted hazard ratio for mortality of 0.43 (P = 0.003). Significant improvements were observed in the model for end-stage liver disease sodium, Asian Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver ACLF Research Consortium, and Child-Turcotte-Pugh scores, and in international normalized ratio, creatinine, lactate, ammonia, and von Willebrand factor (all P < 0.001 for interaction). Hospital stay was shorter with PLEX (19 vs. 24 days; P = 0.023). No major PLEX-related adverse events were observed.
PLEX improves short-term survival and disease severity in A-ACLF and may be a valuable therapeutic option where transplantation is limited.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of a dietary behaviour change education intervention on iron status and linear growth in children aged 6 to 59 months: a cluster-randomised controlled trial in rural Ethiopia.

Abstract.AbstractText: Food insecurity and limited maternal nutrition knowledge contribute to childhood iron deficiency anaemia (IDA) and stunting. This study evaluated community-based Dietary Intake Behaviour Education (DIBE) for improving iron status and linear growth among children aged 6-59 months in rural central Ethiopia.

A cluster-randomized controlled trial with 1:1 allocation was conducted across 16 community units from April 2021 to January 2023, enrolling 1,012 mother-child pairs. Structured assessments collected data on nutritional status, maternal nutrition knowledge, feeding practices, and related factors. IDA was defined as a haemoglobin concentration below 110 g/L, while stunting was defined as a height-for-age Z-score (HAZ) below -2 SD from the WHO child growth standards. Independent-samples t-tests and generalized estimating equations assessed intervention effects and associated factors.

Baseline IDA prevalence was 18.2%, higher in the intervention group (22.13%) than the control group (14.2%). At endline, IDA prevalence decreased to 6.5% in the intervention group but increased to 20.4% in controls. Baseline stunting prevalence was comparable between intervention (41.5%) and control (40.7%) groups. At endline, stunting decreased to 15.0% in the intervention group but increased to 51.8% in controls. DIBE was positively associated with HAZ (B = 0.744, p = 0.003). Maternal food-preparation practices (B = 0.242, p = 0.020) and IDA awareness (B = 0.237) were also positively associated with HAZ.

Community-based DIBE improved linear growth and coincided with reductions in IDA and stunting. Integrating practical nutrition education into routine child health services may improve nutritional outcomes in resource-limited settings.Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov:NCT04846062.Registered: 15 April 2021, View at: https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT04846062.

Article.ArticleTitle: Tetracaine hydrochloride gel delays and reduces catheter-related bladder discomfort after transurethral resection: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Catheter-related bladder discomfort (CRBD) results from involuntary bladder contractions triggered by both the indwelling urinary catheter and surgical trauma during transurethral resection. Systemic analgesics and anticholinergics are often used but carry risks of side effects. Topical anesthetics like tetracaine hydrochloride gel offer a potential targeted approach, but their efficacy in delaying and reducing CRBD remains unclear.

In this randomized, single-blind study, patients undergoing transurethral resection were allocated to the tetracaine gel group (n = 65) or the lubricant control group (n = 65). Before catheter insertion, three g of tetracaine gel or standard lubricant was evenly applied to the catheter surface. The primary outcome was the time to first-reported moderate-to-severe CRBD after tracheal extubation. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of new-onset moderate and severe CRBD at specified intervals, as well as the patient satisfaction, postoperative pain scores, analgesic requirements, and adverse events. The incidence of moderate-to-severe CRBD stratified by age and procedure type was also analyzed.

The time to first-reported moderate-to-severe CRBD was significantly longer in the tetracaine gel group compared to the control group (30 [10.0-61.3] min vs. 5 [4.8-10.0] min, p < 0.001) among patients who developed this event. The incidence of new-onset moderate-to-severe CRBD was significantly lower in the tetracaine gel group within 30 min (15 [23.1%] vs. 43 [66.2%]; RR = 0.153, 95% CI [0.071-0.332]; p < 0.001) and over the total 24 hours assessment period (30 [46.2%] vs. 46 [70.8%]; RR = 0.354, 95% CI [0.172-0.730]; p = 0.004). A transient increase in incidence was noted in the tetracaine group between 30-120 min (11 [16.9%] vs. 2 [3.1%]; RR = 6.417, 95% CI [1.362-30.228]; p = 0.016). The non-significant interaction test indicates that the effect magnitude of tetracaine gel did not differ by age (P for interaction = 0.392) or procedure type (P for interaction = 0.883). Patient satisfaction at 6 hours was higher (6.7 ± 0.5 vs. 6.2 ± 0.8, p < 0.001), and postoperative pain scores were lower at all assessed time points. No significant differences were found in analgesic requirements, postoperative delirium, infections, or hospital stay.
Topical application of tetracaine gel to the urinary catheter effectively delays the onset and reduces the incidence of moderate-to-severe CRBD in the early postoperative period.

Article.ArticleTitle: Optimizing physician-patient communication through an integrated perspective of prospect theory and the ultimatum game: a controlled study among patients undergoing elective surgery or invasive procedures in a Chinese tertiary hospital.

Abstract.AbstractText: This study developed a structured preoperative communication intervention based on the complementary mechanisms of prospect theory and the ultimatum game. It evaluated effects on risk understanding, trust in physicians, treatment decisions, and related clinical outcomes. A two-campus, campus-level randomized, parallel-group controlled design included 320 patients undergoing elective surgery or invasive procedures at a tertiary hospital in Henan Province, China. One campus was assigned to the intervention condition and the other to the control condition, with 160 patients enrolled at each campus. The primary outcomes were risk understanding and trust in physicians. Secondary outcomes were treatment acceptance, 30-day complications after surgery or invasive procedures, and medical disputes within 3 months. Between-group associations were assessed using multivariable linear regression, logistic regression, and a modified Poisson model. In patient-level adjusted analyses, risk understanding was higher in the intervention group (beta = 2.001, 95% CI: 1.869-2.133). Trust in physicians was also higher (beta =2.703, 95% CI: 2.579-2.828). Treatment acceptance was more likely (OR = 3.491, P = 0.001), and the risk of 30-day complications after surgery or invasive procedures was lower (RR = 0.413, P < 0.001). Because medical disputes were uncommon, the corresponding association requires confirmation in larger samples. Structured preoperative communication based on cognitive calibration and interactional fairness was associated with better risk understanding, greater trust in physicians, and higher treatment acceptance. It was also associated with a lower risk of 30-day complications after surgery or invasive procedures.

Article.ArticleTitle: Intranasal CBT101 demonstrates favorable safety and neurophysiological evidence of central activity in healthy male volunteers.

Abstract.AbstractText: CBT101 is a creatine prodrug under development for disorders driven by impaired neuronal energy homeostasis, with initial development focused on creatine transporter deficiency and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. This first-in-human study aimed to assess the safety and tolerability of single and repeated ascending intranasal doses of CBT101 in healthy male volunteers and explored neurophysiological evidence of central pharmacodynamic activity using quantitative EEG (qEEG) and event-related potentials (ERPs).

This was a randomized, double-blind, single-center, placebo-controlled phase 1 trial including single ascending dose (SAD) and multiple ascending dose (MAD) parts. Forty-eight healthy male volunteers were randomized 3:1 to CBT101 or placebo. CBT101 was administered intranasally at 4.2, 8.4, or 12.6 mg in the SAD part and at 4.2, 8.4, or 12.6 mg/day for 14 days in the MAD part. The primary objective was safety and tolerability. Secondary analyses assessed quantitative EEG (qEEG) and event-related potentials (ERPs) as pharmacodynamic evaluations.

No serious or severe treatment-emergent adverse events occurred, no dose-limiting toxicity was observed, and no clinically relevant safety findings were reported. As expected, plasma CBT101 concentrations were below the limit of quantification in all analyzed samples. qEEG analyses identified an acute post-dose increase in relative beta activity after single dosing. After repeated dosing, the qEEG profile evolved toward a more sustained pattern characterized by beta-1 modulation and early gamma-band changes. ERP/P300 analyses showed a transient decrease in P300 latency, with no statistically significant change in P300 amplitude.

Intranasal CBT101 was safe and well tolerated across the evaluated SAD and MAD dose ranges in healthy male volunteers. Convergent qEEG and ERP findings provided early neurophysiological evidence of central pharmacodynamic engagement. These findings support continued clinical development of CBT101 for disorders associated with impaired neuronal energy homeostasis.
ClinicalTrials.gov, identifier: NCT07050316.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of a parenting and unconditional cash transfer intervention on child development and maternal well-being in urban Bangladesh: medium-term follow-up of a cluster randomised controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Despite extensive evidence that early childhood parenting interventions improve children's development, whether these effects are sustained in the longer term remains uncertain. We measured the medium-term effects of a parenting and cash transfer programme compared to a cash transfer alone on child, parenting, and maternal outcomes.

In the original trial, we recruited twenty clusters in Rangpur City Corporation of Bangladesh and randomised them equally to intervention (parenting and unconditional cash, 299 participants) or control groups (unconditional cash transfer only, 300 participants). Participants were mothers of children aged 6-16 months on enrolment. Here, we followed up mother/child dyads five years after the intervention when children were aged 6.2 to 8.4 years. The parenting intervention involved fortnightly home visits by trained facilitators for one year. Funds for the cash transfer were provided by the Government of Bangladesh. The primary child outcome was IQ, while secondary ones included reading and mathematics skills. Parenting outcomes included quality of home stimulation and mothers' childcare knowledge. Maternal outcomes included depressive symptoms, empowerment, violence exposure and quality of life.

Out of the 599 participants enrolled in the initial trial, 555 (92.7%) mother/child dyads participated in this five-year follow-up. We observed no benefits of the combined intervention compared with cash alone for the primary outcome of child IQ (effect size = 0.11; 95% confidence interval = -0.04, 0.27); for the secondary outcomes, we observed benefits for reading, but not for mathematics skills. We also found benefits for home stimulation, mothers' childcare knowledge, depressive symptoms, and empowerment, but none for mothers' violence exposure and quality of life.

Although we found no benefit for the primary outcome of child IQ, a combined parenting and cash transfer intervention showed medium-term benefits compared to cash transfer alone for children's reading skills, home stimulation, mothers' childcare knowledge, depressive symptoms, and empowerment. However, as these findings are related to secondary outcomes of interest for our study, they should be considered as hypothesis-generating only.
clinicaltrials.gov: NCT03753646 (original cluster randomised controlled trial), NCT07432971 (follow-up).

Article.ArticleTitle: Perioperative tislelizumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy for patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer: patient-reported outcomes in the RATIONALE-315 trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: In the phase III RATIONALE-315 trial (NCT04379635), perioperative tislelizumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy significantly improved overall and event-free survival versus placebo plus chemotherapy in patients with resectable stage II-IIIA non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Here, report prespecified patient-reported outcomes (PROs).

PROs were evaluated using the EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-LC13 questionnaires. A mixed-effects model for repeated measures was used for PRO endpoints at neoadjuvant Cycle 3 and adjuvant Cycles 3, 5, and 7. Time to deterioration (TTD) was also analyzed.

453 patients were randomized to tislelizumab (n = 226) or placebo (n = 227). At adjuvant Cycles 3 and 5, chest pain was maintained with tislelizumab versus worsening with placebo (LSM difference -4.99 [95% CI: -9.06 to -0.93]; p = 0.016) and -4.15 [95% CI: -7.86 to -0.44]; p = 0.028, respectively). At adjuvant Cycle 7, greater improvement in coughing was observed in the tislelizumab arm versus placebo (-5.10 [95% CI: -9.79 to -0.40]; p = 0.034). TTD analysis showed a lower risk of chest pain with tislelizumab (HR 0.58; p = 0.004).
Perioperative tislelizumab improved coughing and chest pain compared with placebo in patients with resectable NSCLC. These data provide additional support of this regimen in this patient population.
www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier is NCT04379635.

OtherAbstract.AbstractText: Non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the most prevalent histological subtype of lung cancer, accounting for approximately 85% of all cases. Even when the tumor can be surgically removed, survival outcomes remain poor, and patients frequently experience debilitating symptoms, including coughing, chest pain, and breathlessness that negatively affect their health-related quality of life. Tislelizumab is an anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody that, when administered alongside platinum-based chemotherapy before surgery (neoadjuvant) and continued after surgery (adjuvant), has demonstrated statistically significant improvements in overall and event-free survival in the phase III RATIONALE-315 trial. This analysis reports the final patient-reported outcomes (PROs) from RATIONALE-315, examining how patients felt throughout perioperative treatment using validated questionnaires assessing global health status, physical functioning, fatigue, coughing, chest pain, and dyspnea. Among 453 randomized patients, those treated with tislelizumab maintained chest pain levels across the adjuvant phase, while placebo-treated patients experienced clinically meaningful worsening. Tislelizumab-treated patients also demonstrated greater improvements in coughing at later adjuvant cycles, with significant between-group differences observed. Time-to-deterioration analyses further confirmed that patients receiving tislelizumab had a significantly lower risk of chest pain worsening compared with placebo. These findings demonstrate that perioperative tislelizumab not only improves survival but also maintains or improves patient-reported lung cancer symptoms, supporting its use in resectable NSCLC.

Journal.Title: International journal of methods in psychiatric research

Article.ArticleTitle: Mindfulness-Based Intervention Improves Cognitive Function in Patients With Schizophrenia in Remitted: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Patients with schizophrenia exhibit deficits in facial emotion recognition (FER), attention, P300, and quality of life (QoL), which severely hinder functional recovery. This study aims to explore the effects of mindfulness-based intervention (MBI) on these outcomes and the potential mediating mechanisms.

In this 8-week randomized, single-blind, controlled study, a total of 70 remitted patients with schizophrenia were randomly assigned to the MBI group or the control group. The Five-Factor Mindfulness Scale (FFMQ), FER, P300 indices, Continuous Performance Test-Identical Pairs (CPT-IP), and Schizophrenia Quality of Life Scale (SQLS) were measured at baseline and week 8 to assess mindfulness levels, cognitive function, neurophysiological parameters, and QoL. Linear mixed models evaluated intervention effects. Mediation analyses used pre-post change scores with bootstrap resampling.

For the primary outcome, MBI significantly improved FFMQ (β = 16.750, 95% CI [7.769, 25.731], p < 0.001). For the exploratory outcomes, significant improvements were observed for P300 latency (β = -63.602, 95% CI [-88.651, -38.554], p < 0.001) and CPT-IP (β = 8.219, 95% CI [4.004, 12.433], p < 0.001). FER and P300 amplitude showed nominal improvements only, and SQLS showed a non-significant trend. A significant indirect effect through FER change was observed for change in SQLS (indirect effect = -6.343, 95% CI [-11.467, -2.288]), but CPT-IP change did not mediate P300 amplitude improvement.

MBI significantly improved the primary outcome of mindfulness (FFMQ) and showed promising exploratory improvements in processing speed (P300 latency) and sustained attention (CPT-IP). FER change may represent a potential indirect pathway associated with change in SQLS. These findings support MBI as a promising cognitive rehabilitation intervention.

Article.ArticleTitle: Cost-effectiveness of onabotulinumtoxinA versus topiramate in chronic migraine in the US: an economic analysis of the FORWARD randomized trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Assess the cost-effectiveness of onabotulinumtoxinA (OnabotA) versus topiramate for the preventive treatment of chronic migraine in US adult patients from a payer perspective.

A multistate Markov model evaluated the incremental costs per headache-day avoided and quality adjusted life-year (QALY) over a 2-year period in patients treated with OnabotA versus topiramate. The FORWARD trial data informed model inputs, including reductions in headache-days, while patients receive OnabotA/topiramate. Treatment discontinuation for topiramate was modeled with data from FORWARD and a randomized controlled trial (RCT) to test a range of values for topiramate. Costs of drug acquisition, administration, and monitoring were calculated from prescribing information and physician fee schedules. The model estimated costs of healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and acute migraine treatment by response level. Sensitivity and scenario analyses explored cost drivers and assessed model robustness.

Our model estimated that OnabotA-treated patients experience 122.56 fewer headache-days (0.34 years) than topiramate-treated patients over the 2-year time horizon. With an incremental cost of $4,639, the incremental cost per headache-day avoided was ∼ $37.85/day, and the incremental cost per QALY gained was $63,646. The estimated cost per avoided headache-day was less than half for patients treated with OnabotA in comparison with topiramate ($116 vs. $246). Sensitivity analyses showed that the incremental cost per headache-day avoided remained below $50 and the incremental cost per QALY gained remained below $100,000 across all tested ranges. Results were similar when using a lower, RCT-supported discontinuation rate for topiramate. In scenario analyses, a longer time horizon and a greater price discount for OnabotA substantially reduced the incremental cost-effectiveness ratios.

OnabotA was a cost-effective preventive treatment of chronic migraine versus topiramate. Although OnabotA had higher drug acquisition costs, these were offset by reduced HCRU costs due to fewer migraines, resulting in a low incremental cost per headache-day avoided versus topiramate.

OtherAbstract.AbstractText: Chronic migraine is a neurological disease affecting approximately 80 million people worldwide, substantially diminishing quality of life and imposing a sizable economic burden. Preventive medications, including onabotulinumtoxinA (OnabotA) injections and oral topiramate, are widely used in clinical practice. Although prior studies have evaluated the costs of modern preventive treatments of chronic migraine, direct cost comparisons between these branded treatments and lower cost generic alternatives remain limited. Using the FORWARD clinical trial data, we evaluated the cost-effectiveness of OnabotA versus generic topiramate in US adult patients. The analysis incorporates direct cost components, including drug acquisition, administration, and monitoring, as well as HCRU and acute migraine treatment costs while patients are on treatment and after discontinuation. Although OnabotA carries a higher drug acquisition cost, the analysis demonstrates meaningful cost offsets driven by reduced HCRU associated with improved migraine control (e.g. $859 due to less HCRU, $1,799 due to less use of acute medication in 2 years). As a result, given that OnabotA results in fewer days with headaches, over time, it may be considered a more cost-effective option than topiramate.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of Application of 2% Lignocaine Jelly and Thermal Softening of Oral Endotracheal Tubes on Post-operative Sore Throat and Hoarseness.

Abstract.AbstractText: Background Sore throat and hoarseness are common after general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation. Although most of them are mild in severity, they still cause major patient dissatisfaction. There are many pharmacological and non-pharmacological methods to reduce it, but only a few have promising results and minimal side effects. Objective To compare the incidence of sore throat and hoarseness in the post-anesthesia care unit and 24 hours after general anesthesia between these groups. Method We enrolled 162 patients scheduled for elective abdominal surgery under general anesthesia. This study compared the two routine techniques used at our institute to reduce postoperative sore throat and hoarseness. Patients intubated with lubricated tubes soaked in room temperature saline were assigned to the Normal Tube (NT) group, while those intubated with tubes soaked in saline warmed to 40°C were assigned to the Thermal Tube (TT) group. Numerical data were analyzed using Student's t-test and ANOVA test, whereas categorical variables were analyzed using Pearson's Chi-square test. Result At Post Anesthesia Care Unit (PACU), sore throat occurred in 24.69% (17.29% Normal Tube (NT) group vs 7.40% Thermal Tube (TT) group) and hoarseness in 9.87% (7.40% Normal Tube (NT) group vs 2.47% Thermal Tube (TT) group). At 24 hours, sore throat was 20.37% (16.04% Normal Tube (NT) group vs 4.32% Thermal Tube (TT) group), and hoarseness 9.25% (7.40% Normal Tube (NT) group vs 1.85% Thermal Tube (TT) group). Conclusion Based on our findings, we recommend routinely using thermally softened endotracheal tubes lubricated with 2% lignocaine jelly for all intubations under general anesthesia, as this significantly reduces postoperative sore throat and hoarseness in the Post Anesthesia Care Unit and at 24 hours.

Article.ArticleTitle: Efficacy of Single-dose Ketorolac in Reducing Pain in Patients Undergoing Double J-stent Removal under Local Anesthesia.

Abstract.AbstractText: Background Double J (DJ) stents are regularly used after different urological procedures. They are mostly removed under local anesthesia using lignocaine gel. Patients often experience significant pain during and after stent removal. Objective To determine the effect of preemptive oral ketorolac on pain relief during and after DJ stent removal by rigid cystoscopy under local anesthesia. Method In this prospective comparative study, patients undergoing Double J stent removal under local anesthesia were randomly assigned to two groups: group A received tab ketorolac 10mg one hour before the procedure and group B received no medications. Stent was removed by rigid cystoscope using 2% lignocaine gel. The pain during the procedure, at first void and at 24 hours were assessed by visual analogue scale (VAS) pain score (0 to 10). The patient's characteristics, pain score and any adverse events were recorded. Result Total of 276 patients (137 in group A and 139 in group B) underwent stent removal. The visual analogue scale pain score during the procedure and at first void was significantly lower in group A as compared to group B (3.0 ± 1.3 vs 3.68 ± 1.5, p < 0.001 and 1.98 ± 1.3 vs 2.55 ± 1.4, p = 0.001). However, the pain at 24 hours was similar between two groups (p=0.626). The demographic profiles, stent laterality, duration of stent and occurrence of side effects were comparable between two groups. Conclusion The use of single oral dose of ketorolac before Double J stent removal under local anesthesia using rigid cystoscope decreases pain significantly during the procedure and at first void with minimal side effects.

Article.ArticleTitle: National support for a healthy checkout policy: a randomised message-framing experiment.

Abstract.AbstractText: Healthy checkout policies set nutritional standards for store checkouts and have been implemented in three US jurisdictions. We compared four message frames, each describing a different rationale for the policy, on adults' support for a healthy checkout policy.

Participants were randomised to one of four message frames: (1) expanding healthy choices; (2) reducing parental stress by removing unhealthy items from child eye level; (3) improving community and child health; or (4) addressing predatory marketing. We used Poisson regression with robust standard errors to examine policy support by message frame and explore variation in support by socio-demographic characteristics.
Online randomised experiment.
A convenience sample of US adults (analytic N 3978) recruited online via quota-matching to approximate national socio-demographic characteristics.

Overall, most participants (65 %) supported a healthy checkout policy. Support was moderately higher (68 %) when the policy was framed as reducing parental stress than addressing predatory marketing (64 %) or expanding healthy choices (61 %; all p < 0·05). Policy support was also higher when framed as improving community and child health (67 %) than expanding healthy choices (61 %; p < 0·01). In adjusted models, overall policy support was higher among adults with Hispanic ethnicity (68 %); incomes >$35 000 (range 66-70 %); a prediabetes or type 2 diabetes diagnosis (67 %); at least some college education (67 %) and residence in the Northeast US (70 %; all p < 0·05).

Support for a healthy checkout policy was high, especially when framed around benefits to child health. Adults with certain socio-demographic and clinical characteristics may especially support healthy checkout policies.

Article.ArticleTitle: Comparing the analgesic effect of fluoxetine plus vitamin e with vitamin e alone on mastodynia due to fibrocystic breast disease: a randomized double-blind clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Mastodynia is a common symptom in women with fibrocystic breast disease and can substantially impair quality of life. Although vitamin E is frequently used for symptom relief, the potential additional analgesic effect of fluoxetine remains unclear. This study aimed to compare the analgesic effect of fluoxetine plus vitamin E with that of vitamin E plus placebo in women with mastodynia associated with fibrocystic breast disease.

This double-blind, randomized clinical trial enrolled 78 women with mastodynia associated with fibrocystic breast disease who attended clinics affiliated with Shahrekord University of Medical Sciences, Shahrekord, Iran. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either vitamin E (400 IU/day) plus fluoxetine (10 mg/day) or vitamin E (400 IU/day) plus placebo for 8 weeks. Randomization was computer-generated, allocation was concealed using identical medication packaging, and participants, investigators, and outcome assessors were blinded to treatment allocation. The primary outcome was breast pain intensity, assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) at baseline and at 1 and 2 months after treatment initiation. Secondary outcomes included breast heaviness, breast itching, and adverse events. Data were analyzed using repeated-measures analysis of variance and appropriate categorical tests. Seventy participants (35 per group) completed the study and were included in the analysis.

Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics were comparable between the two groups. Repeated-measures analysis of variance demonstrated significant effects of treatment group (F (1,68) = 11.056, P = 0.001), time (F (2,136) = 164.321, P < 0.001), and the group-by-time interaction (F (2,136) = 60.996, P < 0.001) on breast pain intensity. No significant between-group differences were observed at baseline or after 1 month of treatment; however, after 2 months, breast pain intensity was significantly lower in the fluoxetine plus vitamin E group than in the vitamin E plus placebo group (P < 0.001). Breast heaviness was also significantly less frequent in the combination therapy group after 1 month (P = 0.009). Three participants in the fluoxetine group discontinued treatment because of adverse events, and no serious adverse events were reported in either group.

The addition of fluoxetine to vitamin E improved breast pain after 8 weeks compared with vitamin E plus placebo in women with mastodynia associated with fibrocystic breast disease. These findings suggest that fluoxetine may be a useful adjunctive treatment; however, larger multicenter randomized trials with longer follow-up are needed to confirm its efficacy and safety.

Article.ArticleTitle: Enrolling middle school staff in the CSTOP Now! cRCT to prevent child sex trafficking: preliminary effectiveness of recruitment strategies.

Abstract.AbstractText: Child sex trafficking (CST) has significant, long-term health consequences for children and their families. Given higher risk of CST for middle school-aged children, the significant time spent by students in schools under staff supervision, and the opportunity to provide CST prevention programming to school staff, our team developed and launched the cluster randomized controlled trial (cRCT), CSTOP Now!. The purpose of this investigation is to examine the effectiveness of recruitment strategies to enroll middle school staff into the cRCT.

Both training conditions were delivered through an asynchronous online learning management system to school staff. A two-stage recruitment began with 50 counties randomly assigned to intervention or attention control conditions. Administrators in middle schools within these counties were contacted and invited into the cRCT; 37 middle schools joined the cRCT. Six school-level staff recruitment strategies were used and evaluated for effectiveness in enrolling participants.

The most effective strategy was champion recruitment (69% of 127 invited enrolled via this strategy), followed by direct email invitations from study personnel to school staff (20% enrolled from 1621 invited). Some school administrators opted to provide global links to staff; approximately 11% enrolled of 447 invited via this method. Prepaid incentive mailers enrolled 3.7% of 1774 invited, while mailers without cash enrolled 0.4% of 1122 invited. A geofenced advertising campaign resulted in 1,068 individuals accessing the study signup webform, yet no school staff joined via this recruitment strategy.

These data can inform others' approach to recruitment in school settings. Multiple strategies were needed because school-based recruitment remains challenging in the post-COVID-19 era due to greater demands on fewer school staff.
This clinical trial is registered at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT05722769), last updated 10/14/2024.

Article.ArticleTitle: Bougie guided versus Endotracheal tube with Stylet guided intubation in critically injured patients with Difficult airway characteristics (BEST trial): randomised clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Emergency airway management in critically injured trauma patients is frequently complicated by distorted anatomy, airway contamination, cervical spine immobilisation, and prior airway manipulation. Although bougie and stylet are commonly used adjuncts for tracheal intubation, evidence comparing their effectiveness in difficult trauma airways remains limited. We aimed to compare first-pass intubation success between bougie-guided and stylet-guided tracheal intubation in critically injured trauma patients with predefined difficult airway characteristics.

In this prospective randomised clinical trial, 188 adult critically injured trauma patients requiring emergency tracheal intubation and having at least one predefined difficult airway characteristic were randomised to bougie-guided intubation (Group B, n = 94) or stylet-guided intubation (Group S, n = 94). All first-attempt intubations were performed by trauma anaesthesia senior residents using video laryngoscopy and a standardised drug-assisted delayed sequence intubation protocol. The primary outcome was first-pass intubation success. Secondary outcomes included time to intubation, rescue airway interventions, need for alternate adjunct or front-of-neck access, and peri-intubation complications.

First-pass intubation success was achieved in 67 of 94 patients (71.3%) in Group B and 63 of 94 patients (67.0%) in Group S, corresponding to an absolute difference of 4.3% points (95% CI, - 8.9 to 17.2; p = 0.53). Time to successful first-attempt intubation was similar between groups (39.55 ± 11.72 s in Group B versus 37.97 ± 13.54 s in Group S; mean difference 1.58 s, 95% CI - 2.80 to 5.97; p = 0.48). Emergency front-of-neck access was required in one patient in Group B. Oesophageal intubation occurred in five patients (5.3%) in Group S and in none in Group B; this difference did not reach statistical significance using Fisher's exact test (p = 0.059). On multivariable logistic regression, polytrauma with facial fractures was associated with increased odds of first-pass intubation failure (adjusted OR 2.54, 95% CI 1.10-5.83; p = 0.028).

In selected trauma patients with predefined difficult-airway characteristics undergoing protocolised delayed sequence intubation with video laryngoscopy, no statistically significant difference in first-pass success was observed between bougie-guided and stylet-guided intubation. Oesophageal intubation occurred only in the stylet group, an exploratory finding that requires confirmation in larger studies.
The trial was approved by the Institute Ethics Committee (IEC-INT-2022/MD-543) and registered with the Clinical Trials Registry of India (CTRI/2022/11/047043).

Article.ArticleTitle: Radiographic, histological, and immunohistochemical comparison of allograft, xenograft, and combined graft in maxillary sinus augmentation: a prospective randomized clinical study.

Abstract.AbstractText: This prospective randomized clinical trial aimed to compare the radiographic, histological, and immunohistochemical outcomes of allograft, xenograft, and combined graft use in maxillary sinus augmentation.

Patients with a residual alveolar bone height ≤ 4 mm in the posterior maxilla were randomized into three sinus augmentation groups: allograft (G2), xenograft (G3), and 1:1 combined graft (G4). A control group (G1) underwent implant placement without sinus lifting. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images were obtained preoperatively, immediately postoperatively, and at 6 months. Residual bone height, initial graft height, and graft height reduction were measured. At 6 months, bone biopsies were harvested prior to implant placement and analyzed histologically and immunohistochemically for osteocalcin (OC), osteopontin (OP), and RUNX2 expression. Correlations between radiographic and immunohistochemical findings were evaluated.

Significant vertical bone gain was achieved in all sinus augmentation groups. Although greater initial graft height was observed in the allograft and combined groups in the early postoperative period, no significant differences were detected among the groups at 6 months (p > 0.05). Greater graft height reduction was observed in the allograft group, whereas the xenograft group demonstrated better preservation of graft height. Histological and immunohistochemical analyses revealed higher osteogenic activity in the allograft group. Moderate positive correlations were found between radiographic height gain and OC (r = 0.62, p = 0.004) and RUNX2 (r = 0.57, p = 0.011) expression.

Allograft, xenograft, and combined grafting approaches provided comparable bone height at 6 months following maxillary sinus augmentation. However, graft height changes and biological activity differed according to graft type. Xenografts demonstrated greater graft height stability, whereas allografts exhibited higher osteogenic activity at six months. Graft selection should consider both radiographic graft height changes and biological healing characteristics.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of 8-week brisk walking combined with table tennis exercise on cardiovascular function in middle-aged and elderly individuals.

Abstract.AbstractText: This study aimed to explore the effects and the underlying mechanisms of an 8-week brisk walking combined with table tennis exercise on the cardiovascular function of the middle-aged and elderly individuals.

Forty-eight middle-aged and elderly individuals were randomly divided into the brisk walking (BW) group, table tennis (TT) group, brisk walking combined with table tennis (BT) group, and the control group. Body composition parameters were assessed using a body composition analyzer. Cardiovascular function was analyzed by pulse wave velocity (PWV), flow-mediated dilation (FMD), and heart rate variability (HRV) assessment. Plasma biomarkers levels were detected by ELISA. We also analyzed 8-week changes in a composite CVD-Z score based on established cardiovascular risk factors.

The BT group showed a significant increase in muscle mass (37.85 ± 7.26 to 39.01 ± 6.67). However, all three exercise modalities exhibited a significant reduction in systolic blood pressure (SBP) and central systolic blood pressure (CSBP), with a decrease of diastolic blood pressure (CDBP) observed exclusively in the BT group (75.82 ± 7.96 to 71.00 ± 6.53). The PWV analysis revealed significant decrease of the carotid-femoral Pulse Wave Velocity (cfPWV), augmentation index (AIx) and augmentation index normalized to a heart rate of 75 beats per minute (AIx@75) in BT group. While both TT and BT improved FMD (5.78 ± 0.87 to 7.30 ± 1.76 and 6.02 ± 0.95 to 8.06 ± 1.45). The HRV analysis showed BT decreased heart rate (HR), increased percent of NN intervals that differ by more than 50 ms (PNN50), standard deviation of all normal-to-normal RR intervals (SDNN), and high-frequency power (HF). An Increase in total power (TP) was detected in all the three exercise modalities. Furthermore, only BT upregulated serum levels of endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+), and downregulated intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1), and vascular cell adhesion molecule-1(VCAM-1) levels. All exercise groups had reduced composite CVD-Z score after 8 weeks, with the BT group showing the largest numerical reduction.

Collectively, the BT intervention elicited the numerically greater cardiovascular function benefits, independent of weight loss, potentially via reducing arterial stiffness, enhancing parasympathetic activity, and modulating key cardiovascular biomarkers. However, the majority of these favorable numerical changes did not reach statistical significance when compared with standalone brisk walking (BW) or table tennis (TT). Meanwhile, several limitations of this trial should be noted, including its small sample size, passive control design and potential selective outcome reporting.

This study was retrospectively registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR) on 28 May 2025, registration number: ChiCTR2500103378, available at: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=268481 .

Journal.Title: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie

Article.ArticleTitle: Video double-lumen tube intubation in a modified lateral position for unilateral video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: We aimed to evaluate and report a protocol for video double-lumen tube (VDLT) intubation in a modified lateral position and evaluate whether it shortens in-room to cut time (IRCT; defined as the time from patient entry to incision) compared with conventional supine intubation in patients undergoing elective unilateral video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS).

We conducted a single-centre, prospective, parallel-group, randomized controlled superiority trial at a tertiary university hospital in Xi'an, China. We enrolled adults aged 18-75 yr (American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status I-III) scheduled for elective unilateral VATS requiring VDLT intubation; exclusions included body mass index > 30 kg·m-2, mouth opening < 3 cm, Mallampati class 3-4, or anticipated difficult airway. Participants were randomized 1:1 to modified-lateral-position (Group L) or supine-position (Group S) VDLT intubation using a computer-generated sequence with sealed-envelope allocation concealment. Operators were unblinded; nonoperator staff collecting postoperative data and the outcome analyst were blinded to allocation. The primary outcome was IRCT.

Sixty-two patients were randomized (Group L, N = 31; Group S, N = 31), and all were analyzed for the primary outcome. Mean (standard deviation [SD]) IRCT was shorter in Group L (18.1 [2.0] min) than in Group S (31.1 [3.3] min), with a mean difference (L-S) of -13.0 min (95% confidence interval [CI], -14.4 to -11.6; P < 0.001). Intubation time was similar (mean [SD], 103 [15] sec vs 97 [15] sec; P = 0.10). Video double-lumen tube malpositioning occurred in 1/31 (3%) cases in Group L vs 15/31 (48%) cases in Group S (relative risk [RR], 0.067; 95% CI, 0.009 to 0.474; P < 0.001). Sore throat within 48 h occurred in 9/31 (29%) patients in Group L vs 18/31 (58%) patients in Group S (RR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.27 to 0.94; P = 0.02).

In patients undergoing unilateral VATS, VDLT intubation in a modified lateral position shortened IRCT. In exploratory analyses, several secondary outcomes favoured this approach. Intubation in a modified lateral position may be a feasible alternative to conventional supine position intubation in these patients.

Article.VernacularTitle: Intubation par sonde à double lumière avec option vidéo en position latérale modifiée pour une chirurgie thoracoscopique vidéo-assistée unilatérale : un essai randomisé contrôlé.

OtherAbstract.AbstractText: RéSUMé: OBJECTIF: Dans cet essai, nous avons cherché à évaluer et à décrire un protocole d’intubation par sonde à double lumière avec option vidéo (VDLT, pour l’anglais video double-lumen tube) en position latérale modifiée, et à déterminer si cette approche réduit le délai entre l’arrivée en salle et l’incision (IRCT, in-room to cut time; soit le temps écoulé entre l’arrivée de la personne opérée et l’incision) comparativement à l’intubation classique en décubitus dorsal, chez la patientèle devant bénéficier d’une chirurgie thoracoscopique vidéo-assistée (VATS) unilatérale non urgente. MéTHODES: Nous avons mené un essai monocentrique, prospectif, à répartition aléatoire, à groupes parallèles, de supériorité, dans un centre hospitalier universitaire tertiaire de Xi’an, en Chine. Ont été admises à l’étude les personnes âgées de 18 à 75 ans (statut physique I à III selon l’American Society of Anesthesiologists) devant bénéficier d’une VATS unilatérale non urgente nécessitant une intubation par VDLT; étaient exclues les personnes ayant un indice de masse corporelle > 30 kg·m⁻², une ouverture buccale < 3 cm, une classe de Mallampati de 3 ou 4, ou chez lesquelles une intubation difficile était anticipée. La répartition en groupe intubation en position latérale modifiée (groupe L) ou en position de décubitus dorsal (groupe S) s’est faite selon un rapport 1:1, à l’aide d’une séquence générée par ordinateur avec dissimulation de l’attribution par enveloppes scellées. Le personnel effectuant l’intervention n’était pas en aveugle; le personnel non opérateur chargé de la collecte des données postopératoires ainsi que la personne responsable de l’analyse des résultats l’étaient. Le critère d’évaluation principal était l’IRCT. RéSULTATS: Soixante-deux personnes ont été réparties de façon aléatoire (groupe L, N = 31; groupe S, N = 31), et toutes ont été incluses dans l’analyse du critère d’évaluation principal. L’IRCT moyen (écart type [ET]) était plus court dans le groupe L (18,1 [2,0] min) que dans le groupe S (31,1 [3,3] min), avec une différence moyenne (L moins S) de −13,0 min (intervalle de confiance [IC] à 95 %, −14,4 à −11,6; P < 0,001). La durée d’intubation était similaire (moyenne [ET], 103 [15] s vs 97 [15] s; P = 0,10). Un mauvais positionnement de la sonde à double lumière avec option vidéo est survenu dans 1 cas sur 31 (3 %) dans le groupe L, contre 15 cas sur 31 (48 %) dans le groupe S (risque relatif [RR], 0,067; IC 95 %, 0,009 à 0,474; P < 0,001). Un mal de gorge dans les 48 heures est survenu chez 9 personnes sur 31 (29 %) dans le groupe L, contre 18 personnes sur 31 (58 %) dans le groupe S (RR, 0,50; IC 95 %, 0,27 à 0,94; P = 0,02). CONCLUSION: Chez la patientèle devant bénéficier d’une VATS unilatérale, l’intubation par VDLT en position latérale modifiée a permis de réduire l’IRCT. Dans le cadre d’analyses exploratoires, plusieurs critères d’évaluation secondaires ont favorisé cette approche. L’intubation en position latérale modifiée pourrait constituer une solution de rechange envisageable à l’intubation classique en décubitus dorsal chez cette patientèle. ENREGISTREMENT DE L’éTUDE: ChiCTR.org.cn ( ChiCTR2500112254 ); première publication le 21 octobre 2025.

Article.ArticleTitle: [Optimization of rehabilitation program for abnormal gait in patients with knee osteoarthritis based on comprehensive assessment of muscle strength and joint stability].

Abstract.AbstractText: Based on a comprehensive evaluation of muscle strength and joint stability, rehabilitation protocols were designed for patients with knee osteoarthritis to investigate their effects on rehabilitation outcomes in these patients.

A total of 110 patients with KOA were enrolled between April 2022 and April 2024 and randomly divided into control group and study group using a random number table. The study group comprised 55 patients, including 30 males and 25 females, aged from 45 to 77 years with a mean age of (63.28±5.32) years, disease duration ranged from 2 to 8 years with an average of (5.46±1.21) years. Among them, 26 had left-sided knee involvement and 29 had right-sided involvement. Patients in the study group received a rehabilitation protocol based on comprehensive assessment of muscle strength and joint stability.The control group included 55 patients, 28 males and 27 females, aged from 46 to 78 years with an average of(64.15±5.43) years old, with a disease duration ranging from 2 to 8 years with an average of(5.39±1.18) years old. There were 27 patients of left-sided knee involvement and 28 patients of right-sided involvement. Patients in the control group received conventional rehabilitation for knee osteoarthritis. Before treatment and after 6 weeks of treatment, pain intensity was evaluated using the visual analogue scale(VAS). Spatiotemporal gait parameters were tested in a three-dimensional gait analysis laboratory. Muscle strength was measured using an isokinetic dynamometer. Joint stability was recorded and determined with an infrared camera system. Knee function was assessed using the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities osteoarthritis index (WOMAC) and the Lysholm knee scoring scale.

After 6 weeks of treatment, VAS in both groups were significantly lower than those before treatment, and the score in study group (4.15±0.54) was lower than that in control group (4.92±0.63), with a statistically significant difference (P<0.05). The percentage of support phase, cadence, stride length deviation, step width, and foot progression angle in both groups were significantly lower than those before treatment, and the values in study group were lower than those in control group. The walking speed in both groups was significantly higher than that before treatment, and the value in study group was higher than that in control group, with statistically significant differences (P<0.05). The maximum single repetition volume, torque acceleration energy, average power, and peak torque of the affected knee in both groups were significantly higher than those before treatment, and the values in study group were higher than those in control group, with statistically significant differences (P<0.05). The knee joint stability index in both groups was significantly higher than that before treatment, and the index in study group (0.97±0.13) was higher than that in control group (0.86±0.11), with a statistically significant difference (P<0.05). After treatment, the knee joint function scores in both groups were significantly lower than those before treatment, and the score in study group was lower than that in control group, with a statistically significant difference(P<0.05).

The rehabilitation program based on the comprehensive evaluation of muscle strength and joint stability can reduce the pain degree of knee osteoarthritis patients, improve the spatiotemporal parameters of gait and knee function, and improve muscle strength and joint stability.

Article.ArticleTitle: [Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation combined with fascia iliaca compartment block for preoperative analgesia in elderly patients with intertrochanteric femoral fractures].

Abstract.AbstractText: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS) combined with fascia iliaca compartment block (FICB) for preoperative analgesia in elderly patients with intertrochanteric femoral fractures.

A total of 90 elderly patients with intertrochanteric femoral fractures admitted and treated between January 2024 and April 2025 were enrolled in this study. The cohort consisted of 55 males and 35 females, aged from 65 to 85 years with a mean of (70.83±5.50) years. Patients were randomly allocated into three groups using a random number table:the conventional group, the block group, and the combination group. The conventional group comprised 28 patients (19 males, 9 females), with a mean age of (71.64±5.66) years, who received conventional analgesic treatment after admission. The block group included 29 patients (16 males, 13 females), with a mean age of (73.03±4.64) years, who received FICB for analgesia within 1 hour of admission. The combination group consisted of 28 patients (17 males, 11 females), with a mean age of (71.75±4.95) years, who received TEAS combined with FICB for analgesia within 1 hour of admission. The numeric rating scale (NRS) scores for pain at rest and during movement were recorded at admission and at 6, 12, 24, and 48 hours post-admission. Additionally, the total consumption of injectable tramadol hydrochloride within 48 hours post-admission and the incidence of adverse reactions, including nausea and vomiting, were documented for all three groups.

At 6 and 12 hours post-admission, the resting NRS scores in the block group (1.86±0.74) and (2.24±0.51) respectively and the combination group (2.04±0.69) and (2.18±0.55) respectively, which were significantly lower than those in the conventional group (5.11±0.83) and(4.79±0.69)respectively(all P<0.05). However, there was no significant difference in resting NRS scores between the block group and the combination group(P>0.05). At 24 and 48 hours post-admission, the combination group showed the lowest resting NRS scores(2.79±0.50) and (2.68±0.55), followed by the block group (3.31±0.47) and (3.10±0.56), with the conventional group having the highest scores (4.64±0.68) and (4.68±0.72). The differences among the three groups were statistically significant(all P<0.05). Regarding the NRS scores during movement at 6, 12, 24, and 48 hours post-admission, the conventional group scored (5.71±0.90), (5.61±0.79), (4.54±0.64), and (4.85±0.89), respectively;the block group scored(2.69±0.76), (3.17±0.60), (3.97±0.78), and(4.82±0.80), respectively;and the combination group scored(2.89±0.83), (2.89±0.57), (3.39±0.50), and (3.82±0.72), respectively. At 6 and 12 hours post-admission, the movement NRS scores in both the block and combination groups were significantly lower than those in the conventional group (all P<0.05), with no significant difference observed between the block and combination groups(P>0.05). At 24 hours, the combination group showed the lowest movement NRS scores, followed by the block group, and the conventional group showed the highest (P<0.05). At 48 hours, the combination group showed significantly lower movement NRS scores compared to both the block and conventional groups (P<0.05), whereas no significant difference was found between the conventional and block groups (P>0.05). At 48 hours post-admission, the incidence of nausea was significantly lower in the combination group (1 patient) compared to the block group (4 patients) and the conventional group (7 patients)(P<0.05). However, there was no significant difference in the incidence of vomiting among the three groups (P>0.05). Within 48 hours post-admission, the total tramadol consumption was significantly lower in the combination group (94.65±39.30) mg than in the block group (124.14±25.43) mg and the conventional group (183.93±33.48) mg (P<0.05).

TEAS combined with FICB is highly effective for preoperative analgesia in elderly patients with intertrochanteric femoral fractures. This combined approach significantly alleviates pain both at rest and during movement, while reducing the consumption of analgesic medications and the incidence of complications.

Article.ArticleTitle: Thoracic epidural versus paravertebral blockade for reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain (TOPIC-2): open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: To evaluate the effectiveness of paravertebral blockade versus thoracic epidural during the perioperative period in reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain.
Open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial.
15 thoracic centres in the UK.
Adult patients undergoing thoracotomy randomised (1:1) to either paravertebral blockade or thoracic epidural using a web based service between January 2019 and September 2023.

Participants in the paravertebral group received three single-shot paravertebral injections of local anaesthetic before incision followed by placement of a paravertebral catheter. Participants in the epidural group had a thoracic epidural catheter placed and loaded with local anaesthetic before incision.

The primary outcome was incidence of chronic post-thoracotomy pain at six months after randomisation, defined as a 100 mm visual analogue score greater than or equal to 40 mm (indicating moderate pain) when considering worst chest pain over the past week. Secondary outcomes included acute pain (visual analogue score of 100 mm) and complications.

770 patients were enrolled, of which 428 (56%) were male (mean (standard deviation, SD) age 66.6 (11.0) years). After 33 exclusions of patients after randomisation who did not proceed to thoracotomy, 737 remained in the modified intention-to-treat population (364 in the paravertebral group, 373 in the epidural group). Six months after randomisation, 59 (22%) of 272 participants in the paravertebral group and 47 (16%) of 292 participants in the epidural group developed chronic post-thoracotomy pain (adjusted risk ratio 1.32 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.93 to 1.86), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI -0.01 to 0.11), P=0.12). During the acute phase, worst and average pain was greater on day 1 with paravertebral blockade (adjusted mean difference 7.7 mm (95% CI 2.8 to 12.5 mm) and 7.0 mm (95% CI 2.7 to 11.2 mm), respectively), but no different on days 2-3. Hypotension was less common in the paravertebral group than the epidural group (12% v 18%, respectively, adjusted risk ratio 0.66 (95% CI 0.46 to 0.94), adjusted risk difference -0.06 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.01)), as was pruritis (4% v 12%, adjusted risk ratio 0.37 (95% CI 0.21 to 0.64), adjusted risk difference -0.07 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.03)), although more participants in this group experienced urinary retention (12% v 6%, adjusted risk ratio 2.21 (95% CI 1.35 to 3.61), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI 0.01 to 0.09)), complications were similar otherwise.

Paravertebral blockade did not reduce chronic post-thoracotomy pain at six month follow-up compared to thoracic epidural. Thoracic epidural provided marginally better acute pain relief one day after the operation, but showed no difference thereafter. Postoperative complications were comparable between groups. The findings support the ongoing use of both techniques.

Article.ArticleTitle: Clindamycin and bacterial load reduction as prophylaxis for surgical site infection after below-knee flap and graft procedures.

Abstract.AbstractText: This randomised controlled trial recruited consecutive patients undergoing below-knee flap and graft procedures. Participants were randomised into three study arms: (1) chlorhexidine wash 4% (preoperative bacterial load reduction) plus placebo antibiotics; (2) clindamycin (450 mg orally, 30-60 minutes before surgery and 6 hours postoperatively) plus placebo wash; and (3) control (placebo wash and placebo capsules; standard care). Primary outcome was superficial SSI within 30 days of excision.

SSI occurred in 14/44 (31.8%) of cases overall: 2/14 (14.3%) in the clindamycin arm; 5/15 (33.3%) in the chlorhexidine arm; and 7/15 (46.7%) in the control arm. With clindamycin, the overall absolute reduction in SSI was 32.4% (95% CI 1.2, 63.6; P = 0.06) and among flap repairs, absolute reduction was 46.2% (95% CI 19.1, 73.3; P <0.05). Absolute reduction in SSI with chlorhexidine was 13.3% (95% CI -21.4, 48.1; P = 0.456). DISCUSSION: Clindamycin reduced SSI compared with controls, particularly in flap repairs. Chlorhexidine resulted in modest SSI decrease.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of Lactobacillus crispatus-Containing Probiotics and Metformin on Insulin Resistance, Inflammation, and Gut Microbiome in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Protocol for an Open-Label Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) affects 9% to 12% of reproductive-age women worldwide, with higher prevalence reported in India. Its pathophysiology involves insulin resistance, hyperandrogenism, and chronic low-grade inflammation, increasingly linked to gut dysbiosis and lipopolysaccharide-driven toll-like receptor 4 signaling. Elevated calprotectin and suppressed acylated ghrelin (AGH) reflect this inflammatory-metabolic disruption. While metformin remains standard therapy, it does not address underlying gut dysbiosis. Lactobacillus crispatus, with its antibacterial and immunomodulatory properties, is a promising but untested gut-targeted adjunct. This trial evaluates whether combining metformin with L. crispatus supplementation improves metabolic and inflammatory outcomes beyond either therapy alone.

This study aims to compare probiotic, metformin, and combination therapy for reducing insulin resistance in PCOS over 12 weeks and assess their effects on gut barrier integrity, microbiome composition, hyperandrogenemia, glycemic control, and clinical outcomes.

This open-label randomized, hospital-based trial at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Bhubaneswar, will assess the effects of probiotic and/or metformin therapy in women aged 18 to 40 years diagnosed with PCOS per Rotterdam criteria. A total of 135 participants will be randomized equally into 3 groups: probiotics only, metformin only, and combination therapy. The 3-month intervention includes metformin (1000 mg per day) and a specified L. crispatus-containing probiotic (2 capsules per day). The primary outcome is the change in Homeostatic Model Assessment for Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR). Key secondary outcomes include changes in serum and fecal calprotectin, AGH, total testosterone, and fecal microbiome profile.

Participant recruitment began in January 2026. As of August 30, 2026, 26 of the planned 135 participants had been enrolled. Enrollment and data collection are projected to conclude by December 2026; statistical analysis will begin after database lock, with study completion anticipated by June 2027 and publication targeted for mid- to late 2027.

This trial will provide critical, mechanistic evidence on whether the targeted action of L. crispatus can work additively with metformin to heal the intestinal mucosal barrier, arrest systemic endotoxemia, and rescue disrupted gut-brain-endocrine signaling. By validating this novel metabolic-inflammatory regimen against localized (calprotectin) and systemic (AGH and HOMA-IR) end points, this study intends to establish a highly integrated, microbiome-targeted therapeutic strategy capable of optimizing long-term metabolic and reproductive health outcomes in women with PCOS.

Article.ArticleTitle: The Impact of Narrative Nursing on Psychological Distress, Coping Styles, and Quality of Life in Patients With Cancer Undergoing Radiation Therapy.

Abstract.AbstractText: To investigate the effect of a narrative nursing intervention on psychological distress, coping styles, and quality of life and provide a basis for improving psychological health and overall well-being in patients with cancer undergoing outpatient radiation therapy.

This randomized controlled trial enrolled 62 patients with malignant tumors who were receiving outpatient radiation therapy at Xiangya Hospital of Central South University in Changsha, China. Participants were recruited from April 2023 to May 2025.

Patients were randomly assigned to the usual care group (N = 31) or the narrative nursing intervention group (N = 31). Both groups received standard outpatient radiation therapy care, and the intervention group underwent an additional six-week narrative nursing intervention. Evaluations were performed using a general information questionnaire, the National Comprehensive Cancer Network distress management screening measure, the Medical Coping Modes Questionnaire, and the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-General prior to the first radiation therapy session and within one week after the final session. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.

A total of 62 patients were enrolled and completed the study. After the intervention, psychological distress scores were significantly lower in the narrative nursing intervention group compared to the usual care group (p < 0.05). Postintervention, significant differences were observed in all coping dimensions (confrontation, avoidance, and resignation) in the intervention group after adjusting for baseline characteristics (p < 0.05). The intervention group also exhibited significantly higher overall quality-of-life scores, as well as improvements in physical, social/family, emotional, and functional well-being, compared to the usual care group (p < 0.05).

A narrative nursing intervention can effectively alleviate psychological distress, optimize coping strategies, and enhance quality of life for patients undergoing radiation therapy in the outpatient setting.

Article.ArticleTitle: Efficacy of Lumateperone 42 mg in Major Depressive Disorder: Subgroup Analysis of a Phase 3 Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Objective: Lumateperone is an FDA-approved atypical antipsychotic to treat schizophrenia, bipolar I or II depression, and major depressive disorder (MDD). Post hoc analyses of a randomized, phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (Study 501) evaluated the efficacy of lumateperone 42 mg adjunctive to antidepressant therapy (ADT) in demographic and clinical subgroups of patients with MDD with inadequate ADT response. Methods: Adults with DSM-5 criteria for MDD with inadequate response to 1-2 courses of ADT, Montgomery- Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) Total score ≥24, Clinical Global Impression Scale-Severity (CGI-S) score ≥4, and Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology-Self-Report 16-item (QIDS-SR-16) score ≥14 were randomized 1:1 to 6-week oral lumateperone 42 mg+ADT or placebo+ADT. Efficacy was evaluated in the overall population and patient subgroups by demographic (age, sex, race, ethnicity, and region) and baseline disease characteristics (MADRS Total score, ADT type, number of ADT failures [in current episode and lifetime], and presence of anxious distress). Results: The modified intent-to-treat population comprised 481 patients (lumateperone+ADT, n = 239; placebo+ADT, n = 242). Lumateperone+ADT significantly improved MADRS Total score (least squares mean difference [LSMD], -4.9; P < .0001), CGI-S score (LSMD, -0.7; P < .0001), and QIDS-SR-16 Total score (LSMD, -2.4; P < .0001) at Day 43 versus placebo+ADT. Lumateperone+ADT significantly improved MADRS Total score (P < .01) across all demographic subgroups and baseline disease severity versus placebo+ADT. Significant improvements (P < .05) in CGI-S, QIDS-SR-16 Total scores, and MADRS response and remission rates were also observed across most subgroups. Conclusion: Lumateperone+ADT demonstrated robust efficacy over placebo+ADT across a broad range of demographic and clinical subgroups of patients with MDD. Clinical Trials Registration. Article.ArticleTitle: The effect of propolis oral care on oral mucositis in intensive care patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: This study aimed to evaluate the preventive effect of adding a propolis gargle to standard oral care on the development of oral mucositis in critically ill patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

This randomized controlled trial included 60 critically ill patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Both groups received the institutional standard oral care protocol with 0.2% chlorhexidine gluconate three times daily. The intervention group additionally received a propolis gargle three times daily for 15 days. Oral mucosal status was evaluated using the total oral mucosa score.

There was no significant difference in oral mucosa scores between the groups at baseline, whereas oral mucosa scores were significantly lower in the intervention group than in the control group at the 7- and 15-day follow-ups (p<0.001).

Adding propolis gargle to standard oral care significantly reduced the development of oral mucositis in critically ill patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. However, because the intervention group received additional oral care exposure, the independent effect of propolis cannot be determined and requires further investigation.Clinical Trial Registration Number: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07426198.

Article.ArticleTitle: The experience of family caregivers when their loved one is home hospitalized: a mixed methods analysis of a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Home hospital has been shown to achieve comparable, if not better, clinical and patient-centred outcomes compared to brick-and-mortar (BAM) hospitalisation. Family caregivers (FCs) play an essential role in delivering home hospital care; however, their perceptions towards the home hospital model remain an active area of inquiry, particularly in rural settings.

We conducted a mixed methods analysis of FCs of patients participating in a multicenter randomised controlled trial of rural home hospital in the USA and Canada. We compared pre- and post-intervention burden among home hospital and BAM caregivers with the Zarit Burden Interview-12 (ZBI-12) scale (n = 20 home hospital, n = 10 BAM). We conducted semi-structured qualitative interviews with home hospital caregivers (n = 19). Qualitative data were coded and analysed using thematic analysis to construct core themes and subthemes.

There was no significant difference in median ZBI-12 scores between home hospital and BAM at admission (4 interquartile range [IQR 2-9.3] vs 5 [IQR 0.3-9.3]; P = .723), discharge (6 [3.3-8] vs 7.5 [2.5-11.8], P = .309), or change from admission to discharge (0 [-2.5 to 3] vs 1.5 [0-3.5]; P = .269). Our qualitative analysis revealed three central themes: (i) The caregiving experience was positively shaped by strong communication and shared decision-making with the care team; (ii) Caregivers described receiving high-quality home hospital care, particularly surrounding patient-centeredness and technology; and (iii) Home hospital was perceived to offer greater flexibility, comfort and psychosocial support compared to BAM hospitalisation.
Home hospital provides numerous benefits for FCs without increasing perceived burden; further work is needed to establish potential supports to optimise their experience.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of remote patient monitoring on PAP adherence and patient-reported outcomes in obstructive sleep apnea: a comparative study.

Abstract.AbstractText: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common condition, and positive airway pressure (PAP) is the standard therapy; however, its effectiveness depends on adherence. Remote patient monitoring (RPM) may improve PAP adherence, but evidence remains limited.

We conducted a prospective, open-label, active-comparator, randomized trial comparing an RPM program with standard of care (SOC) in PAP-naive adults (≥ 18 years) with OSA who owned a smartphone. Participants were randomized 1:1 to SOC (PAP therapy with a standard coaching program) or RPM (PAP therapy monitored through a web-based application with coaching). The primary endpoint was Medicare-defined PAP adherence (> 4 h of use on > 70% of nights during a consecutive 30-day period within the first 90 days). Secondary endpoints included nights with elevated mask leak, patient-reported sleep measures, and patient satisfaction (Likert scale), with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment for multiple comparisons. Given the pragmatic sample size, the study was designed to estimate between-arm differences rather than to test superiority with conventional power.

The 196 participants (98 per arm) were 65% male, with a median (interquartile range) age of 51 (41-62) years and body mass index of 32 (29-37) kg/m². Medicare-defined PAP adherence was 80.6% in the RPM group and 73.5% in the SOC group (difference 7.1% points; p = 0.308). At day 90, the RPM group had fewer nights with elevated mask leak (median 11.2 vs. 14.5; unadjusted p = 0.009; adjusted p = 0.113) and a higher proportion of participants reporting the highest satisfaction with timeliness of support, the coaching program, and issue resolution (unadjusted p = 0.031-0.044). None of these differences remained significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons (all adjusted p ≥ 0.11).

Because of the limited sample size, conclusions are primarily descriptive. Medicare-defined PAP adherence did not differ significantly between RPM and SOC. The RPM group had fewer nights with elevated mask leak and higher satisfaction scores, but these differences were not significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons and require confirmation in an adequately powered trial.

Article.ArticleTitle: Photobiomodulation for radiotherapy-induced dysgeusia in head and neck cancer patients: a pilot randomized clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Dysgeusia is a frequent complication in patients with head and neck cancer (HNC) undergoing radiotherapy and may negatively affect nutritional status and quality of life. This pilot study evaluated the effect of photobiomodulation (PBM) on the management of radiotherapy-induced dysgeusia. Sixteen patients undergoing radiotherapy for HNC were randomly assigned to either a PBM group (n = 8) or a zinc sulfate group (n = 8). Objective taste identification tests evaluating sweet, bitter, sour, and salty tastes were performed at three time points: before radiotherapy (T0), at the 15th radiotherapy session (T1), and at the 30th radiotherapy session (T2). Salty taste was the most affected taste modality in both groups. At T2, sweet taste was correctly identified by 75.0% of patients in the zinc group and 50.0% in the PBM group. In contrast, bitter taste was preserved in 87.5% of patients in the PBM group and 75.0% in the zinc group. Sour taste was preserved in 87.5% and 62.5% of patients in the PBM and zinc groups, respectively, whereas salty taste was preserved in 50.0% and 25.0% of patients, respectively. No statistically significant differences were observed between groups at T0, T1, or T2 (all p > 0.05). Although no statistically significant differences were identified, PBM was associated with better preservation of sour, bitter, and salty taste perception, particularly after the 30th radiotherapy session. These preliminary findings suggest that PBM may represent a promising supportive strategy for the management of treatment-related dysgeusia in patients with HNC undergoing radiotherapy.

Article.ArticleTitle: Feasibility and tolerability of combining 6 Hz transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) at 3.2 mA and digital cognitive training in older adults with mild cognitive impairment.

Abstract.AbstractText: Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) may enhance cognition and potentiate digital cognitive training (DCT) in mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Optimal intensity remains uncertain because higher currents may increase cortical electric fields but raise tolerability concerns. We evaluated feasibility and tolerability of 3.2 mA tACS plus DCT, and exploratorily assessed active versus sham effects on inhibitory control and cognitive transfer.

Ten older adults with MCI received five daily 6-Hz tACS sessions over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex during DCT; ten sham-arm participants from a randomized trial completed identical DCT. Feasibility and tolerability were assessed by adherence, attrition, and side-effect monitoring. Exploratory efficacy used repeated-measures ANOVA with Bonferroni-corrected paired comparisons. Outcomes included antisaccade total errors, verbal and visual memory, and visuoconstructive abilities.

All participants completed treatment (100% adherence). Active-session side effects were mild in 67% and moderate in 23%; no severe events occurred. Side-effect burden was unrelated to DCT performance (p = 0.22). Antisaccade total errors showed a group × time interaction (p = 0.028), favoring active stimulation. Reaction time showed no stimulation-specific effects. Verbal and visual memory showed time effects (p = 0.016 and p = 0.002), whereas visuoconstructive abilities showed a trend-level group × time interaction favoring active stimulation (p = 0.054).

Higher-intensity tACS plus DCT was feasible and well tolerated in older adults with MCI. Exploratory findings suggest that active stimulation may improve inhibitory control and facilitate transfer to selected cognitive domains. Confirmation in the ongoing randomized controlled trial is warranted.

Article.ArticleTitle: Randomized Single-Masked Study of Preservative-Free Versus Preserved Hyaluronic Acid in Dry Eye Disease.

Abstract.AbstractText: To compare the effects of preservative-free hyaluronic acid (PF HA) versus benzalkonium chloride-preserved hyaluronic acid (BAK HA) on symptoms and signs of dry eye disease (DED) using identical formulations except for preservative content.

In this randomized, single-masked, 6-month trial, 47 patients with DED were randomized to receive PF HA or BAK HA. The primary outcome was the change in Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI) score from baseline to month 6. Secondary outcomes included non-invasive tear break-up time (NIBUT), Schirmer I test, fluorescein tear break-up time (TBUT), fluorescein corneal staining (FCS), lissamine green conjunctival staining (LCS), best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), and instillation frequency. Continuous and ordinal outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects and mixed-effects ordinal logistic regression models, respectively.

Forty-three patients completed the study. PF HA produced a greater OSDI score reduction than BAK HA (adjusted change, -14.36 vs. -9.42; P = 0.001), and ∼40% of PF HA-treated patients achieved normal OSDI scores at the final visit, compared with none in the BAK HA group. At the final visit, no significant between-group differences were observed for NIBUT, Schirmer I, TBUT, BCVA, FCS, or LCS. PF HA showed more favorable longitudinal changes in symptoms and selected signs, including OSDI (P < 0.001), NIBUT (P = 0.017), FCS (P = 0.002), and LCS (P < 0.001), indicating a treatment-by-time effect. PF HA was associated with lower instillation frequency (P < 0.001).
Both formulations improved DED signs and symptoms. PF HA provided greater symptomatic relief and showed more favorable longitudinal changes.
These findings support the translation of experimental knowledge regarding preservative-induced ocular surface toxicity into evidence-based therapeutic decisions for long-term patient care.
