Journal.Title: Scandinavian journal of medicine & science in sports

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of Multicomponent Training on Body Composition and Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: We investigated whether 14 weeks of multicomponent training delivered as small-sided soccer improves body composition, cardiorespiratory fitness, and metabolic outcomes in adults with type 2 diabetes. Adults aged 40-70 years (n = 111) were randomized to exercise (n = 66; three 60-min sessions per week) or usual care (n = 45). Constrained linear mixed models estimated between-group differences in change. No between-group difference was detected in the primary outcome, lean body mass (0.04 kg, 95% CI -0.97 to 1.05), or in fat mass, body fat percentage, or HbA1c. Compared with usual care, exercise produced greater increases in relative VO2peak (between-group difference: 2.80 mL·kg-1·min-1, 95% CI 1.69 to 3.92), absolute VO2peak (237 mL/min, 95% CI 143 to 331), and Yo-Yo Intermittent Endurance Level 1 test performance (122 m, 95% CI 12 to 232). Exploratory analyses showed lower C-peptide (-10.3%, 95% CI -19.0 to -0.6) and HOMA2-IR (-10.8%, 95% CI -20.1 to -0.6), and higher HOMA2-%S (+12.2%, 95% CI 0.6 to 25.1), in the exercise group relative to usual care. Exploratory three-way interaction tests provided no clear evidence that glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) use modified the effects on lean body mass, fat mass, or absolute VO2peak. Small-sided soccer improved cardiorespiratory fitness, whereas a benefit for lean body mass was not demonstrated. The metabolic findings require confirmation. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06478173.

Article.ArticleTitle: Impacts of Oliceridine versus Sufentanil on the Quality of Postoperative Recovery in Elective Gynecological Laparoscopic Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Oliceridine is a novel μ-opioid receptor agonist selectively activating the G protein signaling pathway. This study aimed to explore the influences of patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) employing oliceridine and sufentanil on the postoperative recovery of patients undergoing elective laparoscopic gynecological surgery.

This study included 136 patients aged 18-65 years who were randomized to receive elective gynecological laparoscopic surgery under general anaesthesia with administering PCIA with oliceridine or sufentanil. The primary outcome was the Quality of Recovery - 15 (QoR-15) score on postoperative day 1 (POD 1). Secondary outcome measures comprised: the overall benefit of analgesic score (OBAS) on POD 1; time to first flatus; time to first ambulation; postoperative hospital stay; QoR-15 score on POD 2 and 3; PCIA total injected drugs; the number of patients requiring rescue analgesia and rescue antiemetics; VAS scores from T1 to T6, and MOAA/S scores from T1 to T5; the incidence rate of adverse events; perioperative vital signs.

In the primary ITT analysis using multiple imputation (n=136), analysis of covariance adjusting for baseline QoR‑15 score showed that the group O had significantly higher QoR‑15 scores on POD 1 than the group S, with the adjusted mean difference of 11.94 points (95% CI: 10.02-13.86; p < 0.001). Statistical differences between the two groups were observed in POD 1 OBAS score, time to first flatus, time to first ambulation, hospital discharge duration, and QoR-15 scores on POD 2 and 3. In addition, compared with the sufentanil group, the oliceridine group was observed to have a lower incidence of opioid-related adverse events.

In this single-center study of relatively young and healthy female patients undergoing gynecologic laparoscopic surgery, oliceridine demonstrated superior recovery quality compared with sufentanil, with a between-group difference exceeding the 6-point MCID threshold. It also significantly accelerated gastrointestinal recovery, shortened hospital stay.
This study was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400090783).

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of Intravenous Acetaminophen on Preemptive Multimodal Analgesia for Pediatric Osteotomy Correction Surgery: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Children undergoing Osteotomy correction surgery can experience substantial postoperative pain and frequently require opioids. We evaluated whether a single preincision dose of intravenous acetaminophen, added to a standardized multimodal analgesic regimen, reduces postoperative pain and perioperative opioid requirements.

In this prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 96 children aged 6-18 years undergoing elective lower-limb osteotomy correction surgery were randomized 1:1 to intravenous acetaminophen 15 mg/kg or volume-matched 0.9% sodium chloride administered 30 minutes before skin incision. The primary outcome was the incidence of moderate-to-severe pain within 72 hours after surgery, defined as a Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability (FLACC) score ≥4 at any scheduled assessment. The primary analysis used the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population (n=95; 48 acetaminophen, 47 placebo). Secondary outcomes included perioperative opioid consumption, pain intensity, rescue analgesia, patient-controlled intravenous analgesia use, subjective sleep quality, and adverse events. The trial was prospectively registered (ChiCTR2500095363; January 6, 2025).

Moderate-to-severe pain occurred in 8/48 (16.7%) versus 21/47 (44.7%) children, an absolute risk reduction of 28.0% (RR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.2-0.8; P=0.004). Intraoperative remifentanil consumption was lower in the acetaminophen group (median, 0.8 vs 1.3 mg; between-group difference, 0.6 mg; 95% CI, 0.3-0.9; P<0.001). Postoperative 72-hour morphine-equivalent consumption was also lower (median, 90.0 vs 105.0 mg; difference, 14.4 mg; 95% CI, 2.7-26.5; P=0.018). Longitudinal ordinal GEE demonstrated significant group-by-time interactions for FLACC scores both at rest (P<0.001) and during movement (P=0.002), with the analgesic benefit concentrated in the early postoperative period. Subjective sleep NRS scores were lower in the acetaminophen group on POD1 (Holm-adjusted P=0.005), although the overall group-by-time interaction was not significant (P=0.411). No increase in perioperative adverse events was observed in the acetaminophen group.

Preincision intravenous acetaminophen was associated with a lower incidence of moderate-to-severe postoperative pain and reduced opioid requirements in children undergoing osteotomy correction surgery. Larger multicenter trials are warranted to confirm these findings.

OtherAbstract.AbstractText: Corrective bone surgery can cause substantial pain in children, while opioids used for pain relief may cause nausea, sedation, and breathing problems. In this randomized trial, we examined whether a single dose of intravenous acetaminophen given before the skin incision could improve pain control when added to conventional multimodal analgesia. Children who received acetaminophen were less likely to experience moderate-to-severe pain during the first 72 hours after surgery and required less opioid medication both during and after surgery. They also had better subjective sleep quality on the first night after surgery. We observed no increase in perioperative adverse events. These findings suggest that preincision intravenous acetaminophen can improve postoperative pain control while reducing opioid requirements in school-aged children and adolescents undergoing lower-limb Osteotomy correction surgery.

Article.ArticleTitle: Long-term effects of a parenting program for advanced cancer: A randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: This study examines effects over time of a telephone-delivered 5-session manualized parenting education program for child-rearing parents with advanced cancer. Primary outcomes were parents' depressed mood and anxiety, parenting skills, parenting self-efficacy, and child behavioral-emotional adjustment.

A total of 84 child-rearing parents diagnosed with advanced, non-curable cancer were recruited from community and comprehensive cancer centers and service providers serving cancer patients. After obtaining signed informed consent and baseline questionnaires, parents were randomized to an experimental treatment group or to an alternative treatment control group. Data (3, 6, and 9 months) were obtained after baseline. Linear Mixed Models were used to compare baseline with 6- and 9-month follow-ups. Outcomes at 3 months were reported earlier.

Of the 84 parents initially randomized, 24 participants completed all data collection time periods. Mixed model analysis showed a significant change in parenting skills over all time periods that benefited the experimental group. There was also a significant improvement in parents' self-efficacy at 6 and 9 months, which benefited the control group.

This is the first known longitudinal study of child and parent-reported outcomes from a randomized controlled trial of a manualized cancer parenting program for parents with advanced cancer. All results should be viewed with caution given the small sample size and the loss of 71% of the participants from baseline to 9 months. Despite these limitations, Linear Mixed Models analysis showed clinically significant improvements in parenting skills over time compared to an alternative treatment control group.

Article.ArticleTitle: The impact of attire on patient approval of staff in psychiatric services: a randomised survey experiment.

Abstract.AbstractText: Staff attire may influence patient perceptions of staff in healthcare settings. However, little is known about how this applies to psychiatric services. To address this gap, we examined whether different types of attire influence patient approval of staff in psychiatric settings.

Adult patients receiving treatment in the Psychiatric Services of the Central Denmark Region were invited to participate in an electronic survey. Respondents were randomly allocated to one of five groups shown photographs of a: I. Doctor wearing personal clothes, II. Doctor wearing white coat over personal clothes, III. Doctor wearing white coat over scrubs, IV. Nurse wearing personal clothes, or V. Nurse wearing scrubs. Each participant answered seven 'approval' question items on a Likert-like scale (range 0-10) covering competence, credibility, empathy, trustworthiness, willingness to follow recommendations, willingness to approach the staff member and perceived professionalism. Composite approval scores were compared across the doctor and nurse groups, respectively, using pairwise t-tests.

Of the 9310 eligible patients, 1431 (15.4% response rate) completed the full questionnaire. Mean composite approval scores (range 0-70) were highly similar and did not differ statistically significantly across the doctor groups (I. 52 ± 14, II. 53 ± 14 and III. 52 ± 14, respectively; all p ≥ 0.244), nor between the nurse groups (IV. 52 ± 14 and V. 52 ± 15, respectively; p = 0.826).

In this randomised survey experiment, approval ratings were highly similar across psychiatric staff attire. Given this apparent parity, and the advantages in terms of hygiene and correct identification of staff, we believe that more consistent use of uniforms should be considered.

Article.ArticleTitle: Targeted uterine artery infusion of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells for severe intrauterine adhesions: a randomized controlled trial with exploratory translational analyses.

Abstract.AbstractText: Severe intrauterine adhesions (IUA) represent a profound failure of endometrial regeneration, characterized by excessive fibrosis and vascular insufficiency. Mesenchymal stem cell-based therapies show regenerative potential, but clinical evidence is inconsistent, and optimal delivery routes and localized microvascular mechanisms of action in human endometrium remain unclear.

This prospective, randomized controlled trial was conducted from July 2020 to December 2024. A total of 60 women with severe intrauterine adhesions (IUA) were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive targeted uterine artery infusion of bone marrow-derived MSCs (BMSCs) plus hormone replacement therapy (HRT), or HRT alone. The primary outcome was endometrial thickness, with secondary outcomes including clinical pregnancy rate, miscarriage rate, and live birth rate. Histological, transcriptomic, and in vitro functional assays were performed as exploratory analyses to characterize treatment-associated tissue and vascular remodeling.

Compared with the control group, the BMSC group showed a greater increase in endometrial thickness (0.79 ± 0.66 mm vs. 0.20 ± 0.44 mm, P < 0.001). In the exploratory per- protocol analysis among participants who underwent embryo transfer, the BMSC group showed a higher clinical pregnancy rate than the control group (50.0% vs. 23.3%, P = 0.038), while the live birth rate was numerically higher but not statistically significant (34.6% vs. 16.7%, P = 0.122). No serious treatment-related adverse events were observed. Exploratory histological and transcriptomic analyses indicated that BMSC treatment was associated with increased microvascular density and the upregulation of angiogenic pathways (e.g., NOTCH/VEGF). In vitro assays showed increased pericyte migration and pericyte-endothelial association under BMSC-associated conditions.

Targeted uterine artery infusion of allogeneic BMSCs was feasible and was associated with improved endometrial thickness in women with severe IUA. Secondary reproductive outcomes and exploratory mechanistic analyses suggested potential clinical and microvascular benefits, but these findings require confirmation in larger multicenter trials powered for live birth and long-term safety.

Article.ArticleTitle: Comparative effectiveness of cognitive behavioral therapy versus group-based optimism training on psychological outcomes in hemodialysis patients: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Patients undergoing hemodialysis (HD) face significant psychological challenges that affect their well-being. Nevertheless, no comparative investigation has yet examined the efficacy of cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) versus group-based optimism training on psychological outcomes in this population. Hence, this study aimed to compare the effectiveness of CBT versus group-based optimism training on psychological outcomes in HD patients.

This three-arm, parallel-group, randomized controlled trial was conducted from September 2024 to May 2025 with a sample of 135 HD patients. Participants were selected through simple random sampling and were randomly allocated to two experimental groups and one active control group. Prior to the intervention, all three groups completed the relevant questionnaires. The CBT and group-based optimism training programs were then implemented for the first and second experimental groups, respectively, each consisting of eight 90-minute sessions delivered once per week for eight consecutive weeks. The control group received standard educational interventions. Following the completion of the training sessions, the questionnaires were completed again immediately and again two and four-months later. The data were analyzed using SPSS software version 21.

All procedures performed on human participants complied with the ethical guidelines of the relevant institutional and national research committees, as well as the Helsinki Declaration and its subsequent revisions, or equivalent ethical frameworks.

Repeated-measures ANOVA revealed significant time × group interactions for anxiety (η²p = 0.068), depression (η²p = 0.085), optimism (η²p = 0.101), and hope (η²p = 0.073), all p < 0.001. Both CBT and optimism training significantly improved all outcomes versus control (p < 0.001). However, optimism training showed superior long-term effects over CBT for depression (d = 0.45, p = 0.032) and optimism (d = 0.36, p = 0.041), while both interventions were equally effective for anxiety and hope (p > 0.05).

The findings indicated that both CBT and group-based optimism training were effective in reducing anxiety and enhancing hope. Nevertheless, a distinction emerged at long-term follow-up, as optimism training yielded more sustained reductions in depression and greater improvements in optimism. This suggests that, although CBT is effective for acute symptom reduction, optimism training may offer additional advantages for sustained psychological well-being.

Article.ArticleTitle: Efficacy of chlorhexidine vaginal preparation in reducing postoperative infections during emergency cesarean deliveries for women in labor: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Postoperative infections are a leading cause of maternal morbidity after emergency cesarean delivery. This trial explores the effectiveness of preoperative vaginal cleansing via the use of chlorhexidine for reducing these complications in women in labor.

This single-blinded superiority randomized controlled trial included 840 women in labor equally distributed to either immediate preoperative chlorhexidine gluconate 0.05% vaginal cleansing or no-cleansing; 826 were analyzed under a modified intention-to-treat approach. The co-primary outcomes were postcesarean endometritis and surgical site infection (SSI). Secondary outcomes included composite wound complications, postoperative fever, significant leukocytosis, hospital readmission, length of stay, and adverse drug reactions. Effects are expressed as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals, with adjusted, sensitivity, and subgroup analyses for the co-primary outcomes.

Chlorhexidine significantly reduced both co-primary outcomes; postcesarean endometritis (1.9% vs. 6.3%; RR 0.303, 95% CI 0.139-0.662; P = 0.001) and SSI (1.4% vs. 5.4%; RR 0.269, 95% CI 0.110-0.656; P = 0.002); both remained significant against a Bonferroni-adjusted threshold of 0.025. Other outcomes were also reduced, including composite wound complications (3.4% vs. 11.0%; RR 0.307, 95% CI 0.171-0.550; P < 0.001), and readmission for infection (1.4% vs. 6.3%; P < 0.001; RR 0.227, 95% CI 0.095-0.547). The co-primary outcome effects persisted after adjustment and in sensitivity analyses. Treatment effects were in the same direction across premature rupture of membranes (PROM) and obesity subgroups with no significant interaction, although the SSI reduction reached significance overall and in the non-obese stratum but not within the obese stratum.

In this single-center trial, preoperative chlorhexidine vaginal cleansing produced lower rates of postcesarean endometritis and SSI and of related infectious morbidity. As a low-cost intervention that can be integrated into existing perioperative workflows, it is a promising strategy for reducing maternal infection; however, adverse events were not systematically solicited, and neonatal exposure was not assessed. Multicenter confirmation, systematic maternal and neonatal safety data, and cost-effectiveness analysis are required before routine adoption.
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04385680 submitted 9 May 2020, first posted 13 May 2020.

Article.ArticleTitle: Influence of acellular dermal matrix on peri-implant soft tissue phenotype and marginal bone loss following immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla: a randomized controlled clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla is associated with dimensional changes in both hard and soft tissues, which may compromise esthetic outcomes. This randomized controlled clinical trial aimed to evaluate the effect of acellular dermal matrix (ADM) on peri-implant soft tissue phenotype and marginal bone loss following immediate implant placement.

Patients requiring replacement of non-restorable maxillary anterior teeth were randomly allocated into two equal groups. The control group received high-density polytetrafluoroethylene (d-PTFE) membrane coverage, while the study group received ADM. Clinical parameters, including keratinized mucosal width (KMW), mucosal thickness (MT), and supracrestal tissue height (STH), were assessed at 6 months. Plaque accumulation and bleeding were monitored using modified sulcus bleeding index (mSBI) and plaque index (PI) at 1, 2, and 3 months after prosthetic loading. Implant stability was measured at placement and after 6 months. Radiographic outcomes, including marginal bone loss (MBL) and bone width (BW), were assessed using fused CBCT images at baseline and 6 months. In the study group, ADM was inserted into facial and palatal pouches. The primary outcome was peri-implant soft-tissue phenotype at 6 months, assessed by KMW, MT, and STH.

Thirty-three patients were assessed for eligibility, and sixteen patients were randomly allocated into two equal groups (n = 8 per group). All implants survived without complications during follow-up. At 6 months, the study group demonstrated significantly greater keratinized mucosal width (5.9 ± 1.0 vs. 3.3 ± 0.6 mm, p < 0.001), mucosal thickness (1.8 ± 0.3 vs. 0.8 ± 0.3 mm, p < 0.001), and supracrestal tissue height (1.2 ± 0.3 vs. 0.8 ± 0.3 mm, p = 0.012) than the control group. No significant differences between groups were observed in mSBI or PI. Implant stability increased significantly in both groups, with higher values in the ADM group at 6 months (p = 0.010). The study group also exhibited significantly less marginal bone loss, whereas horizontal bone width reduction was comparable between groups.

ADM was associated with improved peri-implant soft tissue phenotype and reduced marginal bone loss compared with d-PTFE membranes while maintaining comparable peri-implant health. These findings support the potential use of ADM during immediate implant placement in the anterior maxilla.
The study was retrospectively registered and listed on www.
gov with registration number (NCT07573020) on 07-05-2026.

Article.ArticleTitle: Biomarker-dependent detection of contrast-associated acute kidney injury after intra-arterial contrast procedures: an exploratory randomized trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) remains a controversial clinical entity, partly because incidence estimates vary according to the diagnostic criteria and biomarkers used. Serum creatinine-based definitions may underestimate early functional renal impairment after contrast exposure, whereas cystatin C has emerged as a more sensitive early biomarker of glomerular filtration changes. This study aimed to evaluate how biomarker selection influences CA-AKI detection and interpretation of preventive strategies after intra-arterial contrast procedures.

This prospective, randomized, single-blind exploratory trial included 76 patients with peripheral arterial disease undergoing elective intra-arterial contrast-enhanced vascular procedures, most of which were diagnostic angiographic examinations. Participants were stratified according to baseline renal function and randomized to receive either standardized hydration alone or hydration plus high-dose atorvastatin and N-acetylcysteine. CA-AKI was assessed using two predefined definitions: historical creatinine-based criteria (≥ 25% or ≥ 0.5 mg/dL increase within 72 h) and cystatin C-based criteria (≥ 10% increase within 24 h). Diagnostic concordance and biomarker-dependent differences in event ascertainment were evaluated.

Substantial diagnostic discordance was observed between creatinine- and cystatin C-defined CA-AKI, with no overlapping cases and poor agreement between biomarkers (κ = 0.07). Creatinine-based criteria identified 4 CA-AKI events, whereas cystatin C identified 7 additional early functional injury cases. Biomarker-dependent differences in event detection varied across renal function strata, particularly among patients with preserved baseline renal function. Low event rates using creatinine-based criteria limited definitive assessment of preventive efficacy. Exploratory analyses suggested that biomarker selection influenced the apparent magnitude and direction of treatment-effect estimates.

CA-AKI ascertainment after intra-arterial contrast exposure is strongly biomarker-dependent. Historical creatinine-based definitions may underestimate early functional renal impairment and influence interpretation of preventive strategies. These findings highlight the importance of endpoint selection in CA-AKI clinical trials and support further investigation of sensitive functional biomarkers in larger prospective studies.

Article.ArticleTitle: Virtual reality-assisted rehabilitation after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair for small-to-medium supraspinatus tears: a prospective assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Rehabilitation after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (ARCR) must protect the repair while restoring active shoulder use. Immersive virtual reality (VR) can standardize rehabilitation tasks and provide immediate feedback, but whether VR delivery offers benefit over conventional delivery when exercise dose and therapist supervision are matched remains uncertain.

This assessor-blinded randomized trial assigned 86 adults undergoing ARCR for small-to-medium full-thickness supraspinatus tears 1:1 to VR-assisted or conventional rehabilitation. During postoperative weeks 4-8, both groups received matched exercise content, dose, progression criteria, safety limits, and face-to-face therapist supervision; only the delivery format differed. Assessments were conducted at baseline, weeks 4 and 6, and months 2, 3, and 6. The primary outcome was activity-related pain measured using a 10-cm visual analogue scale (VAS). Secondary outcomes included rest pain, the 17-item Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia (TSK-17), Constant-Murley Score (CMS), global shoulder active range of motion, the 12-item Short Form Health Survey (SF-12), isometric strength, and supraspinatus cross-sectional area; surface electromyography (sEMG) was exploratory. Complete-case longitudinal outcomes were analysed using repeated-measures analysis of variance.

Seventy participants completed all assessments (VR, n = 36; conventional rehabilitation, n = 34); mean age was 58.1 years, 47 (67.1%) were women, and 35 (50.0%) had small tears. Baseline activity-related VAS scores were 7.3 and 7.2 cm, and mean CMS values were 49.2 and 48.7 in the VR and conventional rehabilitation groups, respectively. Mean activity-related pain was 0.7 cm lower with VR at 6 weeks (4.0 vs. 4.7) and 0.8 cm lower at 2 months (3.1 vs. 3.9); both differences were smaller than the published 1.4-cm clinical-importance threshold. The TSK-17 group × time interaction was significant (P = 0.001); at 3 months, the mean difference was - 3.1 points (95% CI - 4.5 to - 1.8; Hedges g = - 1.11). Rest pain was similar between groups, and group × time interactions for CMS, global shoulder active range of motion, SF-12, isometric strength, supraspinatus cross-sectional area, and exploratory sEMG outcomes were nonsignificant. No clear between-group difference in activity-related pain or TSK-17 was apparent at 6 months.

In the complete-case analysis, VR delivery was associated with lower activity-related pain at 6 weeks and 2 months and lower TSK-17 scores at 3 months compared with conventional rehabilitation. The pain differences were below a published clinical-importance threshold, and the clinical importance of the TSK-17 difference remains uncertain. No between-group difference in activity-related pain or TSK-17 was apparent at 6 months, and the trial did not demonstrate broader functional, structural, or neuromuscular benefits.

Article.ArticleTitle: A novel distal radial artery compression device versus elastic bandage compression after coronary angiography or percutaneous coronary intervention via distal transradial access: a prospective randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Distal transradial artery access (dTRA) is increasingly used for coronary interventions because it preserves proximal radial artery patency. However, effective hemostasis at the distal puncture site remains challenging due to the superficial vessel location and limited soft-tissue support. This study evaluated the hemostatic performance, local safety, patient-reported outcomes, and early radial artery patency of a novel distal radial artery compression device compared with conventional elastic bandage compression.

In this prospective randomized controlled trial, 148 patients undergoing coronary angiography (CAG) or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) via dTRA were randomized (1:1) to device-based or conventional compression. The primary outcome was first-attempt hemostasis success after compression release. Secondary outcomes included total hemostasis duration, operation time, access-site complications, pain, comfort, and ultrasound-assessed radial artery outcomes.

First-attempt hemostasis success was achieved in 74 patients (100.0%) in the device group and 70 patients (94.6%) in the elastic bandage group. Compared with elastic bandage compression, the novel device significantly shortened total hemostasis duration and operation time (both P < 0.001). Postoperative hand swelling was significantly less frequent and less severe in the device group (P < 0.001), while bleeding or hematoma formation was descriptively less frequent. No radial artery occlusion was detected by Doppler ultrasound before discharge in either group. Overall repeated-measures analysis showed no significant group effect or group-by-time interaction for pain or comfort scores.

The novel dTRA compression device achieved a high first-attempt hemostasis success rate and significantly shortened operation time and total hemostasis duration compared with conventional elastic bandage compression after CAG or PCI via dTRA. The device was associated with less postoperative hand swelling, while bleeding or hematoma formation was infrequent and should be interpreted cautiously. These findings support the short-term feasibility and procedural hemostatic efficiency of the device compared with conventional elastic bandage compression. Further multicenter studies incorporating standardized patent-hemostasis assessment, longer vascular follow-up, and comparisons with currently available dedicated distal radial compression devices are needed.

Article.ArticleTitle: Clinical outcomes of composite restorations with or without a glass ionomer liner after selective caries removal to soft dentin: a 36-month randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Selective caries removal to soft dentin (SCR-SD) is currently recommended for the management of deep dentine caries lesions in permanent teeth. However, whether a pulp-protective liner is required after SCR-SD remains uncertain. This randomized controlled trial compared the clinical performance and pulp vitality outcomes of composite resin restorations using a universal adhesive with or without a glass ionomer cement (GIC) liner after SCR-SD in deep caries lesions of permanent posterior teeth.

A randomized controlled clinical trial was conducted in 144 deep dentin caries lesions from 98 participants aged 9 to 55 years. After SCR-SD, lesions were randomly allocated to one of two restorative strategies: a universal adhesive applied in selective enamel etching mode (SE) and composite resin without a GIC liner, or a conventional GIC liner followed by the same universal adhesive applied in selective enamel etching mode and composite resin (GIC + SE). Restorations were followed for 30-36 months. The primary outcome was restoration survival, assessed using selected FDI criteria. The secondary outcome was pulp vitality preservation. Survival analyses were performed using Weibull regression models.

Of the 144 treated lesions, 117 were evaluated after 30-36 months. Restoration survival did not differ significantly between groups, with survival rates of 96.0% for SE and 92.4% for GIC + SE (p = 0.37). In contrast, pulp vitality preservation was significantly higher in the SE group than in the GIC + SE group, with success rates of 97.5% and 87.3%, respectively (p = 0.01). In the adjusted Weibull regression model, SE was associated with a lower risk of pulp vitality failure compared with GIC + SE. Restorative failure was also strongly associated with pulp vitality failure.

The use of a GIC liner after SCR-SD did not improve restoration survival and was not associated with better pulp vitality preservation. Composite restorations using universal adhesive applied in selective enamel etching mode placed directly over the remaining dentin showed favorable restorative and biological outcomes after 30-36 months. These findings suggest that routine liner placement after SCR-SD may not be necessary.

In deep dentin caries lesions treated with SCR-SD, placing a glass ionomer liner before composite restoration using a universal adhesive did not improve clinical outcomes. Effective sealing is achieved using universal adhesive applied in selective enamel etching mode and nanofilled composite resin. These simple clinical procedures maintained the restoration integrity and pulp vitality. Registered on https://www.

Article.ArticleTitle: Resistance training and protein supplementation in patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer: a randomized feasibility trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Cancer cachexia is associated with reduced physical performance, quality of life, and survival in patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer. Resistance training and protein supplementation have the potential to improve these outcomes. Whether an intervention comprising resistance training and protein supplementation is feasible during treatment for incurable gastroesophageal cancer is not known.

This was an open-label, parallel-group, two-arm, randomized controlled feasibility trial. Patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer scheduled to undergo first-line chemotherapy were randomized 2:1 to resistance training three times per week and daily protein supplementation or to control. The primary outcome, feasibility, was assessed by recruitment, retention, adherence, and harms. Secondary outcomes included body composition, physical performance, quality of life, and treatment tolerability.

Out of 106 potentially eligible patients, 20 participants (5 female and 15 male, mean age 65) were randomized yielding a recruitment rate of 19%. 18 participants completed the trial with a retention rate of 90%. Median (25th; 75th percentile) adherence to the resistance training sessions and to the protein supplements was 63% (43; 77) and 39% (17; 76), respectively. Five participants (38%) met the minimum feasibility criteria of both interventions. No serious adverse events related to the intervention occurred. We found no between-group differences in body composition, physical performance, quality of life, or treatment tolerability.

Resistance training combined with protein supplementation was not feasible during first-line chemotherapy in patients with incurable gastroesophageal cancer due to low accrual and low adherence to protein supplementation.
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05650827. Study registration date 2022-12-12.

Article.ArticleTitle: Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis BL-99 ameliorates age-related intestinal hypomotility in older adults: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: The decay of smooth muscle contractility is a major trigger of aging-related intestinal hypomotility, which imposes a substantial healthcare burden. Despite this, effective targeted therapy for this condition remains unavailable. Here, we identified the probiotic Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis BL-99 as a microbiota modulator that restores gut motility through the bile acid (BA)-mediated rescue of smooth muscle contractile function. In a randomized, double-blind clinical trial (ChiCTR2300077583, with the primary endpoint of whole-gut transit time [WGTT], and secondary endpoints including bowel movement frequency, symptom severity, and quality-of-life measures) and naturally aged mouse models, BL-99 intervention significantly reduced the WGTT and concurrently remodeled the gut microbiota. This suppressed bile salt hydrolase-expressing bacteria, which preserved conjugated BA pools, including taurochenodeoxycholic acid (TCDCA). Mechanistic investigations revealed that BL-99 was associated with enhanced expression of the serum response factor (SRF)-myocardin (Myocd) transcriptional axis in colonic smooth muscle cells (SMCs), restoring contractile apparatus components (e.g., α-SMA, SM-MHC). Crucially, TCDCA administration recapitulated BL-99 regulation of intestinal SMC contractile protein expression by inhibiting the PI3K/AKT pathway. Our findings established a microbiota-BA-SMC signaling axis that ameliorates age-related intestinal hypomotility, positioning both BL-99 and TCDCA as precision therapeutic candidates targeting SMC-related dysmotility.

Journal.Title: Canadian journal of surgery. Journal canadien de chirurgie

Article.ArticleTitle: Negative pressure incisional wound therapy for high-risk ventral hernia repair: a randomized controlled trial and meta-analysis.

Abstract.AbstractText: Despite advances in prosthetic material and surgical technique, wound-related complications after ventral hernia repairs remain common and a primary determinant of postoperative morbidity. We sought to evaluate negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT), a low-cost intervention to improve wound outcomes that has been proven in other surgical contexts.

We report a multicentre randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluating NPWT versus sterile dressing in adult patients undergoing surgical repair of ventral hernias with 1 or more risk factors for postoperative surgical site complications. Our primary outcome was the composite of any surgical site complication. Secondary outcomes were cost-effectiveness and quality of life, evaluated using the Hernia-Related Quality-of-Life Survey (HerQLes). We conducted a meta-analysis of this study and 2 other RCTs.

Of 110 patients who met inclusion criteria, 107 had primary outcome data at a median follow-up of 33 days. The primary outcome occurred in 15 (27.8%) of 54 patients in the NPWT group and 25 (47.2%) of 53 patients in the control group, for a relative risk of 0.59 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.35 to 0.99). Meta-analysis found a pooled relative risk of 0.56 (95% CI 0.39 to 0.81). Postoperative quality of life was significantly higher in the NPWT group (HerQLes score 88.3 [95% CI 75.8 to 94.2] v. 73.3 [95% CI 52.5 to 93.3]). Cost-effectiveness of the NPWT was US$160 per quality-adjusted life year.
Prophylactic NPWT in high-risk ventral hernia repair reduces the incidence of surgical site complications, is associated with a higher postoperative quality of life, and is highly cost-effective.

Article.ArticleTitle: Perioperative respiratory adverse events in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy with laryngeal mask airway versus endotracheal tube ventilation: multicentre, randomised controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: To assess the effect of ventilation with a laryngeal mask airway (LMA) compared with endotracheal tube (ETT) on perioperative respiratory adverse events (PRAEs) in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy.
Multicentre, randomised, parallel group trial.
Four tertiary hospitals in China, 2023-24.
400 children aged ≥2 years and <7 years who were scheduled for adenotonsillectomy under general anaesthesia.
Participants were randomised 1:1 to receive ventilation with a laryngeal mask airway (n=200) or an endotracheal tube (n=200) during adenotonsillectomy.

The primary outcome was the proportion of participants who developed any perioperative respiratory adverse event (PRAE): laryngospasm, bronchospasm, desaturation, airway obstruction, severe cough, or stridor in the intention-to-treat population.

400 children (mean age 4.7 (standard deviation 1.0) years; 155 (38.7%) girls) were enrolled between 24 May 2023 and 4 April 2024, with last follow-up on 4 May 2024. LMA was converted to ETT in three participants. Overall, 22.5% (45/200) participants in the LMA group experienced PRAEs versus 57.5% (115/200) in the ETT group (absolute risk difference -35.0 percentage points, 95% confidence interval -43.5 to -25.7; P<0.001). The LMA group had fewer PRAEs in both the intraoperative (9.0% (18/200) v 17.5% (35/200); -8.5, -15.2 to -1.8; P=0.01) and the postoperative period (16.5% (33/200) v 49.5% (99/200); -33.0, -41.2 to -24.0; P<0.001). The LMA group also had a lower proportion of participants with laryngospasm (0.0% v 3.0%; P=0.03), desaturation (15.0% v 28.0%; P=0.002), airway obstruction (3.5% v 12.5%; P<0.001), and severe cough (10.5% v 42.0%; P<0.001). Neither group experienced serious adverse events.
Ventilation with an LMA by experienced anaesthesiologists resulted in fewer perioperative respiratory adverse events than ventilation with an ETT in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy.

Journal.Title: Clinical implant dentistry and related research

Article.ArticleTitle: DFDBA With or Without Platelet-Rich Fibrin in Maxillary Sinus Augmentation: A Randomized Split-Mouth Clinical Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: To compare histologic and histomorphometric outcomes after bilateral lateral maxillary sinus augmentation with demineralized freeze-dried bone allograft (DFDBA) alone versus DFDBA combined with platelet-rich fibrin (PRF), and to report 1-year prosthetic follow-up of the restored implants.

This randomized split-mouth clinical trial included subjects requiring bilateral lateral maxillary sinus augmentation before implant placement. In each subject, one sinus was randomly assigned to DFDBA alone and the contralateral sinus to DFDBA combined with leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF) and injectable PRF (i-PRF). Bone biopsy specimens were harvested at the clinically relevant 6-month implant placement time point. The primary outcome was newly formed bone. Secondary histomorphometric outcomes were residual graft material, connective tissue, and fibrosis; inflammation and necrosis were assessed histologically. Clinical and radiographic prosthetic follow-up was performed 1 year after definitive prosthetic loading. Paired comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.

Of 24 enrolled subjects, 21 completed follow-up and contributed 42 sinus sites to the paired analysis. Median newly formed bone was 48.72% (IQR, 33.33%-63.33%) on the PRF side and 45.76% (IQR, 37.14%-54.90%) on the non-PRF side (p = 0.5). Residual graft material was 6.74% versus 4.23% (p = 0.2), connective tissue was 31.48% versus 36.92% (p = 0.016), and fibrosis was 3.42% versus 2.56% (p > 0.9). No inflammation or necrosis was observed. Following replacement of one implant that failed before prosthetic loading, all definitively restored implants remained functional during the 1-year prosthetic follow-up. Clinical and radiographic follow-up was uneventful, and no biologic or prosthetic complications requiring intervention were observed.

Adding PRF to DFDBA did not significantly increase newly formed bone at the 6-month implant placement time point. The lower connective tissue proportion on the PRF side may suggest altered tissue maturation; however, this secondary finding should be interpreted cautiously. Definitively restored implants showed 100% prosthetic survival during 1-year follow-up.
ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07348198; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07348198. This clinical trial was not registered prior to participant recruitment and randomization.

Article.ArticleTitle: A randomised, double-blind, multicentre, placebo-controlled phase 3 efficacy, safety, and immunogenicity study of an Ad26.RSV.preF/RSV prefusion F-protein vaccine for the prevention of respiratory syncytial virus-mediated lower respiratory tract disease in adults aged 60 years and older.

Abstract.AbstractText: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) in older adults. This study evaluated efficacy, immunogenicity, and safety of the investigational recombinant, replication-incompetent, adenovirus type 26 vector RSV preF protein (Ad26.RSV.preF/RSV preF vaccine).

EVERGREEN was a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial conducted in 14 countries. Adults aged 60 years or older (stratified by age and risk of severe RSV disease) were randomly assigned 2:1 using an interactive web response system to receive one dose of vaccine or placebo. Participants, study site personnel, investigators, and sponsor were blinded to vaccine allocation. The primary endpoint was the first occurrence of RSV-mediated LRTD, defined as new onset/worsening of at least three symptoms occurring 14 or more days postvaccination. The study had at least 90% power to demonstrate statistically significant vaccine efficacy greater than 20% against the primary endpoint and to achieve a point estimate for vaccine efficacy of more than 50%. The trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04908683. The study is completed.

The study was conducted between 21 July 2021 and 20 July 2023. At the time of the primary analysis, 26,299 individuals were screened, 23,707 were enrolled and 23,555 were vaccinated, 15,698 (67%) in the active vaccine group and 7857 (33%) in the placebo group. In all 23,555 vaccinated participants, 13,515 (54%) were female, 11,558 (46%) were male and the mean age was 70.2 years (SD 5.24). In the per protocol efficacy set, 17 of 15,337 participants (0.1%) in the vaccine group and 31 of 7683 participants (0.4%) in the placebo group had an RSV-mediated LRTD event. Vaccine efficacy was 72.7% (96.326% confidence interval, 47.2-86.4) for prevention of RSV-mediated LRTD over a mean follow-up time of 233.9 days (database cutoff: 15 September 2022). Solicited local and systemic adverse events were more frequent with vaccine versus placebo; none were grade four. The frequency of serious adverse events was similar in the vaccine (n = 842, 5.0%) and placebo (n = 457, 5.5%) groups, of which 15 (0.1%) and two (<0.1%), respectively, were considered vaccine related. There were 105 (0.63%) deaths in the vaccine group and 61 (0.73%) in the placebo group. None were considered related to study vaccine by the investigator. The study and vaccine development were discontinued in March 2023 due to a strategic decision by the study sponsor.
In adults aged 60 years and older, the Ad26.RSV.preF/RSV preF protein vaccine was efficacious in preventing RSV-mediated LRTD and had an acceptable safety profile.

Article.ArticleTitle: Plozasiran for Severe Hypertriglyceridemia and Risk of Pancreatitis.

Abstract.AbstractText: Severe hypertriglyceridemia is associated with an increased risk of acute pancreatitis. Plozasiran, a small interfering RNA targeting APOC3 messenger RNA, lowers triglyceride levels and potentially mitigates the risk of acute pancreatitis.

In two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, 757 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive plozasiran (25 mg) or placebo at baseline and at months 3, 6, and 9. These trials had identical designs, end points, and analytic plans. The primary end point was the percent change in the fasting plasma triglyceride level from baseline to month 12. Key secondary end points were the percent change in the fasting triglyceride level from baseline to month 10, a fasting triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.6 mmol per liter) and less than 150 mg per deciliter (1.7 mmol per liter), the percent change in the fasting serum triglyceride level at month 12 for patients with a baseline triglyceride level of 880 mg per deciliter or greater, and changes in remnant cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol. A pooled analysis addressed adjudicated acute pancreatitis, incidence, and first-event timing.

At month 12, patients in the plozasiran groups had a median triglyceride level that was lower than the baseline level by 79% and 81% in the two trials. These reductions corresponded to a median difference in the plozasiran groups as compared with the placebo groups (placebo-adjusted change) of -45 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -51 to -38) and -47 percentage points (95% CI, -54 to -39). A triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter at 12 months was reported in 91% and 93% of the patients in the plozasiran groups and in 51% and 50% of those in the placebo groups (P<0.001). The rates of acute pancreatitis were 1 per 100 patient-years with plozasiran and 5 per 100 patient-years with placebo (rate ratio, 0.22; P = 0.008). Adverse events during treatment occurred in 73% of the patients in both the pooled plozasiran and placebo groups.

Among patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, the use of plozasiran resulted in lower triglyceride levels and a lower risk of acute pancreatitis than placebo at 12 months. (Funded by Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals; SHASTA-3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06347003; SHASTA-4, NCT06347016.).

Article.ArticleTitle: An analysis of enrollment rates by admitting service for a secondary analysis of enrollment data from a randomized smoking-cessation trial (FIESTA).

Abstract.AbstractText: Enrollment into clinical trials is challenging and has a major effect on the feasibility and the generalizability of a study. We used data from a previously completed hospital-based smoking cessation study to determine if enrollment rates varied by hospital admitting service, specifically comparing Medicine and Psychiatry departments.

We examined enrollment in the Financial Incentives for Smoking Cessation (FIESTA) study, which was conducted at the Veterans Affairs New York Harbor Healthcare System. FIESTA tested the effectiveness of financial incentives on smoking cessation among hospitalized patients. A total of 268 patients were eligible, with 182 enrolled in the original FIESTA study. In our secondary analysis, a LASSO approach was applied to the data set to create a model examining admitting service, age, sex, race and ethnicity, education, and number of cigarettes per day and their association with enrollment.

The enrollment rates were higher for patients admitted to the Psychiatry service (80.2%) than to the Medicine and other services (59.9%). Patients with a high school education or less also had a higher enrollment rate (87.2%) than those with higher education (57.7%). Increasing age was associated with lower odds of enrollment (aOR = 0.97, 95% CI: 0.94, 0.99). Hispanic ethnicity appeared to associate with a higher odds of enrollment compared to non-Hispanic White (aOR = 2.52, 95% CI 1.11, 5.75). Higher odds of enrollment were observed among patients admitted to the Psychiatry service (aOR = 2.51, 95% CI: 1.23-5.12), while lower odds were observed among those with higher education (aOR = 0.17, 95% CI: 0.06-0.49).

This research suggests that smoking cessation programs can effectively enroll a diverse patient population, including typically underrepresented groups such as those with lower education status and those with mental health diagnoses. Such enrollment efforts would enable studies to be more generalizable to the smoking population. Findings also emphasize the potential of urban hospital settings to support equitable enrollment efforts. The present work is a secondary analysis of the FIESTA RCT (NCT02506829). Future research should explore additional demographic factors, such as comorbidities and confidence in quitting, to better understand motivations for participation.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects and mechanisms of exercise timing on cognitive function in older type 2 diabetes mellitus patients with mild cognitive impairment: A magnetic resonance imaging-based randomized controlled trial protocol.

Abstract.AbstractText: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a prevalent complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Cognitive impairment progressively impairs self-care abilities, thereby triggering a vicious cycle of poor glycemic control and further cognitive decline. Exercise has been widely recognized as an effective strategy to improve both glycemic control and cognitive function; however, an optimal time of day for exercise to mitigate this neurodegenerative trajectory has not been determined. This trial aims to determine the most effective exercise timing to maximize cognitive benefits in older T2DM patients with MCI (T2DM-MCI) and to investigate the underlying neurobiological mechanisms using multimodal magnetic resonance imaging.

In this randomized controlled trial, patients 60-75 years of age with T2DM-MCI will be assigned to a morning exercise group (09:00-10:10), an evening exercise group (19:00-20:10), or a health education group. The exercise groups will complete a 12-week, home-based, remotely supervised exercise program comprising aerobic and resistance exercises. The health education group will receive a 12-week health education program. Cognitive function will be evaluated at baseline and post-intervention using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment, Color-Word Stroop Test, N-back task, Trail making Test, Attention Network Test, and Digit Symbol Substitution Test. Additionally, brain structure and function based on imaging, blood biomarkers, and physical fitness will also be assessed.

In this study, we aim to identify the optimal time of day for exercise to maximize cognitive benefits in patients with T2DM-MCI and to elucidate underlying neurocognitive mechanisms. We will examine whether glycemic control mediates the relationship between exercise and cognitive function improvement. This research is expected to provide "time-specific" evidence for exercise prescription to maximize the neurocognitive benefits and mitigate dementia risk in this population.

Article.ArticleTitle: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Maternal Health Outcomes in Pregnant and Postpartum Individuals: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly used to support maternal health, but randomized evidence is limited.
To evaluate whether access to a generative AI maternal health chatbot improved 12-month maternal health outcomes.

This 2-group randomized clinical trial enrolled 400 participants from October 2023 to December 2024, with 12-month follow-up completed in December 2025. Participants were recruited online across 49 US states and the District of Columbia. Eligible participants were English-speaking, aged 14 years or older, pregnant or parenting an infant younger than 6 months, and self-identified as members of racial and/or ethnic minoritized groups.
Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive access to the chatbot or an active control consisting of monthly children's books.

Primary outcomes were anxiety and depression symptoms at 12 months measured using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 and Patient Health Questionnaire-9. Secondary outcomes included emergency department visits, pregnancy-related complications, postpartum care checkups, effective contraception use, and sleep duration.

Among 400 randomized participants, the mean (SD) age was 32.6 (5.1) years; 200 (50%) were parenting an infant at enrollment; and 10 (2%) identified as American Indian or Alaska Native, 80 (20%) Asian, 188 (47%) Black or African American, 57 (14%) multiracial, and 65 (16%) Hispanic or Latino. The AI chatbot was not associated with differences in anxiety scores (adjusted mean difference, 0.10; 95% CI, -0.77 to 0.96) or depression scores (adjusted mean difference, -0.23; 95% CI, -1.05 to 0.59), nor with emergency department visits, postpartum care, contraception use, or sleep duration. Among participants pregnant at enrollment, the chatbot was associated with more self-reported pregnancy-related complications in the secondary 12-month end point analysis, but not in longitudinal analyses. Higher chatbot engagement was associated with longer sleep duration and higher anxiety scores in exploratory within-group analyses.

In this randomized clinical trial of pregnant and postpartum individuals from racial and ethnic minoritized groups, access to a generative artificial intelligence maternal health chatbot did not improve maternal anxiety or depression at 12 months compared with an active control. Secondary and exploratory findings should be interpreted cautiously.
ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06053515.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of digital stress-management interventions in breast cancer patients 18 months after intervention access.

Abstract.AbstractText: Digital stress-management tools show promise, but their long-term impact remains unclear. In the Coping After Breast Cancer (CABC) trial, the app-based stress-management program StressProffen, with either cognitive behavioral therapy intervention (CBI) or a mindfulness-based intervention (MBI), showed no advantage over usual care after six months of access. However, benefits may emerge gradually, as users need time not only to become familiar with the content and techniques, but also to internalize, apply and automatize their use in response to real-life stressors. The a priori defined aims of the current study were to examine; 1) whether extended (18 months) access to the digital stress-management interventions CBI and MBI were associated with changes in perceived stress (stress) (primary outcome), measures of health-related quality of life, mindfulness, fatigue, coping, anxiety, depression, and sleep (secondary outcomes), 2) association between app use and changes in stress level and investigate baseline characteristics as moderators of change in stress in the intervention groups, and 3) identify predictors of change in stress among patients with breast cancer.

Of 430 patients randomized to MBI, CBI, or usual care, 76% (n = 327) completed the 18-month survey. Linear mixed-effects models were used to assess between-group differences in primary and secondary outcomes. Moderator analyses were performed to examine whether specific baseline characteristics modified the intervention effects on stress levels. Predictor analysis of change in stress was performed for the total sample.

At 18 months, all three groups showed stable trends over time, with no significant difference between either intervention group and controls. A larger stress reduction was observed among younger participants (≤50 years) in both CBI and MBI compared to controls. Higher baseline stress levels predicted significantly larger stress reductions in the total sample, but the moderator analysis showed that the effects were only significant in the CBI group.

Neither CBI nor MBI showed statistically significant improvements at 18 months compared to controls. The results however suggest that long-term access to stress management interventions may help young women with breast cancer and those with high initial stress to reduce their stress levels.
ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT04480203.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of high-power radiofrequency combined with a hypocaloric diet on abdominal subcutaneous and visceral fat: a preliminary randomized pilot study.

Abstract.AbstractText: Visceral and subcutaneous abdominal fat are associated with metabolic and cardiovascular risk. This preliminary randomized pilot study evaluated a high-power radiofrequency energy-based device (EBD) treatment, alone or combined with a hypocaloric dietary intervention, for visceral and subcutaneous abdominal fat reduction. Twenty middle-aged participants were randomly allocated to one of two parallel groups: EBD combined with dietary intervention (7 males, 3 females; mean age 58.2 ± 8.89 years) and EBD alone (5 males, 5 females; mean age 54.4 ± 12.5 years). Both groups received 12 EBD sessions over 6 weeks using a four-channel high-power radiofrequency device. Anthropometric, biochemical, and volumetric abdominal fat measurements were assessed at baseline and post-treatment, with visceral fat additionally evaluated at the 3-month follow-up. Both groups demonstrated reductions in abdominal fat volume. The EBD + diet group showed greater reductions in visceral fat (15.0%) and subcutaneous fat (18.6%) than the EBD-only group, which showed reductions of approximately 9.1% and 9.2%, respectively. Between-group change-score analyses favored the EBD + Diet group for weight and BMI, while differences in visceral and subcutaneous fat did not reach statistical significance. Most biochemical variables showed no clear between-group differences, although exploratory between-group differences were observed for triglycerides, insulin, and HOMA-IR. At the 3-month follow-up, mean visceral fat remained below baseline in both groups. Reductions in visceral and subcutaneous abdominal fat were observed in both treated groups. These findings should be interpreted cautiously due to the exploratory design and small sample size. Larger studies are required to confirm efficacy and long-term outcomes.

Journal.Title: Journal of orthopaedics and traumatology : official journal of the Italian Society of Orthopaedics and Traumatology

Article.ArticleTitle: Robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty demonstrates superior early functional outcomes compared with conventional total knee arthroplasty: a quasi-randomised controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (TKA) has gained popularity over the last decade, with claimed advantages in implant positioning accuracy and soft-tissue balance. Whether these technical advantages translate into better clinical outcomes for patients remains debated. This investigation compared 1-year patient-reported outcomes between robotic-assisted and conventional TKA performed within the same institution but following structurally different surgical workflows.

This quasi-randomised controlled trial enrolled patients who underwent primary TKA at the Department of Orthopaedic and Trauam Surgery of the Eifelklink St. Brigida (Simmerath, Germany) between 2022 and 2025. Group allocation was determined by surgeon assignment through the institutional digital scheduling system. All patients received the same implant (Smith & Nephew Legion Genesis II, posterior-stabilised). Robotic-assisted procedures were performed using the CORI Robotic System (Smith & Nephew, UK) following a four-dimensional personalised alignment workflow (coronal, sagittal, transversal and balancing) guided intraoperatively by the Knee Balancing Score (KBS). Conventional procedures followed a femur-first technique with adjusted mechanical alignment. Outcomes included WOMAC total and subscores, visual analogue scale (VAS), Tegner activity score and a dedicated functional questionnaire, all assessed at 1-year follow-up.

A total of 845 patients were included (robotic-assisted: n = 390; conventional: n = 455). At 1-year, 383 and 445 patients completed follow-up, respectively. The two groups were comparable at baseline. The robotic-assisted cohort showed significantly better results across WOMAC and related subscales (P < 0.001), VAS (P < 0.001), Tegner (P < 0.001), functional and satisfaction items, including walking distance and knee stability. No difference was found in the use of walking aids.

Robotic-assisted TKA was associated with superior functional and patient-reported outcomes at the 1-year follow-up. The clinical benefit observed is likely not attributable to robotic precision alone, but reflects the structured, personalised intraoperative workflow that robotic assistance enables. Article.ArticleTitle: A randomized comparison of comprehensive weight loss intervention vs. usual care on recurrences of atrial fibrillation in obese patients after catheter ablation: HOBIT-AF trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Obesity is one of the strongest risk factors for the development of atrial fibrillation (AF), and its reduction is associated with the alleviation of AF burden. The HOBIT-AF study aimed to evaluate the impact of complex weight loss interventions on AF recurrence rate in obese individuals after catheter ablation (CA).

The HOBIT-AF was a randomized controlled trial with a 15-month treatment period (3-18 months post CA) involving complex weight-reducing interventions in the active arm. The primary outcome was the change in AF/atrial tachycardia (AT) burden assessed from baseline and the final 14-day Holter monitoring. A total of 167 individuals (aged 59 years, body mass index of 35.6 kg/m2) were randomized into the active (n = 85) and control group (n = 82). At the end of the treatment period, a mean reduction of 6.8 ± 7.0% of the initial body weight accompanied by improvement of metabolic parameters was achieved in the active group. The AF/AT burden change was 0.6 ± 2.5% (95% CI: -4.2-5.5%) in the active group and -0.9 ± 1.8% (95% CI: -4.5-3.0%) in the control group. The AF/AT recurrence-free survival during the 3-18-month follow-up period was comparable between groups (70.4% vs. 69.6%).

HOBIT-AF trial showed that despite the beneficial effect of body weight reduction on metabolic profile of obese patients with predominantly paroxysmal AF after CA, no reduction in AF/AT recurrence was observed in comparison with control patients. This may be likely due to low AF burden after previous CA, limiting further improvement.

Article.ArticleTitle: Comparability of Pharmacokinetics, Safety, and Tolerability of Canakinumab Administration With One Injection (200 mg) of Pre-Filled Syringe or Auto-Injector Versus Two Injections (150 and 50 mg) of Pre-Filled Syringe in Healthy Subjects.

Abstract.AbstractText: This phase 1, randomized, open-label, single-dose, parallel-group study aimed to describe the pharmacokinetic (PK) comparability and safety of canakinumab administered as a single 200 mg subcutaneous injection via pre-filled syringes assembled within a needle safety device (PFS-NSD) by HCP and auto-injector (AI) by subject self-administration versus two injections of 150 + 50 mg via PFS-NSD by HCP. Healthy adults (18-55 years) were allocated to three arms: canakinumab 150 + 50 mg (PFS-NSD; n = 78), canakinumab 200 mg (AI; n = 76), and canakinumab 200 mg (PFS-NSD; n = 76). Multiplicity was addressed as two tests were compared with the same reference. Primary PK parameters were comparable across arms. The geometric mean ratios and 95% CI values of AUCinf, AUClast, and Cmax were within bioequivalence limits of 0.80-1.25 for both comparisons: (a) canakinumab 200 mg AI versus canakinumab 150 + 50 mg PFS-NSD and (b) canakinumab 200 mg PFS-NSD versus canakinumab 150 + 50 mg PFS-NSD. Median Tmax was comparable: 7, 9, and 7 days for canakinumab 150 + 50 mg PFS-NSD, 200 mg AI, and 200 mg PFS-NSD, respectively. Exploratory post-hoc analyses, assessing the impact of pause during the pandemic (N = 131 subjects recruited pre-pandemic) and evaluating partial AUC4weeks, suggested similar results. Canakinumab was well-tolerated, and no treatment-induced immunogenicity was observed.

Article.ArticleTitle: Transbronchial Cryobiopsy for the Diagnosis of Peripheral Pulmonary Lesions: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Study.

Abstract.AbstractText: Peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs) are increasingly detected by chest computed tomography, yet bronchoscopic diagnosis remains challenging for small and distal lesions. This prospective, single-center, randomized controlled study evaluated radial endobronchial ultrasound combined with a guide sheath (R-EBUS-GS)-assisted transbronchial cryobiopsy using a 1.1-mm ultrathin cryoprobe. Fifty patients with PPLs were randomized after successful R-EBUS-GS localization to either transbronchial cryobiopsy (TBCB) or conventional transbronchial lung biopsy with forceps (TBLB), with 25 patients in each group. The prespecified primary endpoint was pathological diagnostic yield. Pathological diagnostic yield was 84.0% in the TBCB group and 64.0% in the TBLB group; the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.107). TBCB yielded a greater maximum total histologic tissue area than TBLB (14.6 ± 4.2 mm2 vs. 3.1 ± 0.9 mm2, p < 0.001) and was associated with a lower frequency of severe crush artifact (8.0% vs. 52.0%, p < 0.001). Grade 2 bleeding occurred in 32.0% and 24.0% of patients, respectively, and no Grade 3 bleeding occurred. One patient in the TBCB group developed pneumothorax and recovered with conservative treatment. These findings show that R-EBUS-GS-assisted 1.1-mm ultrathin cryobiopsy is technically feasible for PPL sampling and provides larger, better-preserved histologic specimens, while improvement in pathological diagnostic yield was not statistically demonstrated in this small randomized cohort.

Article.ArticleTitle: Targeting Accelerated Aging in COPD: The AMICO (A Trial of Metformin In COpd) Trial Design.

Abstract.AbstractText: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is increasingly recognized as a disease of accelerated biological aging characterized by progressive lung function decline, emphysema progression and multiple age-related comorbidities. Current therapies improve symptoms and reduce exacerbations but have limited effects on disease progression. Metformin has demonstrated anti-aging properties through modulation of pathways involved in oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction and cellular senescence, making it a potential disease-modifying treatment in COPD.

AMICO (A Trial of Metformin In COPD) is an investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III trial conducted in anonymous. A total of 212 patients with clinically stable COPD, centrilobular emphysema on computed tomography, post-bronchodilator FEV1 40%-70% predicted and accelerated FEV1 decline (>40 mL·year-1) will be randomized (1:1) to receive metformin (850 mg twice daily) or matching placebo for 36 months in addition to standard COPD treatment. Assessments include pulmonary function, chest computed tomography, exercise capacity, health status, muscle strength, body composition, age associated comorbidities development and aging-related biomarkers.The primary endpoint is the annual rate of FEV1 decline over 36 months. Secondary endpoints include emphysema progression, changes in diffusing capacity, COPD Assessment Test score, 6-minute walk distance, BODE index, handgrip strength, exacerbations, major cardiovascular events, cancer incidence and renal dysfunction.

AMICO is the first randomized trial specifically designed to evaluate metformin as a gerotherapeutic and disease-modifying intervention in COPD. The study may provide novel evidence supporting geroscience-based approaches to slow disease progression and improve long-term outcomes in patients with COPD.

Abstract.AbstractText: FitPreV assessed the feasibility of integrating polygenic risk scores and wearable health devices into cardiovascular primary prevention in general practice. In this four-arm pilot randomized trial, 120 adults with metabolic syndrome were followed for 12 months. Recruitment was high and acceptability was favourable, with low anxiety after polygenic risk score (Prs) disclosure. However, 12-month follow-up completeness and GP willingness to implement the intervention require improvement.

Article.ArticleTitle: First-in-Human Phase 1 Evaluation of the DegradaBALL Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticle Delivery System: An mRNA SARS-CoV-2 Vaccine Study in Healthy Korean Adult Volunteers.

Abstract.AbstractText: mRNA vaccines require an effective delivery system for intracellular uptake, and alternative carriers with improved stability and tolerability remain of continued interest. This study evaluated the safety, tolerability, and exploratory immunogenicity of LEM-mR203, an mRNA SARS-CoV-2 receptor binding domain (RBD) booster vaccine formulated with DegradaBALL, a mesoporous silica nanoparticle-based delivery system developed to improve mRNA stability and enable localized delivery.

In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-escalation phase 1 study, a single intramuscular dose of LEM-mR203 (40 μg or 100 μg) or placebo was administered to 20 healthy Korean adult volunteers. Safety endpoints included solicited and unsolicited adverse events (AEs), serious AEs, and AEs of special interest. Exploratory immunogenicity comprised anti-RBD antibody concentrations and neutralizing antibody (Nab) titers through Day 366, together with interferon-γ (IFN-γ)/interleukin-4 (IL-4) ELISpot responses.

LEM-mR203 was well tolerated at both dose levels, with mild (Grade 1) injection-site reactions and infrequent solicited systemic AEs; no fever, serious AEs, or AEs of special interest were reported. Transient, asymptomatic decreases in white blood cell count occurred across active and placebo groups and resolved without sequelae. In this pre-immune cohort (85% anti-nucleocapsid reactive), anti-RBD IgG was maintained through Day 366 without a clear booster-induced increase and Nab titers against the Kappa variant (B.1.617.1) waned, consistent with known mRNA vaccine kinetics. Exploratory ELISpot results suggested an IFN-γ-oriented cellular response in the 100 μg group, without evidence of IL-4/Th2 skewing.

A single booster dose of LEM-mR203 was well tolerated, with no major safety concerns over 366 days, and with exploratory cellular responses suggesting an IFN-γ-oriented profile without Th2 skewing. Given the small sample size and high pre-existing immunity, these findings require confirmation in larger, adequately powered studies of DegradaBALL-based mRNA vaccines.

Article.ArticleTitle: Bioequivalence of budesonide inhalation suspension with and without activated charcoal in healthy Chinese subjects: two randomized four-period crossover trials.

Abstract.AbstractText: Demonstrating bioequivalence for locally acting inhaled products is challenging because systemic exposure may reflect both pulmonary absorption and gastrointestinal absorption of the swallowed fraction. Activated charcoal can suppress gastrointestinal uptake and may help interpret lung-derived exposure more directly.

Two open-label, randomized, single-dose, four-period crossover pharmacokinetic bioequivalence trials were conducted in healthy Chinese adults, one under non-block conditions and one under charcoal-block conditions. Thirty-six subjects were enrolled in each trial. In each period, subjects inhaled a single 1 mg dose of the test or reference budesonide inhalation suspension via a standardized jet nebulizer procedure, with a 5-day washout between periods. Plasma budesonide concentrations were measured for 15 h. The primary pharmacokinetic endpoints were Cmax, AUC0-t, and AUC0-inf, and bioequivalence was concluded if the 90% confidence intervals for the test/reference geometric mean ratios were within 80.00%-125.00%.

Under both non-block and charcoal-block conditions, the 90% confidence intervals for Cmax, AUC0-t, and AUC0-inf met the predefined bioequivalence criteria. In exploratory between-cohort comparisons based on subject-level arithmetic summaries, activated-charcoal blockade was associated with numerically lower AUC values, whereas Cmax remained similar; however, nominal exploratory P values for Cmax, AUC0-t, and AUC0-inf were all >0.05 and were not used for confirmatory inference. These findings are consistent with, but do not establish, a predominant pulmonary contribution to systemic exposure after nebulization. Both formulations were well tolerated, and no serious adverse events were reported.

The test and reference budesonide inhalation suspension formulations were bioequivalent under both non-block and charcoal-block conditions. Exploratory between-cohort comparisons showed no statistically significant differences in Cmax, AUC0-t, or AUC0-inf based on nominal P values. The charcoal-related findings are consistent with, but do not establish, a predominant pulmonary contribution to systemic exposure after nebulization and should be interpreted cautiously because the conditions were evaluated in separate cohorts. Overall, the two studies provide supportive pharmacokinetic evidence for the evaluation of generic nebulized budesonide products.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of Kunxian capsule, a novel Tripterygium wilfordii preparation, on reducing proteinuria and slowing renal function decline in diabetic kidney disease: a 48-week randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD), a leading cause of chronic kidney disease, remains a clinical challenge despite renin-angiotensin system blockade. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of adding Kunxian capsule to standard therapy with irbesartan in patients with DKD.

Eighty patients with DKD were randomly assigned to either the experimental group (standard therapy with irbesartan plus Kunxian capsule) or the control group (standard therapy with irbesartan) for 48 weeks. Primary outcomes included the proteinuria remission rate, degree of proteinuria reduction, and median time to remission. Secondary outcomes included the slope of eGFR decline and the incidence of renal composite hard endpoint. Safety was assessed by monitoring adverse events. This trial was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov on March 2, 2021 (No. NCT04981613).

In the intention-to-treat analysis, the experimental group had a higher proteinuria remission rate (57.50% vs. 25.00%), a shorter median time to remission (5 months vs. not reached), and a greater reduction in 24-hour urinary protein than the control group. A lower incidence of renal composite hard endpoint was observed in the experimental group (10.00% vs. 32.50%), accompanied by a slower eGFR decline. No significant differences in the incidence of adverse events were observed between the two groups. Inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate, were significantly reduced in the experimental group.

Adding Kunxian capsule to standard therapy with irbesartan improved the proteinuria remission rate and attenuated renal function decline in patients with DKD, supporting its potential as a promising adjunctive therapy.

OtherAbstract.AbstractText: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a serious complication of diabetes that can cause proteinuria and progressive loss of kidney function. Although current medications help protect the kidneys, many patients still experience persistent proteinuria and worsening kidney function. In this 48–week clinical trial involving 80 patients, researchers evaluated whether adding Kunxian capsule – a traditional Chinese medicine formulation – to standard therapy with irbesartan could improve outcomes. The results showed that patients who took Kunxian capsule alongside standard therapy with irbesartan achieved a higher rate of proteinuria remission and a greater reduction in proteinuria, experienced a slower decline in kidney function, and had fewer composite renal events compared with those receiving irbesartan alone. These findings suggest that Kunxian capsule may be a promising adjunctive treatment option to help reduce proteinuria and protect kidney function in patients with DKD.
