Article.ArticleTitle: Efficacy of real-time feedback exercise therapy in patients following total hip arthroplasty: a pilot cluster-randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: The prevalence of hip osteoarthritis is increasing and frequently requires total hip arthroplasty (THA). However, a standardized rehabilitation protocol to ensure sustainable functional recovery from THA has yet to be established. Therefore, this study compared the effects of real-time feedback-assisted home-exercise versus standard written instructions on the functional performance of patients following unilateral THA.

This study was designed as a cluster-randomized controlled pilot trial with two parallel groups. Data from three-dimensional movement analysis, clinical examination, body-composition, activity monitoring and questionnaires were collected at baseline four weeks post-surgery, and follow-ups at three- and six-months post-surgery. Baseline measurements were followed by an eight-week supervised group exercise therapy. For home-exercise the control-group received printed instructions, whereas the intervention-group was provided a real-time feedback prototype.

A total of 22 patients, aged 52 to 73 years (mean 62.9), participated in the study, 21 completed the intervention and thereof, 19 could be assessed at six-months post-surgery. No statistically significant differences were found for the primary outcomes frontal knee, pelvis and trunk range-of-motion during level walking, nor the secondary outcomes Harris Hip Score (HHS), SF-12 and IPAQ short form. Both groups improved their mean walking speed, cadence, step length, isometric knee flexion force of operated limb, SF-12 physical domain and HHS.

Real-time feedback assisted home-exercise after THA did not differ when compared to commonly used written instructions in improving function and quality of life. However, patients in the real-time feedback group reported greater motivation and self-confidence regarding exercise performance, which was not reflected in the recorded numbers of home-exercise sessions.
The study was prospectively registered on 7th December 2023 at ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06161194.

Article.ArticleTitle: Protocol for the GAPA person-centred dental care at home intervention: a substudy within a cluster randomised controlled trial in Swedish home care.

Abstract.AbstractText: Oral health is essential to healthy ageing and closely linked to well-being, social participation, and quality of life. Frail older adults are at high risk of oral diseases, yet oral health is often insufficiently integrated into home care. Care staff frequently report limited competence and unclear routines, while older adults wish to participate actively in decisions about their oral health. GAPA Person-Centered Dental Care @ Home (Dental PCC@Home) is a co-designed model developed with older adults, significant others (informal caregivers), municipal care staff, and dental professionals. This substudy evaluates if Dental PCC@Home will promote oral health, participation, and self-determination among older adults living with complex care needs.

Dental PCC@Home is embedded within the parent GAPA cluster randomised controlled trial. Decisions about dental care are guided by a patient decision aid and discussion of needs expressed by the older adult or identified by care staff. Participation in the substudy is voluntary. Eligible intervention-group participants are offered a patient decision aid to support decisions about whether and how to receive dental care, followed by one of four pathways: online dental consultation, mobile home dental care, a dental clinic visit, or declining dental care. Eligible control-group participants receive standard care. Oral health and quality-of-life assessments are conducted at baseline and at six and twelve months; cognitive function is assessed at baseline only. Co-primary outcomes are changes in oral health status (ROAG) and oral health-related quality of life (GOHAI) from baseline to twelve months. General health-related quality of life (EQ-5D-5 L) is a secondary outcome. Quantitative analyses will account for clustering and repeated measurements. Semi-structured interviews with older adults, significant others, and care staff will explore experiences of care, decision-making, and implementation and will be analysed using qualitative content analysis.

This project will generate evidence on a new cross-organisational model designed to improve access to oral health care for frail older adults living at home. By integrating dental care into existing care processes and offering flexible care pathways, the model has the potential to strengthen autonomy, reduce inequalities, promote health and, when indicated, address oral diseases earlier in home care. The findings may inform future practice, policy development, and person-centred approaches to oral health in ageing populations.

Article.ArticleTitle: A live biotherapeutic product for adult allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients: a partially randomized, placebo-controlled phase 1b trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Gastrointestinal (GI) microbiome disruption and impaired GI barrier integrity increase the risk of bloodstream infection (BSI) following allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant. Here we report results from a two-cohort (open-label, n = 15; randomized, placebo-controlled, n = 45) phase 1b study of SER-155, an investigational, cultivated, multi-strain, oral live biotherapeutic designed to address GI microbiome disruption GI epithelial barrier integrity in allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant recipients. In cohort 2, 34 of 45 participants received either SER-155 treatment (n = 20, SER-155 following microbiome conditioning with oral vancomycin), or placebo (n = 14), and subsequently received transplant. For the primary safety endpoint, SER-155 was well tolerated, with a safety profile comparable to placebo, no treatment-related serious adverse events and no infections with SER-155 species; the most common adverse events were diarrhea and nausea. Four participants in cohort 1 and four participants in cohort 2 (two participants in the SER-155 arm and two in the placebo arm) died during the study; none was attributable to SER-155. For the primary pharmacokinetic endpoint, engraftment was detected for 16 of 16 SER-155 strains, with a median of 11.5 strains detected after the first treatment course. The key secondary efficacy endpoint revealed a significantly lower incidence of BSI with SER-155 versus placebo (10.0% versus 43%; OR 0.15; 95% CI 0.01-1.13; P = 0.0423; 77% relative risk reduction). Other secondary efficacy endpoints (GI infection, acute graft-versus-host disease ≥grade 2, febrile neutropenia and a composite endpoint of BSI, GI infection or acute graft-versus-host disease) were not statistically significant. The secondary pharmacodynamic endpoint of GI domination by Enterococcus and Enterobacteriaceae spp. was not achieved. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04995653 .

Journal.Title: The American journal of geriatric psychiatry : official journal of the American Association for Geriatric Psychiatry

Article.ArticleTitle: Therapeutic Alliance is Linked With Suicidality Trajectories in Psychotherapy for Late-Life Depression.

Abstract.AbstractText: Late-life suicidality is rapidly increasing; psychotherapy may reduce suicidality, but trajectories of change in suicidality remain unclear. A strong therapeutic alliance may protect against persistent suicidality. We examined the association of alliance with suicidality trajectories during brief, remote interventions for depression.

Sixty middle-aged and older adults with major depression were randomized to brief remote psychosocial interventions. Suicidality and alliance were assessed during treatment. Patients' suicidality trajectories were classified as: 1) absent; 2) improved; 3) persistent, based on pre- to post-treatment changes. All three groups were included in mixed-effects models to examine the association between suicidality and alliance.

At baseline, 53% of patients endorsed suicidality, with 45% in the absent group, 45% improved, and 10% persistent. Patients in the absent and improved groups showed stable, strong alliance while the persistent group showed worsening alliance.

Simple, remote psychosocial interventions are promising first-line treatments for late-life suicidality. A strong alliance may reduce suicidality and enhance outcomes, guiding timely, personalized interventions.

Article.ArticleTitle: Calibrating risk perception in household food safety: A mixed-methods field trial of framing and regulatory fit.

Abstract.AbstractText: Food safety remains a critical global challenge. In recent years, China has placed increasing emphasis on food safety through household-level education. However, campaigns focusing on knowledge dissemination have demonstrated limited effectiveness because of the knowledge-behaviour gap. Evidence suggests that consumers' risk perceptions, defined as their subjective assessments of the health risks associated with improper household food-handling behaviours (HFHBs), influence behaviour more strongly than knowledge alone. This study identified previously unrecognised determinants of risk perception and developed and evaluated a novel intervention targeting perceptions of the risks associated with two critical improper HFHBs: cross-contamination and improper storage of leftovers. Semi-structured interviews with 27 residents identified three previously unrecognised factors influencing risk perception: simplification of complex risks, blunted perception of future risks, and high discounting of future risks. Guided by these insights, we developed gain- and loss-framed intervention videos. However, the gain-framed video was excluded from the formal experiments because it produced a weak framing effect in the pretest. Two field trials-a randomised controlled trial (N = 295) and a single-factor between-subjects experiment (N = 280)-subsequently confirmed that the loss-framed intervention videos significantly enhanced consumers' risk perceptions. Furthermore, intervention effects were significantly enhanced when loss-framed messages matched individuals' prevention regulatory focus, demonstrating a regulatory fit effect. To our knowledge, this is the first study to demonstrate both framing and regulatory fit effects in household food safety interventions. The findings provide public health agencies with validated, ready-to-use intervention materials and a replicable, evidence-based framework for designing behavioural interventions in other public health domains.

Journal.Title: Journal of drugs in dermatology : JDD

Article.ArticleTitle: Randomized Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study of a Supplement and Serum on Grey Hair.

Abstract.AbstractText: Worldwide, 74% of men and women between the ages of 45 and 65 have some grey hair. Currently, there is no treatment that has been shown in a clinical trial to repigment or slow the development of grey hair. In this study, we investigated the efficacy of a topical and supplement regimen (To The Root® serum and Not Today Grey supplement (Two Lines Inc.). A total of 173 men and women aged 28 to 65 years, with 5–25% grey hair, completed the study. Participants were randomized to include at least 40 subjects in each of the 4 groups: combination (supplement + serum), supplement (supplement + placebo serum), serum (serum + placebo supplement), and placebo (placebo supplement + placebo serum). There was a statistically significant and clinically meaningful reduction in the number of grey hairs in the group that received the combination of supplement and serum. This group had a 9.2% reduction in grey hair at week 12 (P=0.034 vs baseline) and a 13.0% reduction at week 24 (P=0.016 vs baseline). The placebo group had 9.7% increase (worsening) in the mean number of grey hairs from baseline to week 24. The comparison of the combination group vs the placebo group at week 24 showed a significant difference (P=0.004). These results were confirmed by photo grading of grey hair (P=0.002, week 24 vs baseline) and by subject observation of grey hair (P=0.002 vs baseline). These results represent synergistic effects of the proprietary blends in the oral supplement and the patented topical serum. &nbsp.

Journal.Title: Journal of drugs in dermatology : JDD

Article.ArticleTitle: A Moisturizer With Centella asiatica and Mandelic Acid Reduces Bruising and Speeds Recovery in Mature Skin.

Abstract.AbstractText: Dermatoporosis is a chronic cutaneous insufficiency syndrome characterized by skin atrophy, purpura, bruising, delayed healing, and increased injury susceptibility. This study evaluated an investigational cream, GC (Galderma Laboratories, L.P., Fort Worth, TX), in subjects with mature, crepey, bruise-prone skin, using a novel method to assess bruise severity and duration.

This 12-week multicenter, randomized, blinded, in-use study recruited men and women aged 40 to 60 years with fragile, bruise-prone skin to apply GC cream twice daily to knees and thighs. A subset of 15 subjects underwent electric cupping on 1 randomized upper knee at baseline and week 12 to induce localized ecchymosis. Bruise severity was evaluated 15 minutes postinduction by investigators using standardized photography, and subjects captured daily images until resolution. Safety, tolerability, and subject satisfaction were assessed throughout.

After 12 weeks of GC cream use, investigator-assessed bruise severity score was significantly lower than baseline (mean [SD] 3.27 [1.33] vs 4.13 [1.02]; [P=.0087]). Days to bruise resolution were also numerically shorter at week 12 compared with baseline (mean [SE] 6.33 [0.91] vs 8.00 [0.56]; [log-rank P=.3134]). Serial photography confirmed expected temporal evolution and resolution of bruising and supported improvement in investigator-assessed severity. Subject satisfaction was high, and there were no related adverse events.

Twelve weeks of twice-daily GC cream use significantly reduced bruise severity induced by electric cupping and helped bruises resolve faster. These findings support GC cream as an important new option to reduce bruise potential and improve skin health of subjects with dermatoporosis. &nbsp.

Article.ArticleTitle: Co-Designed Text Messaging Intervention for Parents of Children With Early Childhood Caries: Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Early childhood caries (ECC) is a prevalent yet preventable disease that significantly impacts young children's health and quality of life. The World Health Organization's Global Strategy and Action Plan on Oral Health 2023-2030 highlights the potential of mobile health programs to enhance engagement and support sustained oral health behavior change.

The aim of this study was to assess the effectiveness of the SmilesUp 12-week SMS text messaging-based education and support program to improve parents' management of their children's oral health behaviors compared to standard clinical care.

We conducted a multisite, assessor-blinded, parallel-design randomized controlled trial among parents of children aged 0 to 6 years who had an ECC diagnosis and attended 1 of 6 public dental clinics in metropolitan, regional, and rural New South Wales, Australia. Participants were randomly assigned to either an intervention group receiving the fully automated 12-week SmilesUp program (3 SMS text messages weekly) or a control group. Both groups continued to receive usual standard dental clinical treatment. The primary behavioral outcome was parent-reported twice-daily toothbrushing with fluoride toothpaste. Secondary outcomes included adherence to oral health-promoting bedtime routines and child consumption of sugar-sweetened foods and beverages. Oral health self-efficacy was measured using 6 behavioral theory-mapped items across oral hygiene, diet, and bedtime routines.

A total of 154 participants were enrolled and randomized (n=78, 50.6% in the control group; n=76, 49.4% in the intervention group) across 6 sites, with 80.5% (124/154) completing the follow-up assessment. High program adherence was observed, with 96.1% (73/76) of intervention participants completing the program. At 12 weeks, a greater proportion of SmilesUp participants reported brushing their children's teeth twice daily (45/61, 73.8% vs 42/63, 66.7%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.45, 95% CI 0.95-6.74; P=.07), though this difference was not statistically significant. Significant improvements were observed in adherence to bedtime routines (54/61, 88.5% vs 45/63, 71.4%; aOR 3.25, 95% CI 1.15-10.18; P=.03) as well as oral health knowledge on toothbrushing (46/50, 92.0% vs 41/52, 78.8%; aOR 5.47, 95% CI 1.48-25.19; P=.02). No statistically significant differences were found in sugar-sweetened food (10/61, 16.4% vs 4/63, 6.3%; aOR 3.72, 95% CI 1.02-17.14; P=.06) or beverage (25/61, 41.0% vs. 27/63, 42.9%; aOR 1.08, 95% CI 0.49-2.30; P=.85) consumption.

These findings suggest that co-designed SMS text messaging-based programs show promise and may represent a feasible strategy for oral health behavior change. However, larger-scale and longer-term studies are needed to confirm sustained effectiveness using clinical outcomes. Future research should also explore ways mobile health can be scaled and cost-effectively embedded into comprehensive, interdisciplinary primary models of care.

Article.ArticleTitle: Improving CommonGround, an Online Peer Support Intervention for People Living With Long-Term Physical Health Conditions and Subthreshold Depression: Theory of Change-Informed Qualitative Study.

Abstract.AbstractText: People living with long-term physical health conditions who are also experiencing subthreshold depression are at risk of developing major depression. In partnership with lived experience experts, clinicians, and software developers, we co-designed CommonGround, an online peer support and psychoeducation platform. CommonGround's Theory of Change (ToC) was also conceptualized to outline the intermediate outcomes (and associated indicators of whether such outcomes are achieved) needed to improve the mental health of the target population.

This qualitative study, informed by the ToC, aimed to examine the acceptability, usability, and intervention mechanisms of CommonGround and ultimately refine the ToC and corresponding intervention design ahead of definitive evaluation.

A nested qualitative study was conducted within a remote, 12-week feasibility randomized controlled trial comparing CommonGround (intervention group) to signposting to National Health Service (NHS) web pages (control group). Thirty-nine participants were purposively sampled and interviewed within 6 weeks postintervention about their experiences of CommonGround and trial participation. The interview schedule and thematic framework analysis were rooted in a pretrial ToC while being responsive to emergent themes.

Evaluating the assumptions and intermediate outcomes (via their indicators) refined our understanding of how CommonGround may support mental well-being. Overall, participants viewed CommonGround as an appropriate, safe space to access self-management information and support from others with a unique shared understanding of chronic illness. However, many participants felt more time was needed for genuine social relations to form and community culture to evolve. Anonymity helped foster a sense of safety but, for some participants, limited the formation of genuine connections. Other factors contributing to low engagement included personal circumstances (eg, limited time). Key suggestions for future development included creating a mobile app that would be easier and more intuitive to access and navigate.

CommonGround was considered an acceptable and appropriate space to access peer support, with the potential to positively impact psychological well-being by fostering shared understanding, support, and knowledge exchange. Beyond informing the future evaluation of CommonGround in a definitive trial, the refined ToC identifies the key preconditions, intermediate outcomes, and associated indicators, and assumptions that may underpin the acceptability and usability of digital peer support interventions in achieving their intended outcomes. We also demonstrate how evaluating and refining components of the ToC after the intervention had been implemented in the trial enabled a more nuanced understanding of how and why the intervention may work, for whom, under what circumstances, and informed changes to improve the co-designed intervention.

Article.ArticleTitle: Pain, sensory acceptability, and treatment compliance following cryotherapy and topical anesthetics in children: A randomized clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: This randomized clinical trial aimed to compare the effects of cryotherapy, anesthetic spray, and gel on pain, anxiety, physiological responses, taste acceptability, and treatment compliance in children aged 7-10 years undergoing their first dental treatment. 100 healthy children were randomly allocated into four groups: 10% lidocaine spray, 20% benzocaine gel, cryotherapy with distilled water cooled to +4 °C, and lidocaine spray cooled to +4 °C. Following topical application, buccal infiltration anesthesia was administered. Anxiety, pain, and physiological responses were assessed using the Modified Dental Anxiety Scale and Facial Image Scale, Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale, and pulse-oximeter. Taste acceptability and treatment compliance were evaluated using a three-point Hedonic Scale and the FRANKL Scale. Repeated Measures ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U, and Kruskal-Wallis tests were applied. No significant differences were observed among the groups in anxiety, pain, pulse rate, oxygen saturation, or taste acceptability (p > 0.05). Pulse rate increased from the pre-operative to the post-operative period in all groups (p = 0.006), with no significant group × time interaction. FRANKL scores were significantly higher in the cryotherapy-distilled water group compared with the gel and cooled-spray groups (p = 0.001), a finding considered exploratory. Pain and anxiety outcomes following cryotherapy did not differ significantly from those of the topical anesthetic agents, while treatment compliance was higher, suggesting that cryotherapy may be a promising non-pharmacological option, pending confirmation in non-inferiority trials.

Article.ArticleTitle: Immunothrombosis Biomarkers and Multi-Omics Profiles After Successful Recanalization in Patients Receiving Ischemic Postconditioning: An Exploratory Analysis of the INSPIRE Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Successful recanalization after endovascular thrombectomy does not always restore microvascular perfusion, highlighting the need for adjunctive strategies. Ischemic postconditioning (IPostC) involves brief, controlled​ cycles of flow interruption and restoration at the onset of reperfusion to attenuate ischemia-reperfusion injury. In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h. This exploratory secondary analysis included all 60 randomized patients. We investigated whether IPostC was associated with early changes in immunothrombosis, coagulation, and microvascular transit and explored associated plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiles. Arterial blood obtained approximately 15 min after successful recanalization was analyzed using flow cytometry and thromboelastography. Quantitative digital subtraction angiography-derived microcirculation time was analyzed in 55 patients, and plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling was performed in 29 patients. Compared with controls, patients receiving IPostC had lower neutrophil CD11b expression (median, 52.15 versus 64.27 mean fluorescence intensity ×10²; P = 0.011), a lower thromboelastography α-angle (65.15° versus 67.95°; P = 0.037), and shorter microcirculation time (2.11 versus 3.03 s; P = 0.020). Longer microcirculation time was associated with greater infarct growth (r = 0.533; P < 0.001). Proteomic and metabolomic analyses identified signals involving blood-brain barrier and extracellular-matrix organization and mitochondrial bioenergetics. Biomarker comparisons were not adjusted for multiple comparisons; in the omics analyses, no protein and 17 metabolites remained significant after false discovery rate correction. In summary, IPostC was associated with lower neutrophil activation, slower clot propagation, and faster microvascular transit after recanalization, and multi-omics profiling pointed to blood-brain barrier integrity and mitochondrial bioenergetics as candidate pathways. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger studies. Trial registration: NCT06545734, registered 9 August 2024.

Article.ArticleTitle: Coronary artery calcification is not associated with survival in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer: a secondary analysis of the EXPAND trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Computed tomography (CT) is the clinical standard for staging of gastrointestinal cancer. Previous studies have highlighted the prognostic significance of coronary artery calcification (CAC) detected by CT in various types of cancer. However, the prognostic role of CAC scoring in gastrointestinal cancers is still unclear. The aim of this study was to investigate the impact of CT-defined CAC on overall survival (OS) in patients with advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer.

CAC was semiquantitatively measured using the visual Weston method on baseline CT scans in 785 patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction cancer from the phase III EXPAND trial. This present study is a secondary analysis of the base line CT images. In the original analysis patients were randomly assigned to first-line treatment with cisplatin/capecitabin ± cetuximab. The primary endpoint of the current subanalysis is the OS. For statistical analysis group differences were calculated using the Mann-Whitney-U test and ANOVA test. Kaplan-Meier curves and multivariable Cox regression analysis were used to test the effect of CAC on mortality.

The median CAC score was 1 (IQR 0; 3). A total of 337 patients (42.9%) had no visible CAC (CAC score 0). Male patients had statistically significant higher CAC score compared to female patients (median 1 versus 0, p < 0.0001). In univariable Cox regression CAC showed no significant association with survival when analysed as a continuous value (HR: 0.99, 95% CI: 0.96-1.02, p = 0.74), and when dichotomized for absence and presence of calcification (HR:1.08, 95% CI: 0.92-1.26, p = 0.34). Similar results were identified in further subgroup analyses.

CT-defined CAC scoring has no relevant prognostic impact in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer undergoing first-line chemotherapy. The present study cannot confirm the promising results for CAC scoring in lung cancer patients.

Article.ArticleTitle: Benson relaxation technique for perioperative anxiety and depressive symptoms in patients undergoing brain tumor surgery: a clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Patients undergoing craniotomy for brain tumors confront psychophysiological crisis. Managing perioperative distress poses a clinical paradox, as standard pharmacological sedatives are carefully restricted based on neurological status and institutional protocols to avoid masking critical postoperative neurological signs. This study investigated the efficacy of the Benson relaxation technique (BRT), a nonpharmacological mind-body intervention, on perioperative anxiety and depressive symptoms in this vulnerable population.

In this clinical trial, out of 84 patients assessed for eligibility, 74 eligible patients undergoing brain tumor resection were allocated to either the BRT intervention group (n = 37) or the control group (n = 37). The intervention group completed supervised BRT sessions (muscle relaxation, diaphragmatic breathing, and word repetition) on the evening of ICU admission, 60 min preoperatively, and 24 h postoperatively. Both groups received routine care, and anxiety and depressive symptoms were evaluated at identical time points (baseline on the evening of ICU admission prior to the intervention, 30 min preoperatively, and 24 h postoperatively). Data were analyzed using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA).

Seventy patients completed the trial (35 per group). At 24 h postoperatively, ANCOVA adjusted for baseline scores showed that the BRT group had significantly lower anxiety scores compared to the control group, with an adjusted mean difference of - 4.16 points (95% CI, - 5.40 to - 2.93; P < 0.001). Regarding depressive symptoms, baseline scores were below the threshold for clinically significant symptoms (HADS-D < 8) in both cohorts; however, at 24 h postoperatively, the BRT group had significantly lower adjusted depressive symptom scores than the control group, with an adjusted mean difference of - 2.32 points (95% CI, - 3.51 to - 1.12; P < 0.001), indicating a preventive effect against postoperative reactive depressive symptoms.

The Benson relaxation technique is a safe, feasible, and well-tolerated nurse-led mind-body strategy that effectively mitigates perioperative anxiety and reduces postoperative depressive symptoms without adverse events. These findings support integrating structured nonpharmacological modalities into neurosurgical care.

Article.ArticleTitle: Prognostic value of Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio after percutaneous coronary intervention.

Abstract.AbstractText: Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) physiological indices have prognostic relevance. Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (μQFR) enables wire-free, rapid, single-view functional assessment, yet its long-term prognostic value after PCI remains incompletely established.
We sought to evaluate the prognostic value of post-PCI μQFR for long-term adverse outcomes.

This prespecified subgroup analysis of the FAVOR III China trial included 3,825 patients. All PCI-treated vessels with a reference diameter ≥2.5 mm and 50-90% diameter stenosis were analysed for offline post-PCI μQFR. The primary endpoint was 5-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; including death from any cause, myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven revascularisation).

Post-PCI μQFR was successfully analysed in 4,196 vessels from 3,455 patients, with similar distributions between the randomised treatment groups. At 5 years, a low post-PCI μQFR was associated with a higher incidence of MACE compared with the intermediate and high post-PCI μQFR tertiles (23.1% vs 19.0% vs 17.2%; p=0.001). Using the highest tertile (μQFR>0.95) as a reference, adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) were 1.08 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.87-1.34) for the intermediate tertile (0.92-0.95) and 1.30 (95% CI: 1.06-1.60) for the lowest tertile (μQFR ≤0.91). Using a receiver operating characteristic-derived cutoff, MACE occurred more frequently in patients with post-PCI μQFR <0.94 (22.3% vs 17.4%, aHR 1.23, 95% CI: 1.04-1.47; p=0.02) than in those with post-PCI μQFR ≥0.94. No significant interaction was observed between treatment strategy and post-PCI μQFR (p for interaction=0.23).

Post-PCI μQFR distributions were similar between treatment groups, but lower values were associated with higher 5-year adverse event risk without significant treatment interaction. Its limited binary discrimination supports use as a continuous metric for post-PCI physiological risk stratification. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT03656848).

Article.ArticleTitle: Full-Service Mobile Food Markets and Dietary Quality in Low-Income Housing Communities: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Full-service mobile markets, also known as grocery stores on wheels, may improve diet-related outcomes by bringing low-cost, nutritious food to individuals experiencing low incomes and low food access.
To determine the impact of the full-service Twin Cities Mobile Market on dietary outcomes in low-income communities.

This cluster randomized clinical trial was conducted over 3 waves (January 2022 to October 2025) across 12 public or private subsidized housing sites in the Minneapolis-St. Paul, Minnesota, area. Participants were screened for interest in the mobile market. Follow-up assessments began after 6 months of market service. Analyses were finalized September 2026.
Sites were randomized to weekly market service or waiting list control groups.

Primary outcome: diet quality (Healthy Eating Index-2020 via 24-hour recalls). A priori secondary outcomes: dietary intake (fruit and vegetable, energy, sodium, and percentage of calories from added sugar), food security (18-item US Department of Agriculture Food Security Screening Module), and fruit and vegetable servings procured for the home (validated tracking tool). Adjusted intention-to-treat (ITT) generalized estimating equations were used to assess outcome differences between treatment groups.

Among 262 adults who enrolled in the mobile market study, 242 participants (mean [SD] age, 66.5 [11.5] years; 156 women [64.5%]) across 12 sites completed baseline assessments and were randomized to mobile market service or waiting list control groups. There were 137 individuals (56.6%) who received Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits. Sites had a mean (SD) of 18.2 (4.4) weekly transactions (mean of 110 of 1071 households [10.3%]). Of 109 intervention site participants, 47 individuals (43.1%) shopped at the mobile market 1 or more times in implementation months 5 to 6, while 90 of 94 individuals who reported ever using the market (95.7%) reported that they would recommend the market service. Participant retention was 218 of 242 participants (90.0%). In ITT models, the primary outcome of diet quality (adjusted mean difference, 1.25 [95% CI, -1.60 to 4.10]) among 215 participants and 6 of 7 secondary outcomes (fruit and vegetable, energy, and added sugar intake; food security and food security improvement; fruit and vegetable procurement) were not significantly different between groups. Intervention site participants consumed an adjusted mean difference of 397 mg (95% CI, -636 to -158 mg) less sodium daily compared with participants in the waiting list control group. Main findings were consistent across 4 sensitivity and supplemental analyses, except the per-protocol sensitivity analysis, which found that participants in the intervention group consumed an adjusted mean difference of 2.35% (95% CI, 0.66%-4.04%) more calories from added sugar compared with the control group.

In this study, satisfaction with the mobile market was high, but the mobile market did not improve diet quality or most outcomes examined. The mobile market was associated with a meaningful sodium reduction that could improve population-level health.

Article.ArticleTitle: Rifamycin use and gut microbial antibiotic resistance genes in cirrhosis: Results from a double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Antimicrobial resistance gene (ARG) carriage is associated with poor outcomes in patients with liver cirrhosis, which is worsened by repeated antibiotic exposure and hospitalizations. While the semi-synthetic rifamycin derivative, rifaximin, has recently been linked to ARG expansion preclinically, the effects of rifamycin SV MMX (RiVM) on the gut resistome remain unknown. We evaluated longitudinal resistome changes with RiVM in cirrhosis. The randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled RIVET trial (15 RiVM, 15 placebo) included compensated cirrhosis patients who underwent shotgun metagenomic sequencing before/after 30 days of therapy. ARGs were annotated using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database. The longitudinal resistome was evaluated using univariable and multi-variable methods (LEfSe, paired-Wilcoxon testing, and MaAsLin3), and machine learning (ML) was used to determine ARG changes at subject and group levels. RiVM induced minimal perturbation of the gut resistome, without significant change in ARGs versus after FDR adjustment. Complementary approaches (univariable and multivariable) identified a trend towards lower vancomycin resistance ARGs, including vanW and vanT operon-associated genes, after RiVM exposure. In contrast, several Enterobacteriaceae-associated multidrug efflux regulators (including evgS, emrK, and mdtA) showed nominal increases post-rifamycin that did not withstand FDR. Group-level ML demonstrated limited discrimination between groups; however, within-subject longitudinal models achieved improved classification performance. No increase in infections or treatment-related safety concerns was observed. We conclude that rifamycin MMX was not associated with infections and did not enrich antimicrobial resistance genes compared to placebo in a small randomized 30-day clinical trial in patients with compensated cirrhosis. There was a tendency towards reduced vancomycin resistance and ARG reduction after rifamycin exposure. Registration: NCT04082780 www.clinicaltrials.gov.

Article.ArticleTitle: Added Value of Preoperative Contrast Enhanced Mammography in Staging of Malignant Breast Lesions (PROCEM): A Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Background Contrast-enhanced mammography (CEM) is increasingly used in breast cancer diagnostics; however, randomized trials assessing the added value of CEM in preoperative staging of breast cancer beyond digital mammography, digital breast tomosynthesis, and US are lacking. Purpose To assess the added value of CEM for preoperative breast cancer staging in a randomized controlled trial. Materials and Methods This prospective randomized controlled trial (Added Value of Preoperative Contrast Enhanced Mammography in Staging of Malignant Breast Lesions) enrolled women diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer eligible for primary surgery at two breast centers in Sweden. Participants were randomized 1:1 to preoperative CEM or control from November 2020 through April 2024. The primary outcome was a 10% change in treatment due to preoperative CEM findings. Secondary outcomes included differences in reoperation and mastectomy rates between groups and accuracy of malignant extent estimation with CEM, mammography/tomosynthesis, and US using histopathologic extent as the reference, assessed with Bland-Altman statistics and concordance analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed according to menopausal status, breast density, histopathologic type of cancer, lesion size, and presence of microcalcifications at baseline imaging. Results In total, 415 participants (median age, 66 years; IQR, 56-73 years) completed the trial: 202 in the CEM group and 213 in the control group. Treatment was changed in 17 of 202 participants (8.4%; 95% CI: 5.3, 13.1) based on CEM findings. No evidence of differences was observed between the CEM and control groups with regard to mastectomy (17% [35 of 202] vs 18% [39 of 213]; P = .78) or reoperation (7.9% [16 of 202] vs 10% [22 of 213]; P = .39) rates. CEM showed the closest agreement with histopathologic malignant extent (bias, 3.5 mm), outperforming mammography and/or tomosynthesis (4.8 mm) and US (10.7 mm) overall and in nine of 10 predefined subgroups, except for ductal carcinoma in situ. Conclusion This trial did not meet its primary end point of a 10% treatment change; however, preoperative CEM improved malignant extent estimation. Article.ArticleTitle: Comparison of Traumatic Complications following Prostate Biopsy in Men with Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Due to Prostate Disease Using Biopty Gun versus Semiautomatic Needle.

Abstract.AbstractText: Prostate biopsy has evolved to improve yield and reduce complications. The development of biopty guns added to this trend. It is an improvement on the semiautomatic needle.

This study aimed to compare semi-automatic and fully-automatic biopsy devices used for digitally guided transrectal prostate biopsy for the rate and extent of post-biopsy pain and bleeding complications.

Sixty-four patients were randomised into two groups, each with 32 patients. Group 1 patients were biopsied with 16G Medplus ® semi-automatic biopsy needles, whereas Bard-Magnum ® biopty gun with 16G needles was used for Group 2. Twelve systematic cores were taken from both groups. Post-biopsy pain was assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale and Wong-Baker Faces Pain Rating Scale. The rate and extent of post-biopsy haematuria/urethral bleeding and rectal bleeding were evaluated. Data were collected using a structured pro forma and analysed using IBM-SPSS.

Sixty-four men participated in the study. Haematuria/urethral bleeding occurred in 37.5% (12) and 31.25% (10) patients in Groups 1 and 2, respectively. Bladder irrigation was done for 8.3% (1) and 20% (2) of those who bled from Groups 1 and 2, respectively. Significant rectal bleeding occurred in 31.25% (10) and 28.13% (9) patients from Groups 1 and 2, respectively. More pain was noted in Group 1. These differences in bleeding complications and pain were not statistically significant.
The two devices did not exhibit significant differences in terms of pain or bleeding complications when used for prostate biopsy.

Article.ArticleTitle: Visual Perceptual Learning Based on Adaptive Contrast Detection Training Enhances Vision and Contrast Sensitivity in Diabetic Retinopathy.

Abstract.AbstractText: To evaluate the efficacy of home-based visual perceptual learning (VPL) on visual function and explore the residual visual plasticity in diabetic retinopathy (DR).

Thirty-six DR patients following routine therapies were randomized (1:1). Twenty-eight completed the study (VPL, n = 12; control, n = 16) after excluding eight for poor adherence or incomplete follow-up. The VPL group underwent 3-month home-based grating detection training at individual cutoff spatial frequencies. Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), grating acuity (GA), contrast sensitivity to first-order motion stimuli (1stM), optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), and Low Vision Quality-of-Life (LVQOL) questionnaire were assessed at baseline, 1 month, and 3 months for the VPL group and at baseline and 3 months for the control group.

BCVA improved from 0.36 to 0.26 logMAR (P = 0.003), GA improved from 12.42 to 17.47 cycles per degree (2.96 dB) and 1stM increased from 64.26 to 83.42 (2.27 dB) in the VPL group. A significant group × time interaction was found for GA (F1, 26 = 63.595, P < 0.001, \( \eta_{p}^2 \) = 0.710), 1stM (F1, 26 = 32.663, P < 0.001, \( \eta_{p}^2 \) = 0.557), and BCVA (F1, 26 = 10.872, P = 0.003, \( \eta_{p}^2 \) = 0.295). The LVQOL score increased (+4.33; P < 0.001) and correlated with ΔGA (r = 0.671, P = 0.017). OCTA parameters remained stable in both groups.

The results reveal significant plasticity in the visual system in DR and suggest that contrast detection training may extend to motion perception tasks. Our study provides additional support for VPL as a potential treatment for DR.

Article.ArticleTitle: Visual rigid laryngoscope versus Macintosh laryngoscope using low-dose relaxants in thyroid surgery.

Abstract.AbstractText: This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of the Macintosh laryngoscope versus the visual rigid laryngoscope (VRL) for tracheal intubation under a low-dose muscle relaxant protocol in thyroid surgery, to provide clinical evidence for the selection of optimal intubation tools for this setting.

In this single-center, randomized controlled trial, two experienced anesthesiologists performed tracheal intubation using either the Macintosh laryngoscope (Mac group, n = 47) or VRL (VRL group, n = 45) in patients undergoing elective thyroid surgery with Intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM). The primary outcome was intubation time. Secondary outcomes included first-attempt intubation success rate, hemodynamic changes during the peri-intubation period, laryngoscopic view graded by the Cormack-Lehane classification, and intubation-related complications.

The intubation time was significantly shorter in the VRL group (mean ± SD, 33.27 ± 8.36 s) than in the Mac group (52.19 ± 9.83 s) (P < 0.001). The intubation success rate and heart rates did not differ between groups (P > 0.05). The mean arterial pressure (MAP) at intubation and the amplitude of MAP increase during intubation was lower in Group VRL than in Group Mac (P < 0.005). No statistically significant differences were observed between the two groups in peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2), Cormack-Lehane classification, or intubation-related complications (P > 0.05).

For thyroid surgery using a low-dose muscle relaxant protocol to enable IONM, the VRL provides significantly shorter intubation time and better hemodynamic stability at intubation compared with the Macintosh laryngoscope. No significant differences were observed between the two devices in intubation success rate, laryngoscopic view, or intubation-related complications.

Article.ArticleTitle: Five-year outcomes of the STOP-AD randomised controlled trial: Long-term effects of early emollient therapy in high-risk infants.

Abstract.AbstractText: Early-life skin barrier enhancement has been proposed as a strategy to prevent atopic dermatitis (AD), but results from emollient prevention trials have been inconsistent, and long-term outcomes remain poorly defined. The STOP-AD trial previously demonstrated a reduction in AD incidence following brief early emollient use in high-risk infants. Whether these effects persist beyond infancy is unknown.

This study reports the blinded five-year follow-up of the STOP-AD single-centre, randomised controlled trial. Term infants at high risk of AD were randomised within 4 days of birth to either twice-daily whole-body emollient application for the first 8 weeks of life or to standard routine skin care. At 5 years, participants underwent blinded, in-person clinical assessment. AD was diagnosed using UK Working Party Diagnostic Criteria, and disease severity was assessed using SCORAD. Primary outcome was point prevalence of AD at 5 years. Secondary outcomes included AD severity. Complete-case analyses were supplemented by multiple imputation to assess the impact of missing data.

A total of 177 children completed the five-year follow-up. The point prevalence of AD at 5 years was lower in the intervention group than in the control group (12.3% vs. 24.0%; RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.26-1.02; p = .048). Among children with AD, disease severity was also lower in the intervention group (median SCORAD 12.0 [IQR 8.2-15.2] vs. 19.6 [IQR 11.8-23.4]; p = .034). Multiple imputation to account for missing outcome data produced a similar treatment effect (OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.19-1.03; p = .060), although with greater uncertainty.

Early, short-term emollient use initiated in the neonatal period was associated with lower AD prevalence and severity at 5 years in high-risk children. Although the effect estimate remained similar following multiple imputation, uncertainty due to attrition remained. These findings suggest that brief early-life barrier support may influence longer-term AD outcomes and support further investigation of the timing and formulation of preventive skin-barrier interventions.

Article.ArticleTitle: [The therapeutic effect of drug-eluting stent placement in the resection of frontal sinus orbital communication lesions].

Abstract.AbstractText: Objective:To analyze the clinical efficacy of drug stent placement after resection of frontal sinus orbital communication lesions. Methods:Forty-six patients who underwent frontal sinus orbital communication lesion resection surgery in the hospital from January 2021 to December 2024 were selected and randomly divided into an observation group and a control group using a random number table method, with 23 patients in each group. The control group received routine treatment after surgery, while the observation group placed a fully degradable sinus drug stent in the surgical area on the basis of the control group. Compare the patency rate of frontal sinus drainage, classical Lund Kennedy（c-LK） score, modified olfactory fissure Lund Kennedy（oc-LK） score, and Lund Mackay CT score between two groups of patients at 30 and 90 days after surgery, and calculate the postoperative intervention rate and incidence of adverse reactions. Results:At 30 and 90 days after surgery, the frontal sinus drainage patency rates in the observation group were 95.65% and 86.96%, respectively, which were significantly higher than the control group's 52.17% and 43.48%（P<0.05）; The c-LK score, oc LK score, and Lund Mackay CT score of the observation group were significantly lower than those of the control group（P<0.05）; At 30 and 90 days after surgery, the intervention rate in the observation group was 8.70%, which was lower than the control group's 43.48% and 47.83%（P<0.05）; There was no statistically significant difference in the incidence of adverse reactions between the two groups（8.70% vs 4.35%）（P>0.05）. Conclusion:Implantation of fully degradable sinus drug stent after resection of frontal sinus orbital communication lesions can effectively maintain smooth drainage of the frontal sinus, reduce inflammation in the surgical area, lower the rate of postoperative re intervention, and effectively improve surgical efficacy. For patients with extensive lesion areas, severe intraoperative sinus mucosal damage, or high-risk factors for restenosis such as eosinophilic inflammation, the benefits are more definitive.

OtherAbstract.AbstractText: 目的：分析额窦眼眶沟通病变切除术后放置药物支架的临床疗效。 方法：选取2021年1月至2024年12月医院收治的行额窦眼眶沟通病变切除术的46例患者，采用随机数字表法分为观察组和对照组，每组23例。对照组术后给予常规治疗，观察组在对照组基础上在术区放置全降解鼻窦药物支架。比较2组患者术后30、90 d的额窦引流通畅率、经典Lund-Kennedy（c-LK）评分、改良嗅裂Lund-Kennedy（oc-LK）评分、Lund-Mackay CT评分，统计术后干预率及不良反应发生率。 结果：术后30、90 d，观察组额窦引流通畅率分别为95.65%、86.96%，显著高于对照组的52.17%、43.48%（P<0.05）；观察组c-LK评分、oc-LK评分及Lund-Mackay CT评分均显著低于对照组（P<0.05）；术后30、90 d，观察组术后干预率均为8.70%，低于对照组43.48%和47.83%（P<0.05）；2组不良反应发生率比较（8.70% vs 4.35%），差异无统计学意义（P>0.05）。 结论：额窦眼眶沟通病变切除术后植入全降解鼻窦药物支架可有效维持额窦引流通畅，减轻术区炎症，降低术后再干预率，有效提高手术疗效。对于病变范围广泛、术中窦口黏膜损伤较重或伴有嗜酸粒细胞性炎症等再狭窄高风险因素的患者，获益更为明确。.

Article.ArticleTitle: [Clinical exploration of near-infrared autofluorescence imaging for parathyroid gland preservation in thyroid cancer surgery].

Abstract.AbstractText: Objective:To evaluate the clinical value of near-infrared autofluorescence（NIRAF） imaging for intraoperative identification and preservation of parathyroid glands（PGs） during thyroid cancer surgery, with a particular focus on its efficacy in identifying inferior PGs-which have significant anatomical variability-and its role in preventing permanent hypoparathyroidism. Methods:A prospective randomized controlled trial was conducted. A total of 96 patients with thyroid cancer scheduled for total thyroidectomy and bilateral central neck dissection at Chengdu Sixth People's Hospital between January 2023 and June 2024 were consecutively enrolled and randomly assigned to an observation group （n=44） or a control group （n=52）. In the observation group, a NIRAF imaging device（excitation wavelength: 785 nm; emission detection: 820-850 nm） was used intraoperatively, with a fluorescence ratio ≥1.4 set as the identification threshold; preservation decisions（in situ preservation or autotransplantation） were guided by simultaneous perfusion assessment. The control group received conventional visual inspection combined with carbon nanoparticle negative staining. The primary outcomes were the identification rate of inferior PGs and the incidence of permanent hypoparathyroidism. Secondary outcomes included the overall PG identification rate, inadvertent excision rate, and incidence of transient hypoparathyroidism. Parathyroid function was evaluated during a 6month postoperative followup. Results:Baseline characteristics were balanced between the two groups. The observation group showed significantly higher identification rates for both inferior PGs（92.0% vs. 58.7%, P<0.001） and overall PGs（94.3% vs. 73.1%, P<0.001）, as well as a lower inadvertent excision rate（1.1% vs. 7.2%, P=0.008）. The incidence of permanent hypoparathyroidism showed a decreasing trend in the observation group（0 vs. 5.8%, P=0.155）; the incidence of transient hypoparathyroidism was also lower（9.1% vs. 23.1%, P=0.046）. No statistically significant difference was observed in operative time between the two groups（P>0.05）. Conclusion:NIRAF imaging enables efficient and accurate identification of inferior parathyroid glands, significantly improves intraoperative PG preservation, effectively reduces the incidence of transient hypoparathyroidism, and shows a decreasing trend in permanent hypoparathyroidism.

OtherAbstract.AbstractText: 目的：探讨基于自体荧光特性的近红外荧光显像仪在甲状腺癌手术中识别与保护甲状旁腺（parathyroid glands，PGs）的临床价值，特别是对解剖变异较大的下位PGs的识别效果及对术后永久性甲状旁腺功能减退的预防作用。 方法：采用前瞻性随机对照研究设计，连续纳入2023年1月至2024年6月成都市第六人民医院耳鼻咽喉头颈外科拟行甲状腺全切除及双侧中央区淋巴结清扫术的甲状腺癌患者96例，随机分为观察组（44例）与对照组（52例）。观察组术中应用近红外荧光显像仪（激发光785 nm，探测荧光820～850 nm），以荧光比率≥1.4为识别阈值，并结合血供评估指导原位保留或自体移植；对照组采用传统肉眼识别联合纳米碳负显影技术。主要观察指标为下位PGs识别率与术后永久性甲旁减发生率；次要指标包括PGs总识别率、误切率及暂时性甲旁减发生率。术后随访6个月评估甲状旁腺功能。 结果：2组基线资料均衡。观察组下位PGs识别率显著高于对照组（92.0% vs 58.7%，P<0.001），PGs总识别率亦更高（94.3% vs 73.1%，P<0.001）；误切率显著降低（1.1% vs 7.2%，P=0.008）。观察组永久性甲旁减发生率呈下降趋势（0 vs 5.8%，P=0.155）；暂时性甲旁减发生率亦较低（9.1% vs 23.1%，P=0.046）。2组手术时间比较，差异无统计学意义（P>0.05）。 结论：近红外荧光显像仪可实现对下位甲状旁腺的高效、精准识别，显著提升术中PGs保护效果，有效降低术后暂时性甲旁减发生率，永久性甲旁减发生率呈下降趋势。.

Article.ArticleTitle: Pilot Implementation of an Adapted Online Clinic-Community Model for Childhood Obesity.

Abstract.AbstractText: Intensive health-behaviour lifestyle treatment is recommended for paediatric obesity, but evidence for young children and synchronous online delivery remains limited.
To evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary effectiveness of an adapted online clinic-community model for children aged 4 to < 8 years with overweight or obesity.

In this two-arm randomized controlled trial, children were randomized to an online family-based intervention or usual care. The primary outcome was treatment dose at 6 months, defined as intervention contact hours. Secondary outcomes included BMI z-score, percentage of the 95th BMI percentile, health-related quality of life, eating behaviours, and perceived movement skills at 3 and 6 months.

Forty children were enrolled; mean age was 6.6 ± 1.0 years and 58% were male. At 6 months, 70% of intervention participants achieved at least 26 treatment hours. Although the between-group differences were not statistically significant, the intervention group demonstrated numerically greater reductions in BMI z-score (-0.2 ± 0.3 vs. -0.1 ± 0.1; p = 0.091) and percentage of the 95th BMI percentile (-3.5 ± 6.4 vs. -0.2 ± 4.0; p = 0.075). Physical quality of life improved at 3 and 6 months, object control skills at 3 months, and perceived locomotor skills at 6 months.

The adapted online model was feasible and acceptable, with preliminary improvements in physical quality of life, movement skills, and BMI metrics. Larger adequately powered trials are needed to confirm effectiveness and longer-term outcomes.

Article.ArticleTitle: Multiple intra-articular injections of umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells in treating severe knee osteoarthritis: a triple-blind randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (UC-MSCs), with multidirectional differentiation potential, immunomodulatory properties, and paracrine repair functions, have emerged as a promising therapeutic approach for knee osteoarthritis (KOA). This study aimed to compare the 1-year clinical efficacy, structural repair, and safety of multiple intra-articular injections of UC-MSCs versus sodium hyaluronate (SH) in patients with advanced KOA (Kellgren-Lawrence grade III-IV).

In this single-center, prospective, triple-blind randomized controlled trial, 50 eligible patients were randomly allocated to the UC-MSCs group (n = 25) or the SH group (n = 25). The UC-MSCs group received 4 intra-articular injections at 2-week intervals to sustain continuous paracrine effects and tissue repair, while the SH group received 5 weekly injections following its standard clinical dosing regimen. Evaluations were performed at baseline and 1, 3, 6, and 12 months post-treatment, including the visual analog scale (VAS), Western Ontario and McMaster University Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC), Lequesne score, subjective satisfaction score, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based radiological assessments (MOCART cartilage repair score, bone marrow edema remission rate, and meniscal injury repair rate).

The UC-MSCs group showed a significantly greater and sustained reduction in VAS scores without rebound: the mean VAS score decreased from 7.2 ± 1.1 to 3.36 ± 0.8 at 12 months (a reduction of 3.84 ± 1.02 points), compared with a decrease from 7.0 ± 1.2 to 4.6 ± 0.9 in the SH group (a reduction of 2.42 ± 0.95 points) (P < 0.001). The 12-month WOMAC total score decreased by 23.2 ± 6.5 points in the UC-MSCs group (from 62.4 ± 8.7 to 39.2 ± 7.4), which was significantly larger than the 15.6 ± 5.8-point reduction in the SH group (from 60.8 ± 9.2 to 45.2 ± 8.1) (P < 0.05). For radiological outcomes, the mean MOCART score improved by 13.6 ± 4.2 points in the UC-MSCs group (from 18.2 ± 5.3 to 31.8 ± 6.1), versus 7.8 ± 3.5 points in the SH group (from 17.6 ± 5.1 to 25.4 ± 5.7) (P < 0.05). The remission rate of femoral bone marrow edema was 80.0% in the UC-MSCs group, significantly higher than 44.0% in the SH group (P = 0.007). No serious adverse events - defined per CTCAE v5.0 as joint infection, severe allergic reaction, tumorigenesis, or events requiring hospitalization - were observed in either group.

Compared with SH, multiple intra-articular injections of UC-MSCs provide more durable pain relief and greater functional improvement in severe KOA, coupled with significant advantages in cartilage repair, bone marrow edema resolution, and meniscal healing. This therapy represents an innovative and effective alternative to traditional conservative management for advanced knee osteoarthritis.

Article.ArticleTitle: Comparison of ultrasound-guided oblique-axis versus short-axis approaches for right internal jugular vein cannulation in the left decubitus position: a prospective, randomized, single-center trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Central venous cannulation in the left decubitus position is more difficult than in the supine position and may be required when patients cannot safely return to supine. Whether the oblique-axis (OA) approach improves the success and safety of right internal jugular vein (RIJV) cannulation compared with the short-axis (SA) approach remains unknown.

Seventy-four patients (ASA I-III) scheduled for elective surgery in the left decubitus position under general anesthesia requiring RIJV cannulation were randomly assigned 1:1 to the OA or SA group (n = 37 each). Under real-time ultrasound guidance and a 20° Trendelenburg tilt, cannulation was performed by one of three experienced attending anesthesiologists, each with more than 15 years of experience in ultrasound-guided central venous cannulation. Venipuncture attempts and total procedure time were recorded by a separate investigator; patients were blinded by general anesthesia. The primary outcome was first-time puncture success; secondary outcomes were overall cannulation success, procedure time, venipuncture attempts, and mechanical complications.

All 74 randomized patients completed the trial and were analyzed. The first-time puncture success rate was higher in the OA group (27/37 [73.0%] vs. 18/37 [48.6%]; risk difference 24.3%, 95% CI 2.8% to 45.9%; P = 0.032, Pearson chi-square test; Fisher exact test P = 0.056). Venipuncture attempts were fewer in the OA group (median 1 vs. 2; IQR 1-2; P = 0.037). Total procedure time did not differ significantly between groups (median 2.79 [IQR 2.46-3.19] vs. 3.01 [2.72-3.45] min; P = 0.060). Mechanical complications occurred in 6 of 37 patients (16.2%) in the SA group (one arterial puncture and five posterior wall penetrations) and in none in the OA group (P = 0.025); overall cannulation success was 100% in both groups.

For RIJV cannulation in the left decubitus position, the oblique-axis approach was associated with a higher first-time puncture success rate than the short-axis approach and with fewer mechanical complications detected during or immediately after the procedure; however, the primary-endpoint evidence was borderline and the complication estimates were imprecise.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training combined with iron supplementation versus iron supplementation alone on postural control in young women with iron deficiency anemia: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Recent research revealed postural control deterioration in young women with Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA). To address this postural deficit, it is crucial to develop intervention strategies for postural rehabilitation in these individuals. This study aimed to explore the effect of 8-week extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training (HIIT) based on plyometric exercises combined with iron supplementation versus simple iron treatment on postural control of young women with IDA.

This randomized controlled trial enrolled young women with IDA aged 18-25 years, who were randomly assigned to a training group (TG; n = 16) or a non-training group (NTG; n = 17). All participants received oral iron supplementation (ferrous sulfate, 494.5 mg/day, administered as 247.25 mg twice daily), while the TG additionally completed an 8-week extremely low-volume HIIT program based on plyometric exercises. Hemoglobin (Hb) and serum ferritin concentrations were assessed, alongside muscle endurance, reaction time performance, and postural control. Muscle endurance was evaluated using the Killy test, reaction time performance using an online simple reaction time test, and postural control using a stabilometric platform under bipodal and semi-tandem stance conditions. Postural assessments were conducted with eyes open (EO) and eyes closed (EC) on firm and foam surfaces. All outcomes were measured at baseline and 72 h after the final intervention session.

After the 8-week intervention, this study demonstrated significant improvements across both groups, irrespective of the intervention. However, TG showed significantly greater post-intervention improvements than NTG in Hb concentration (P = 0.042), muscle endurance (P < 0.001), and postural control. Superior postural control in TG was observed during a bipedal stance on a foam surface (EO: P = 0.001); EC: P = 0.035), as well as during semi-tandem stance on a firm surface (EO: P = 0.015; EC: P = 0.040) and on a foam surface (EO: P = 0.019; EC: P = 0.003), compared to the NTG. With a Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold for multiple comparisons (α = 0.00625), between-group differences in postural control remained significant for bipedal foam EO (P = 0.001) and semi-tandem foam EC (P = 0.003).

The study showed that women with IDA improved their postural performance regardless of the intervention used. However, an 8-week program of extremely low-volume HIIT combined with plyometric exercises and iron supplementation had a more beneficial effect compared to traditional iron therapy. These greater improvements in postural control occurred alongside greater improvements in the Hb concentration and muscle endurance in the TG compared to the NTG.

Article.ArticleTitle: Caring Contacts and Suicidality Among American Indian and Alaska Native Communities: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: For American Indian and Alaska Native communities, connectedness and belonging are strengths that may reduce suicide risk.

To evaluate the effectiveness of culturally-adapted Caring Contacts combined with optimal available resources (intervention) compared with optimal available resources alone (control) in reducing suicidal ideation, suicide attempts, and suicide-related hospitalizations.

The CARE study was a blinded, 2-group randomized clinical trial conducted between May 2018 and September 2023 among 5 American Indian and Alaska Native communities in Alaska, the Northern Plains, and the Southern Plains, including 4 tribal communities and 1 tribal health organization. Participants were English-speaking adults (age ≥18 years) self-identifying as American Indian or Alaska Native with active suicidality. Analysis was conducted January through April 2024.

Caring Contacts is a low-cost intervention via brief, nondemanding messages exclusively focused on expressing care and interest sent by text message or greeting card on a pre-determined schedule over 12 months.

Outcomes included suicidal ideation in the past month (measured using the Suicidal Ideation Questionnaire-Junior [SIQ-Jr]), number of suicide attempts, and suicide-related hospitalizations over 12 months. Retention of active suicidality at follow-up was added as an additional outcome.

Of 1390 individuals prescreened for eligibility, 1202 consented and were screened for eligibility, and 709 (457 [64.5%] female; mean [SD] age, 35.4 [11.5] years) were enrolled and randomized, including 357 participants in the control group and 352 participants in the Caring Contacts intervention. Most participants (549 [77.4%]) self-identified as American Indian or Alaska Native only, and 160 participants (22.6%) as American Indian or Alaska Native plus another racial group. More than half of participants (392 [55.3%]) were never married. The mean (SD) SIQ-Jr score at baseline was 42.0 (13.8), and 604 participants (85.2%) had ever made a suicide attempt. Overall, 454 participants (64.0%) provided 12-month follow-up data. Between baseline and the 12-month follow-up, both groups showed significant reductions in suicidal ideation (mean [SD] score: Caring Contacts, 41.4 [13.7] vs 22.7 [15.3]; enhanced usual care, 42.5 [13.9] vs 23.1 [14.5]) and participants with a past-year suicide attempt (Caring Contacts, 169 of 352 participants [48.0%] vs 34/240 participants [14.2%]; enhanced usual care 155 of 357 participants [43.4%] vs 39 of 238 participants [16.4%]); however, no statistically significant between-group differences were found.

In this randomized clinical trial of culturally adapted Caring Contacts among American Indian or Alaska Native adults with active suicidality, Caring Contacts did not improve suicidal outcomes beyond optimal available resources alone. Similar improvements in both groups may reflect regression to the mean, the therapeutic impact of compassionate baseline engagement with supportive community staff, or the active components of optimal available resources. Further research should explore these dynamics and other culturally grounded interventions.

Article.ArticleTitle: Role of magnesium as a protective agent in cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity in head and neck cancer.

Abstract.AbstractText: This study seeks to evaluate the safety and efficacy of magnesium (MgSO4) as a protective agent against cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity (CIN) in cases with head and neck cancers (HNC).

One-hundred newly diagnosed squamous cell carcinoma HNC were randomly allocated into 4 groups: 25 cases in each. Group 1 (control group) received cisplatin 40 mg/m2 for 7 cycles (each cycle is 1 week). Group 2 received cisplatin 40 mg/m2 and 1 g of parenteral MgSO4 intravenous infusion (IVI) for 7 cycles. Group 3 received cisplatin 40 mg/m2 and 2 g of parenteral MgSO4 IVI for 7 cycles. Group 4 received cisplatin 40 mg/m2 and 3 g of parenteral MgSO4 for 7 cycles. All four groups received radiotherapy concurrent with cisplatin for 7 cycles.

The groups containing Mg IVI as (MgSO4) had a significant improvement (lower level) in Urine kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) and Urine Neutrophil gelatinase associated lipocalin (NGAL) than Group I (control group) (P < 0.05). Serum soluble Fas ligand (sFasL) and Malondialdehyde (MDA) after the end cycle (7 cycle) was significantly decreased in Group IV than group I (control group) (P < 0.05), MgSo4 was significantly decreased in Group IV (3 g Mg) than Group III (2 g Mg) (P < 0.001) and Group II (1 g Mg).

Mg can serve as a protective agent against CIN, as it reduces renal injury biomarkers, including urinary KIM-1, urinary NGAL, serum sFasL, and serum MDA when incorporated into treatment regimens at different doses, compared to cisplatin alone. Moreover, Mg had a promising role in the improvement of quality of life in cases with HNC receiving cisplatin.

Article.ArticleTitle: Comparison of the opioid-sparing effects of a combination of dexamethasone, paracetamol, and ketorolac versus paracetamol and ketorolac in patients undergoing total laparoscopic hysterectomy: A prospective double-blind randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Total laparoscopic hysterectomy (TLH) is quickly replacing the open abdominal hysterectomy, but is associated with unexpectedly high levels of pain.

The objective of this study was to compare the analgesic efficacy of adding dexamethasone to paracetamol and ketorolac (PaK) combination versus PaK combination in female patients undergoing elective TLH.

After approval from the institutional ethical committee, 100 American Society of Anesthesiologists I and II patients aged 18-60 years undergoing TLH under general anesthesia were included in this study. The patients were assigned to one of the two treatment groups (C and D). Patients in Group D received dexamethasone (0.2 mg/kg) intravenously (IV) dissolved in 100 ml of 0.9% saline 1 h before surgery and ketorolac 30 mg + paracetamol (PCM) 1 g IV prior to anesthesia being induced, while the patient in Group C received a placebo (100 ml of 0.9% normal saline) 1 h before surgery and ketorolac 30 mg + PCM 1 g IV before induction of anesthesia.

Fentanyl consumption in the first 24 h was significantly higher in Group C (231.72 ± 84.07 μg) than in Group D (138 ± 48.7 μg) (P < 0.0001). Pain scores on the 0-100 Visual Analog Scale demonstrated notable variations at each point among the groups (P < 0.05). Postoperative nausea and vomiting scores differed at 15 and 30 min (P < 0.05). A transient rise in blood glucose occurred in Group D at 16 h (122 g/dl vs. 115 g/dl in Group C, P = 0.013).
In patients undergoing TLH, a combination of dexamethasone, PCM, and ketorolac reduced 24-h opioid use, improved pain scores, and minimized immediate postoperative nausea and vomiting.

Article.ArticleTitle: Six-Month Music Practice Versus Psychomotor Interventions in Mild Cognitive Impairment: Behavioral and Hippocampal Outcomes.

Abstract.AbstractText: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is characterized by measurable cognitive decline with largely preserved daily functioning and increased risk of dementia. MCI patients may also exhibit sensorimotor and communication impairments, while hippocampal atrophy and altered functional connectivity are prominent neural features associated with further cognitive decline. Evidence from nonpharmacological interventions integrating cognitive challenge, coordinated movement, and emotional engagement remains limited in early-stage MCI. In this pilot intervention study, we examined whether 6 months of intensive musical instrument training versus psychomotor interventions were associated with changes in cognitive and sensorimotor performance, hippocampal gray matter volume, and functional connectivity. Outcomes were compared between randomized MCI groups, with matched healthy controls as reference for test-retest and age-related neural effects. Improvements in global cognition were modest, reaching marginal significance only in the music group, while both interventions were associated with complementary domain-specific cognitive and sensorimotor gains. Hippocampal gray matter volume remained stable across all three groups, whereas hippocampal functional connectivity declined in healthy controls but remained stable in both intervention groups, consistent with possible functional neural maintenance. These preliminary findings suggest that group-based, low-risk music and psychomotor interventions may support cognitive, sensorimotor, and neural functioning in early MCI, warranting further investigation in larger controlled trials.

Journal.Title: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

Article.ArticleTitle: Spatial Acid-Associated Niches Inform Irinotecan-Based DEB-TACE in Colorectal Liver Metastases: A Multicentre Randomized Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Drug-eluting bead transarterial chemoembolisation (DEB-TACE), particularly irinotecan-based regimens, has emerged as a liver-directed option for unresectable colorectal liver metastases (CRLM), yet how metastatic-niche biology relates to local drug delivery remains poorly defined.

We integrated bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics with spatial pharmacogenomic inference (SpaDR) to characterize acid-associated states in CRLM and predict regional drug sensitivity, compared pH-dependent irinotecan release of UniPearls and HepaSphere microspheres, and evaluated both platforms in a four-centre randomised trial of 35 patients with unresectable CRLM.

CRLM exhibited an acid-associated transcriptional phenotype (AcidScore), partly shared with TACE-nonresponder hepatocellular carcinoma and associated with shorter overall survival in CRLM. This phenotype localized to a spatially organized niche of SPP1+ macrophages and cancer-associated fibroblasts, in which AcidScore and malignant epithelium increased with distance from the vasculature, consistent with a putative stromal-metabolic barrier. SpaDR linked higher AcidScore to lower predicted SN-38 IC50 in most sections, identifying candidate sensitivity beyond this interface. Accordingly, UniPearls released more irinotecan than HepaSphere within 24 h at every pH tested, with the largest difference at pH 5.7. Disease control after the final DEB-TACE was higher with UniPearls (per-protocol, 100% vs. 68.75%; p = 0.018), as was final technical success (100% vs. 76.47%; p = 0.046); objective response and adverse-event frequencies were similar. Non-inferiority held across sensitivity analyses, whereas superiority was sensitive to missing-outcome assumptions.

Acid-associated spatial organization and drug-response predictions provide a rationale for local irinotecan delivery in CRLM. These findings support further evaluation of UniPearls-based DEB-TACE and prospective biomarker-stratified studies linking niche biology to clinical benefit.

Article.ArticleTitle: Adjunctive neodymium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet laser therapy for periodontitis in type 2 diabetes: A randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: ObjectiveTo determine whether adjunctive neodymium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet laser therapy added to conventional nonsurgical periodontal therapy provides greater improvement in baseline-adjusted 6-month probing depth than conventional nonsurgical periodontal therapy alone in patients with periodontitis and type 2 diabetes mellitus.MethodsThis randomized controlled trial included 120 patients with periodontitis and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the laser group (conventional nonsurgical periodontal therapy plus adjunctive neodymium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet laser therapy, n = 60) or the control group (conventional nonsurgical periodontal therapy alone, n = 60). Conventional nonsurgical periodontal therapy comprised scaling and root planing with standardized home oral-hygiene instruction and reinforcement. Periodontal and glycemic outcomes were assessed at baseline and 6 months. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in the 6-month mean probing depth, adjusted for baseline probing depth using analysis of covariance. Secondary outcomes included baseline-adjusted between-group differences in clinical attachment level, bleeding on probing-positive sites, gingival recession, glycosylated hemoglobin, and fasting plasma glucose level.ResultsBaseline characteristics were generally comparable between groups, except a modest difference in mean gingival recession. Based on the primary analysis, the baseline-adjusted 6-month mean probing depth was significantly lower in the laser group than in the control group (adjusted difference, -0.70 mm (95% confidence interval, -0.84 to -0.56) p < 0.001). Baseline-adjusted differences also favored the laser group for clinical attachment level (-0.67 mm; 95% confidence interval, -0.79 to -0.55), bleeding on probing-positive sites (-11.3 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.9 to -8.7), glycosylated hemoglobin (-0.26%; 95% confidence interval, -0.34 to -0.17), and fasting plasma glucose level (-0.62 mmol/L; 95% confidence interval, -0.81 to -0.44) (all p < 0.001). Gingival recession was slightly higher in the laser group after baseline adjustment (+0.09 mm; 95% confidence interval, 0.03 to 0.14; p = 0.004). No serious treatment-related adverse events were recorded.ConclusionsAdjunctive neodymium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet laser therapy was associated with greater short-term improvement in periodontal clinical outcomes than conventional nonsurgical periodontal therapy alone. Favorable changes in secondary glycemic outcomes were also observed; however, these results should be interpreted cautiously because cautiously because glycemic variables were secondary endpoints, and the follow-up duration was limited to 6 months.Research registration numberresearchregistry12005.
