Article.ArticleTitle: Early psychosocial-behavioral phenotypes associated with subsequent engagement and longitudinal outcomes in a digital health intervention for heart failure.

Abstract.AbstractText: The effectiveness of digital interventions for heart failure (HF) is limited by variable engagement. Psychosocial phenotyping can characterize engagement heterogeneity, but it remains unclear whether early phenotypes are associated with subsequent engagement and HF outcomes.
To identify early psychosocial-behavioral phenotypes and examine associations with longitudinal affective and motivational states, digital engagement, and HF outcomes.

We conducted a secondary analysis of a 6-month decentralized randomized controlled trial, using k-medoids clustering of baseline psychosocial characteristics and the first 4 weeks of device engagement among 175 adults with HF. Kruskal-Wallis tests examined phenotype differences in engagement during weeks 5-24. Linear mixed-effects models tested differences in anxiety, depressed mood, motivation, and patient-reported outcomes across 24 weeks.

Three phenotypes emerged: Engaged Self-Regulators (42%), Activated Learners (31%), and Challenged Survivors (26%), characterized by psychological profiles, social and structural resources, and early engagement patterns. Phenotypes differed in subsequent device engagement (all P values less than or equal to .03), with Engaged maintaining the highest use. Differences in anxiety, depressed mood, and motivation persisted over time (P < .001). All phenotypes improved in functional status, quality of life, and self-care; however, Engaged maintained functional status and quality of life scores 20-23 points higher than both other phenotypes (P < .001). Heart failure knowledge trajectories diverged; Engaged and Challenged improved comparably, while Activated showed no gains (P = .008).

Psychosocial-behavioral phenotypes identified early in a digital intervention were associated with engagement and HF outcomes. Early phenotyping may provide a foundation for prospectively testing phenotype-informed tailoring of digital interventions.

OtherAbstract.AbstractText: Heart failure requires daily self-care, and many programs now use smartphone apps, activity trackers, and connected scales to provide support. However, people vary considerably in how they use these tools, and the reasons are not well understood. We studied 175 adults living with heart failure in a 6-month remote study. Using baseline information and the first 4 weeks of device use, we identified 3 groups with different patterns of mood, motivation, confidence, social and financial resources, and technology use. These groups continued to differ over the next 5 months. One group started with lower psychological distress, higher motivation, and stronger social resources. They used the devices most and reported substantially higher physical functioning and quality of life across the 6 months. People in the other 2 groups had higher psychological distress alongside greater food, housing, and transportation challenges, and lower device use. All three groups improved over time, but substantial gaps in physical functioning and quality of life remained. Recognizing people’s psychological, social, and practical circumstances early in a digital program may help researchers design and test more personalized approaches to support.

Article.ArticleTitle: Extraoral Versus Intraoral Photobiomodulation for the Prevention of Oral Mucositis in Pediatric Patients Undergoing High-Dose Methotrexate Chemotherapy.

Abstract.AbstractText: To compare intraoral (IO) and extraoral (EO) photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) for preventing oral mucositis (OM) in pediatric patients receiving high-dose methotrexate (HD-MTX).

This prospective, open-label, randomized clinical trial included 75 HD-MTX treatment episodes from 31 pediatric patients aged 1-18 years. Each episode was randomized to IO-PBMT or EO-PBMT with red light at 660 nm. Preventive PBMT was initiated before HD-MTX infusion and administered daily until discharge. OM was assessed at baseline and on days 3, 5, and 10 using the World Health Organization scale. Pain, salivary pH, and salivary biochemical profiles were secondary or exploratory outcomes. Cumulative OM occurred in 22/37 IO-PBMT episodes (59.5%) and 12/38 EO-PBMT episodes (31.6%). After accounting for repeated episodes within patients, OM risk was higher with IO-PBMT (risk ratio, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.07-3.19; p = 0.029). Pain scores, salivary pH, and biochemical profiles did not differ significantly between groups. EO-PBMT required substantially less application time, and no adverse effects were reported.

EO-PBMT was associated with lower cumulative OM occurrence, shorter application time, and good tolerability, supporting its use as a promising, less burdensome preventive strategy in pediatric oncology.

Journal.Title: Journal of health care for the poor and underserved

Article.ArticleTitle: Integrating Financial Coaching into Smoking Cessation Treatment for Low-Income Adults Receiving Food Assistance: Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Food assistance recipients face high smoking rates and limited cessation support. This study evaluated an intervention targeting smoking and financial stress among food assistance recipients recruited from two safety-net medical centers.

Data were drawn from a randomized controlled trial (RCT) testing an intervention integrating money management coaching, financial empowerment services, and social needs referrals into smoking cessation treatment for low-income adults. The current analysis includes n=146 RCT participants receiving food assistance at baseline (n=79 intervention, n=67 waitlisted control).

At two months, 89% of intervention participants were "very satisfied." At six months, intervention participants were more likely to report seven-day abstinence (22% vs. 9%, p=.04), less worry about meeting monthly living expenses (54% vs. 73%, p=.03), reduced living paycheck-to-paycheck (73% vs. 87%, p=.04), and lower food insecurity scores than control participants (p=.01).
The intervention reduced self-reported smoking, food security, and financial stress among adult food assistance recipients.

Article.ArticleTitle: Pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block vs. surgical articular infiltration for direct anterior total hip arthroplasty under general anaesthesia: a randomized pilot trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: The effectiveness of ultrasound-guided pericapsular nerve group (PENG) blocks for postoperative analgesia following direct anterior total hip arthroplasty under general anaesthesia remains uncertain. We conducted a prospective randomized trial to determine whether a PENG block would reduce postoperative intravenous morphine consumption compared with surgical local anaesthetic infiltration.

Consecutive patients were randomized to receive either an ultrasound-guided PENG block after induction of anaesthesia or surgical local anaesthetic infiltration after femoral neck resection. General anaesthesia and perioperative analgesic management were standardized according to institutional practice, and all procedures were performed by a single surgeon. The primary outcome was total intravenous morphine consumption during the post-anaesthesia care unit (PACU) stay. The secondary outcome measure was total oral morphine consumption from PACU discharge to postoperative day 1 (POD#1), expressed in oral morphine equivalents (OME).

Of the 60 recruited patients, 56 were analysed using a modified intention-to-treat analysis. Median (interquartile range) PACU morphine consumption did not differ significantly between the control and PENG groups (0 [0-6] mg vs. 0 [0-3] mg; median difference 0 mg, 95% confidence interval (CI) -2 to 4.5; P = 0.235). Total OME consumption through POD#1 was lower in the PENG group compared to the control group (0 [0-10] mg vs. 7 [3-20] mg; P = 0.040).

In patients undergoing direct anterior total hip arthroplasty, PENG block, when implemented as part of a multimodal analgesic pathway, did not reduce PACU intravenous morphine consumption compared with surgical local infiltration.

Article.ArticleTitle: Investigating the Effect of RACZ Epidural Neuroplasty With Ozone Injection in Patients With Chronic Radicular Lumbar Pain: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Although the exact causes of chronic lumbar radicular pain are still unknown, potential causes include epidural fibrosis, arachnoiditis, mechanical failure, nerve root inflammation, and structural and degenerative changes to the spine.
This study was conducted to assess the analgesic effect of using epidural ozone injection along with routine RACZ neuroplasty in patients with low back pain.

This is a prospective randomized clinical trial conducted on 40 patients with chronic radicular lumbar pain allocated into two equal groups of RACZ caudal neuroplasty with and without ozone injection. Two groups of twenty people each were created from forty patients with chronic radicular lumbar pain who did not improve with conservative measures. In Group B, RACZ neuroplasty was performed, while in Group A, RACZ neuroplasty was administered along with epidural ozone injection. Before the intervention, baseline pain intensity and the degree of back pain-related disability were determined using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) and Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), respectively. Twenty-four hours, 1 month, and 3 months after the procedure, the NRS was recorded again. ODI was also assessed 1 month and 3 months after the procedure.

The mean NRS scores in the intervention group before, and 24 h, 1 month, and 3 months after the procedure were 8.80 ± 1.47, 4.45 ± 2.01, 5.25 ± 1.25, and 5.40 ± 2.16, respectively, and corresponding values in the control group were 8.70 ± 1.30, 4.60 ± 1.60, 5.70 ± 1.66, and 6.40 ± 1.64, respectively (Group effect: F = 0.784, p = 0.381 and Time effect: F = 81.910, p < 0.001). The mean scores of the ODI before, 1 month, and 3 months after the procedure were 48.60 ± 17.65, 40.75 ± 15.38, and 43.70 ± 18.50, respectively, in the intervention group, while in the control group, the respective values were 57.20 ± 15.67, 43.90 ± 19.92, and 48.75 ± 12.83. (Group effect: F = 1.246, p = 0.271 and Time effect: F = 24.496, p < 0.001).

While the addition of ozone to RACZ neuroplasty showed no significant benefit in this study, these findings are limited by the modest sample size and short follow-up. Further large-scale, well-powered trials are required to definitively establish the therapeutic role of ozone in this population.

Article.ArticleTitle: A First-In-Human, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Single and Multiple Ascending Dose Study of Izicopan (INF904), A Second-Generation Oral Small Molecule C5a Receptor Inhibitor, in Healthy Participants.

Abstract.AbstractText: This was a first-in-human, single-center, Phase 1 study of izicopan (formerly INF904), a potent oral, second-generation small molecule antagonist of C5aR1, in healthy adults. Participants were randomized to a single oral dose of izicopan 3-240 mg or matched placebo (single ascending dose [SAD]), or multiple doses of izicopan 30 mg once daily (QD), 30 or 90 mg twice daily (BID), or matched placebo, for 14 days (multiple ascending dose [MAD]). In the SAD study, izicopan plasma concentration increased with dose from 3 to 240 mg; the mean maximum plasma concentration (Cmax) was 21.5-1216.0 ng/mL, reached at a median time (tmax) of 3.5-6.0 h, followed by a biphasic decline. In the MAD study, a steady state appeared to have been reached within 14 days, and AUC0-tau exhibited an accumulation ratio of ∼2-fold following BID dosing, suggesting an effective half-life of ∼12 h. In an ex vivo whole blood PD assay, izicopan resulted in >90% blockade of CD11b upregulation by recombinant human C5a across almost all dose cohorts from Days 2-15. Adverse events were mild or moderate in severity. In conclusion, izicopan was safe across all single and multiple doses evaluated. Sufficient izicopan exposure was achieved rapidly to exert >90% blockade of C5a-C5aR1 signaling.

Journal.Title: Journal of nutritional science and vitaminology

Article.ArticleTitle: Intake of ETAS® Improves Cognitive Function in Healthy Middle-Aged and Older Adults: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: As the aging population grows, the prevalence of dementia continues to increase, creating an urgent need for preventive strategies. ETAS, a standardized extract of Asparagus officinalis stem, has been shown to influence brain functions such as stress reduction and autonomic regulation. However, its specific effects on cognitive functions remain unclear. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigated the effects of ETAS on cognitive function in healthy adults. Sixty-six adults aged ≥40 y with normal cognitive function (Japanese version of the Mini-Mental State Examination [MMSE-J] ≥24) were randomly assigned to receive 300 mg/d of ETAS or placebo for 12 wk. A comprehensive evaluation of cognitive function was conducted using Cognitrax, which includes various domains such as memory, attention, and visual information processing. Primary endpoint was the change in standardized score for composite memory, defined as the sum of verbal and visual memory scores, after continual intake of the test product for 12 wk. Sixty participants were included in the efficacy analysis. Compared with the placebo group, the ETAS group showed significantly greater improvements in composite memory score at 6 wk (difference: 12.8 points, p=0.006) and 12 wk (difference: 9.0 points, p=0.048). No adverse events related to ETAS were reported. These findings suggest that ETAS may help maintain and enhance memory function in healthy adults and individuals with suspected mild cognitive impairment. Clinical Trial No.: UMIN000048006.

Article.ArticleTitle: Safety and treatment duration of ribociclib + nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor in HR+/HER2- early breast cancer: a phase 3 randomized controlled trial (NATALEE).

Abstract.AbstractText: The phase 3 NATALEE trial demonstrated sustained invasive disease-free survival benefit for patients with stage II or III HR+/HER2- early breast cancer (EBC) treated with ribociclib + nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor (NSAI) vs. NSAI alone. Here we report detailed safety and tolerability data from NATALEE to further inform clinical decision-making.

In NATALEE, men and pre- and postmenopausal women with HR+/HER2- EBC were randomized 1:1 to ribociclib 400 mg/day (3 weeks on/1 week off; 36 months) + NSAI (anastrozole or letrozole; ≥60 months) or NSAI alone. Men and premenopausal women also received goserelin. Safety analyses included incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events (AEs) as well as severity, timing, management, and outcomes. Safety parameters among older vs. younger patients were also assessed.

At this 45.7-month median follow-up (data cutoff: April 29, 2024), the safety analysis set comprised 4967 patients receiving ribociclib + NSAI (n = 2526) or NSAI alone (n = 2441). The most common grade ≥ 3 AEs occurring with ribociclib + NSAI vs. NSAI alone, respectively, were neutropenia (grouped term; 44.4% vs. 0.9%), liver-related AEs (grouped term; 8.6% vs. 1.7%), and leukopenia (grouped term; 8.0% vs. 0.4%). Drug-related serious AEs occurred in 2.8% vs. 0.5%, respectively. Among patients receiving ribociclib + NSAI, AE-related ribociclib discontinuation occurred in 20.2% (median onset, 4.3 months), with 9.0% of instances occurring because of liver-related AEs. AE-related ribociclib dose interruptions (66.8%; median onset, 1.8 months) and dose reductions (23.0%; median onset, 3.2 months) were primarily driven by neutropenia (dose interruptions, 43.4%; dose reductions, 14.1%). In the ribociclib + NSAI arm, AE incidence and ribociclib dose interruptions or reductions occurred at similar rates among older patients (≥ 65 years) and younger patients (< 65 years). A higher proportion of older patients permanently discontinued ribociclib due to AEs (28.1%; n = 113/402) vs. younger patients (18.6%; n = 396/2124), most commonly due to alanine aminotransferase increased (older, 8.5%; younger, 7.0%).

Overall, ribociclib 400 mg was well tolerated, including in older patients, and AEs were manageable with current NATALEE label recommendations of dose interruptions and reductions. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03701334 (registered September 21, 2018).

Article.ArticleTitle: Accelerating tracheostomy decannulation with intermittent oro-esophageal feeding in neurogenic dysphagia: a multicenter randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Neurogenic dysphagia frequently constitutes a major barrier to decannulation for tracheostomized patients. Conventional nasogastric tube (NGT) feeding may promote disuse atrophy of swallowing musculature and persistent aspiration risk. Intermittent oro-esophageal tube (IOE) feeding, a physiologically oriented modality mimicking natural swallowing, may accelerate decannulation, yet high-quality evidence is lacking.

In this multicenter randomized controlled trial conducted at three tertiary academic centers in China, tracheostomized adults with neurogenic dysphagia were randomly assigned 1:1 to IOE or NGT. All participants received standardized pharmacological treatment, pulmonary rehabilitation, and structured swallowing training, and entered an institutional decannulation protocol with predefined readiness criteria. The primary outcome was time from protocol entry to actual decannulation. Secondary outcomes included the 30-day successful decannulation rate, nutritional indices, swallowing function, and swallowing-related quality of life. Outcome assessors and statisticians were blinded to allocation. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle.

A total of 140 patients were randomized to IOE (n = 70) or NGT (n = 70). Time to decannulation was shorter with IOE (22.16 ± 1.86 vs. 26.33 ± 1.30 days; between-group difference, 4.17 days; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.90-6.44; p < 0.001; log-rank p = 0.005). The 30-day successful decannulation rate was higher with IOE (65.71% vs. 47.14%; absolute difference, 18.57% points; 95% CI, 2.43-34.71; p = 0.028). At 1 month, the IOE group demonstrated greater improvements in body mass index, serum albumin, serum prealbumin, swallowing function, and swallowing-related quality of life (all p < 0.001). Pharyngeal discomfort was less frequent with IOE (14.06% vs. 34.21%; p = 0.006); no Grade Ⅲ or higher adverse events occurred.

Intermittent oro-esophageal tube feeding shortens time to decannulation and improves nutritional, swallowing, and quality-of-life outcomes compared with nasogastric tube feeding in tracheostomized patients with neurogenic dysphagia.
ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06791590, registration date January 19, 2025.

Article.ArticleTitle: Clinical presentation of severe malaria in children who received the RTS,S/AS01E malaria vaccine, seasonal malaria chemoprevention or the combination of both interventions in Burkina Faso and Mali.

Abstract.AbstractText: Severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria is a leading cause of death in sub-Saharan Africa, with most deaths occurring in children younger than five years of age. The RTS,S/AS01E (RTS,S) malaria vaccine delivered seasonally with Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention (SMC) led to a two-third reduction in severe malaria and malaria deaths compared with either intervention given alone. The aim of this study was to assess and compare the clinical phenotype distribution among severe malaria admissions by intervention groups and country.

We conducted a secondary ad-hoc analysis of hospital admissions in children aged 5 to 17 months of age when enrolled in the RTS,S + SMC trial in April 2017 in Houndé, Burkina Faso, and Bougouni, Mali, and who were followed until they reached five years of age.

Among the 5,920 children enrolled in Burkina Faso and Mali, 337 serious adverse events were reported during the trial with 222 (65.9%) in Burkina Faso and 115 (34.1%) in Mali, and 48.1% (162/337) due to severe malaria. The mean age of children with severe malaria was 2.9 years; 79.0% (128/162) of the cases occurred in children aged 3 years or less and 21.0% (34/162) in those aged 4 to 5 years. The most common presentation was severe anemia reported in 50% (81/162) of children, followed by repeated convulsions 25.3%, (41/162), prostration 11.1%, (18/162), hyperparasitaemia 8.0%, (13/162) and cerebral malaria 6.2%, (10/162). The proportion of children with the severe malaria anemia phenotype was higher among severe malaria cases in the SMC alone arm 62.1%, (36/58) compared to those in the SMC + RTS,S arm 37.1%, (13/35), p = 0.048. There was no significant difference in the proportion of other clinical presentations between the study arms. Most severe malaria cases, 85.8% (139/162) occurred during the transmission season (July to December).

Severe anemia was the most common presentation of severe malaria in study children and its proportion among severe malaria cases was highest in the SMC alone arm. Children aged 3 years or less were the most affected and almost all the severe malaria cases occurred between July and December. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04319380.

Article.ArticleTitle: Implementing physical activity counselling versus structured exercise for breast cancer survivors in the PAC-WOMAN trial: mapping TICD-based determinants to the behaviour change wheel.

Abstract.AbstractText: Physical activity (PA) benefits breast cancer survivorship, yet translation into routine care faces multilevel barriers. This study examined implementation determinants of two group-based PA interventions within the PAC-WOMAN trial, brief PA counselling (PAC) and supervised structured exercise (ExG), using the Tailored Implementation for Chronic Diseases (TICD) checklist and the Behaviour Change Wheel (BCW).

Process evaluation included six online focus groups with 24 participants, semi-structured interviews with three implementers and six stakeholders, and implementation monitoring logbook assessment. Content analysis followed a framework approach, mapping TICD determinants onto BCW COM-B elements, intervention functions, and policy categories.

Fifty-one TICD determinants were identified across six domains. Facilitators were primarily individual and interpersonal, including participant motivation, implementer trust, and supportive group dynamics. Barriers were largely structural, encompassing time constraints, transport difficulties, limited financial coverage, and insufficient policy support. Both interventions demonstrated feasibility and acceptability, with comparable attrition and predominantly non-intervention-related adverse events. BCW-informed strategies highlighted education, modelling, enablement, environmental restructuring, and policy actions to address key barriers.

Sustainable implementation of PA interventions in cancer care requires supportive systems beyond evidence alone. Key determinants included motivation, professional capability, organisational networks, and financial incentives. Future efforts should prioritise policy reform, multisectoral collaboration, professional training, and fiscal mechanisms to embed PA within standard breast cancer survivorship care, using BCW-guided strategies to enhance capability, opportunity, and motivation.

Article.ArticleTitle: Dorsomedial prefrontal cortex repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with antidepressants in major depressive disorder: a randomized, double-blind, single-center, sham-controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Dorsomedial prefrontal cortex repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (DMPFC-rTMS) has shown some evidence of an antidepressant effect. This study aimed to examine the efficacy and safety of DMPFC-rTMS as a combination strategy with concurrently initiated selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) compared with conventional high-frequency left-prefrontal rTMS (HF-rTMS) + SSRI or sham stimulation + SSRI.

In this prospective, single-center, six-week, randomized, three-arm, double-blind, sham- and active-comparator-controlled trial, patients with a current episode of major depressive disorder (MDD) were randomly allocated in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive either DMPFC-rTMS (20 sessions, 110% motor threshold, 2000 pulses), HF-rTMS (20 sessions, 110% motor threshold, 2000 pulses), or sham stimulation, all in combination with a concurrently initiated SSRI. The primary outcome was the change in the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) score at week six of the study. The secondary outcomes included changes in subjective assessment; response, remission, and dropout rates; and side effects of both rTMS and antidepressant treatment.

Sixty patients (20 per group) were randomized and included in the analysis. The mean change in the MADRS total score from baseline to week 6 was -14.3 points (95% confidence interval [CI]: -18.3, -10.3) in the DMPFC-rTMS group, -8.2 points (95% CI: -11.7, -4.7) in the HF-rTMS group, and -12.6 points (95% CI: -16.1, -9.0) in the sham group. However, no pairwise comparisons between these groups reached statistical significance. The response/remission rates (DMPFC-rTMS: 35%/20%; HF-rTMS: 30%/15%; sham: 55%/45%) and the dropout rates (45%, 25%, and 25%, respectively) did not differ significantly between the groups. No serious adverse events occurred.

This study did not demonstrate superior efficacy of DMPFC-rTMS or HF-rTMS over sham stimulation when initiated concurrently with SSRIs. These findings should be interpreted as exploratory. The trial was underpowered to detect the likely incremental effect of adding rTMS to a concurrently initiated SSRI and was further limited by a high sham response and differential attrition in the DMPFC-rTMS arm. Optimal stimulation parameters and patient selection require further validation.

Article.ArticleTitle: Comparison of the anaesthetic efficacy and safety of different doses of esketamine combined with propofol in hysteroscopic surgery: a randomised, double-blind controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Hysteroscopy is increasingly performed under day-surgery total intravenous anaesthesia, but propofol alone provides insufficient analgesia and the routine adjunct of opioids is associated with respiratory depression and emetic complications. Esketamine, the S-enantiomer of ketamine, offers analgesia together with sympathomimetic support and represents a promising opioid-sparing alternative; however, its optimal dose for combination with propofol in this setting has not been firmly established.

In this prospective, randomised, double-blind, controlled trial, 160 women aged 18-60 years (ASA I-II) scheduled for elective hysteroscopy were assigned to four groups using computer-generated random numbers: K1 (esketamine 0.15 mg/kg), K2 (esketamine 0.3 mg/kg), K3 (esketamine 0.5 mg/kg) or S (sufentanil 0.1 µg/kg). All patients received an induction dose of propofol 1.5 mg/kg followed by maintenance infusion of 4-6 mg·kg⁻¹·h⁻¹. The primary outcomes were postoperative pain (Numeric Rating Scale, NRS) and total intra-operative propofol consumption; secondary outcomes were perioperative haemodynamics, recovery time and adverse events. After exclusion of three patients with major protocol deviation, 157 patients were analysed (K1 = 40, K2 = 38, K3 = 40, S = 39).

Demographics, surgical and anaesthesia times were comparable between groups. NRS scores at 10 and 30 min post-recovery were significantly lower in groups K2, K3 and S than in group K1 (p < 0.001). Mean arterial pressure at the start of surgery (T2, immediately after the start of surgery) and at the end of surgery (T3) was significantly higher in K1 than in the other three groups (p < 0.001). Total propofol consumption did not differ between groups (p = 0.95). The incidence of intra-operative hypertension was significantly greater in K1 (22.5%) than in K2 (0%), K3 (5.0%) and S (5.1%) (p = 0.002), and the incidence of SpO₂ < 90% was significantly greater in S (20.5%) than in K1 (0%), K2 (5.3%) and K3 (5.0%) (p = 0.004). The incidence of emergence agitation differed among groups, with the highest incidence observed in K3 (10.0%) (p = 0.034).

Among the regimens tested, esketamine 0.3 mg/kg combined with propofol 1.5 mg/kg was associated with a favourable balance of analgesia, haemodynamic stability and safety. The 0.15 mg/kg dose was associated with higher postoperative pain scores and a higher incidence of intra-operative hypertension, while 0.5 mg/kg was associated with a higher incidence of agitation and a longer recovery time without additional analgesic benefit at 30 min. All three esketamine doses were associated with a lower incidence of hypoxaemia than the sufentanil regimen.
The trial was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400092022) with the retrospective registration date 2024/11/07.

Article.ArticleTitle: Neoadjuvant concurrent or sequential anthracycline-containing chemotherapy and HER2-targeted agents for HER2-positive breast cancer: a randomized phase 2 study (METIS).

Abstract.AbstractText: The integration of anthracyclines with HER2-targeted agents in neoadjuvant therapy for HER2-positive breast cancer has been limited by cardiotoxicity concerns. This randomized phase II METIS trial (NCT04172259) assessed whether concurrent pegylated liposomal doxorubicin (PLD)-containing chemotherapy plus dual HER2 blockade (trastuzumab/pertuzumab) could improve efficacy without increasing cardiac risk. A total of 156 patients with stage II-III HER2-positive breast cancer were randomized to a PLD-based concurrent regimen or an epirubicin and cyclophosphamide (EC)-based sequential regimen. The PLD-based concurrent group achieved a higher pathological complete response (pCR) rate (67.5% vs. 48.7%; difference, 18.8%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.6-34.0; P = 0.033) compared with the EC-based sequential group, with greater benefit in hormone receptor-positive disease (58.7% vs. 36.7%) and stage II tumors (82.1% vs. 48.0%). After a median follow-up of 37.5 months, fewer event-free survival (EFS) events occurred in the PLD-based concurrent group (3 vs. 8), yielding a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.35 (95% CI, 0.09-1.32; P = 0.105). The estimated 3-year EFS rates were 96.0% (95% CI, 88.1-98.7) versus 90.7% (95% CI, 81.5-95.6). Achieving pCR was significantly associated with improved EFS (HR = 0.15; 95% CI, 0.03-0.71; P = 0.006). Cardiac safety was comparable, with no symptomatic cardiac dysfunction and only one grade ≥3 cardiotoxicity in the EC-based sequential group. These findings support PLD-based concurrent therapy with trastuzumab and pertuzumab as an effective and safe neoadjuvant option for high-risk HER2-positive breast cancer, warranting further evaluation in phase III trials.

Article.ArticleTitle: First-line dolutegravir/lamivudine in HIV-1 infection: lymph node penetration and reservoir decline in a randomized open-label clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Dual antiretroviral therapy with dolutegravir and lamivudine (DTG/3TC) is a recommended first-line regimen for people with HIV, but whether reduced-drug therapy maintains adequate antiviral pressure within lymph node (LN) reservoirs remains uncertain. In the DUALITY clinical trial (EudraCT number 2019-002733-10), the prespecified primary endpoint-change in proviral HIV-1 DNA in peripheral blood CD4 + T cells from baseline to week 48-was similar between participants initiating DTG/3TC or dolutegravir-based triple therapy. Here, we investigated prespecified secondary endpoints comprising viral persistence and antiretroviral drug penetration and distribution in LN using multimodal imaging. In 39 participants undergoing inguinal LN excision at baseline or during the first year of treatment, HIV-1 DNA and RNA were detected by DNAscope/RNAscope and antiretroviral spatial distribution was mapped by mass spectrometry imaging. HIV-1-infected cells declined rapidly after treatment initiation across both treatment groups. Antiretrovirals were widely detected within LN tissue regions containing or adjacent to HIV-positive cells. These findings provide spatial evidence that DTG/3TC reaches LN tissue and HIV-positive cells, extending peripheral blood observations to a key anatomical HIV reservoir.

Article.ArticleTitle: [Safety and efficacy of the adjustable monitoring filtered type-B transnasal specialized airway catheter in anesthesia for ambulatory gastrointestinal endoscopic surgery in obese patients].

Abstract.AbstractText: Objective: To evaluate the clinical safety and efficacy of the adjustable monitoring and filtering type B transnasal specialized airway catheter (hereafter referred to as the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway) during anesthesia for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under digestive endoscopy in obese patients. Methods: This randomized controlled trial enrolled 92 obese patients (body mass index≥28 kg/m²) scheduled for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under digestive endoscopy at the General Hospital of Northern Theater Command between June and December 2025. Using a random number table, we split the participants evenly into an adjustable airway group (Group R, n=46) and a standard nasal cannula group (Group C, n=46). Anesthesia was inducted and maintained with remimazolam and alfentanil. Patients in Group R were fitted with the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway for oxygen delivery and end-tidal carbon dioxide (etCO2) monitoring, and Group C received supplemental oxygen through conventional nasal cannula. The primary outcome was defined as the incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia [pulse oximetry saturation(SpO2)<90%]. Secondary outcomes were the variations in respiratory rate, heart rate and mean arterial pressure (MAP) at time points before induction (T0), upon endoscope insertion (T1), 5 minutes post-insertion (T2), at the end of surgery (T3), and 5 minutes after waking up (T4). Additional secondary outcomes included arterial partial pressure of oxygen (PaO₂) and arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO₂) at T2 in both groups, and partial pressure of end-tidal carbon dioxide (PetCO₂) in group R. The duration of endoscopic therapy, dosages of remimazolam and alfentanil, the frequency of hands-on airway interventions, nasal bleeding episodes, and overall physician satisfaction scores were all systematically documented. Results: The baseline demographic and clinical characteristics matched up well between the two groups (all P>0.05). The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia was significantly lower in group R compared with group C [2.2%(1/46) vs 32.6%(15/46),χ2=14.829,P<0.001]. Patients in Group R exhibited significantly elevated SpO2 levels at T1, T2, and T3 (all P<0.05). At T2, Group R demonstrated significantly higher PaO2 and lower PaCO2 compared to Group C, their heart rates also stayed distinctly lower (P<0.05). MAP remained comparable across both cohorts at every measured interval (P>0.05). Intraoperative PetCO2 values in Group R were consistently maintained within normative physiological parameters, accompanied by continuous and stable monitoring waveforms. Compared with Group C, Group R registered a significantly lower rate of necessity for airway interventions, shorter endoscopic procedure duration and emergence time, lower remimazolam consumption, and highter physician satisfaction (all P<0.05). Conclusions: During anesthesia for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under gastrointestinal endoscopy in obese patients, the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway directly protects against hypoxemia by improving oxygen delivery and curtails carbon dioxide retention. Concurrently, accurate ventilation tracking helps maintain a highly stable hemodynamic profile, the clinical safety and efficacy of this airway device substantially surpass those of the conventional nasal cannula.

OtherAbstract.AbstractText: 目的： 探讨可调监测过滤B型经鼻异型气道导管（简称可调监测型鼻咽通气道）在肥胖患者接受日间消化内镜胃肠息肉切除手术麻醉中的安全性与有效性。 方法： 随机对照试验，选取2025年6至12月在北部战区总医院择期行日间消化内镜胃肠息肉切除术的肥胖患者（体质指数≥28 kg/m²）（n=92），采用随机数字表法将患者分为可调监测型鼻咽通气道组（R组，n=46）和鼻导管组（C组，n=46）。两组都使用瑞马唑仑及阿芬太尼进行麻醉诱导与维持。R组置入可调监测型鼻咽通气道供氧并监测呼气末二氧化碳（etCO2）波形，C组采用传统鼻导管吸氧。主要结局指标为术中低氧血症（脉搏血氧饱和度<90%）发生率，次要结局指标为两组诱导前（T0）、置镜时（T1）、入镜5 min（T2）、手术结束时（T3）及苏醒5 min（T4）时的呼吸频率、心率、平均动脉压（MAP）变化情况；两组T2时动脉血氧分压（PaO2）、动脉血二氧化碳分压（PaCO2）；R组呼气末二氧化碳分压（PetCO2），其他指标为两组内镜诊疗时间、瑞马唑仑和阿芬太尼用量、气道干预情况、鼻黏膜出血率以及医师满意度。 结果： 两组患者基线资料具有可比性（均P>0.05）。R组低氧血症发生率低于C组［2.2%（1/46）比32.6%（15/46），χ2=14.829，P<0.001）。与C组比较，R组T1、T2、T3时的脉搏血氧饱和度更高；T2时PaO2更高，PaCO2及心率更低，差异均有统计学意义（均P<0.05）。两组不同时间点MAP差异无统计学意义（均P>0.05）。R组术中PetCO2在正常生理范围内波动，监测波形连续、稳定。与C组相比，R组内镜诊疗时间短，瑞马唑仑用量少，苏醒时间短，气道干预率低，医师满意度高，差异均有统计学意义（均P<0.05）。 结论： 肥胖患者进行日间消化内镜胃肠息肉切除手术麻醉期间，应用可调监测型鼻咽通气道可改善氧合，减少二氧化碳蓄积，避免低氧血症的发生，同时提供及时准确的通气监测，使血流动力学更加稳定，其临床安全性和有效性优于传统鼻导管。.

Article.ArticleTitle: An integrated Healthy Lifestyle Program (HeLP) and physiotherapy care for low back pain: a mixed methods process evaluation.

Abstract.AbstractText: Integrated lifestyle and low back pain care is a novel treatment approach. This study describes the fidelity and adoption; barriers and facilitators to engagement and delivery; acceptability, appropriateness and feasibility of the Healthy Lifestyle Program (HeLP) intervention.
Mixed-methods process evaluation.

Data were included from n = 174 adults with chronic low back pain randomised to HeLP, and delivering clinicians. The 26-week intervention included five consultations , information resources, and referral to telephone support services. We collected quantitative data via fidelity checklists, administrative records and surveys, and qualitative data via semi-structured interviews and focus groups with a subsample of participants and clinicians. We used descriptive statistics, thematic analyses and triangulation to identify meta-themes.

Intervention fidelity was high (clinicians delivered >90% to protocol). Participants' adoption was moderate attending a mean 3.2 consultations, 54% (referred) engaged with telephone services and 46% used online resources; however, adoption of smoking cessation services was low (6.5% of smokers completed ≥1 call). A total of 23% of participants discontinuted HeLP by 26 weeks. Clinicians and participants considered the intervention acceptable, and addressing lifestyle factors appropriate for low back pain.
HeLP was acceptable, although uptake varied across components. Improving clinicians' behaviour change communication and personalising care may optimise implementation.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of Preoperative Intranasal Dexmedetomidine on Postoperative Myocardial Injury in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.

Abstract.AbstractText: To evaluate the effects of preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine on postoperative myocardial injury biomarkers in patients undergoing on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).

In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 70 patients undergoing on-pump CABG were assigned to receive intranasal dexmedetomidine (1 μg/kg) or saline 30 min before bedtime on the night before surgery and again 30 min before anesthesia induction. The primary outcome was serum high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) at 24 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes included perioperative cardiac biomarkers, preoperative sleep quality, postoperative delirium, and adverse events.

For the prespecified primary outcome, hs-cTnT concentrations at 24 h after surgery were significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group than in the control group (estimated marginal means, 170.29 vs 357.29 ng/L; P < 0.001). Postoperative creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) concentrations were also lower in the dexmedetomidine group (all P < 0.05). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide showed a significant group-by-time interaction (P = 0.030), although between-group differences at individual postoperative time points were not significant. The dexmedetomidine group had higher Leeds Sleep Evaluation Questionnaire scores (62 [60-64] vs 44 [41-50]; P < 0.001) and a lower incidence of postoperative delirium (14.3% vs 37.1%; P = 0.029). Adverse events, mechanical ventilation duration, and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay did not differ significantly between groups.

In this single-center trial, two-dose preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine was associated with lower postoperative hs-cTnT and CK-MB concentrations, better subjective preoperative sleep quality, and a lower observed incidence of postoperative delirium. These findings are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered multicenter randomized trials to determine whether the biomarker reductions translate into clinically meaningful cardiovascular benefits.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of Adding Esketamine to Patient-Controlled Intravenous Analgesia on Rebound Pain After Interscalene Brachial Plexus Block: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Rebound pain after peripheral nerve block (PNB) may diminish the analgesic benefits of regional anesthesia. Whether esketamine administered via postoperative patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) can prevent rebound pain remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of esketamine-containing PCIA on rebound pain after interscalene brachial plexus block in patients undergoing shoulder arthroscopic surgery.

132 patients scheduled for arthroscopic shoulder surgery under general anesthesia combined with interscalene brachial plexus block were randomized 1:1 to receive postoperative PCIA with esketamine (1.25 mg/kg) plus sufentanil (100 μg) and flurbiprofen axetil (100 mg) (ES group, n=66) or sufentanil plus flurbiprofen axetil alone (Control group, n=66). The primary outcome was rebound pain, defined as an increase from well-controlled pain (NRS ≤ 3) to severe pain (NRS ≥ 7), typically after resolution of the nerve block. Secondary outcomes included time to rebound pain, modified pain score, rebound pain duration, analgesic consumption, numerical rating scale (NRS) at 6, 12, 24, and 48 h postoperatively, Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15), Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ) sleep quality, and adverse events.

The incidence of rebound pain did not differ significantly between groups (25.8% vs 39.4%; OR, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.39 to 1.09; P=0.095). Among patients who developed rebound pain, the ES group had a lower modified rebound pain score and shorter pain duration. For other secondary outcomes, patients receiving esketamine had lower NRS pain scores at 12, 24, and 48 h, fewer PCIA demands, less rescue analgesic use, and higher QoR-15 and RCSQ scores (all P<0.05). The incidence of the assessed adverse events did not differ significantly between groups.

Adding esketamine to postoperative PCIA did not demonstrate a reduction in rebound pain incidence after interscalene brachial plexus block. Exploratory subgroup findings suggested lower rebound pain intensity and duration, while improvements in postoperative analgesia, sleep, and recovery had uncertain clinical relevance. Further multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings and to evaluate different dosing strategies and routes of administration.

Journal.Title: The Journal of orthopaedic and sports physical therapy

Article.ArticleTitle: First-Hand Experience and the Value of Telerehabilitation for Chronic Knee Pain: A Discrete Choice Experiment Nested in a Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess whether first-hand experience of receiving physical therapy via telerehabilitation affected patient preferences and willingness to pay for telerehabilitation. DESIGN: This study used a discrete choice experiment nested within a randomized controlled trial. METHODS: We recruited 319 Australian adults aged 45 years or over, with chronic knee pain consistent with osteoarthritis, who had completed a clinical trial where they were randomized to receive physical therapy via telerehabilitation or in-person. Participants were presented hypothetical scenarios and asked to choose between physical therapy delivered via telerehabilitation or in-person. Each scenario presented seven attributes of consultations at varying levels. Data were analyzed using a generalized multinomial logit and latent class models. RESULTS: There were 164 participants from the in-person trial arm (80% of those randomized) and 155 from the telerehabilitation arm (82% of those randomized) who participated. Participants in the telerehabilitation arm (ie, with first-hand experience of telerehabilitation) were willing to pay AU$ 87.49 (95% confidence interval: 72.83, 102.14) more than people in the in-person arm for telerehabilitation consultations (all other attributes fixed at reference values for categorical variables and at mean values for continuous variables). Four subgroups were identified. In the telerehabilitation arm, 105 (68% of 155) participants preferred telerehabilitation, and 50 (32%) preferred in-person consultations. In the in-person arm, 63 (39% of 164) held a strong preference for in-person consultations, and 101 (61%) had a mild preference for in-person consultations. CONCLUSION: People with first-hand experience using telerehabilitation for physical therapy expressed a greater willingness to use and pay for it than people who experienced in-person care. Journal.Title: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research

Article.ArticleTitle: Short-Term Pain Outcomes of Trigger Point Injection Versus Dry Needling for Acute Myofascial Low Back Pain in the Emergency Department: A Prospective Randomized Comparative Study.

Abstract.AbstractText: BACKGROUND Acute myofascial low back pain prompts emergency department visits, where rapid pain relief matters. Trigger point injection and dry needling are used for myofascial trigger points, but comparative evidence in emergency care is limited. This study compared the short-term analgesic effectiveness of trigger point injection and dry needling in patients with acute myofascial low back pain presenting to the emergency department. MATERIAL AND METHODS This prospective, randomized, comparative study randomized 52 patients; 49 patients who completed at least 1 post-procedure pain assessment were included in the analysis. Pain was assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) at baseline and 5, 15, 30, and 60 minutes after the procedure. The principal effectiveness outcome was the between-group difference in percentage pain reduction at 30 minutes. Intravenous fentanyl (1 µg/kg) was administered as rescue analgesia after the 60-minute assessment when required. RESULTS Baseline NRS scores were similar between groups (P=0.191). Percentage pain reduction at 30 minutes was greater after trigger point injection than after dry needling (86.85±17.53% vs 32.98±13.48%; mean difference, 53.86 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, 44.78-62.94; P<0.001). Pain scores were lower and pain reduction was greater after trigger point injection at all post-procedure timepoints (all P<0.001). Rescue analgesia was required in 0 of 26 patients after trigger point injection and 15 of 23 patients (65.2%) after dry needling (P<0.001). No procedure-related adverse events were observed. CONCLUSIONS Trigger point injection was associated with greater short-term pain reduction and less frequent rescue analgesia than dry needling during the first hour of emergency department care. These preliminary findings require confirmation in larger studies.

Article.ArticleTitle: Supervised physiotherapeutic scoliosis-specific exercises provide limited additional benefit at 24 months in braced adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis: a randomized trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Physiotherapeutic scoliosis-specific exercises (PSSE) are used as an adjunct to bracing in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS), although evidence for their long-term benefit remains limited. This randomized trial assessed whether supervised PSSE provide clinically important radiological and patient-reported benefits compared with self-directed exercise in patients with AIS undergoing brace treatment.

Patients with AIS (major Cobb angle 25° to 45°; Risser grade 0 to 2) were recruited from a tertiary scoliosis centre between December 2018 and December 2022. Patients were randomized to supervised Schroth-based PSSE, consisting of physiotherapist-led sessions plus daily home exercises, or to self-directed general exercise. The co-primary outcomes were change in major Cobb angle and change in health-related quality of life measured using the Chinese Brace Questionnaire-34. A 5° between-group difference in Cobb angle was prespecified as the minimal clinically important difference (MCID). To provide a clinically anchored interpretation, 24-month radiological outcomes were classified as improved (> 5° decrease), stable (-5° to +5°), or worsened (> 5° increase), and compared using adjusted ordinal logistic regression in intention-to-treat (ITT) and per-protocol (PP) analyses.

Supervised PSSE resulted in a greater reduction in major Cobb angle than self-directed exercise at 24 months (adjusted between-group difference -3.23° (95% CI -3.51 to -2.96); p < 0.001); however, this did not reach the prespecified MCID. There was no clinically meaningful difference in quality of life. Using the 5° threshold, radiological status was similar between groups. In the intention-to-treat analysis, the adjusted odds ratio (OR) for improved/stable/worsened status was 1.08 (95% CI 0.58 to 2.03; p = 0.805); per-protocol findings were similar (OR 1.48 (95% CI 0.75 to 2.92); p = 0.263).

Supervised PSSE provided a statistically significant but clinically modest radiological benefit over self-directed exercise. This did not translate into a higher likelihood of clinically meaningful radiological improvement. No sustained clinically meaningful quality-of-life benefit was shown.

Journal.Title: Annals of physical and rehabilitation medicine

Article.ArticleTitle: Hand-Arm Bimanual Intensive Therapy Including Lower Extremities (HABIT-ILE) in adults with chronic stroke: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Stroke rehabilitation guidelines recommend goal-oriented, task-specific, intensive interventions. Yet most programs emphasize upper extremity (UE) recovery, overlooking lower extremities (LEs) and trunk, which are essential for activities of daily living. Consequently, Hand-Arm Bimanual Intensive Therapy Including LEs (HABIT-ILE) represents a promising approach for stroke rehabilitation.

This randomized controlled trial aimed to determine the effect of HABIT-ILE and to compare its efficacy with a control group in adults with chronic hemiparetic stroke by promoting greater improvements across the body functions, activity, and participation domains of the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health.

Forty-six adults with hemiparetic chronic stroke were randomized to either a 2-week (50 h, 5 h/day) HABIT-ILE camp-setting program in Brussels, Belgium, or to continue their usual neurorehabilitation (mean = 4 h 36 min) for over the same period. Participants were assessed before, immediately, and at 3 months after intervention using the Adult Assisting Hand Assessment Stroke (Ad-AHA Stroke, primary outcome), the Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (COPM), the Fugl Meyer Assessment for UEs (FMA-UE), the Wolf Motor Function Test (WMFT), the ABILHAND-CS and ACTIVLIM-CS questionnaires, the six-minute walk test, the modified Rankin Scale and the Stroke Impact Scale (SIS).

The ANCOVA revealed a significant between-groups difference favoring the HABIT-ILE group (TG), with a time effect observed for the Ad-AHA Stroke (TG: at 2 weeks = +6.24% of logits; at 3 months = +7.05% of logits), WMFT (Functional Ability Scale, all P ≤ 0.041), and COPM (P < 0.001, performance and satisfaction) at both 2 weeks and 3 months. We found a similar significant effect for the SIS (hand function, P = 0.003) at 2 weeks and the FMA-UE and ABILHAND-CS at 3 months (all P ≤ 0.033). We observed no significant between-group differences for the other outcomes, including LEs measures.

In adults with chronic stroke, HABIT-ILE intervention significantly improved spontaneous bimanual use, motor function, and ability of the paretic UE (both externally rated and self-perceived) and reduced participation restrictions compared with the control group.

This randomized controlled trial was registered on December 11th, 2020, on ClinicalTrials.gov as "HABIT-ILE in Adults With Chronic Stroke (HABIT-ILE Stroke)", with the registration number NCT04664673 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04664673?cond=NCT04664673&rank=).

Journal.Title: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

Article.ArticleTitle: Efficiency of different approaches in teaching tracheal suctioning procedure to caregivers of tracheostomy patients: randomized controlled study.

Abstract.AbstractText: This study focuses on enhancing the supportive care process for patients who have undergone tracheostomy due to head and neck cancers and various clinical conditions. In this context, the effects of a mobile application and simulation-based training on tracheal suctioning knowledge and skills were evaluated in comparison with a control group.

This experimental study employed a pretest-posttest control group design. A total of 77 primary caregivers were randomized sequentially during the study period. Eleven participants subsequently withdrew from the study, and 66 caregivers (22 per group) completed the study and were included in the final analysis. Participants were randomly assigned to simulation, mobile application-based training, and control groups using block randomization. Data were collected using the Introductory Information Form, Tracheostomy Suctioning Knowledge Evaluation Form, Tracheostomy Suctioning Skill Evaluation Form, Evaluation Form of the Training Provided, and Result Evaluation Form. The simulation group received model-based training, while the mobile group used the developed application. The control group received routine bedside training from healthcare professionals. Data were collected at pre-intervention, immediately after training, and on the 30th day post-training.

All assessment scores differed significantly between groups (p = 0.000). The simulation group achieved the highest scores, followed by the mobile group, while the control group had the lowest. Improvements in knowledge and skills were greater at the 30-day follow-up compared to immediately post-training.

Both simulation-based and mobile application-based training significantly improved caregivers' knowledge and skills. While simulation was the most effective method, the 'Trakaspirasyon' mobile application provides a scalable alternative that may enhance patient safety and the quality of home-based supportive care.

Article.ArticleTitle: Early functional deterioration during first-line ICI-based therapy in advanced NSCLC: implications for supportive care.

Abstract.AbstractText: To compare objective functional measures for identifying early functional deterioration during first-line ICI-based therapy in advanced NSCLC and explore their relevance for supportive-care monitoring.

This secondary exploratory analysis used prospectively collected data from a randomized trial of pulmonary rehabilitation. Forty-two participants with baseline and 8-week assessments were evaluated using quadriceps force, SPPB, and 6MWD. Early deterioration was defined as decline in at least one domain. Deterioration frequency, cross-domain agreement, baseline associations, and subsequent PFS were examined, accounting for randomized treatment allocation.

Under the primary operational definitions, deterioration in at least one functional domain occurred in 29/42 participants (69.0%) despite stable ECOG performance status. Deterioration affected quadriceps force in 23 (54.8%), SPPB in 14 (33.3%), and 6MWD in 5 (11.9%); 16 participants deteriorated in one domain and 13 in two. Frequencies differed significantly across measures (Cochran's Q=16.76, p<0.001), with low pairwise agreement. No examined baseline characteristic was significantly associated with deterioration after adjustment for PR/UC allocation. Participants with deterioration had numerically less favorable subsequent PFS, but the association was not statistically significant.

Early functional deterioration during first-line ICI-based therapy was common and heterogeneous across domains. Repeated objective assessment across complementary functional measures may help identify emerging functional vulnerability and support timely individualized supportive-care evaluation.

Article.ArticleTitle: Application of Electrical Impedance Tomography-Guided Pulmonary Rehabilitation Strategy in Patients with Respiratory Failure.

Abstract.AbstractText: This study investigated pulmonary rehabilitation strategies guided by electrical impedance tomography (EIT) in patients with respiratory failure. A total of 92 patients with respiratory failure admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) of a tertiary Grade A hospital in Chongqing from July 2024 to January 2025 were selected and randomly divided into a control group and an experimental group, with 46 cases in each group, using a random number table. The control group received conventional pulmonary physical therapy nursing strategies. The experimental group additionally received EIT-guided positioning, vibratory sputum clearance, and early mobilization. Relative regional tidal-ventilation distribution, PaO₂/FiO₂, respiratory rate, and pulse oxygen saturation were assessed at baseline and on the following three days; ICU stay, and delirium incidence were also compared. Finally, 44 cases in the control group and 44 cases in the experimental group completed the study. Repeated-measures ANOVA showed significant time effects across the four ventral-to-dorsal layers and significant group and interaction effects for the dorsal layer. Dorsal ventilation share was higher in the experimental group on days 2 and 3, but not significantly different on day 1. No significant group, time, or interaction effects were found for the four lung quadrants. The experimental group had higher PaO₂/FiO₂, shorter ICU stay (6.55 vs. 7.75 days), and lower delirium incidence (25.0% vs. 45.5%). Respiratory rate decreased, and pulse oxygen saturation increased over time in both groups, without significant group or interaction effects. The EIT-guided strategy may improve regional ventilation distribution and oxygenation, shorten ICU stay, and reduce delirium in patients with respiratory failure.

Article.ArticleTitle: Sequential Lidocaine and Liposomal Bupivacaine for Popliteal Sciatic Nerve Block in Foot and Ankle Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: In foot and ankle surgery, prolonged analgesia after popliteal sciatic nerve block (PSNB) may be accompanied by delayed motor recovery. The effects of sequential lidocaine and liposomal bupivacaine (LB), particularly on early motor function, remain uncertain.

Eighty adults undergoing foot and ankle surgery were randomized to preoperative 1.5% lidocaine (20 mL) followed by postoperative 0.665% LB (20 mL), or preoperative 0.5% ropivacaine (20 mL). Participants and outcome assessors were blinded; block providers were not. For the coprimary comparisons, resting pain was assessed at 24 hours using a 0-10 visual analog scale and motor function at 3 hours using the modified Bromage score.

In complete-case analyses, 37 lidocaine-LB and 38 ropivacaine recipients were included. Median (IQR) 24-hour resting pain was 0 (0-2) versus 1 (0-3) (difference, -1; 95% CI, -3 to 0; P<0.001); the difference was below the prespecified 1.5-point threshold for clinical importance. The 3-hour motor score was 1 (1-1) versus 0 (0-0) (difference, 1; 95% CI, 1 to 1; P<0.001), meeting the study-defined 1-point threshold. Exploratory comparisons favored lidocaine-LB for later pain, 24-hour rescue analgesia and recovery quality, and postoperative nausea and vomiting. One suspected local anesthetic systemic toxicity event-mild tinnitus 15 minutes after preoperative lidocaine-was recorded; no specific treatment was given.

Compared with single-injection ropivacaine, sequential lidocaine-LB was associated with better early motor scores and statistically lower 24-hour resting pain. The pain difference did not meet the prespecified threshold for clinical importance. Functional benefit and comparative safety remain unestablished. Larger multicenter trials should assess mobility and safety, together with the cost and feasibility of the additional block.

Article.ArticleTitle: Thalidomide dose selection for prevention of camrelizumab-induced reactive cutaneous capillary endothelial proliferation: a multicenter, randomized phase II trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Reactive cutaneous capillary endothelial proliferation (RCCEP) is a characteristic cutaneous adverse event associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors. This study compared two prophylactic thalidomide doses to identify the more promising dose for further evaluation.

In this multicenter, randomized clinical trial, patients with advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma or non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomly assigned to receive thalidomide 50 mg/day (Group A) or 100 mg/day (Group B) during first-line treatment with camrelizumab plus standard chemotherapy. The primary endpoint was overall RCCEP incidence; secondary endpoints included grade ≥3 RCCEP, median time to RCCEP onset, week 6 and week 9 RCCEP incidence, and safety.

A total of 72 patients were randomized. RCCEP occurred in 12 of 36 patients (33.3%) in Group A and 9 of 36 patients (25.0%) in Group B. RCCEP incidence at week 6 was 13.9% in Group A and 19.4% in Group B, and by week 9 was 25.0% and 19.4%, respectively. No grade ≥3 RCCEP occurred; all first RCCEP events were grade 1, with 1 grade 2 event reported in Group A. Among patients who developed RCCEP, median onset time was 1.49 and 1.31 months, respectively. Thalidomide-related adverse events occurred in 22.2% and 41.7% of patients, and grade 3 or higher thalidomide-related adverse events occurred in 8.3% and 22.2%, respectively. Serious adverse events occurred in 11.1% and 13.9% of patients, respectively.

Thalidomide 100 mg/day met the prespecified incidence-based dose-selection criterion compared with 50 mg/day but was associated with a higher incidence of grade 3 or higher toxicity. Further controlled evaluation is warranted.

Article.ArticleTitle: Needle-knife lumbosacral therapy for lumbar disc herniation: a single-center, outcome assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Lumbar disc herniation (LDH) is a common spinal disorder causing significant pain and dysfunction. Traditional acupuncture is a widely used non-pharmacological treatment for LDH. Recently, needle-knife therapy has emerged as a potential alternative.
This study aims to explore the clinical efficacy of needle-knife lumbosacral therapy for LDH and compare its advantages with those of conventional acupuncture therapy.

This study adopted an outcome assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial design. A total of 74 patients with LDH were enrolled and randomly assigned to the experimental group (n = 37), which received needle-knife lumbosacral therapy, or the control group (n = 37), which received conventional acupuncture at the same anatomical treatment sites. Seventy patients completed the 2-week treatment and 3-month follow-up. Visual analog scale (VAS) and Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) were designated as primary repeated outcomes; lumbar flexion mobility (LFM) was a secondary repeated outcome, and inflammatory cytokines served as non-repeated secondary outcomes. Mixed-effects linear models were used for repeated measurements, with the group-by-time interaction predefined as the primary estimand. Bonferroni correction was applied for the three repeated outcomes (VAS, ODI, and three LFM components), setting an adjusted significance threshold of α = 0.017. Unadjusted α = 0.05 was adopted for inflammatory cytokines. VAS, ODI, and LFM were evaluated at baseline, post-treatment, and 3-month follow-up; inflammatory markers (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β) were detected at baseline and post-treatment only. Adverse events were monitored throughout the trial. Patient recruitment was conducted from March 15, 2025, to July 15, 2025, and the final follow-up was performed on November 18, 2025.

Both groups demonstrated within-group reductions in VAS and ODI scores across all time points. For the prespecified group-by-time interaction analyses under Bonferroni correction (α = 0.017), the needle-knife group showed significantly larger longitudinal improvements than the acupuncture group for both primary outcomes: VAS interaction (95% CI: 0.21-0.83), adjusted p = 0.001; ODI interaction (95% CI: 1.89-4.35), adjusted p < 0.0001. At post-treatment, the model-based between-group differences (needle-knife minus acupuncture) were VAS: -1.16 (95% CI: -1.78 to -0.54), adjusted p = 0.0004; ODI: -3.78 (95% CI: -4.95 to -2.61), adjusted p < 0.0001. At 3-month follow-up, sustained between-group differences were VAS: -0.43 (95% CI: -0.68 to -0.18), adjusted p = 0.001; ODI: -1.89 (95% CI: -2.56 to -1.22), adjusted p < 0.0001. For LFM components, all three subindices showed greater numerical improvements in the needle-knife group, but their group-by-time interaction adjusted p-values exceeded the 0.017 threshold: lumbar flexion (95% CI: 0.62-5.00), adjusted p = 0.034; left lateral flexion (95% CI: -1.02 to 2.42), adjusted p = 0.423; right lateral flexion (95% CI: -1.10 to 1.92), adjusted p = 0.594. Among serum inflammatory biomarkers, only IL-6 showed a statistically significant unadjusted between-group difference at post-treatment: IL-6 difference = -0.47 ng·L (95% CI: -0.89 to -0.05), unadjusted p = 0.03; TNF-α difference = -0.18 ng·L (95% CI: -0.52 to 0.16), unadjusted p = 0.30; IL-1β difference = -0.13 ng·L (95% CI: -0.37 to 0.11), unadjusted p = 0.28. No serious adverse events were reported.

Two-week lumbosacral needle-knife therapy effectively relieves pain and lumbar dysfunction in LDH patients, with statistically verified sustained superiority over conventional acupuncture for VAS and ODI under the Bonferroni-adjusted threshold (α = 0.017). Although numerical advantages in lumbar mobility were observed in the needle-knife group, these differences did not reach the prespecified adjusted significance level after multiple testing correction. As an outcome assessor-blinded exploratory trial with unmasked participants and therapists, large-sample and multicenter clinical studies are needed to further verify the conclusions, and future trials should optimize blinding schemes to reduce reporting bias.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of morning versus evening exercise on vascular function in older adults with type 2 diabetes: a randomised controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Cardiovascular disease is a common complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), with increased risk closely associated with vascular dysfunction. Exercise is an effective strategy for improving vascular health, but whether exercise timing influences long-term vascular adaptations in patients with T2DM remains unclear. In this study, we investigated the effects of morning versus evening exercise on vascular function in older adults with T2DM.

Sixty-six older adults with T2DM were randomised to morning exercise, evening exercise, or control (n = 22 each). The exercise groups received 12 weeks of online moderate-intensity aerobic and resistance exercises, three times per week. The morning group exercised from 9:00 to 10:10, and the evening group from 19:00 to 20:10. The control group maintained their usual lifestyle and attended weekly health education sessions without structured exercise. Blood pressure, brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV), flow-mediated vasodilation (FMD) and plasma nitric oxide (NO) levels were assessed at baseline and post-intervention. Outcomes were analysed using two-way repeated-measures analysis of variance, with exploratory analyses directly comparing the two exercise groups.

Fifty-eight participants were included in the final analysis (morning, n = 20; evening, n = 19; control, n = 19). Significant group × time interactions were observed for FMD, baPWV, systolic blood pressure (SBP), mean arterial pressure (MAP), and plasma NO (all p < 0.05). Both exercise groups increased FMD and reduced SBP, MAP, and baPWV from baseline (all p < 0.05). Plasma NO increased significantly following the evening exercise (p = 0.003), whereas no significant changes were observed following the morning exercise (p = 0.722). At post-intervention, the evening group exhibited lower MAP (p = 0.012) and higher FMD (p = 0.019) and NO levels (p = 0.012) than controls. Exploratory analyses showed a greater baPWV reduction with evening exercise (group × time interaction, p = 0.034). The increase in plasma NO was numerically greater with evening exercise, although the interaction was not statistically significant (p = 0.051).
Exercise timing may influence vascular adaptations in older adults with T2DM, with evening exercise potentially offering additional benefits, particularly for arterial stiffness.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of discharge planning rooted in the integrated Care for Older People Concept on the maintenance of intrinsic capacity in older adults.

Abstract.AbstractText: To assess how integrated care for older people (ICOPE)-based discharge planning (DP) affects older patients' intrinsic capacity (IC).

Between December 2023 and June 2024, 112 geriatric inpatients were randomly assigned to control (routine care) or Experimental (routine care + ICOPE discharge services) groups. Intrinsic capacity domains were evaluated using the Short Physical Performance Battery, Saint Louis University Mental Status, Geriatric Depression Scale-Short Form and Mini Nutritional Assessment-Short Form tools and self-report at discharge and 3 months post-discharge. Analysis of covariance and binary logistic regression were used, with baseline scores, living status and gender as covariates. The primary analysis was supplemented by a sensitivity analysis using continuous domain scores as separate outcomes to verify the robustness of the composite score findings.

108 patients completed follow-up. Intrinsic capacity decline was lower in the experimental group (1.2 ± 0.2) than in the control group (3.1 ± 0.3; mean difference: -1.9, 95% CI: -2.5 to -1.3, p < 0.001). Motor, cognitive, psychological and nutritional domains improved more in the Experimental group (all p < 0.001); sensory function showed no difference (p = 0.267).
The ICOPE-based DP approach slows IC decline and enhances multiple functional domains, offering a valuable reference for transitional care for older adults.

Article.ArticleTitle: Eltrombopag during induction chemotherapy in older patients with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia is safe and reduces platelet transfusion requirements: The EPAG-2015 French Innovative Leukemia Organization phase 2 randomized trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Elderly patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) treated with intensive chemotherapy are at risk of developing thrombopenia, which requires platelet transfusions. It would be interesting to provide them with thrombopoietin receptor agonists such as eltrombopag.

The EPAG-2015 multicenter phase 2 trial (18 French hospitals from October 2018 to June 2021) blindly randomized elderly patients (aged ≥60 years) with placebo or eltrombopag administered on Day 11 after induction chemotherapy and continued until AML response evaluation (Day 45) or a platelet count of >100 × 109/L. A cohort of 110 patients with a median age of 70 years was included and randomized (55 per arm) to receive placebo or eltrombopag.

After induction, 90 patients (81.8%) achieved complete response (CR) or CR with incomplete reconstitution (CRi) (45 in each group), including 74 patients with CR (38 with eltrombopag and 36 with placebo). With a median follow-up for alive patients of 20.9 months the primary objective was not reached, given that there was no difference in overall survival (hazard ratio, 1.59; 95% CI, 0.65-3.89; p = .31). Eltrombopag, however, did not lead to increased grade 3/4 adverse events, and was associated with a lower median number of platelet transfusions (eight; interquartile range [IQR], 6-14; vs. 10; IQR, 7-14; i.e., a 20% benefit).

This study failed to demonstrate a survival advantage after eltrombopag addition, at variance with previous reports, but shows that initiating eltrombopag after chemotherapy washout is feasible and safe, and resulted in a decreased need for platelet transfusions.

Article.ArticleTitle: Factors associated with missed video directly observed therapy sessions among persons with TB.

Abstract.AbstractText: <sec><title>BACKGROUND</title>Advanced digital technologies, such as video directly observed therapy (VDOT), are increasingly used to support TB treatment adherence monitoring. However, missed VDOT sessions remain a challenge, particularly in low-resource settings. This study aimed to determine the factors associated with the number of missed VDOT submissions among patients using VDOT.</sec><sec><title>METHODS</title>We conducted a secondary analysis of data from the DOT Selfie randomised controlled trial implemented in Uganda. The outcome of interest was the number of missed VDOT sessions throughout treatment. A negative binomial regression model was used to examine factors associated with the outcome. Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) and 95% confidence intervals were reported.</sec><sec><title>RESULTS</title>Among the 71 patients included in the analysis, 32% were HIV positive. HIV co-infection (cIRR = 2.2; 1.2-4.0), age >30 years (cIRR = 2.0; 1.1-3.6), alcohol consumption (aIRR = 2.3; 1.1-5.1), being married (aIRR = 2.2; 1.1-4.1), and having ≤4 household members (aIRR = 1.9; 1.1-3.3) were associated with a higher incidence rate of missed VDOT sessions.</sec><sec><title>CONCLUSION</title>In this study, alcohol use and HIV co-infection independently affected missed video sessions. However, after adjusting for confounding, marital status and household size remained important factors that should be further studied.</sec>.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of dairy product intake and home-based resistance exercise on the physical function in Japanese community-dwelling older adults: results of a real-world randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Although the combination of dairy product intake and resistance training has shown benefits for muscle health in older adults, most intervention studies have been conducted under highly controlled conditions, limiting their applicability to real-world settings.

We conducted a 12-week pragmatic, open-label randomized controlled trial involving community-dwelling Japanese older adults. Fifty-four adults aged ≥ 65 years were assigned to either a dairy product intake plus home-based resistance training group (milk and exercise; ME) or a home-based resistance training only group (E). The dairy intervention targeted an increase equivalent to approximately 10-15 g of dairy-derived protein per day within habitual meals. Both groups were instructed to perform home-based resistance training at least three days per week. The physical function, including upper and lower limb strength, handgrip strength, gait speed, and body composition, was assessed before and after the intervention. Exploratory subgroup analyses were conducted according to baseline dairy consumption and skeletal muscle mass.

Fifty-one participants (mean age, 78.2 ± 6.9 years; BMI, 22.9 ± 3.2 kg/m²) completed the study (retention rate: 94.4%). Adherence to milk supplement consumption was exceptionally high (median 7.00 times/week, IQR 7.00-7.00 times/week). The median frequencies of milk and dairy product intakes were 6.83 (IQR 5.60-7.00) and 6.83 (IQR 6.17-6.94) times/week, respectively. Resistance exercise adherence was comparable between the ME and E groups (3.13 [2.81-3.65] vs. 3.25 [2.71-3.96] times/week; p = 0.940). No significant differences were observed between the groups in terms of muscle strength, physical function, or body composition. However, some functional outcomes improved over time in both groups. In exploratory subgroup analyses, participants with lower habitual dairy consumption at baseline showed improvements in upper and lower limb strength only in the ME group.

Adding modest dairy product intake to home-based resistance training did not provide additional overall benefits compared to exercise alone. However, exploratory findings suggest that baseline dairy consumption may influence the responsiveness of older adults to combined nutrition and exercise interventions.

Article.ArticleTitle: A multilevel intervention to improve adherence to prostate cancer active surveillance versus usual care: results from a pilot randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Active surveillance is the primary management strategy for men with low-risk prostate cancer and yet, adherence to active surveillance remains suboptimal. Men choose to receive surgery or radiation therapy even without any evidence of their cancer progressing or because of anxiety. Novel interventions to improve adherence are needed.

We designed and implemented a pilot randomized clinical trial comparing usual care (control) versus a multilevel intervention (Management of Active surveillance in Prostate cancer [MAP] for patients with low-risk prostate cancer and their primary care providers (PCPs) between November 2022 and May 2023. Our primary outcomes were feasibility (defined by enrollment and survey completion rates) and acceptability (assessed by a participant satisfaction survey). Exploratory outcomes included additional surveys and interviews assessing patient- and PCP-reported measures. Eligible patients were adult men > 55 years old diagnosed with low-risk prostate cancer on active surveillance. Eligible PCPs were identified by enrolled patients. For the intervention arm, participants had access to a personalized website addressing barriers to adherence (knowledge, provider roles in team-based care delivery, managing cancer-related anxiety). PCPs of patients in the intervention arm received a templated visit summary from the urologist with the recommended active surveillance care plan.

Thirty-five patients were randomized and survey completion rate across both arms was 86%. Overall, 70% of intervention arm participants found MAP acceptable. Patients in the intervention arm (versus control) were more likely to prefer either PCP or urologist (versus urologist only) for various aspects of active surveillance care at 6-months. Other exploratory patient-reported outcomes were similar across arms.

This study demonstrated a multilevel intervention (MAP) is feasible to deploy and acceptable. Importantly, MAP shows promise in building patient confidence about team-based active surveillance care delivery and increased primary care involvement through targeted education around the role or primary care.
