Article.ArticleTitle: Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSpect): an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Data on prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV) used separately or in combination in patients with paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS) are inconclusive, leading to wide practice variability. We aimed to compare the effects of prone positioning with supine positioning and the effects of HFOV with conventional mechanical ventilation on ventilator-free days in children with early, moderate-to-severe PARDS.

PROSpect was an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial done in 75 paediatric intensive care units in 18 countries. Eligible patients were aged 2 weeks to 20 years, and were intubated and mechanically ventilated for less than 96 h before meeting criteria for moderate-to-severe PARDS. Patients were centrally randomly assigned using a web-based system to supine positioning and conventional mechanical ventilation, prone positioning and conventional mechanical ventilation, supine positioning and HFOV, or prone positioning and HFOV. Initially, the allocation was 1:1:1:1 stratified by age group and direct or indirect lung injury using a permuted block design with blocks of four and eight. Response-adaptive randomisation updates were planned to adjust allocation probabilities 28 days after 300 patients were randomly assigned and then 28 days after every 100 additional patients. Given the nature of the interventions, masking was not possible. The primary outcome was ventilator-free days through to day 28 among all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed prospectively by daily monitoring for the occurrence of prespecified adverse events. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03896763) and is closed to enrolment.

Between May 1, 2019 and Jan 13, 2026, 1045 patients were eligible for enrolment. The trial was stopped early for futility and slow enrolment after 424 of 600 planned patients were recruited. 126 patients were randomly assigned to the supine and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 130 to the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 90 to the supine and HFOV group, and 78 to the prone and HFOV group. Median age was 3·3 years (IQR 1·1-10·1), 211 (50%) patients were female, and 213 (50%) were male. There were no significant differences in ventilator-free days between prone and supine positioning (median 17·9 days [IQR 8·9-21·3] vs 17·4 days [6·4-21·9]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for ventilation 0·0 [95% CI -0·8 to 1·0]) or between HFOV and conventional mechanical ventilation (17·3 [5·7-21·6] vs 18·0 [9·9-21·5]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for positioning -0·3 [95% CI -1·5 to 0·5]). 41 (10%) patients had died at day 28, without group differences. Plugging or obstruction of the artificial airway occurred more frequently with prone than supine positioning (14 events in 12 [6%] of 188 patients vs three events in three [2%] of 197 patients; 0·74 [95% CI 0·44-1·26] vs 0·15 [0·05-0·47] events per 100 artificial airway days; rate ratio 4·83 [95% CI 1·38-16·82]). Stage 2 or worse immobility-related pressure injuries also occurred more frequently with prone versus supine positioning (12 [6%] vs two [1%]; relative risk 6·13 [95% CI 1·45-25·97]). Haemodynamic instability occurred more frequently with HFOV than conventional mechanical ventilation (41 events in 19 [13%] of 141 patients vs 38 events in 22 [9%] of 244 patients; 2·21 [95% CI 1·63-3·00] vs 1·22 [0·89-1·68] events per 100 paediatric intensive care unit days; rate ratio 1·84 [95% CI 1·18-2·87]). One serious adverse event, an unwitnessed self-extubation followed by cardiopulmonary arrest, occurred in a patient in the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group.

We found no evidence to support prone positioning or HFOV as first-line strategies to improve ventilator-free days in patients with early, moderate-to-severe PARDS. Thus, the routine use of these strategies in this population is not recommended.

Article.ArticleTitle: Decitabine plus busulfan-cyclophosphamide versus busulfan-cyclophosphamide myeloablative conditioning before allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation for reducing risk of relapse in adult KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia in China: an open-label, multicentre, randomised phase 3 trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: An unmet need persists for optimal myeloablative conditioning before allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) in adult KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia. We investigated whether decitabine plus busulfan-cyclophosphamide (DAC-BuCy) conditioning reduced the risk of relapse compared with busulfan-cyclophosphamide (BuCy) conditioning.

In this open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial at eight transplantation centres in China, eligible patients were aged 14-65 years, had morphologically confirmed KMT2A-rearranged leukaemia, and had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-2. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) before HSCT to DAC-BuCy (intravenous decitabine 20 mg/m2 once a day on days -14 to -10, intravenous busulfan 3·2 mg/kg once a day on days -7 to -4, and intravenous cyclophosphamide 60 mg/kg once a day on days -3 to -2) or BuCy (same dose and duration of busulfan and cyclophosphamide). Randomisation was done with permuted blocks (block size four) with no stratification and was implemented through an independent, interactive, web-based response system. The primary endpoint was 2-year cumulative incidence of relapse in the intention-to-treat population. Safety was assessed in all patients who received treatment. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03596892) and is complete.

Between May 1, 2019, and Jan 31, 2023, 130 patients were randomised to receive a DAC-BuCy (n=65; 34 [52%] female and 31 [48%] male) or BuCy (n=65; 29 [45%] female and 36 [55%] male) regimen. Median follow-up was 34·7 months (IQR 30·2-52·5). 2-year cumulative incidence of relapse was 12% (95% CI 6-22) in the DAC-BuCy group and 29% (19-41) in the BuCy group (hazard ratio 0·41 [0·20-0·87]; p=0·017). The most common grade 3-5 adverse events were infections or infestations (DAC-BuCy group 27 [42%] and BuCy group 25 [38%]), acute graft-versus-host disease (DAC-BuCy group 23 [35%] and BuCy group 22 [34%]), and gastrointestinal disorders (DAC-BuCy group 14 [22%] and BuCy group 15 [23%]). Four (6%) patients in the DAC-BuCy group and five (8%) patients in the BuCy group died from adverse events, of which two were due to regimen-related toxicities: one nervous system disorder in the DAC-BuCy group and one cardiac disorder in the BuCy group.

The addition of decitabine to BuCy conditioning reduced the risk of relapse with an acceptable safety profile in adult patients with KMT2A‑rearranged leukaemia and could be a suitable therapeutic option for this population.

Article.ArticleTitle: An intervention based on acceptance and commitment therapy for people experiencing work- or career-related difficulties: A randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: This randomized controlled trial assessed the effectiveness of a group intervention based on acceptance and commitment therapy designed for people facing work- or career-related difficulties (e.g., job loss, burnout). Participants were recruited with the assistance of community organizations providing career counseling services, and they were randomly assigned to either an intervention group (n = 82) or a waitlist group (n = 82). They completed questionnaires aimed at measuring process (i.e., psychological flexibility and inflexibility) and outcome variables (i.e., psychological well-being, psychological distress, meaning in life, and career engagement) on three occasions (baseline, postintervention, and follow-up). Participants took part in seven 2.5-hr sessions offered online during a 7-week period. Results of mixed-effects models on intention-to-treat data showed that the intervention led to an increase in psychological flexibility (d = .64), well-being (d = .32), and meaning in life (d = .42) and a decrease in psychological inflexibility (d = -.51) and distress (d = -.36). These effects were maintained at follow-up (17 weeks later), moderated by participants' initial levels of distress and precarity (for some outcomes). Indirect effect analyses showed that changes in psychological flexibility/inflexibility statistically accounted for these effects. The intervention had no significant effect on career engagement. Overall, this trial suggests that the intervention helped promote well-being and flourishing among people struggling with work- or career-related difficulties. Article.ArticleTitle: Histomorphometry and Immunohistochemistry of Xenogeneic Collagen Matrix: A Randomized Split-Mouth Clinical Study.

Abstract.AbstractText: To histomorphometrically evaluate collagen formation and immunohistochemically assess soft tissue vascularization around implants after treatment with xenogeneic acellular collagen matrix versus connective tissue graft in a randomized split-mouth clinical study.

Nine patients underwent implant rehabilitation with connective tissue graft and xenogeneic acellular collagen matrix in contralateral edentulous areas. A total of 24 grafts were performed (12 each). Grafts were assigned to healing times of 30 (n = 4), 90 (n = 4), or 180 days (n = 4), at which time samples were collected for histological and immunohistochemical analysis. Collagen quality and density were assessed histologically. Vascularization, vessel density, and diameter were evaluated immunohistochemically. Samples were stained with Masson's trichrome for collagen and immunostained with CD34 for vascular endothelium; the grafted site was the unit of analysis.

The percentage of collagen was higher in sites biopsied at 180 days for both grafts and was similar between groups at all healing periods. Xenogeneic acellular collagen matrix showed vascularization patterns similar to autogenous connective tissue graft, with higher vessel density and vascular percentage at 90 days, while differences between groups were observed only at 30 days.

Within the limitations of this study, xenogeneic acellular collagen matrix demonstrated collagen maturation at the later healing periods and vascularization patterns with histological characteristics similar to those of the connective tissue graft during the evaluated healing periods.

Article.ArticleTitle: Immunogenicity and safety of Institut Pasteur du Cambodge (IPC) and updated Thai Red Cross (UTRC) intradermal rabies vaccine regimens among healthy adults in India: A phase 4, open label, equivalence randomised controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Shorter rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) regimens could improve compliance and access by reducing the number of clinic visits and vaccine requirement per patient. We compared the immunogenicity and safety of a 1-week intradermal Institut Pasteur du Cambodge (IPC) regimen with a 1-month intradermal Updated Thai Red Cross regimen (UTRC) using two rabies vaccines widely used in India: Purified Chick Embryo Cell vaccine (PCECV) and the Purified Vero Cell Rabies vaccine (PVRV).

We conducted a phase 4, single-centre, open-label randomised controlled equivalence trial among adult healthy volunteers. Participants were block randomised (1:1:1:1) to receive either the IPC (Days 0, 3, 7) or UTRC (Days 0, 3, 7, 28) intradermal regimen with either PCECV or PVRV. Rabies virus neutralising antibody (RVNA) titres were measured up to 1 year. The primary objective of the trial was to determine the immunogenicity of the Intradermal abridged Cambodia regimen with updated intradermal Thai red cross regimen using two different vaccine types among healthy volunteers in India. The primary outcome was geometric mean concentration ratios (GMR) of RVNA on day 42, assessed separately for each vaccine type. Equivalence for each vaccine was predefined as the entire 95% confidence interval for GMR lying between 0.72 and 1.04. The secondary outcomes included proportion of participants with RVNA titres >= 0.5 IU/mL on Days 14, 28, 42, 90, 180, and 365 and vaccine safety. Between October 10, 2023, and December 23, 2023, 400 participants were randomly assigned (100 per group) to PCECV-IPC, PCECV-UTRC, PVRV-IPC, and PVRV-UTRC. 362 (90.5%) completed PEP regimen and blood draw on day 42. In the prespecified modified intention-to-treat analysis, the Day 42 GMR (IPC vs UTRC) was 0.59 (95% CI: 0.47-0.75) for PCECV and 0.76 (95% CI: 0.61-0.95) for PVRV, which did not meet the prespecified equivalence criterion. All participants, irrespective of baseline serostatus, in four groups had RVNA titres ≥0.5 IU/mL at every assessment from day 14-1 year. Adverse events were similar between regimens and mostly mild. There are important limitations in this study. Nearly one-quarter of participants had baseline RVNA titres ≥0.5 IU/mL despite exclusion of participants with a reported history of rabies vaccination or dog bite, suggesting unrecognised prior immunological priming that may have influenced GMC estimates. As the trial was conducted among healthy volunteers rather than people receiving PEP after animal bites, the findings may not fully reflect vaccine performance in routine post-exposure settings.

The IPC regimen did not meet the prespecified equivalence criterion compared to UTRC. All participants achieved RVNA titres ≥0.5 IU/mL indicative of seroprotection from day 14 till 1 year. Policy decisions regarding replacement of UTRC should consider these immunogenicity findings together with compliance, cost, and vaccine availability.
The trial was registered with the Clinical Trial Registry - India (CTRI/2023/10/058418). URL: https://ctri.nic.in/Clinicaltrials/pmaindet2.php?EncHid=OTAxMDA=&Enc=&userName=).

Article.ArticleTitle: The Effect of Bupropion in Peripheral Neuropathic Pain A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study.

Abstract.AbstractText: Monoamine reuptake inhibitors are evidenced first-line treatments of peripheral neuropathic pain. The aim was to investigate if bupropion, a drug that specifically inhibits neuronal noradrenaline and dopamine reuptake, relieves neuropathic pain and if a potential effect depends on status of conditioned pain modulation (CPM) and sensory phenotype (irritable vs. non-irritable nociceptor).

Study design was randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, and cross-over. Patients with peripheral neuropathic pain were treated with bupropion and placebo in a random order, with treatment periods lasting 6 weeks preceded by a 1-week baseline. Change in daily average pain was the primary outcome. Other outcomes included pain relief and 30% and 50% pain reduction.

67 patients were randomized and included in the analysis. The mean daily average pain changed from NRS 6.4 to 5.5 after bupropion treatment with an average effect as compared with placebo of -0.5 (95% CI -0.8 to -0.1, p = 0.005). No relation was found between response to treatment and efficiency of CPM or sensory phenotype. There was no significant effect on the pain relief scale. A 30% and 50% pain reduction was found in 10 and 6 patients respectively with a NNT for 50% pain reduction of 15. Bupropion was well tolerated.

Bupropion had a pain-relieving effect independent of CPM efficiency and sensory phenotype. NNT for 50% pain reduction was higher than reported for first-line treatments, but bupropion treatment may still be an option in patients with insufficient response or intolerable side effects on such treatments.

This study finds a modest pain-relieving effect of bupropion on peripheral neuropathic pain independent of function of conditioned pain modulation. Bupropion could be an alternative treatment for patients with a lack of effect or intolerable side effects to first-choice treatments of peripheral neuropathic pain. Further, larger studies are needed to determine optimal dosage.

The study is registered with the EU clinical trials Register (EudraCT 2019-000243-27) on March 15th 2019. The study is approved by the Ethical Committee of the Region of Southern Denmark (also included approval for Regions of Central Denmark; no. S-20190010) and the Danish Medicine Agency (no. 2019012986) and is registered with the Danish Data Protection Agency (via the Region of Southern Denmark's internal notification; no. 19/17111).

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of nutrition counseling on complementary feeding practices among mothers with children aged 6-23 months in West Gojjam Zone, Northwest Ethiopia: A cluster-randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Appropriate complementary feeding is essential for children's growth and cognitive development. However, these practices remain inadequate in the study area. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the effect of nutrition counseling on complementary feeding practices among mothers with children aged 6-23 months in West Gojjam Zone, Northwest Ethiopia.

A two-arm, parallel, cluster-randomized controlled trial was conducted from June 2023 to December 2024 in rural districts of West Gojjam Zone. Thirty clusters (15 per arm) were assigned to either an intervention group (n = 401), which received Health Belief Model-based nutrition counseling by Women's Development Army leaders, or to a control group (n = 401), which received routine education. The intervention was delivered monthly for nine months from infant age 6-8 months. The primary outcome was appropriate complementary feeding practices. Secondary outcomes included minimum dietary diversity, meal frequency, acceptable diet, and egg/flesh food consumption. Data were collected via interviewer-administered questionnaires. The intervention effect was analyzed using Generalized Estimating Equations with adjustment for potential confounders. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.

The difference-in-differences in appropriate complementary feeding practices between groups was 13.2 percentage points. After adjustment, mothers in the intervention group were nearly 2.5 times more likely to practice appropriate complementary feeding than controls [AOR = 2.49, 95% CI: (1.40, 4.42)]. Children of counseled mothers were also more likely to achieve minimum dietary diversity [AOR = 1.75, 95% CI: (1.04, 2.93)], minimum meal frequency [AOR = 1.62, 95% CI: (1.01, 2.61)], and minimum acceptable diet [AOR = 2.13, 95% CI: (1.26, 3.59)] compared with controls.

Health Belief Model-based nutrition counseling was positively associated with improvements in appropriate complementary feeding practices, minimum dietary diversity, meal frequency, and acceptable diet. Integrating such counseling into routine maternal and child health services may strengthen child nutrition programs in similar rural settings.

Article.ArticleTitle: A randomised controlled crossover trial comparing two mandibular repositioning appliances for treatment of moderate obstructive sleep apnoea.

Abstract.AbstractText: To compare two custom-made bi-block mandibular repositioning appliances, the SomnoDent® Flex and the OrthoApnea NOA®, in adults with moderate obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA).

Randomised two-period, two-sequence crossover trial at a single centre (Genk, Belgium). Adults with polysomnography-confirmed AHI 5-30 events/h were eligible; all enrolled had moderate OSA (AHI 15.1-29.7). Participants were randomised 1:1 to SomnoDent® Flex-NOA® or the reverse sequence, each worn for three months with a two-week washout. Participants and clinicians were unblinded; outcome scorers were blinded to appliance. The registered primary outcome was the change in AHI from baseline for each appliance. The between-appliance difference in post-treatment AHI was assessed in a non-prespecified principal comparative analysis using linear mixed-effects models with appliance, period and sequence as fixed effects.

Sixteen participants were randomised, eight per sequence, and all were analysed. Median AHI fell from 17.6 events/h at baseline to 3.1 with the SomnoDent® Flex and 2.3 with the NOA® (both p < 0.001 versus baseline). The between-appliance difference was + 0.16 events/h (95% CI - 2.56 to + 2.87; p = 0.904), with a period effect (+ 3.82 events/h in period 2, coinciding with the change from home polygraphy to in-laboratory polysomnography; p = 0.009). No secondary outcome differed significantly; post hoc, AHI < 5 events/h was reached in 12/16 (SomnoDent® Flex) and 10/16 (NOA®). No participant discontinued for an adverse event; adverse events were not systematically recorded.

Both appliances were associated with reductions in AHI. The non-prespecified between-appliance comparison detected no statistically significant difference and does not establish equivalence. Complete confounding between period and measurement methodology, together with insufficient adherence, titration and adverse-event data, limits conclusions about the overall comparative merits of the appliances.
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06810479, registered 5 February 2025, prior to first enrolment.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of intraoral glossopharyngeal nerve block on hemodynamic response to mouth retractor placement in transoral robotic surgery: a randomized clinical trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Placement of rigid oral retractors during transoral robotic surgery (TORS) elicits a sympathetic hemodynamic response that may be harmful in high-risk patients. The glossopharyngeal nerve provides sensory innervation to the oropharyngeal structures stimulated during retractor placement, yet no previous trial has evaluated glossopharyngeal nerve block (GPN block) for attenuating this response. In this prospective, single-center, randomized clinical trial, 42 patients (ASA I-II, aged 18-65 years) undergoing TORS were allocated 1:1 to the block group, which received bilateral intraoral GPN block with 2 mL of 2% lignocaine per side or the Control group, which received no block. The outcome assessor was blinded; no sham procedure was performed, and the anaesthesiologist performing the block was not blinded. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients with a > 20% increase in mean arterial pressure (MAP) from the pre-retractor baseline within 10 minutes of Feyh-Kastenbauer retractor insertion. Bayesian logistic regression with a Normal (0, 5) prior on the group coefficient was used; the pre-specified decision criterion was a posterior probability of directional benefit P (ARD < 0) exceeding 0.95. The trial was registered in the Clinical Trial Registry of India (CTRI/2022/03/041013, dated 11 March 2022) https://ctri.nic.in/Clinicaltrials/searchbyctri.php , with a date of first patient enrolment of 21/03/2022. The increase in MAP > 20% occurred in 8 of 21 patients (38.1%) in the control group versus 3 of 21 (14.3%) in the block group. The posterior mean absolute risk difference was - 23.9% (95% credible interval [CrI]: - 49.4% to 2.2%), with P (ARD < 0) = 0.964, exceeding the pre-specified threshold. Sensitivity analyses generally supported the direction of effect under neutral, sceptical, and optimistic priors (P(ARD < 0) range: 0.934-0.967), although the posterior probability under the sceptical prior did not exceed the prespecified 0.95 threshold; evidence was equivocal under the pessimistic prior (P(ARD < 0) = 0.57). Maximum MAP and heart rate were lower in the block group (P (difference < 0) = 0.998 and 0.995, respectively). Bispectral index values were comparable between groups throughout the procedure. The GPN block is associated with a high posterior probability of attenuating the hemodynamic response to mouth retractor placement in TORS. The credible intervals were wide, reflecting uncertainty about effect magnitude. A larger confirmatory trial assessing clinical endpoints is warranted.

Article.ArticleTitle: Controlled postoperative red wine intake versus abstinence in habitual wine drinkers undergoing elective urological surgery (WISE): a translational randomized controlled trial assessing quality of life, surgical outcomes and complications.

Abstract.AbstractText: To date, no prospective randomized study has evaluated whether controlled postoperative red wine intake, compared with abstinence, affects recovery in habitual wine drinkers undergoing surgery.

In this single-center randomized controlled trial (NCT05261620), habitual wine drinkers scheduled for elective urological surgery were randomized 1:1 to abstinence from alcohol (Control Arm) or standardized red wine intake (150 mL of 13% v/v red wine with lunch and with dinner) from postoperative day 1 to day 30 (Experimental Arm). The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in change from baseline to 30 days in the SF-36 Mental Health Index (MHI). Secondary endpoints included postoperative complications, hospital readmission, length of hospitalization, blood parameters, and oxidative stress markers.

The mean change in MHI was - 0.6 in the Control Arm and + 0.7 in the Experimental Arm (difference 1.3 points; 95% CI - 1.9 to 4.6; p = 0.4). Overall complications (16.1% vs. 9.8%; p = 0.4), length of hospital stay and 30-day readmissions (8.1% vs. 0%; p = 0.06) did not differ significantly between the Control and Experimental Arms, respectively. Blood parameters and oxidative stress markers showed no clinically relevant differences.

Among predominantly older male habitual wine drinkers undergoing elective urological surgery, controlled postoperative red wine intake did not improve 30-day quality of life compared with abstinence. Complications and blood parameters did not differ meaningfully. These findings do not support the initiation or promotion of alcohol use.
This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05261620, registered on 02/20/2022. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05261620 ).

Article.ArticleTitle: Robot-assisted minimally invasive versus conventional open transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion for lumbar degenerative disease: a prospective randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Robotic guidance may improve pedicle screw placement during minimally invasive transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (MIS-TLIF), but its clinical value remains uncertain. In this prospective, single-center, assessor-blinded trial, 128 patients were randomly assigned in a prespecified 1:3 ratio to robot-assisted MIS-TLIF (n = 32) or conventional fluoroscopy-guided open TLIF (n = 96) using an independent statistician's computer-generated sequence. The primary outcome was the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) at 2 weeks. Technical, perioperative, and radiographic outcomes were assessed through 18 months; later assessments were exploratory.At 2 weeks, ODI favored robotic assistance (28.25 ± 6.64 vs 31.52 ± 6.55; mean difference, -3.27; 95% confidence interval, -5.98 to -0.56; P = 0.019), but was below the 10-point sample-size target and nonsignificant at 3 months. Robotic assistance favored grade A screw placement (98.9% vs 94.5%; P = 0.037) and reduced intraoperative adjustment (2.8% vs 7.3%; P = 0.030); facet joint violation and reoperation did not differ significantly. Operative time was longer, whereas blood loss, ambulation, drain removal, and hospital stay favored robotic assistance. Fusion rates and adjacent-segment disc height were similar. Multifidus cross-sectional area was greater with robotic assistance at 12 and 18 months in patients with evaluable imaging. Robot-assisted MIS-TLIF was associated with earlier recovery, higher screw accuracy, and greater postoperative multifidus cross-sectional area, but longer operative time without demonstrated mid-term clinical or fusion benefits. Larger multicenter trials are warranted. Trial Registration:Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2400082553.

Article.ArticleTitle: AI-facilitated individualized nutritional guidance with ABC-structured prompts improves short-term dietary intake adequacy and patient-reported symptoms after gastrointestinal cancer surgery: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Postoperative nutritional management is critical for gastrointestinal cancer surgery patients, yet discharge advice is often standardized and lacks individualization. Whether an AI-facilitated individualized and quantified strategy improves short-term dietary intake compared with standard generic advice remains unclear; this trial does not isolate the independent effect of AI.

To determine whether AI-facilitated individualized nutritional guidance using structured prompts improves short-term dietary intake adequacy and patient-reported symptoms versus standard discharge advice.

In this single-center, randomized controlled trial, 90 patients undergoing laparoscopic gastric or colorectal cancer surgery were assigned 1:1 to AI-facilitated individualized guidance generated by DeepSeek v3.2 using an ABC-structured prompt plus clinician review or standard discharge dietary advice (standard care group). The intervention combined AI, individualization, quantified targets, written guidance, and clinician review; the trial cannot isolate AI alone. Primary outcome was energy intake adequacy (≥ 90% of target) at 30 days post-discharge. Secondary outcomes included protein intake adequacy, nutritional status, patient-reported outcomes, process measures (expert-rated quality scores, provider time), and 30-day complications. Outcome assessors were blinded to group assignment.

Baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups. The AI-guided group achieved significantly higher energy adequacy (66.7% vs. 40.0%, OR 3.0, 95% CI 1.3-7.1, P = 0.01) and protein adequacy (62.2% vs. 35.6%, OR 2.9, 95% CI 1.2-6.8, P = 0.01) at 30 days. Expert-rated quality scores were superior in the AI-guided group for completeness (4.6 vs. 3.2), individualization (4.8 vs. 2.8), and actionability (4.5 vs. 3.5) (all P < 0.001), while provider time per patient was reduced (8.2 vs. 12.5 min, P < 0.001). Patient-reported outcomes showed significant improvements in fatigue, nausea/vomiting, appetite loss, and gastrointestinal symptoms (GSRS total score 2.1 vs. 2.5, P = 0.03) in the AI-guided group. No significant differences were observed in weight change, serum nutritional markers, or complication rates.

AI-facilitated individualized nutritional guidance improved short-term dietary intake adequacy and patient-reported symptoms and reduced provider time compared with standard generic advice. These findings do not show that AI itself is superior to similarly individualized non-AI counseling and do not establish longer-term nutritional or clinical benefit. Clinical supervision remains essential.

Article.ArticleTitle: Experiences of Immersive Virtual Reality Among Older Adults With Physical Disabilities: Qualitative Process Evaluation of a Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Emerging evidence indicates that immersive virtual reality can be used therapeutically and has demonstrated efficacy in promoting the mental health of older adults. Nevertheless, there remains a paucity of qualitative research examining the specific experiences underpinning these benefits.

This study aimed to explore the perspectives of older adults who received the 12-session Immersive Virtual Reality Therapeutic Programme (IVRTP) intervention and health-related undergraduate students who delivered it as interventionists, within the context of residential care homes.

A descriptive qualitative study was conducted as a qualitative exploration embedded in a multicenter randomized controlled trial evaluating the effects of IVRTP in promoting the mental health of older adults with disabilities living in residential homes. The IVRTP incorporated therapeutic elements of tourism, natural scenes, and reminiscence. Data were collected through focus group interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis.

Seven groups of older adults (n=28) and 3 groups of student interventionists (n=9) participated in the study. Five themes emerged: IVRTP contributes to "broadening horizons" through embracing new technology, learning new things, and engaging in new activities. Participants noted that the IVRTP provided "a realistic journey and immersive escape" from their residential home environment and mobility issues. They expressed that the IVRTP evoked "reminiscent memories" from the past and were amazed at the observed changes in tourist destinations over time. The interviews were filled with laughter and affirmations of positive emotions associated with this "joyful adventure," although a few participants mentioned "minor discomfort," such as eye soreness and dizziness, from wearing the head-mounted devices. Students' accounts corroborated these themes; their meaning-making and colearning with older adults underscored the pedagogical value of authentic, community-based, intergenerational learning and reinforced the case for integrating a community practicum into the curriculum.

Implementing an IVRTP in residential care settings, particularly for older adults with mobility limitations, is positively viewed as an accessible, enjoyable, and beneficial intervention to support psychosocial well-being. Therapeutically oriented content delivered through a structured protocol, coupled with the use of advanced IVR technology, was appreciated by both older adults and student interventionists.

Article.ArticleTitle: User Interface Designs to Address Cancer Misinformation: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Misinformation about false and potentially harmful cancer treatments is common on social media. Strategies are needed to encourage reporting to reduce exposure to inaccurate treatment claims.
To evaluate the impact of 2 user interface designs (prompts on posts) on intervening and sharing cancer misinformation on social media.

This 3-group, parallel-group, randomized clinical trial assessed outcomes at 5 time points from March 31 to May 12, 2025. US adults (ages 18-65 years) who had a cancer diagnosis or identified as a cancer caregiver and used social media were recruited from Prolific. Participants interacted with cancer misinformation posts on a simulated realistic social media platform. Data were analyzed from May 13, 2025, to July 27, 2026.
Participants were randomized to cancer misinformation posts shown with social cue-enhanced prompts that specify others' actions and a review policy, standard prompts, or no prompts (control).

The primary outcome was a participant flagging a post to intervene. Primary and secondary outcomes included recorded social media behavior (flagging, disliking, liking) and self-reported willingness to flag, dislike, like, comment, and share about the posts. Intervening outside the study platform was also assessed. A separate generalized estimating equations model was used for each outcome.

A total of 294 individuals (mean [SD] age, 39.3 [11.7] years; 179 [62%] women) with cancer or who were caregivers for individuals with cancer were randomized, with 88 participants receiving social cue prompts, 92 receiving standard prompts, and 114 receiving no prompts. Posts with inaccurate claims were flagged 2 to 3 times more often with social cue (224 of 592 posts [38%]) and standard (180 of 689 posts [26%]) prompts than those without prompts (84 of 675 posts [12%]) (social cue vs control: rate ratio [RR], 3.12 [95% CI, 1.79-5.42]; standard vs control: RR, 2.15 [95% CI, 1.20-3.88]). Prompts led to less sharing behavior (ie, liking: 20 posts [3%] with social cue prompts; 10 posts [1%] with standard prompts) compared with posts without prompts (65 posts [10%]) (social cue vs control: RR, 0.07 [95% CI, 0.04-0.15]; standard vs control: RR, 0.13 [95% CI, 0.04-0.42]). Prompts also led to greater willingness to flag and dislike (intervening) and less willingness to like and share compared with no prompt. Standard prompts led to more flagging on existing social media (outside the study platform) than no prompts.
In this randomized clinical trial of user interface designs, simple prompts encouraged responsible behavior online. Prompts on posts led to more intervening and less sharing of cancer misinformation.
ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07588607.

Journal.Title: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

Article.ArticleTitle: Impact of obesity on clinical outcomes and the treatment effect of catheter ablation in atrial fibrillation: insights from CABANA.

Abstract.AbstractText: Obesity and atrial fibrillation (AF) are global epidemics, often co-existing and compounding cardiovascular risk. While catheter ablation has emerged as an effective strategy for rhythm control in symptomatic AF, it remains unclear whether obesity modifies its benefit. This post hoc analysis of the CABANA trial investigates the influence of baseline obesity on clinical outcomes after catheter ablation vs. drug therapy in AF patients.

A total of 2170 CABANA participants with available body mass index (BMI) were included. Obesity was defined by BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2, and Class II obesity by BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2. Adverse outcomes, AF recurrence, and functional status were analysed using Cox, mixed-effects, and generalized estimating equation models, assessing treatment-by-obesity interactions. Obese patients exhibited higher comorbidity burden, worse baseline functional status, and more persistent AF compared to non-obese counterparts. Higher BMI was associated with increased cardiovascular hospitalization and a higher New York Heart Association functional class. Catheter ablation significantly reduced the risk of AF recurrence and improved symptom burden and functional capacity, irrespective of obesity status. No significant interaction was found between BMI and treatment effect on the primary composite endpoint of cardiovascular hospitalization or all-cause mortality. However, patients with Class II obesity or higher had worse absolute outcomes despite similar relative benefits from ablation.

While obesity is associated with worse baseline status and outcomes, it was not shown to significantly alter the relative effectiveness of AF ablation compared to drug therapy. These findings support a multifaceted approach integrating rhythm control with upstream interventions targeting obesity-related atrial remodelling and comorbidity management.

Article.ArticleTitle: Evaluation of Fibre-Reinforced Composites and Nanohybrid Composites as Post-Endodontic Restorations in Primary Teeth - A Comparative Study.

Abstract.AbstractText: Fibre-reinforced composites (FRCs) have been introduced to improve the mechanical properties of conventional composite restorations. However, clinical evidence supporting their use in primary teeth remains limited.
To compare the clinical performance of FRCs and nanohybrid composites (NHCs) as post-endodontic restorations in primary teeth over 12 months.

A parallel-arm randomised controlled trial was conducted among 66 children aged 5-9 years requiring pulpectomy in primary molars. Participants were randomly allocated into two groups ( n = 33 each): Group A (FRC) and Group B (NHC). Standardised pulpectomy procedures were followed by placement of the respective experimental restorative materials. Clinical evaluation was performed at baseline, 6 months and 12 months using the modified United States Public Health Service criteria by two calibrated examiners. Intragroup comparisons were analysed using the Friedman test and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Bonferroni correction, and intergroup comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test.

Both groups showed comparable baseline scores ( P = 0.18), confirming homogeneity. A statistically significant decline in clinical performance was observed within both groups over time ( P < 0.05). However, no statistically significant differences were found between FRCs and NHCs at baseline, 6 months or 12 months ( P > 0.05). Although slightly greater deterioration was noted in the NHC group, it was not significant.

Both FRCs and NHCs demonstrated comparable clinical performance over 12 months. Despite improved mechanical properties, FRCs did not show superior clinical outcomes. Restoration success appears to be multifactorial, emphasising the importance of clinical technique and case selection.

Article.ArticleTitle: Implant Stability and Crestal Bone Levels of Dental Implants with and without Injectable Platelet Rich Fibrin (i-PRF) - A Comparative Study.

Abstract.AbstractText: Restoring teeth with implants has become the treatment of choice to reduce the adverse effects of tooth loss. Injectable platelet-rich fibrin (i-PRF), an autologous platelet concentrate rich in growth factors, has recently gained attention for its potential to enhance osseointegration, accelerate healing and reduce crestal bone loss around dental implants.

Twenty patients were randomised into Group I (Test) treated with i-PRF-coated implants and Group II (Control) without i-PRF coating. Implant stability quotient (ISQ) values and crestal bone evaluation were obtained at baseline and three months in both groups.

Mean overall ISQ values of Group I at baseline and 3 months were 68.10 ± 3.73 and 70.60 ± 2.84, respectively. No statistical significance in overall crestal bone levels between Group I and Group II at baseline ( P = 0.5815) and three months ( P = 0.4500) was observed.
Conditioning of the implant surface using autologous i-PRF could enhance resonance frequency analysis at 3-month evaluation but does not have an influence on the bone level.

Article.ArticleTitle: The Effect of Resveratrol, Quercetin, and Curcumin on Drusen Volume in Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: To evaluate the effect of resveratrol, quercetin, and curcumin (RQC) compared with curcumin alone on drusen volume and clinical outcomes in patients with age-related macular degeneration (AMD).

In this open-label, randomized phase 2a clinical trial, patients with early and intermediate AMD were randomized 2:1 to oral RQC or curcumin for 24 months. The primary outcome was the mean change in central drusen volume from baseline measured using spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT). Secondary outcomes included analyses of drusen volume and number by baseline size, categorical analyses of individual drusen response, change in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), frequency of vision loss, progression to advanced AMD, and safety.

Thirty-eight patients were included in the final analysis. After 24 months, central drusen volume decreased significantly with RQC compared with curcumin (-13.4% vs. +6.9%; P = 0.02). Mean BCVA increased by 0.8 letters in the RQC group and decreased by 2.1 letters in the curcumin group (P = 0.08). The frequencies of both mild and moderate vision loss were lower in the RQC group. Progression to advanced AMD occurred in 3.7% of participants and 2.3% of eligible eyes in the RQC group.
RQC treatment was associated with reductions in drusen volume, low rates of progression to advanced AMD, and maintenance of BCVA over 24 months.
This study provides preliminary clinical evidence that this oral therapy may reduce drusen burden and warrants further evaluation as a potential treatment for early to intermediate AMD.

Article.ArticleTitle: The Effects of Force-Velocity Profile-Based Load Prescription on Muscle Power and Functional Performance in Velocity-Deficient Older Adults.

Abstract.AbstractText: Muscle power is essential for functional capacity in older adults and can be improved through power-focused resistance training (PRT). PRT adaptations are load- and velocity-specific, yet optimal load prescription remains unclear. As force and velocity capacities vary between individuals, this 12-week intervention compared two force-velocity (F-V) profile-guided loading strategies: training at loads matched versus not matched to the F-V deficit. F-V profiles of 80 adults ≥ 65 years were assessed on a pneumatic leg press, with maximal force (F0) and velocity (V0) expressed as z-scores relative to a younger reference group (n = 60, 20-35 years). A difference ≥ 1 between z-scores was considered indicative of a deficit, with the direction determining a force- or velocity-deficit profile. As force deficits were rare (n = 4), the intervention only included participants with a velocity deficit (n = 59), of whom 57 initiated the intervention. Participants were randomly assigned to train at loads matched to their deficit (individualized; IND) or at loads deliberately not matched to their deficit (non-individualized; NON-IND). Maximal power, F-V profile parameters and functional performance were assessed at baseline, 6 and 12 weeks. From baseline to 12 weeks, F0 increased more in NON-IND than IND (p = 0.040), while V0 increased more in IND than NON-IND (p = 0.009). Changes in power and functional performance did not differ between groups (all p ≥ 0.065). In velocity-deficient older adults, differences in F-V-guided load prescription led to distinct F-V adaptations but did not lead to differences in power or functional performance. Trial Registration: The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06449716).

Article.ArticleTitle: Real-Time Electronic Patient-Reported Outcome Monitoring With Digital Triage and Care-Team Integration in Early Breast Cancer: ENABLE Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Electronic patient-reported outcomes (ePROs) can support patient-centered oncology care, but in early breast cancer, it is unclear whether real-time ePRO-triggered triage adds benefit beyond lower-intensity app-based support and scheduled ePRO collection.

We tested whether adding weekly ePRO screening, rule-based triage, and care-team escalation to app-based support improves health-related quality of life (HRQoL) during systemic therapy for early breast cancer.

ENABLE was a multicenter, open-label, parallel-group randomized controlled trial at 2 German university hospitals. Adults with early (stage I-III) breast cancer initiating systemic therapy were randomized 1:1 to reactive patient-reported outcome assessment (RPA) or control. Both arms received the ENABLE app with educational and organizational support and scheduled HRQoL assessments at 6 fixed time points; only RPA received weekly EuroQol Visual Analogue Scale screening (trigger: score <50 or ≥10-point decline) followed by symptom assessment, digital triage, and care-team alerts. Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System-29 was analyzed as an 8-measure HRQoL end-point family (7 domains plus pain intensity); no single domain, composite score, or binary global success rule was prespecified. Group-by-visit mixed-effects models were fitted with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate adjustment. The recruitment period was March 22, 2021, to September 8, 2023.

Of 605 randomized patients, 487 entered the modified intention-to-treat analysis (RPA: n=242; control: n=245). End-of-treatment between-group differences (RPA minus control, T-score points, 95% CI, and adjusted P) were: fatigue -3.90 (95% CI -5.77 to -2.03; P=.004), social participation +2.84 (95% CI 1.18 to 4.49; P=.01), anxiety -2.10 (95% CI -3.65 to -0.55; P=.049), depression -1.95 (95% CI -3.25 to -0.65; P=.10), sleep disturbance -1.82 (95% CI -3.43 to -0.20; P=.051), pain interference -1.44 (95% CI -3.38 to 0.49; P=.18), physical function +1.33 (95% CI -0.22 to 2.88; P=.18), and pain intensity -0.26 (95% CI -0.73 to 0.21; P=.32; 0-10 scale). All T-score differences were below the 5-point minimally important difference (MID). Exploratory time-to-deterioration analyses favored RPA for fatigue (hazard ratio [HR] 0.69, 95% CI 0.54-0.89), social participation (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.59-0.97), and depression (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.44-0.98). Of 209 monitored RPA patients, 160 (76.6%; 95% CI 70.4-81.8) triggered at least 1 alert. No intervention-related harms were identified.

ENABLE tests real-time, rule-based ePRO triage with care-team escalation against an active digital comparator rather than usual care, isolating the response pathway itself; it extends this design from metastatic disease into early breast cancer and escalates to the care team rather than to the patient alone. Benefits were domain-specific and sub-MID, in anxiety, fatigue, and social participation, tempering the expectation of a global HRQoL effect. For practice, symptom-triggered triage is a supportive-care workflow tool worth embedding where alerts reach a team that acts and documents, not a stand-alone remedy for treatment-related morbidity.

Article.ArticleTitle: Brief Motivational Workplace Intervention to Reduce Sugar-Sweetened Beverage Consumption Among Health Care Workers: Intervention Description, Feasibility, Fidelity, and Exploratory Outcomes From a Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Metabolic disease, including type 2 diabetes, is a major public health concern. Reducing sugar-sweetened beverage (SSB) consumption is a critical target for disease prevention and lifestyle modification. Workplace interventions offer a promising opportunity to address barriers to behavior change while strengthening motivation and self-efficacy.

The authors describe the intervention protocol, fidelity, and feasibility of a theory-informed brief intervention based on motivational interviewing principles to support reductions in SSB consumption among health care workers. The authors also explore changes over time in proposed mechanisms of behavior change.

Participants (N=314) allocated to the intervention arm of a multicenter randomized controlled trial received a 4-dose intervention consisting of an introductory phone call, a brief counseling session, and 2 booster calls, supplemented by at-home tools targeting stress and craving management. We assessed fidelity to motivational interviewing principles (competence scores) and described feasibility via session adherence. Finally, we explored changes over time in motivation for change and perceived self-efficacy.

More than 60% of enrolled participants completed all 4 sessions, suggesting feasibility and high retention in the context of a remotely delivered workplace intervention. Health coaches achieved basic levels of proficiency in 2 of 4 competency scores: technical (mean 3.23, SD 0.48) and complex reflections (mean 41.91%, SD 15.17%). Preliminary exploratory findings indicate improvements in motivation for change and self-efficacy over time. Finally, we found that the use of brief mindfulness practices were associated with acute reductions in stress and cravings.

This theory-grounded brief motivational intervention may offer a cost-effective and accessible approach for employers to support behavior change related to SSB consumption. Findings from the fully powered randomized controlled trial are needed to determine if the brief intervention can effectively change behavior. This paper establishes the intervention and its framework to inform future implementation.

Article.ArticleTitle: An mHealth Stress Management Intervention for Latino Millennial Caregivers: Pilot Feasibility Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Latino millennial caregivers comprise over one-quarter of millennial family caregivers in the United States. Latino millennial family caregivers face unique challenges due to cultural, structural, and economic burdens that may increase stress and stress-related health effects. These caregivers also report time limitations due to their multiple roles. Technology may be a way to deliver an accessible and flexible intervention to support stress management and emotional regulation in this population.

This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary outcomes of a culturally tailored mobile health (mHealth) intervention to support stress management and emotional regulation for Latino millennial caregivers.

Participants (N=30) were recruited nationally in the United States using a recruitment agency and were randomized to the intervention or waitlist control groups. The 4-week fully automated intervention included daily mindfulness exercises and journaling prompts delivered via a custom mHealth platform. The waitlist control group received a written handout with mindfulness, journaling, and support information. Feasibility data, including recruitment and retention rates and intervention adherence, and postintervention acceptability surveys were collected. Study outcome measures were collected electronically at baseline and 2, 4, and 6 weeks. Primary outcomes included caregiver burden and perceived stress, and secondary outcomes included well-being, informational support, and emotional support. Feasibility and acceptability data were analyzed descriptively alongside study outcome measure data from participants who completed week 6 data collection (n=21). No efficacy testing was conducted.

Enrollment was completed in 12 weeks (N=30), with a 70% (21/30) retention. Participants showed differential adherence, with 60% (6/10) completing a daily journal activity and 30% (3/10) completing a daily mindfulness activity. Adherence patterns were reflected in the acceptability findings, with journaling being preferred over mindfulness. Preliminary outcomes showed varying patterns between the intervention and control groups, with the intervention group showing decreased median burden levels from before (median 20, IQR 15-27.25) to after the intervention (median 15, IQR 10.50-28.75) but increased median stress levels from 19.50 (IQR 12-26.75) to 21 (IQR 8.75-22.75), while the control group burden and stress levels remained the same before and after the intervention. Positive affect and well-being and informational support increased for both groups. Median emotional support levels increased from 15 (IQR 12-20) before the intervention to 16 (IQR 13-19) after the intervention for the control group and decreased from 14.5 (IQR 11.5-17.75) to 14 (IQR 12-17.25) for the intervention group.

Findings demonstrate areas for further intervention iteration to address both adherence and acceptability issues with the mindfulness component of the intervention. Intervention implementation also needs to be addressed, including participant retention rates. Our team will use lessons learned alongside feedback from Latino millennial caregivers to address these issues.

Article.ArticleTitle: Job Coaching and Smartphone-Based Cognitive Behavioral Techniques for Returning to Work and Coping With Unemployment (DRIVEN): Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Unemployment has economic consequences and is associated with emotional distress and impairment. Joblessness is often associated with depression, leading to a vicious cycle of reduced drive to seek work, deepening financial stress, and worsening depression. Few scalable interventions exist that integrate job-search strategies with cognitive behavioral techniques.

The study aimed to determine the efficacy of a Distress-Informed Return-to-Work Intervention (DRIVEN). The primary hypothesis was that DRIVEN would be more efficacious than the control condition in improving job-search behavior. Secondary analyses examined job attainment, depression, and positive affect.

A randomized controlled trial was conducted from August 2023 to September 2024. Assessments were at baseline, weeks 1 through 6, and 8 and 16 weeks postintervention. Participants were a nationwide sample of unemployed job seekers aged 18 years or older who had never earned more than US $100,000 in a year. Participants received either (1) DRIVEN, which included 6 weeks of cognitive behavioral exercises in a mobile app combined with three 1-hour coaching sessions over videoconference or (2) emailed articles containing job-search advice. Primary outcome measures were subscales of a modified Job Search Behavior Scale (preparatory and active job search). Secondary outcomes included job attainment and mental health outcomes.

Participants were a nationwide sample (N=126; mean age 33.6, SD 6.6 y), including 62 (49.2%) females. During the acute treatment phase, mixed-effects linear models showed that for DRIVEN, preparatory job-search behavior increased by an estimated 0.053 (95% CI 0.031-0.076) units per day from baseline, which was a larger effect than in the control condition (0.011, 95% CI -0.011 to 0.033 units per day; P=.008). Active job-search behavior increased by 0.061 (95% CI 0.038-0.084) units per day from baseline, which was significantly larger than in the control group (point estimate: 0.025, 95% CI 0.001-0.047; P=.03). Depression decreased more in the DRIVEN group vs control (DRIVEN point estimate=-0.214, 95% CI -0.255 to -0.172 vs control group point estimate=-0.122, 95% CI -0.163 to -0.081; P=.002), and participants were more likely to get a job in the DRIVEN group (68.3% vs 50.8%; P=.046). Self-report outcomes did not significantly differ during the follow-up periods.

DRIVEN was superior to emailed job-search advice for the primary outcome (job-search behavior) and secondary outcomes (job attainment, depression, and positive affect). This intervention may be beneficial for distressed unemployed individuals seeking work.

Article.ArticleTitle: Quadratus Lumborum versus Transversus Abdominis Plane Block with Oxycodone or Sufentanil for Recovery Quality After Laparoscopic Gastrointestinal Cancer Surgery: A Factorial Randomized Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Quadratus lumborum block (QLB) theoretically provides broader visceral analgesia than transversus abdominis plane block (TAPB), while oxycodone, a dual μ- and κ-opioid receptor agonist, may offer superior visceral pain control compared with sufentanil. We evaluated these two regional techniques and two opioid regimens simultaneously in a factorial design to determine their effects on recovery after laparoscopic gastrointestinal cancer surgery.

In this single-center, randomized, 2×2 factorial trial, 120 adults were randomly assigned to bilateral QLB or TAPB (0.375% ropivacaine 20 mL per side) and oxycodone or sufentanil patient-controlled analgesia. All patients received intraoperative dexmedetomidine and flurbiprofen axetil. The primary outcome was 24-h recovery quality (15-item quality of recovery scale; minimal clinically important difference 6 points). Secondary outcomes included recovery quality at 48 and 72 h, visceral and incisional pain, opioid consumption, rescue analgesia, and adverse events.

For 24-h recovery quality, no significant interaction was found between block and opioid (P = 0.283); QLB vs TAPB (mean [SD] 102.1 [7.9] vs 102.6 [7.6]; mean difference -0.5, 95% CI -3.3 to 2.4; P = 0.740) and oxycodone vs sufentanil (103.7 [6.9] vs 100.9 [8.3]; mean difference 2.8, 95% CI 0.1 to 5.6; P = 0.045) did not reach the Bonferroni-corrected threshold (P < 0.025) or the 6-point difference. Oxycodone was associated with lower visceral pain scores at 1, 6, 24 and 48 h, lower incisional pain scores at 1 and 6 h, and decreased rescue analgesia use (13.3% vs 29.3%). Other outcomes were comparable.

Within comprehensive multimodal analgesia, neither QLB nor oxycodone demonstrated superior recovery compared with TAPB or sufentanil. Exploratory findings of lower postoperative pain and less rescue analgesia with oxycodone should be considered hypothesis-generating.

Article.ArticleTitle: Opioid-Free versus Opioid-Based Anesthesia for Quality of Recovery After Knee Arthroscopy: A Randomized Non-Inferiority Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: We determined whether dexmedetomidine- and esketamine-based opioid-free anesthesia (OFA) was non-inferior to opioid-based anesthesia (OA) for 24-hour Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) after elective knee arthroscopy with femoral nerve block.

In this patient- and assessor-blinded randomized trial, 70 adults undergoing knee arthroscopy with femoral nerve block were allocated to OFA or OA. The primary outcome was 24-hour QoR-15 (non-inferiority margin, -6 points). Secondary outcomes included pain, rescue analgesia, and adverse events. The primary modified intention-to-treat (mITT) analysis included 66 randomized participants with an assessable 24-hour QoR-15 score (33 per group).

Mean 24-hour QoR-15 scores were 126.7 ± 6.4 with OFA and 125.3 ± 6.1 with OA (mean difference 1.45, 95% confidence interval [CI] -1.60 to 4.51), establishing non-inferiority but not superiority. OFA increased rescue opioid requirements (Hodges-Lehmann estimate 10 mg oral morphine equivalents, 95% CI 0 to 10; p=0.037), shortened time to rescue analgesia (hazard ratio 2.11, 95% CI 1.14 to 3.92; p=0.018), and increased early pain. OFA reduced postoperative nausea and vomiting (21.2% vs 48.5%; relative risk 0.44, 95% CI 0.21 to 0.92; p=0.038). Two postoperative bradycardia events occurred with OFA.

In adults undergoing elective knee arthroscopy with femoral nerve block, dexmedetomidine- and esketamine-based OFA was non-inferior to OA for 24-hour QoR-15. OFA was associated with lower postoperative nausea and vomiting, but higher early pain and an earlier need for rescue analgesia.

Article.ArticleTitle: Persistent monocyte activation and remodeling in people with HIV after 36 months of switching from a 3-drug regimen to B/F/TAF or DTG/3TC: a sub-study of the DEBATE trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: The DEBATE study is a randomised trial comparing standard three-drug antiretroviral therapy (ART) with either a two-drug regimen (DTG/3TC) or an alternative three-drug regimen (B/F/TAF) in people with HIV who are virally suppressed. While these regimens are effective in controlling the virus, their impact on the innate immune system is less well understood. Monocytes play a pivotal role in inflammation by bridging innate and adaptive immunity and maintaining the viral reservoir. Persistent monocyte activation in individuals treated with ART, as indicated by altered subsets, proinflammatory cytokines and soluble markers, has been associated with chronic inflammation and non-AIDS comorbidities. This highlights the clinical relevance of monocyte activation even when viral suppression is achieved.

Eleven virally suppressed people with HIV (PWH) randomized to switch to dolutegravir/lamivudine (DTG/3TC, n=6) or to bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (B/F/TAF, n=5) were studied. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) collected at baseline and 36 months after the switch were analyzed using a 17-parameter flow cytometry panel to characterize monocyte phenotype.

Monocyte remodeling in chronically infected, ART-treated PWH involved chemokine receptors such as CX3CR1, CCR5 and CXCR4, which play important roles in cell migration, inflammation and viral reservoir maintenance. Moreover, the upregulation of TAM receptors (MerTK and Tyro3) and CD38 might enhance inflammatory effects in people switching to another three-drug regimen (3DR, B/F/TAF) rather than in those switching to a two-drug regimen (2DR, DTG/3TC). Nonetheless, in DTG/3TC-treated people, inflammation and viral reservoir maintenance might be promoted by the pSTAT3 pathway.

Persistent monocyte activation and immune senescence remain detectable in ART-experienced, virologically suppressed people with HIV after switching to either B/F/TAF or DTG/3TC, indicating that regimen optimization alone does not restore innate immune homeostasis. The enhanced expression of migratory and HIV-related receptors suggests ongoing reservoir maintenance and residual inflammation.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effects of exercise snacks combining resistance training and Wuqinxi on older adults with possible sarcopenia in nursing homes: protocol for a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: To evaluate the effectiveness and feasibility of a Fogg Behaviour Model-based exercise-snack intervention combining resistance training and Wuqinxi for improving physical function among older adults with possible sarcopenia living in nursing homes.
This study is a single-centre, assessor-blinded, two-arm randomised controlled trial protocol.

Older adults with possible sarcopenia will be recruited from a nursing home in Changchun, China, and randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to either a 12-week exercise-snack intervention group or a wait-list control group. Guided by the Fogg Behaviour Model, the intervention combines resistance training and Wuqinxi delivered through short, repeated bouts of exercise to enhance exercise motivation, ability and adherence. Outcome assessments will be conducted at baseline and at weeks 4, 8 and 12. The primary outcome is physical function measured using the Short Physical Performance Battery. Secondary outcomes include upper- and lower-limb muscle strength, dynamic and static balance ability, cognitive function, exercise adherence and adverse events. Data will be analysed using linear mixed-effects models, with group, time and the group × time interaction included as fixed effects and participant-specific random intercepts.
Participant recruitment and data collection are ongoing. Study findings will be disseminated following completion of the trial and final analyses.

This trial will provide evidence regarding the feasibility, safety and effectiveness of a Fogg Behaviour Model-based exercise-snack intervention for improving physical function among older adults with possible sarcopenia in nursing homes.

Article.ArticleTitle: Anaprazole-based versus rabeprazole-based quadruple therapy for Helicobacter pylori eradication: a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: To compare the efficacy and safety of a bismuth-containing quadruple therapy comprising the novel proton pump inhibitor (PPI) anaprazole versus the classical PPI rabeprazole, both combined with amoxicillin and furazolidone, for Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) eradication.

A prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label, non-inferiority design was employed. Consecutive treatment-naïve patients positive for H. pylori who visited the gastroenterology departments of four hospitals in Jiangsu Province between August 2025 and February 2026 were enrolled. Eligible patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to two groups: the anaprazole group (anaprazole 20 mg, amoxicillin 1000 mg, furazolidone 100 mg, and colloidal bismuth pectin 300 mg, twice daily) and the rabeprazole group (rabeprazole 20 mg, amoxicillin 1000 mg, furazolidone 100 mg, and colloidal bismuth pectin 300 mg, twice daily). Both groups received a 14-day treatment course. H. pylori eradication was assessed by ¹³C-urea breath test at 4 weeks after the completion of therapy.

A total of 320 patients were enrolled, with 160 in each group. In the intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis, the eradication rate was 81.9% (95% CI: 75.2% to 87.1%) in the anaprazole group and 80.0% (95% CI: 73.1% to 85.5%) in the rabeprazole group, with a difference of 1.9% (95% CI: -6.7% to 10.5%, P=0.67). In the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) analysis, the eradication rates were 89.1% (95% CI: 83.1% to 93.2%) and 88.9% (95% CI: 82.7% to 93.1%), respectively (difference: 0.2%; 95% CI: -7.0% to 7.4%, P=0.95). In the per-protocol (PP) analysis, the eradication rates were 90.9% (95% CI: 85.2% to 94.6%) and 90.0% (95% CI: 83.9% to 94.0%), respectively (difference: 0.9%; 95% CI: -5.8% to 7.6%, P=0.80). Regarding safety, the incidence of adverse events was slightly higher in the anaprazole group compared to the rabeprazole group (22.50% vs. 15.00%), but the difference was not statistically significant (P=0.09). Medication adherence was similar between the two groups (P=0.60).

The quadruple regimen consisting of anaprazole combined with amoxicillin, furazolidone, and bismuth is non-inferior to the rabeprazole-based quadruple regimen for the eradication of H. pylori infection. There were no significant differences between the two groups in terms of eradication rate, incidence of adverse reactions, or medication adherence. Anaprazole, as an acid-suppressive agent, achieves satisfactory efficacy in H. pylori eradication therapy and holds promise for clinical application.

Article.ArticleTitle: Selected adverse events during the 12-week induction period of a phase III trial of vunakizumab: an exploratory post-hoc analysis.

Abstract.AbstractText: This study aimed to investigate the impact of vunakizumab on adverse events (AEs) in patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.

This exploratory post-hoc analysis used data from a phase III trial (NCT04839016). A total of 690 patients were included. The primary outcome was any AE occurrence during the 12-week induction treatment period.

The incidence of any AE during the induction period was 69.9%. No significant difference in the incidence of any AE was observed between the two groups [risk difference (RD): -2.6%; 95% confidence interval (CI): -9.8% to 4.6%]. Sensitivity analyses showed that vunakizumab was not an independent influencing factor for the occurrence of any AE [odds ratio (OR): 0.828; 95% CI: 0.574 to 1.193; P = 0.311]. At the system organ class (SOC) level, investigations, metabolic and nutritional disorders, infectious and parasitic diseases, and skin and subcutaneous tissue diseases had incidences of 31.9%, 26.7%, 18.0%, and 14.6%, respectively. At the preferred term (PT) level, incidences were 11.3% for hyperuricemia, 7.1% for elevated liver enzymes, and 5.1% for injection site reaction. At the SOC level, the incidence of skin and subcutaneous tissue diseases was lower in the vunakizumab group than in the placebo group (RD: -6.2%; 95% CI: -12.1% to -0.3%). At the PT level, the incidence of injection site reaction was higher in the vunakizumab group than in the placebo group (RD: 4.3%; 95% CI: 1.4% to 7.3%). Notably, after excluding psoriasis exacerbation, the association between vunakizumab and skin and subcutaneous tissue diseases was no longer significant.

Vunakizumab is not significantly associated with the occurrence of any AE or most selected AE categories in patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, whereas vunakizumab is associated with a higher likelihood of injection site reaction and a lower likelihood of skin and subcutaneous tissue diseases. The observed lower incidence of skin and subcutaneous tissue diseases may largely reflect improved control of psoriasis rather than a specific safety benefit of vunakizumab.

Article.ArticleTitle: Rhythmic auditory stimulation combined with split-belt treadmill training improves spatiotemporal gait parameters in hemiparetic stroke patients: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Split-belt walking training (SWT) primarily ameliorates spatial gait asymmetry after stroke, yet its effect on temporal gait parameters remains limited. Rhythmic auditory stimulation (RAS) enhances cadence and rhythmicity via auditory-motor coupling. This study examined whether combining RAS with SWT yields greater walking benefits than SWT alone or conventional rehabilitation.

Thirty patients with post-stroke hemiparesis were randomized to RAS+SWT (n = 11), SWT alone (n = 8), or conventional rehabilitation (control, n = 11). Interventions were delivered for three weeks (five sessions/week). Primary outcomes were spatiotemporal gait parameters: walking speed, cadence, step length, and limping index. Linear mixed-effects models were used, with Hedges' g for effect sizes.

No dropouts occurred. Significant time-group interactions were found for walking speed (F = 10.68, p < 0.001), cadence (F = 5.01, p = 0.014), and affected-side step length (F = 6.21, p = 0.006). The RAS+SWT group showed greater improvements than controls in walking speed (mean difference = 0.167, 95% CI [0.090, 0.245]), cadence (mean difference = 9.340, 95% CI [4.456, 14.223]), and step length (unaffected: mean difference = 0.077, 95% CI [0.039, 0.116]; affected: mean difference = 0.081, 95% CI [0.035, 0.127]), and greater walking speed improvements than the SWT group (mean difference = 0.110, 95% CI [0.022, 0.197]). For the limping index, a significant main effect of group was observed (F = 5.41, p = 0.011); however, the time-by-group interaction was not significant (F = 0.430, p = 0.655).

RAS combined with SWT is more effective than conventional rehabilitation in improving multidimensional spatiotemporal gait parameters-including walking speed, cadence, and affected-side step length-in patients with post-stroke hemiparesis. Compared with SWT alone, the combined intervention yielded greater improvements in walking speed, while no significant between-group differences were observed for cadence or step length. The combined protocol is feasible and safe.

Article.ArticleTitle: Virtual Social Interaction and Psychological Capital in Chemotherapy Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Cancer-related psychological distress remains underaddressed globally. Virtual interventions offer promising alternatives but lack evidence for enhancing Psychological Capital (PsyCap) in chemotherapy patients.
This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of a virtual social interaction intervention on PsyCap in patients undergoing chemotherapy.

This single-blind randomized controlled trial (RCT) enrolled 76 chemotherapy patients hospitalized in the oncology ward of Imam Sajjad Hospital, Ramsar, Mazandaran, Iran. Participants were selected via convenience sampling and then allocated to intervention or control groups using an odd-even (alternating) assignment method. The intervention group participated in 6 weeks of virtual social interactions, consisting of asynchronous materials (recorded audio, short videos, images, PDF, and PowerPoint files) uploaded weekly to Iranian messaging platforms (Eitaa), as well as live synchronous group sessions conducted on the Skyroom platform with a minimum of 10 participants per session. The control group received standard care. The PsyCap was measured using Luthans' Psychological Capital Questionnaire at both baseline and post-intervention. The Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) models (A/B) were adjusted for baseline scores and age.

The intervention group showed improvements across all outcomes, with the total PsyCap score increasing by 23.6 points. Components significantly increased: self-efficacy by 5.8 points, resilience by 5.8, hope by 5.5, and optimism by 6.5 (p < 0.0001). ANCOVA models confirmed robust effects after adjusting for baseline scores and age (Δ SMD > 1).

Virtual social interactions significantly enhance PsyCap in chemotherapy patients. However, to confidently generalize these findings and make recommendations, similar studies need to be conducted and replicated in larger, multicenter trials.

Article.ArticleTitle: Sense of Coherence in Patients After Intensive Care Treatment: A 1-Year Follow-Up Cohort Study.

Abstract.AbstractText: Patients endure physical, mental and cognitive symptoms after critical illness, and coping is vital to their healing process. Little research exists on associations between sense of coherence (SOC) and patients' health improvements after intensive care unit (ICU) discharge.
To describe the trajectory of SOC and how demographic, clinical and psychosocial variables affect SOC in discharged ICU patients during 12 months of follow-up.

A prospective cohort substudy of a neutral randomized controlled trial in Norway involving discharged ICU patients receiving nurse-led follow-up consultations or standard care. Data were collected in the ward (baseline) and after 3, 6 and 12 months. Univariate and multivariate linear mixed models for repeated measures were fitted with SOC-13 score as the dependent variable.

We included 523 patients with a median of three ICU days, median age 57 years, 47% females, 54% receiving mechanical ventilation and stable SOC during follow-up. Higher SOC was associated with increased age (B = 0.12, 95% CI [0.05, 0.18]), no prior mental health problems (B = 6.69, 95% CI [4.19, 9.19]), no prior use of psychotropics (B = 2.37, 95% CI [0.16, 4.58]) and lower post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) at baseline (B = 5.56, 95% CI [3.50, 7.61]). Low educational level (B = -2.25, 95% CI [-4.10, -0.40]), higher pain interference at baseline (B = -0.46, 95% CI [-0.84, -0.08]) and less social support 3 months later (B = -5.93, 95% CI [-7.87, -3.99]) were associated with lower SOC.

During 12 months after ICU discharge, SOC remained stable. Higher age, no previous mental health problems or use of psychotropics, and lower PTSS were associated with higher SOC. Low education, more pain and low social support were associated with lower SOC.
More vulnerable patients deserve greater attention during general rehabilitation after ICU treatment due to low SOC.

Journal.Title: The science of diabetes self-management and care

Article.ArticleTitle: Sustained Psychosocial Benefits of Telehealth Occupational Therapy for Young Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: Long-Term Follow-Up of the Resilient, Empowered, Active Living-Telehealth (REAL-T) Randomized Controlled Trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: The purpose of this study was to examine 12-month outcomes of the Resilient, Empowered, Active Living-Telehealth (REAL-T) intervention for young adults with diabetes.

Young adults ages 18 to 30 years with type 1 diabetes ≥1 year and A1C ≥7.5% (≥58 mmol/mol) were randomized 1:1 to REAL-T (6 months of telehealth occupational therapy) or usual care. Continuous glucose monitor metrics, diabetes distress, and diabetes-related quality of life (DQoL) were assessed at baseline, 6, and 12 months, while A1C and hypothesized mediators were assessed quarterly. Linear mixed-effects models estimated longitudinal treatment effects.

Of 209 randomized participants, 171 (82%) contributed 12-month data. No significant between-group differences were observed for glycemia. REAL-T participants showed greater improvements in emotional distress and diabetes self-efficacy than control group participants. Per protocol analyses excluding untreated participants yielded stronger effects, with significantly improved DQoL and regimen distress.

A telehealth occupational therapy intervention produced durable improvements in emotional distress and self-efficacy over 12 months, supporting psychosocial outcomes as central treatment targets in young adults with type 1 diabetes.
