Article.ArticleTitle: Incidence of Intensive Care Unit Delirium After Heart Surgery: A Feasibility Study of a Forest Environment Intervention.

Abstract.AbstractText: Postoperative delirium is a serious complication in intensive care units (ICUs), particularly following cardiac surgery. It is associated with circadian rhythm disruption, sleep disturbances and adverse outcomes. ICU environments often lack natural time cues, which may exacerbate circadian misalignment and increase delirium risk.

The primary aim of the study was the evaluation of the implementation of two chronotherapeutic ICU interventions regarding recruitment, implementability and safety. Its secondary aim was to descriptively assess postoperative delirium across intervention groups.

This randomized feasibility study was conducted in a tertiary cardiac surgery ICU in Austria. Adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery were allocated to one of three groups: (1) forest environment, (2) light exposure or (3) standard ICU care. Interventions were applied for 12 h daily. Delirium was assessed at three postoperative time points using the confusion assessment method for the ICU (CAM-ICU) and intensive care delirium screening checklist (ICDSC).

This study was conducted between March 2020 and 2025. Seventy-seven patients were enrolled, and 64 remained in the final analytical cohort. Interventions were delivered within routine care. Patients and ICU staff did not report intervention-related concerns. Implementation challenges included ICU restructuring, patient transfers due to COVID-19 and deviations from randomized allocation because of operational constraints. No intervention-related adverse events occurred. Delirium assessments were limited at several time points because of sedation, early ICU discharge or transfer. Across all groups, postoperative delirium was detected in 5 of 130 CAM-ICU completed assessments (3.8%) and 8 of 115 ICDSC completed assessments (6.9%), precluding inferential group comparisons.

Chronotherapeutic environmental interventions were feasible and safe in ICU care. Feasibility results highlighted challenges related to ICU logistics, sedation-related assessment limitations and pandemic-related disruptions. The unexpectedly low delirium incidence limited conclusions regarding intervention efficacy. Future trials should include larger high-risk populations and prospectively defined feasibility outcomes.
Optimized ICU environments, including noise reduction and light management, may support delirium prevention. Chronotherapeutic environmental interventions are feasible additions to routine ICU care.

Article.ArticleTitle: Liquid Compared to Solid Oral Formulations of the Thyroid Hormone Receptor Agonist Elunetirom Under Fasted and Fed Conditions in Healthy Participants.

Abstract.AbstractText: Elunetirom (ABX-002) is a brain-targeted, oral prodrug being developed for the adjunctive treatment of major depressive disorder and bipolar depression. The active moiety, LL-340001, is a thyroid hormone receptor agonist with modest selectivity for beta over alpha thyroid hormone receptors. Upon entering the brain, the intended site of action, elunetirom is hydrolyzed by fatty acid amide hydrolase to LL-340001. In this 3-way randomized, crossover, bioequivalence study, the pharmacokinetics (PK) and safety of an oral liquid formulation used in early clinical development were compared with those of an oral solid formulation intended for later-stage development and potential commercialization, under fasted and fed conditions. Healthy adult participants received single doses of elunetirom (45 μg) as a liquid formulation under fasted conditions and as a solid formulation under fasted conditions and 30 min after consumption of a high-fat meal. Administration of the solid formulation under fasted conditions resulted in elunetirom and LL-340001 exposures similar to those observed with the liquid formulation and is therefore considered to have comparative bioavailability. Food intake increased elunetirom total exposure (AUC) compared with the fasted state but did not affect maximum exposure (Cmax). In contrast, administration with food reduced LL-340001 Cmax compared with the fasted state but did not affect AUC. Food intake delayed the time to reach Cmax (Tmax) for both elunetirom and LL-340001. Elunetirom, administered orally as a liquid and as a solid formulation, was safe and well tolerated under fed and fasted conditions.

Journal.Title: Oral surgery, oral medicine, oral pathology and oral radiology
Journal.ISOAbbreviation: Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol

Article.ArticleTitle: Analgesic effect of full-spectrum cannabidiol oil in burning mouth syndrome: randomized single-blind placebo trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Burning mouth syndrome is a chronic oral pain condition with limited effective treatments. Cannabidiol (CBD) has emerged as a potential therapeutic option, but clinical evidence remains limited. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of full-spectrum CBD oil.

A randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial was conducted in a single-center outpatient clinic for orofacial pain. Thirty-five individuals were screened, and 26 patients were included and randomly assigned to receive CBD oil (n = 13) or placebo (n = 13). Pain intensity and impact were assessed using a visual analog scale, and oral health-related quality of life was evaluated using the Oral Health Impact Profile-14. Safety outcomes included adverse event monitoring.

The sample comprised 96% women, with a mean age of 61.9 years. Baseline measures were comparable. The CBD group showed significant reductions in pain intensity and impact over time, with between-group differences from the third assessment onward (P < .001), while the placebo group remained stable. Quality of life improved significantly in the CBD group (P = .001). No serious adverse events were observed.
Full-spectrum CBD oil improved pain and quality of life with a favorable safety profile, supporting further investigation.
